title: Continuity of the percolation phase transition on Z^d for 3 ≤ d ≤ 10
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For Bernoulli bond (or site) percolation on Z^d at the critical point p_c there is almost surely no infinite open cluster: θ(p_c) = 0. Open for 3 ≤ d ≤ 10. Benjamini and Schramm ask the same for every quasi-transitive graph with p_c < 1.
statement_caveat: The Benjamini–Schramm locator was confirmed on 14 Oct through Häggström, Percolation beyond Z^d: the contributions of Oded Schramm (Ann. Probab. 39, 2011, arXiv:1111.6763), Conjecture 2.5; the DOI matches Electron. Comm. Probab. 1 (1996), paper 8.
source: G. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed. (Springer, 1999); I. Benjamini and O. Schramm, Percolation beyond Z^d, many questions and a few answers, Electron. Comm. Probab. 1 (1996)
locator: Benjamini–Schramm 1996, Conjecture 4 (confirmed: Häggström 2011, Conjecture 2.5); Grimmett 1999, Chapter 10 (to verify)
why_important: The best-known open problem in percolation. A proof in d = 3 needs a method that works below the upper critical dimension, and none exists.
where_it_stands: Proved for d = 2 (Harris 1960, Kesten 1980) and d ≥ 11 (Hara–Slade 1990 for d ≥ 19; Fitzner–van der Hofstad 2017 for d ≥ 11), in half-spaces (Barsky–Grimmett–Newman 1991), on slabs Z^2 × {0,…,k} (Duminil-Copin–Sidoravicius–Tassion 2016), on nonamenable unimodular graphs (Benjamini–Lyons–Peres–Schramm 1999), on graphs of exponential growth and on nonunimodular graphs (Hutchcroft 2016, 2020). Open on Z^3 to Z^10.

title: Conformal invariance and universality of planar critical percolation
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: Critical bond percolation on Z^2, and site percolation on other periodic planar lattices suitably (isotropically) embedded, has a conformally invariant scaling limit: crossing probabilities converge to Cardy's formula and exploration interfaces converge to SLE(6). On Z^2 this would give the arm exponents and ν = 4/3, β = 5/36.
source: R. Langlands, P. Pouliot and Y. Saint-Aubin, Conformal invariance in two-dimensional percolation, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 30 (1994); O. Schramm, Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems, Proc. ICM 2006
locator: Schramm ICM 2006, Section 2 (to verify)
why_important: Smirnov's 2001 proof covers only site percolation on the triangular lattice; why all planar lattices give the same limit is the central universality question of 2D statistical mechanics.
where_it_stands: Known only for site percolation on the triangular lattice (Smirnov 2001; exponents by Lawler–Schramm–Werner and Smirnov–Werner 2001). On Z^2: RSW theory, Kesten's scaling relations (1987), and rotational invariance for FK models with 1 ≤ q ≤ 4, q = 1 included (Duminil-Copin–Kozlowski–Krachun–Manolescu–Oulamara, arXiv:2012.11672, whose abstract names Bernoulli percolation on the square lattice). Two claimed proofs of conformal invariance for bond percolation on Z^2, Tsai–Yam–Zhou (arXiv:1112.2017, 2011) and Zhou (arXiv:2409.03235, 2024), have not been accepted as far as checked; a solver should read both first. Conformal invariance on Z^2 is open. T002 is the q = 1 case of T013.

title: The planar self-avoiding walk converges to SLE(8/3)
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The self-avoiding walk on a planar lattice, taken chordally in a domain at the critical fugacity x_c = 1/μ, converges in the scaling limit to chordal SLE(8/3); and the uniform n-step walk has mean-square end-to-end distance of order n^{2ν} with ν = 3/4.
source: B. Nienhuis, Exact critical point and critical exponents of O(n) models in two dimensions, Phys. Rev. Lett. 49 (1982); G. Lawler, O. Schramm and W. Werner, On the scaling limit of planar self-avoiding walk, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 72 (2004)
locator: Lawler–Schramm–Werner 2004, Section 3 (the conjectures are unnumbered: 3.2 critical exponents, 3.4 scaling limit)
why_important: The flagship problem for two-dimensional polymers. SLE(8/3) is forced by the restriction property; only the existence of the limit is missing.
where_it_stands: The connective constant of the honeycomb lattice is √(2+√2) (Duminil-Copin–Smirnov 2012) and the walk is sub-ballistic (Duminil-Copin–Hammond 2013). On random quadrangulations the walk converges to SLE(8/3) on √(8/3)-Liouville quantum gravity (Gwynne–Miller, arXiv:1608.00956), a random geometry rather than a lattice. No scaling limit and no exponent is proved on any planar lattice.

title: p_c < p_u on every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For every connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive nonamenable graph, the critical probability p_c for an infinite cluster is strictly smaller than the uniqueness threshold p_u, so an intermediate phase with infinitely many infinite clusters exists.
statement_caveat: The converse (amenable implies at most one infinite cluster, so p_c = p_u) is Burton–Keane 1989.
source: I. Benjamini and O. Schramm, Percolation beyond Z^d, many questions and a few answers, Electron. Comm. Probab. 1 (1996)
locator: Benjamini–Schramm 1996, Conjecture 6 (confirmed: Häggström 2011, Conjecture 2.7)
why_important: It would characterise amenability by percolation; the best-known question of percolation beyond Z^d.
where_it_stands: Proved for planar nonamenable graphs (Benjamini–Schramm 2001), Gromov hyperbolic graphs (Hutchcroft 2019), nonunimodular quasi-transitive graphs (Hutchcroft, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 33, 2020), nonamenable Cayley graphs of high girth (Nachmias–Peres, Electron. Commun. Probab. 17, 2012), highly nonamenable graphs and products with trees (several authors), and for some Cayley graph of every nonamenable group (Pak–Smirnova-Nagnibeda 2000). Open in general.

title: KPZ universality beyond exactly solvable models
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: Last-passage percolation, directed polymers and random growth in 1+1 dimensions with general non-degenerate, light-tailed weights or noise have fluctuations of order n^{1/3} with Tracy–Widom limits whose type depends on the geometry (GUE point-to-point, GOE point-to-line), transversal fluctuations of order n^{2/3}, and converge to the KPZ fixed point and the directed landscape.
source: M. Kardar, G. Parisi and Y.-C. Zhang, Dynamic scaling of growing interfaces, Phys. Rev. Lett. 56 (1986); I. Corwin, The Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation and universality class, Random Matrices Theory Appl. 1 (2012)
locator: Corwin 2012, Section 1 (to verify)
why_important: Universality is the content of the KPZ conjecture, and every proof so far rests on an exact formula of an integrable model.
where_it_stands: Proved for integrable models: Poissonian LPP (Baik–Deift–Johansson 1999), geometric and exponential LPP (Johansson 2000), ASEP (Tracy–Widom 2009), the log-gamma and other solvable polymers, the KPZ equation (Amir–Corwin–Quastel 2011), convergence to the directed landscape for integrable LPP (Dauvergne–Ortmann–Virág 2022) and of the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point (Quastel–Sarkar 2023; Virág 2020). For general iid weights even the exponent 1/3 is unproved.

title: Fluctuation exponents of first-passage percolation
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For first-passage percolation on Z^2 with iid nonnegative continuous edge weights with enough moments, Var T(0, nx) is of order n^{2/3} and geodesics wander distance n^{2/3} from the straight line; in every dimension the exponents satisfy χ = 2ξ − 1.
source: H. Kesten, On the speed of convergence in first-passage percolation, Ann. Appl. Probab. 3 (1993); A. Auffinger, M. Damron and J. Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation (AMS, 2017)
locator: Auffinger–Damron–Hanson 2017, Chapter 3 and the open questions there (to verify)
why_important: FPP is the oldest model expected in the KPZ class; the distance between the known bounds and n^{2/3} measures how little of KPZ is understood outside integrable cases.
where_it_stands: Known: Var T ≤ Cn (Kesten 1993) and ≤ Cn/log n (Benjamini–Kalai–Schramm 2003; extended by Benaïm–Rossignol and Damron–Hanson–Sosoe); lower bounds of order log n in d = 2 (Newman–Piza 1995, Pemantle–Peres 1994). χ = 2ξ − 1 is proved assuming the exponents exist (Chatterjee 2013; Auffinger–Damron 2014). The exponents are open.

title: Polyakov's conjecture: the planar O(N) model with N ≥ 3 has a mass gap at every temperature
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the classical O(N) spin model on Z^2 (spins on the sphere S^{N−1}, nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic coupling) with N ≥ 3, spin correlations decay exponentially at every inverse temperature β.
source: A. M. Polyakov, Interaction of Goldstone particles in two dimensions. Applications to ferromagnets and massive Yang–Mills fields, Phys. Lett. B 59 (1975)
locator: Peled–Spinka, Lectures on the spin and loop O(n) models, Section 2.2
why_important: The lattice model of asymptotic freedom. It separates N = 2, where the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition holds (Fröhlich–Spencer 1981), from N ≥ 3, and its four-dimensional gauge analogue is the mass-gap problem.
where_it_stands: Open for every N ≥ 3. Known: no spontaneous magnetisation (Mermin–Wagner), exponential decay at high temperature, the large-N limit. Patrascioiu and Seiler argued for a massless low-temperature phase instead, so the conjecture is not universally believed. Aru–Garban–Sepúlveda (arXiv:2212.06767) still treat it as open; a search on 14 Oct found no 2025–26 claim.

title: Critical behaviour of the three-dimensional Ising model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: At the critical temperature the nearest-neighbour Ising model on Z^3 has ⟨σ_0σ_x⟩ = |x|^{−(1+η)+o(1)} for some 0 < η < 1, its critical exponents exist, and its scaling limit is a non-Gaussian conformally invariant field (the 3D Ising CFT; η ≈ 0.0363 by the conformal bootstrap).
statement_caveat: As stated this is a programme; the checkable forms are the existence of η and the non-Gaussianity of the scaling limit.
source: A. M. Polyakov, Conformal symmetry of critical fluctuations, JETP Lett. 12 (1970); H. Duminil-Copin, 100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice, Proc. ICM 2022
locator: Duminil-Copin ICM 2022, open problems (to verify)
why_important: The most studied unsolved model of statistical mechanics; d = 3 lies below the upper critical dimension and no exact solution is expected.
where_it_stands: Known in d = 3: continuity of the transition (Aizenman–Duminil-Copin–Sidoravicius 2015), sharpness, and c|x|^{−2} ≤ ⟨σ_0σ_x⟩ ≤ C|x|^{−1} at criticality (Simon–Lieb and the infrared bound). Triviality is proved for d ≥ 5 (Aizenman 1982, Fröhlich 1982) and d = 4 (Aizenman–Duminil-Copin 2021). Existence of exponents in d = 3 is open.

title: Extended states for the Anderson model in three dimensions
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For the Anderson model H = −Δ + λV on ℓ²(Z^d), d ≥ 3, with iid potential V whose single-site law is non-degenerate with a bounded density, and small disorder λ, some interval of energies carries absolutely continuous spectrum (delocalised states).
source: P. W. Anderson, Absence of diffusion in certain random lattices, Phys. Rev. 109 (1958); B. Simon, Schrödinger operators in the twenty-first century, in Mathematical Physics 2000 (Imperial College Press, 2000)
locator: Simon 2000, Problem 1 (confirmed)
why_important: Localization is proved in many regimes, but delocalization for a random operator on Z^d never has been; the main open problem of random Schrödinger operators.
where_it_stands: An OpenAI preprint (23 Sep 2026, on GitHub, unrefereed) proves purely absolutely continuous spectrum on a fixed interval near the bottom of the band for iid uniform potentials, every d ≥ 3 and small λ; Jakšić–Last (arXiv:2610.11611) cite it. Before that: absolutely continuous spectrum on regular trees (Klein 1998; Aizenman–Sims–Warzel 2006; Aizenman–Warzel 2013), quantum diffusion up to times of order λ^{−2−κ} in d ≥ 3 (Erdős–Salmhofer–Yau 2007–08), localization at large disorder and band edges (Fröhlich–Spencer 1983, Aizenman–Molchanov 1993). Becker–Oltman (arXiv:2609.20798) treat the product of Z^d with a hyperbolic lattice, not Z^d. General bounded-density laws are open.
retired_reason: REPORTED SOLVED for the uniform law: an OpenAI preprint, Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three (23 Sep 2026, posted on GitHub, not on arXiv, unrefereed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/math/main/preprints/Absolutely-Continuous-Spectrum-for-Weak-Disorder-Anderson-Models-in-Dimensions-at-Least-Three-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), proves for iid potentials uniform on [−1, 1] that for every d ≥ 3 there is λ_d > 0 such that for 0 < λ < λ_d the spectrum on a fixed interval I_d near the bottom of the band, (−6 + e_2/2, −6 + e_2) for d = 3 and −2d + (1/200, 1/100) for d ≥ 4, is almost surely nonempty and purely absolutely continuous (Theorem 1.1). The paper says it settles Simon's Problem 1 for this model; it does not locate the mobility edge or treat quantum diffusion (Simon's Problem 3), and general bounded-density laws, which this row asks for, are not covered. It is the preprint Jakšić–Last cite. Read from the paper 14 Oct by the w673 audit.

title: Localization of the two-dimensional Anderson model at every disorder
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For the Anderson model on ℓ²(Z^2) with iid non-degenerate potential (not almost surely constant) of any strength λ > 0, the spectrum is pure point with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.
source: E. Abrahams, P. W. Anderson, D. C. Licciardello and T. V. Ramakrishnan, Scaling theory of localization, Phys. Rev. Lett. 42 (1979); B. Simon (2000), as in T009
locator: Simon 2000, Problem 2 (confirmed)
why_important: The scaling theory makes d = 2 the marginal dimension and predicts localization at any disorder; a proof at weak disorder would need control on all scales.
where_it_stands: Known at large disorder and band edges; near the spectral edge for Bernoulli potentials on Z^2 (Ding–Smart 2020) and Z^3 (Li–Zhang 2022). In d = 1 localization holds at all disorders (Goldsheid–Molchanov–Pastur 1977, Kunz–Souillard 1980). Weak disorder in d = 2 is open.

title: Confinement in four-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For four-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory with Wilson action and any compact non-Abelian gauge group G ⊆ U(N), N ≥ 2 (SU(2) and SU(3) are the main cases), at every coupling β, Wilson loops of rectangular R × T loops obey an area law |⟨W_{R,T}⟩| ≤ C(β) e^{−c(β)RT}, and the theory has a mass gap.
statement_caveat: The continuum version (existence and mass gap) is a Clay Millennium problem; this row is the lattice, probabilistic form.
source: K. G. Wilson, Confinement of quarks, Phys. Rev. D 10 (1974); S. Chatterjee, Yang–Mills for probabilists, in Probability and Analysis in Interacting Physical Systems (Springer, 2019)
locator: Chatterjee 2019, Problems 4.1 and 5.1
why_important: The deepest open problem joining probability and particle physics: confinement at weak coupling is the physics of the strong force.
where_it_stands: Known: area law at strong coupling (Osterwalder–Seiler 1978); two-dimensional theories solved (Gross, Driver, Sengupta, Lévy); deconfinement for U(1) in 4D at weak coupling (Guth 1980, Fröhlich–Spencer 1982); large-N and gauge-Higgs results (Chatterjee; Jafarov; Basu–Ganguly; Adhikari–Cao; Cao–Park–Sheffield) [verify list]. Weak coupling for SU(N) on Z^4 is open.

title: Infinite cycles in the random interchange process on Z^3 and Z^4 (Tóth's conjecture)
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: In the random interchange process on Z^3 and Z^4 (each edge has a rate-one Poisson clock and transposes its endpoints when it rings), the random permutation at time β has infinite cycles for every large β. Tóth's representation of the spin-1/2 quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet uses the same process weighted by 2^{#cycles}; long-range order there is a related but separate question.
statement_caveat: Tóth's conjecture (1993), as quoted by Elboim and Sly: on Z^2 only finite cycles at every β > 0, and on Z^d, d ≥ 3, infinite cycles for every β > β_c. The planar half is open too. The row was first written for every d ≥ 3; the case d ≥ 5 is proved (see where it stands).
source: B. Tóth, Improved lower bound on the thermodynamic pressure of the spin 1/2 Heisenberg ferromagnet, Lett. Math. Phys. 28 (1993)
locator: Tóth 1993, as quoted in Elboim–Sly 2022, Section 1
why_important: Order in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet in d = 3 is a famous open problem of quantum statistical mechanics (for the antiferromagnet reflection positivity gives order, Dyson–Lieb–Simon 1978); the interchange process makes it a question about random permutations.
where_it_stands: Proved on Z^d for every d ≥ 5 at every large β (D. Elboim and A. Sly, arXiv:2211.17023, 2022). Earlier: regular trees of high degree (Angel 2003; Hammond 2013, 2015), the complete graph with Poisson–Dirichlet cycle structure (Schramm 2005; Berestycki–Kozma), the hypercube, Hamming graphs, random regular graphs and some high-dimensional tori (Miłoś, Ueltschi and coauthors) [verify attributions]. Open for d = 3 and 4.

title: Conformal invariance of the critical FK random-cluster model for 1 ≤ q ≤ 4
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the critical random-cluster model on Z^2 with cluster weight q ∈ [1, 4], interfaces converge to SLE(κ) with κ = 4π / arccos(−√q/2) (κ = 6 at q = 1, 16/3 at q = 2, 4 at q = 4) and the full loop ensemble converges to CLE(κ).
source: O. Schramm, Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems, Proc. ICM 2006; S. Smirnov, Discrete complex analysis and probability, Proc. ICM 2010
locator: Schramm 2006, the FK conjecture in Section 2 (to verify)
why_important: One statement covering percolation (q = 1), Ising (q = 2) and the 3- and 4-state Potts models; only q = 2 is done.
where_it_stands: q = 2 proved (Smirnov 2010; Chelkak–Smirnov 2012; Kemppainen–Smirnov 2019). For 1 ≤ q ≤ 4: continuity of the transition (Duminil-Copin–Sidoravicius–Tassion 2017) and rotational invariance (Duminil-Copin–Kozlowski–Krachun–Manolescu–Oulamara 2020). For q > 4 the transition is discontinuous (Duminil-Copin–Gagnebin–Harel–Manolescu–Tassion 2016). For q = 4 the loops converge to CLE(4) (Averous–Duminil-Copin–He–Lammers–Manolescu, arXiv:2610.08507, Oct 2026, unrefereed). Conformal invariance is open for q ∈ [1, 4) other than q = 2; its q = 1 case is T002.

title: Mean-field critical behaviour of percolation in dimensions 7 to 10
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: Nearest-neighbour Bernoulli percolation on Z^d satisfies the triangle condition for every d > 6, so its critical exponents take their mean-field values (β = 1, γ = 1, δ = 2, η = 0) for all d ≥ 7.
source: M. Aizenman and C. M. Newman, Tree graph inequalities and critical behavior in percolation models, J. Stat. Phys. 36 (1984); G. Slade, The Lace Expansion and its Applications (Springer, 2006)
locator: Slade 2006, introduction (to verify)
why_important: Six is the upper critical dimension; the gap between d = 7 and the proved d ≥ 11 is a known hard limit of the lace expansion.
where_it_stands: Proved for d ≥ 11 (Fitzner–van der Hofstad 2017; Hara–Slade 1990 for d ≥ 19) and for spread-out models in every d > 6 (Hara–Slade 1990; Hara–van der Hofstad–Slade 2003). A renormalisation framework makes mean-field behaviour semi-decidable (Blanc-Renaudie, arXiv:2609.20764); its abstract does not claim d = 7 to 10. Open for nearest-neighbour Z^7 to Z^10; it would settle T001 there.

title: The self-avoiding walk in dimensions 2 to 4 is at least diffusive
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the self-avoiding walk on Z^d with 2 ≤ d ≤ 4, the mean-square end-to-end distance satisfies E|ω(n)|² ≥ cn; in d = 3 it grows like n^{2ν} with ν ≈ 0.588, and in d = 4 like n (log n)^{1/4}.
source: N. Madras and G. Slade, The Self-Avoiding Walk (Birkhäuser, 1993)
locator: Chapter 1 and the open problems listed there (to verify)
why_important: That a self-repelling walk spreads at least as fast as simple random walk looks obvious and is unproved; it is the standard measure of how little is known about SAW in low dimensions.
where_it_stands: Diffusive with Brownian limit for d ≥ 5 (Hara–Slade 1992). In 2 ≤ d ≤ 4: sub-ballistic, E|ω(n)|² = o(n²) (Duminil-Copin–Hammond 2013), and the polynomial lower bound E|ω(n)|² ≥ c n^{4/(3d)} (Madras 2014). In d = 4 the log^{1/4} correction is proved for the susceptibility of the weakly self-avoiding walk (Bauerschmidt–Brydges–Slade 2015); the mean-square displacement n (log n)^{1/4} is open even there.

title: Planar diffusion-limited aggregation has dimension less than 2
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: The diffusion-limited aggregation cluster in Z^2 with n particles has radius at least n^{1/2+ε} for some ε > 0, so its growth dimension is strictly below 2 (numerically about 1.71).
source: T. A. Witten and L. M. Sander, Diffusion-limited aggregation, a kinetic critical phenomenon, Phys. Rev. Lett. 47 (1981); H. Kesten, How long are the arms in DLA?, J. Phys. A 20 (1987)
locator: Kesten 1987, J. Phys. A 20, L29 (the upper bound); the model is Witten–Sander 1981
why_important: DLA is the best-known growth model without a rigorous theory; the only general bound is almost forty years old.
where_it_stands: Kesten (1987) proved the radius is at most C n^{2/3} in d = 2 and C n^{2/d} in d ≥ 3; the higher-dimensional bounds were improved later (Kesten 1990; Benjamini–Yadin 2017, (n log n)^{1/2} in d = 3) [check Kesten 1990 for n^{2/(d+1)}]. Losev–Smirnov (arXiv:2307.14931) extend Kesten's estimate to the dielectric breakdown model in two and three dimensions. The trivial lower bound n^{1/2} has never been improved, so it is not even known that DLA is not a disc-like blob.

title: The satisfiability threshold of random k-SAT for small k
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: For each k ≥ 3, random k-SAT on n variables with αn clauses has a sharp threshold at a constant α_k independent of n, equal to the one-step replica-symmetry-breaking prediction (α_3 ≈ 4.2667).
source: E. Friedgut, Sharp thresholds of graph properties, and the k-sat problem, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999); M. Mézard, G. Parisi and R. Zecchina, Analytic and algorithmic solution of random satisfiability problems, Science 297 (2002)
why_important: The canonical random constraint satisfaction problem; the cavity-method prediction is proved only for large k.
where_it_stands: Proved for k ≥ k_0 (Ding–Sly–Sun 2015). For k = 3 Friedgut's threshold might depend on n. The lower bound 3.52 (Kaporis–Kirousis–Lalas 2006; Hajiaghayi–Sorkin 2003); the upper bound 4.4898 (Díaz–Kirousis–Mitsche–Pérez-Giménez 2009) was lowered to 4.268 by Vorobyev (arXiv:2610.10599, Oct 2026: rigorous, the last step a finite check in exact fractions, also encoded in Lean 4; unrefereed), against the one-step RSB value 4.2667. So 3.52 ≤ α_3 ≤ 4.268. Open for small k.

title: The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: There is a universal c > 0 such that every isotropic log-concave probability measure on R^n has Cheeger constant at least c, independent of n (equivalently, its Poincaré constant is bounded by a universal multiple of the covariance operator norm).
source: R. Kannan, L. Lovász and M. Simonovits, Isoperimetric problems for convex bodies and a localization lemma, Discrete Comput. Geom. 13 (1995)
why_important: The central conjecture of high-dimensional convex probability; it implies the thin-shell conjecture and, through Eldan–Klartag, the slicing problem.
where_it_stands: Bounds improved to n^{o(1)} (Chen 2021), (log n)^5 (Klartag–Lehec 2022) and about √(log n) (Klartag 2023) [verify]. The slicing problem was settled by Klartag–Lehec in 2024 using Guan's bound; KLS itself is open.
retired_reason: SOLVED: a proof is presented by P. Bizeul, B. Klartag and J. Lehec, Presenting a proof of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture, arXiv:2610.05474 (4 Oct 2026), using a criterion of Song and Zhang. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged first by the w672 audit.

title: Glauber dynamics for proper colourings mixes rapidly when q ≥ Δ + 2
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For every graph of maximum degree Δ and every q ≥ Δ + 2, Glauber dynamics on proper q-colourings mixes in time O(n log n).
source: M. Jerrum, A very simple algorithm for estimating the number of k-colorings of a low-degree graph, Random Structures Algorithms 7 (1995)
locator: to verify
why_important: The best-known open problem on the mixing of spin-system Markov chains; Δ + 2 is where the chain is ergodic on every graph.
where_it_stands: Known for q > 2Δ (Jerrum 1995; Salas–Sokal 1997), q > (11/6)Δ (Vigoda 1999), q > (11/6 − ε)Δ (Chen–Delcourt–Moitra–Perarnau–Postle 2019), and q ≥ 1.809Δ for the flip dynamics (Carlson–Vigoda, arXiv:2407.04870, 2024); much better on trees or large girth (Hayes–Vigoda; spectral independence, Chen–Liu–Vigoda 2020–21). For every δ > 0 and large Δ, q ≥ (1 + δ)Δ gives O(n log n) mixing on graphs of girth at least 7 (Jain–Mizgerd–Vigoda, arXiv:2604.11938, Apr 2026) and rapid mixing on graphs of girth at least 5 (Chen–Liu, arXiv:2608.25491, Aug 2026). Open at Δ + 2 on general graphs.

title: The de Almeida–Thouless line of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature β with external field h, the replica-symmetric solution holds (the Parisi measure is a point mass) exactly when β² E[sech⁴(β√q Z + h)] ≤ 1, where q solves q = E[tanh²(β√q Z + h)].
source: J. R. L. de Almeida and D. J. Thouless, Stability of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick solution of a spin glass model, J. Phys. A 11 (1978); M. Talagrand, Mean Field Models for Spin Glasses, Vol. II (Springer, 2011)
locator: Talagrand 2011, research problem on the AT line (to verify)
why_important: With the Parisi formula proved (Talagrand 2006; Panchenko 2013), the location of the replica-symmetry-breaking transition is the best-known remaining question about the SK model.
where_it_stands: Replica symmetry breaking above the AT line is proved (Toninelli 2002). Replica symmetry below it is known away from the line (Talagrand; Jagannath–Tobasco 2017) and for centred Gaussian external fields (W.-K. Chen 2021) [verify]. Open in full.
retired_reason: SOLVED: replica symmetry holds for every (β, h) below the de Almeida–Thouless line with uniform h > 0 (P. Lopatto, Replica symmetry up to the de Almeida–Thouless line in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model, arXiv:2604.11921, Apr 2026); with Toninelli 2002 the line is settled. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged first by the w672 audit.

title: The Friedgut–Kalai entropy–influence conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: There is a universal C such that every Boolean function f: {−1,1}^n → {−1,1} satisfies Σ_S f̂(S)² log(1/f̂(S)²) ≤ C Σ_S |S| f̂(S)²: the spectral entropy is at most C times the total influence.
source: E. Friedgut and G. Kalai, Every monotone graph property has a sharp threshold, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 124 (1996)
why_important: It would say that a function of small total influence is concentrated on few Fourier coefficients, with consequences for learning and sharp thresholds; the best-known open problem of Boolean Fourier analysis.
where_it_stands: Proved for symmetric functions, read-once formulas, random functions and other classes, and with extra factors (O'Donnell–Wright–Zhou 2011; Chakraborty–Kulkarni–Lokam–Saurabh 2016) [verify]. Kelman–Kindler–Lifshitz–Minzer–Safra (FOCS 2020) show that the spectrum of a constant-variance Boolean f is concentrated on 2^{O(I[f] log I[f])} characters; removing the log I[f] factor would essentially give the conjecture. X. Han, A new bound for the Fourier-entropy-influence conjecture, Combinatorica 45 (2025), DOI 10.1007/s00493-024-00133-z, proves H(f) ≤ O(I(f) + Σ_k I_k(f) log(1/I_k(f))); the extra term is not bounded by a multiple of I(f) in general. The weaker Fourier min-entropy–influence conjecture is also open.

title: No bi-infinite geodesics in planar first-passage percolation
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: In first-passage percolation on Z^2 with iid nonnegative continuous edge weights satisfying E min(t_1, …, t_4)^2 < ∞ (the minimum of four independent copies), almost surely no bi-infinite geodesic exists.
source: H. Kesten, Aspects of first passage percolation, École d'Été de Probabilités de Saint-Flour XIV (1986), where the question is attributed to Furstenberg; A. Auffinger, M. Damron and J. Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation (2017)
locator: Auffinger–Damron–Hanson 2017, Chapter 4 (to verify)
why_important: It is the FPP form of the absence of non-trivial ground states in disordered ferromagnets, and part of the KPZ picture of geodesics.
where_it_stands: Proved for exponential last-passage percolation (Basu–Hoffman–Sly 2022; Balázs–Busani–Seppäläinen 2020) and for fixed directions under curvature assumptions (Licea–Newman 1996; Damron–Hanson 2017). Open for FPP.

title: Random planar maps embedded conformally converge to Liouville quantum gravity
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: Uniform random triangulations (and quadrangulations), embedded in the plane by circle packing or by the Tutte (harmonic) embedding, with the counting measure on vertices suitably rescaled, converge to √(8/3)-Liouville quantum gravity. Maps decorated by critical statistical-mechanics models are expected to converge to γ-LQG with γ fixed by the model; that is the wider programme.
statement_caveat: The precise target is the uniform-map case, with the topology (weak convergence of the vertex measure, and the normalisation of the embedding) stated as in the source. Spanning-tree-weighted maps (γ = √2) were done in October 2026 (Holden; Holden–Yu) and no longer count toward the open part.
source: B. Duplantier and S. Sheffield, Liouville quantum gravity and KPZ, Invent. Math. 185 (2011); J. Miller and S. Sheffield, Liouville quantum gravity and the Brownian map I–III (2015–2021)
locator: to verify
why_important: The conformal half of two-dimensional quantum gravity: the metric half (convergence to the Brownian map) is proved, the embedding half is not.
where_it_stands: Known: Gromov–Hausdorff convergence to the Brownian map (Le Gall 2013; Miermont 2013) and its identification with √(8/3)-LQG (Miller–Sheffield); convergence of uniform triangulations under the Cardy embedding (Holden–Sun, announced 2019, published 2023 [verify]); Tutte embedding of mated-CRT maps (Gwynne–Miller–Sheffield 2021). For spanning-tree-weighted maps (γ = √2) the Tutte embedding (Holden, arXiv:2610.10501) and circle packing and Riemann uniformization (Holden–Yu, arXiv:2610.10505), both Oct 2026, converge to √2-LQG. Circle packing and the Tutte embedding of uniform maps are open.

title: Cutoff for random walk on vertex-transitive expanders
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Lazy (or continuous-time) simple random walk on every sequence of vertex-transitive expanders (bounded degree, spectral gap bounded below, size tending to infinity) has cutoff in total variation.
statement_caveat: Statement as usually quoted; source and current status to verify, including whether a transitive counterexample to Peres's product condition is known.
source: Y. Peres, problem posed at the AIM workshop on sharp thresholds for mixing times (2004); E. Lubetzky and A. Sly, Cutoff phenomena for random walks on random regular graphs, Duke Math. J. 153 (2010)
locator: to verify
why_important: Cutoff is proved for random regular graphs and Ramanujan graphs without a structural explanation; transitivity is the natural setting for a general theorem.
where_it_stands: Known for random regular graphs (Lubetzky–Sly 2010), Ramanujan graphs (Lubetzky–Peres 2016), random Cayley graphs of many groups (Hermon–Olesker-Taylor 2021) and explicit families (Lubetzky–Sly 2011). Without transitivity the product condition does not imply cutoff (Aldous; Pak). Open for transitive expanders [verify].

title: A spin-glass phase for the three-dimensional Edwards–Anderson model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The Edwards–Anderson spin glass on Z^3 with symmetric (for example Gaussian) couplings has a low-temperature spin-glass phase: for large β, the overlap of two replicas drawn independently from the Gibbs measure in a box with periodic boundary conditions does not converge to 0 in law as the box grows.
statement_caveat: The structure of that phase (replica symmetry breaking versus the droplet picture, the number of ground-state pairs) is a further open question; statement and source to verify.
source: S. F. Edwards and P. W. Anderson, Theory of spin glasses, J. Phys. F 5 (1975); C. M. Newman and D. L. Stein, Spin Glasses and Complexity (Princeton, 2013)
why_important: The short-range spin glass is the hardest disordered system of statistical mechanics, and even its transition is unproved.
where_it_stands: Open. Known: uniqueness at high temperature; results on ground states in two dimensions and half-planes (Newman–Stein; Arguin–Damron–Newman–Stein 2010); a zero-temperature form of spin-glass order (Chatterjee 2023) [verify]. Positive-temperature spin-glass order is proved on the diamond hierarchical (Migdal–Kadanoff) lattice of effective dimension 3 (Pei, arXiv:2609.38220, Sep 2026), not on Z^3. Pei (arXiv:2609.22301) proves percolation of the blue clusters of the Chayes–Machta–Redner representation in the high-dimensional limit, and for ±1 couplings in d = 7 to 12 with computer assistance; the density imbalance that would give spin-glass order is left open. No proof of a positive-temperature transition in d = 3.

title: Absolute continuity of Bernoulli convolutions (Erdős)
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: For λ ∈ (1/2, 1) let ν_λ be the law of Σ_{n≥0} ±λ^n with independent fair signs. Then ν_λ is absolutely continuous for every λ that is not the reciprocal of a Pisot number (Pisot reciprocals give singular measures, Erdős 1939).
statement_caveat: Sometimes stated as 'the Pisot reciprocals are the only exceptions'; the almost-every form is proved.
source: P. Erdős, On a family of symmetric Bernoulli convolutions, Amer. J. Math. 61 (1939); Y. Peres, W. Schlag and B. Solomyak, Sixty years of Bernoulli convolutions, in Fractal Geometry and Stochastics II (2000)
locator: Peres–Schlag–Solomyak 2000, Section 1 (to verify)
why_important: An eighty-year-old question joining probability, fractal geometry and algebraic number theory; recent progress came from entropy methods and additive combinatorics.
where_it_stands: Absolutely continuous for almost every λ (Solomyak 1995); dimension 1 outside a set of zero Hausdorff dimension (Hochman 2014); dimension 1 for all transcendental λ (Varjú 2019); absolute continuity for Garsia numbers (Garsia 1962) and for explicit algebraic λ near 1 (Varjú 2019). Whether any non-Pisot λ gives a singular measure is open.
retired_reason: REPORTED DISPROVED in the form stated: for every quartic Salem number β the measure ν_{1/β} has Hausdorff dimension strictly below one, so it is singular although 1/β is not a Pisot reciprocal (G. Cheng, X. Fang, X. Ma and H. Zhang, Strict Hausdorff-dimension drop for quartic Salem Bernoulli convolutions, arXiv:2610.12072, Oct 2026, unrefereed; their arXiv:2610.09902 had shown correlation dimension below one). Only two quartic Salem numbers lie in (1, 2), about 1.7221 and 1.8832; for those the drop rests on an exact interval computation with margins near 1e-22, so an independent recomputation should come before the conjecture is treated as dead. Read from the arXiv abstracts 14 Oct; flagged first by the w672 audit and checked by claude-734be81d. Which non-Pisot parameters give absolutely continuous measures stays open; the transcendental case is T075.

title: Conformal invariance of the loop O(n) model for 0 < n ≤ 2
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: For the loop O(n) model on the hexagonal lattice with 0 < n ≤ 2 at Nienhuis' critical weight x_c(n) = 1/√(2 + √(2 − n)), the loops converge to CLE(κ) with n = −2cos(4π/κ), κ ∈ (8/3, 4]. A separate and less precise conjecture: for x > x_c (the dense phase) the limit is CLE(κ′) with κ′ ∈ [4, 8).
source: B. Nienhuis (1982), as in T003; O. Schramm, Proc. ICM 2006, as in T002; S. Sheffield, Exploration trees and conformal loop ensembles, Duke Math. J. 147 (2009)
locator: Schramm ICM 2006 (to verify)
why_important: One conformally invariant picture for the self-avoiding walk (n = 0), the Ising model (n = 1) and the XY-type loop models (n = 2); only n = 1 is proved.
where_it_stands: n = 1 is the Ising model's low-temperature expansion and converges to CLE(3) (Smirnov; Benoist–Hongler 2019). Macroscopic loops at x_c for n ∈ [1, 2] (Duminil-Copin–Glazman–Peled–Spinka 2021). Conformal invariance is open for n ≠ 1.

title: Roughening transition of the three-dimensional Ising interface
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the Ising model on Z^3 with Dobrushin boundary conditions (+ above, − below a horizontal plane) there is a roughening temperature T_R < T_c: below T_R the interface is rigid, and between T_R and T_c the variance of its height above a fixed column grows like log L in a box of side L (the height needs a definition, since the interface is not a graph).
source: R. L. Dobrushin, Gibbs states describing coexistence of phases for a three-dimensional Ising model, Theory Probab. Appl. 17 (1972); H. van Beijeren, Interface sharpness in the Ising system, Comm. Math. Phys. 40 (1975)
why_important: Dobrushin's rigidity theorem is a founding result of rigorous statistical mechanics; the roughening transition predicted above it has never been proved for the Ising model itself.
where_it_stands: Rigidity at low temperature (Dobrushin 1972; van Beijeren 1975). Roughening is proved for integer-valued surface models such as the discrete Gaussian and SOS models (Fröhlich–Spencer 1981). Fine results on the low-temperature interface (Gheissari–Lubetzky 2021–23). Roughening of the Ising interface is open.

title: Furstenberg's ×2 ×3 conjecture
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: Every Borel probability measure on R/Z that is invariant and ergodic under the joint action of x ↦ 2x and x ↦ 3x is either Lebesgue measure or supported on finitely many rational points.
source: H. Furstenberg, Disjointness in ergodic theory, minimal sets, and a problem in Diophantine approximation, Math. Systems Theory 1 (1967)
why_important: The model case of measure rigidity for higher-rank actions; its zero-entropy case blocks a family of conjectures of Margulis and Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss type.
where_it_stands: Furstenberg proved the topological version (closed invariant sets). Positive entropy forces Lebesgue measure (Rudolph 1990; Johnson 1992; Host 1995). Without any invariance hypothesis, positive entropy alone pushes a measure toward Lebesgue under sublacunary multiplier sets, the semigroup generated by 2 and 3 included (Burton–Juschenko, arXiv:2610.07317, Oct 2026, with a companion paper arXiv:2610.04745). The zero-entropy case is open.

title: Rauch's hot spots conjecture for convex domains
domain_name: Brownian motion, stochastic analysis and SPDE
statement: For a bounded convex domain in R^2, every eigenfunction of the second Neumann eigenvalue of the Laplacian attains its maximum and minimum only on the boundary.
statement_caveat: Rauch's original form, for general domains, is false (Burdzy–Werner 1999; Burdzy 2005); the open form is for convex domains, and in higher dimensions.
source: J. Rauch, Five problems: an introduction to the qualitative theory of partial differential equations, Lecture Notes in Math. 446 (1975); R. Bañuelos and K. Burdzy, On the 'hot spots' conjecture of J. Rauch, J. Funct. Anal. 164 (1999)
why_important: A clean statement about heat flow whose main proofs and counterexamples came from reflected Brownian motion and couplings.
where_it_stands: Proved for obtuse triangles (Bañuelos–Burdzy 1999), lip domains (Atar–Burdzy 2004), convex domains with two axes of symmetry (Jerison–Nadirashvili 2000), all triangles (Judge–Mondal 2020) and further classes. Open for general convex planar domains.

title: Zero-one law and ballisticity for random walk in random environment on Z^d
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For iid uniformly elliptic random walk in random environment on Z^d: (a) Kalikow's zero-one law, P(X_n·ℓ → ∞) ∈ {0, 1} for every direction ℓ; (b) Sznitman's conjecture that, for d ≥ 2, transience in direction ℓ implies ballisticity (a non-zero limiting velocity).
statement_caveat: Dimension ranges and exact forms to verify.
source: O. Zeitouni, Random walks in random environment, École d'Été de Saint-Flour XXXI (2004); A.-S. Sznitman, Topics in random walks in random environment, ICTP Lecture Notes 17 (2004)
why_important: The central open problems of multidimensional RWRE, where a non-reversible walk in a random medium resists every general method.
where_it_stands: (a) holds in d = 2 (Zerner–Merkl 2001) and is open in d ≥ 3. (b): Sznitman's conditions (T) and (T′) are equivalent to a polynomial condition (Berger–Drewitz–Ramírez 2014), and ballisticity is known under them and for small perturbations of simple random walk in d ≥ 3 (Sznitman 2003); open in general.

title: Bose–Einstein condensation for interacting bosons in three dimensions
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The interacting Bose gas in three dimensions (for example with a repulsive pair potential), in the thermodynamic limit at fixed density, condenses at low temperature: the one-body density matrix has off-diagonal long-range order.
statement_caveat: Condensation and infinite cycles of the Feynman–Kac permutation are distinct: infinite cycles are necessary but not sufficient for condensation of the interacting gas (Süto, Phys. Scr. 2024, DOI 10.1088/1402-4896/ad8602). Macroscopic cycles are a related open question.
source: R. P. Feynman, Atomic theory of the λ transition in helium, Phys. Rev. 91 (1953); E. H. Lieb, R. Seiringer, J. P. Solovej and J. Yngvason, The Mathematics of the Bose Gas and its Condensation (Birkhäuser, 2005)
why_important: Condensation of interacting bosons at positive temperature is a basic physical phenomenon without a proof; the random-permutation form makes it a percolation-type question.
where_it_stands: Proved for the ideal gas and for interactions that do not couple cycles (Süto 1993, 2002); ground-state and trapped-gas results in dilute limits (Lieb–Seiringer 2002 and later); macroscopic cycles in spatial random permutation models with special interactions (Betz–Ueltschi 2009) [verify]. Open for the interacting gas at positive temperature.

title: Fourier's law from deterministic microscopic dynamics
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: A pinned, non-integrable chain of anharmonic oscillators, coupled at its two ends to Langevin heat baths at different temperatures, has a non-equilibrium steady state whose heat current is of order 1/N in the length N, that is, finite thermal conductivity; in a three-dimensional lattice the same holds for the current per unit cross-section.
statement_caveat: One-dimensional momentum-conserving chains without pinning are expected to violate the law (anomalous conductivity); the open problem is a proof of either behaviour for a deterministic Hamiltonian system.
source: F. Bonetto, J. L. Lebowitz and L. Rey-Bellet, Fourier's law: a challenge to theorists, in Mathematical Physics 2000 (Imperial College Press, 2000)
why_important: Deriving macroscopic heat conduction from microscopic deterministic dynamics is one of the oldest problems of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
where_it_stands: Harmonic chains violate it (Rieder–Lebowitz–Lieb 1967). Proved for models with stochastic exchange of energy or momentum (Bernardin–Olla 2005; Basile–Bernardin–Olla 2006, with anomalous conductivity in 1D) and in weak-coupling limits (Dolgopyat–Liverani 2011) [verify]. Open for deterministic anharmonic chains.

title: Rokhlin's problem: does mixing imply mixing of all orders?
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: Every mixing measure-preserving transformation T of a probability space is mixing of all orders: μ(A_0 ∩ T^{−n_1}A_1 ∩ … ∩ T^{−n_k}A_k) → μ(A_0)⋯μ(A_k) as n_1 and all gaps n_{i+1} − n_i tend to infinity.
source: V. A. Rokhlin, On endomorphisms of compact commutative groups, Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. 13 (1949)
why_important: Open for over seventy years; for Z^2 actions the analogue fails (Ledrappier 1978), so a proof must use something specific to a single transformation.
where_it_stands: Proved for rank-one transformations (Kalikow 1984), finite rank (Ryzhikov 1993), mixing transformations with singular spectrum (Host 1991), and many smooth and algebraic systems. Open in general.

title: The localization transition of random band matrices
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For an N × N random band matrix of band width W (one-dimensional geometry), bulk eigenvectors are localized with localization length of order W² when W ≪ √N, and delocalized with GOE/GUE local statistics when W ≫ √N.
statement_caveat: The delocalized half appears to have been proved in 2025 (Yau–Yin) [verify]; the localized half at the sharp scale is the open part.
source: Y. V. Fyodorov and A. D. Mirlin, Scaling properties of localization in random band matrices: a σ-model approach, Phys. Rev. Lett. 67 (1991); T. Spencer, Random banded and sparse matrices, in The Oxford Handbook of Random Matrix Theory (2011)
why_important: The cleanest model of the Anderson transition: one parameter interpolates between Wigner matrices and one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators.
where_it_stands: Delocalization for W ≫ N^{1/2} (Yau–Yin 2025 [verify]; earlier N^{3/4} and N^{6/7}, Bourgade–Yau–Yin and Erdős–Knowles–Yau–Yin). Localization for W ≪ N^{1/4} (Cipolloni–Peled–Schenker–Shapiro 2023) and earlier W ≪ N^{1/8} (Schenker 2009). Open between N^{1/4} and N^{1/2}.
retired_reason: SOLVED for one-dimensional band matrices: delocalization with Wigner–Dyson statistics and quantum unique ergodicity for W ≫ √N (Yau–Yin, arXiv:2501.01718; L. Erdős and V. Riabov, The zigzag strategy for random band matrices, arXiv:2506.06441, 2025) and exponential localization at scale W² for W² ≪ N (R. Drogin, Localization of one-dimensional random band matrices, arXiv:2508.05802, 2025) together give the conjectured transition for a large class of band matrices. Read from the arXiv abstracts 14 Oct; flagged by the w672 audit. Band matrices in dimensions two and three are T076.

title: First-order transition of the Potts model for q ≥ 3 in three dimensions
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the q-state Potts model on Z^d with d ≥ 3 and every q ≥ 3 the phase transition is discontinuous (the magnetisation jumps at the critical temperature); in particular the 3-state Potts model on Z^3 has a first-order transition.
source: R. B. Potts, Some generalized order-disorder transformations, Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 48 (1952); F. Y. Wu, The Potts model, Rev. Mod. Phys. 54 (1982)
why_important: Mean-field theory and numerics agree, but proofs exist only for large q or large d; q = 3, d = 3 is the standard test case.
where_it_stands: Proved for large q (Kotecký–Shlosman 1982) and for q ≥ 3 in large d (Biskup–Chayes 2003). In d = 2 the transition is continuous for q ≤ 4 (Duminil-Copin–Sidoravicius–Tassion 2017) and discontinuous for q > 4 (Duminil-Copin–Gagnebin–Harel–Manolescu–Tassion 2016). Open for q = 3 in d = 3.

title: The Hausdorff dimension of Liouville quantum gravity
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: Determine the dimension d_γ of γ-Liouville quantum gravity, with its LQG metric, for γ ∈ (0, 2) other than γ = √(8/3), where d_γ = 4.
statement_caveat: Watabiki's formula d_γ = 1 + γ²/4 + √((1 + γ²/4)² + γ²) was the standard prediction; rigorous bounds contradict it for small γ (Ding–Gwynne 2020) [verify], so even the conjectured value is unsettled.
source: Y. Watabiki, Analytic study of fractal structure of quantized surface in two-dimensional quantum gravity, Prog. Theor. Phys. Suppl. 114 (1993); J. Ding and E. Gwynne, The fractal dimension of Liouville quantum gravity: universality, monotonicity, and bounds, Comm. Math. Phys. 374 (2020)
why_important: The basic geometric constant of LQG; it governs distances on random planar maps decorated by critical models (for example spanning-tree-decorated maps, γ = √2).
where_it_stands: The LQG metric exists and is unique (Ding–Dubédat–Dunlap–Falconet 2020; Gwynne–Miller 2021); d_{√(8/3)} = 4; d_γ is continuous and increasing with explicit bounds (Ding–Gwynne 2020). No other value is known.

title: Néel order in the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on the square lattice
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The ground state of the spin-1/2 quantum Heisenberg antiferromagnet H = Σ_{x~y} S_x·S_y on Z^2 (as a limit of finite boxes) has Néel long-range order: the staggered correlation (−1)^{|x|}⟨S_0·S_x⟩ stays bounded away from zero as |x| → ∞.
source: F. J. Dyson, E. H. Lieb and B. Simon, Phase transitions in quantum spin systems with isotropic and nonisotropic interactions, J. Stat. Phys. 18 (1978); T. Kennedy, E. H. Lieb and B. S. Shastry, Existence of Néel order in some spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnets, J. Stat. Phys. 53 (1988)
why_important: The parent model of the cuprate superconductors; reflection positivity proves order for larger spins and higher dimensions and stops exactly at spin 1/2 in the plane. The ferromagnetic counterpart is T012.
where_it_stands: Order at low temperature in d ≥ 3 for S ≥ 1 (Dyson–Lieb–Simon 1978); ground-state order on Z^2 for S ≥ 1 (Neves–Perez 1986; Kubo–Kishi 1988) and for S = 1/2 in d ≥ 3 (Kennedy–Lieb–Shastry 1988) [verify]. Quantum Monte Carlo gives a staggered magnetisation near 0.31 for S = 1/2 on Z^2. Open for S = 1/2 on Z^2.

title: Plurality is stablest and the standard simplex conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For k ≥ 3 and ρ ∈ (0, 1), among partitions of Gaussian space R^n (n ≥ k − 1) into k sets of Gaussian measure 1/k each, the probability that ρ-correlated standard Gaussians X, Y land in the same set is maximised by the standard simplex partition (the Voronoi cells of a regular simplex centred at 0). The discrete form: among low-influence functions [k]^n → [k] with balanced outputs, plurality is the most noise-stable.
statement_caveat: k = 2 is Borell's theorem (and Majority is Stablest, Mossel–O'Donnell–Oleszkiewicz 2010). The conjecture fails for some unequal measures (Heilman) [verify].
source: S. Khot, G. Kindler, E. Mossel and R. O'Donnell, Optimal inapproximability results for MAX-CUT and other 2-variable CSPs?, SIAM J. Comput. 37 (2007); M. Isaksson and E. Mossel, New maximally stable Gaussian partitions with discrete applications, Israel J. Math. 189 (2012)
why_important: It would give the optimal hardness of approximation for MAX-k-CUT under the Unique Games Conjecture, and it is the multi-set extension of Borell's isoperimetric theorem.
where_it_stands: The ρ → 1 limit, the Gaussian multi-bubble conjecture, was proved by Milman and Neeman (Ann. of Math. 2022, and later papers for more sets). Heilman (arXiv:2608.00333) proves k = 3 for ρ ∈ [−1/2, 2/5], which settles the MAX-3-CUT conjecture of Khot–Kindler–Mossel–O'Donnell under the Unique Games Conjecture; earlier k = 3 results for small ρ > 0 (Heilman 2014; Heilman–Tarter) [verify]. Open for k = 3 with ρ > 2/5 and for every k ≥ 4.

title: The Courtade–Kumar conjecture (most informative Boolean function)
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Let X be uniform on {−1,1}^n and Y the output of X through a binary symmetric channel with crossover probability α, applied coordinatewise. Then every Boolean f: {−1,1}^n → {−1,1} satisfies I(f(X); Y) ≤ 1 − h(α), with equality for dictator functions (h the binary entropy).
source: T. A. Courtade and G. R. Kumar, Which Boolean functions maximize mutual information on noisy inputs?, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 60 (2014)
why_important: A one-line information-theoretic statement about the hypercube that resists hypercontractivity and every Fourier argument tried so far.
where_it_stands: True for α close to 1/2 (Samorodnitsky 2016) and for balanced f in further ranges [verify]; the two-function version I(f(X); g(Y)) ≤ 1 − h(α) was proved by Pichler–Piantanida–Matz (2018) [verify]. Open for general α.
retired_reason: SOLVED: two independent proofs, Vu Khac Ky and Tuan Tran, Dictators are most informative, arXiv:2609.24184, and Z. Chen, A. Gohari, A. Javanmard, H. Lin, V. Mirrokni, C. Nair and D. P. Woodruff, A proof of the most informative Boolean function conjecture, arXiv:2609.24931 (computer-assisted, with the argument verified in Lean), both 21 Sep 2026 and unrefereed. Read from the arXiv abstracts 14 Oct; flagged first by the w672 audit and checked by claude-734be81d.

title: Talagrand's convolution conjecture on the hypercube
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For f ≥ 0 on {−1,1}^n with E f = 1 and a fixed noise parameter t > 0, the noised function P_t f satisfies P(P_t f > s) ≤ C_t / (s √(log s)) for all s > e, with C_t independent of n: noise improves Markov's inequality by a factor √(log s).
source: M. Talagrand, A conjecture on convolution operators, and a non-Dunford–Pettis operator on L^1, Israel J. Math. 68 (1989)
why_important: Talagrand offered a prize for it; it asks for a form of regularisation by the heat flow that survives with no moment beyond L^1.
where_it_stands: The Gaussian analogue (Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup) is proved: Ball–Barthe–Bednorz–Oleszkiewicz–Wolff 2013 and Eldan–Lee 2018 up to a log log factor, Lehec 2016 removing it [verify]. On the cube, bounds with an extra log log factor are known (Eldan–Lee–Lehec 2017; later work [verify]). Open on the cube with the sharp factor.
retired_reason: REPORTED SOLVED: J. Lu, S. Guo and E. X. Fang, Weak-type bounds for convolution on the Boolean hypercube, arXiv:2608.15515 (Aug 2026, unrefereed), prove ψ_{μ_a}(u) ≤ C_a/√(log u) for the biased product measures μ_a, which is Talagrand's 1989 conjecture. The abstract credits the discovery of the proof to an automated research agent ('Odin'), so it wants a careful human check. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged first by the w672 audit and checked by claude-734be81d.

title: The Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Every polynomial f: {−1,1}^n → [0,1] of degree at most d has a variable whose influence is at least (Var f / d)^{O(1)}.
source: S. Aaronson and A. Ambainis, The need for structure in quantum speedups, Theory of Computing 10 (2014)
why_important: It would show that quantum query algorithms give at most a polynomial speedup on almost all inputs for every total-domain problem without structure; it is a bounded-function strengthening of the Friedgut–Kalai–Naor and Bourgain theorems.
where_it_stands: Proved for symmetric polynomials and several structured classes, and reduced to block-multilinear (decoupled) forms (O'Donnell–Zhao 2016) [verify]; known with influence exponentially small in d. It holds after a positive fraction of random restrictions under a variance hypothesis (Bhattacharya, arXiv:2402.13952) and for completely bounded block-multilinear forms (Escudero Gutiérrez–Saucedo–Palazuelos, arXiv:2609.05201). Open for bounded polynomials in general.

title: Logarithmic corrections for self-avoiding walk in four dimensions
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the strictly self-avoiding walk on Z^4, c_n ~ A μ^n (log n)^{1/4} and the mean-square end-to-end distance is ~ D n (log n)^{1/4}.
source: Renormalisation-group prediction (Brézin, Le Guillou and Zinn-Justin 1973; Duplantier 1986) [verify]; G. Slade, Self-avoiding walk, the renormalisation group and the lace expansion, Proc. ICM 2022 [verify]
why_important: Four is the upper critical dimension: above it the lace expansion gives Brownian behaviour, below it nothing is proved; the logarithm at d = 4 is the test case for a rigorous renormalisation group.
where_it_stands: Proved for the continuous-time weakly self-avoiding walk (Bauerschmidt–Brydges–Slade 2015; Bauerschmidt–Slade–Tomberg–Wallace 2017) and for hierarchical models (Brydges–Imbrie 2003). Open for the strictly self-avoiding walk. See also T015.

title: The crystallization problem
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: Classical particles in R^2 or R^3 interacting through the Lennard-Jones pair potential V(r) = r^{−12} − 2r^{−6} crystallize: ground states are periodic (triangular in the plane, close-packed in space), and at low positive temperature the infinite-volume Gibbs states have long-range order, positional in d = 3 and orientational in d = 2.
statement_caveat: Three conjectures share this row: ground-state crystallization, order at low positive temperature, and the freezing of hard spheres at high density. Positional order is impossible in d = 2 at positive temperature (a Mermin–Wagner theorem, Richthammer 2007), which is why the planar statement is orientational.
source: C. Radin, Low temperature and the origin of crystalline symmetry, Int. J. Mod. Phys. B 1 (1987); X. Blanc and M. Lewin, The crystallization conjecture: a review, EMS Surv. Math. Sci. 2 (2015)
why_important: Why matter forms crystals is among the oldest unproved facts of statistical mechanics; even the zero-temperature problem is open for realistic potentials.
where_it_stands: Zero temperature: proved in d = 2 for some short-range potentials (Radin 1981; Theil 2006) and in d = 3 for special potentials (Flatley–Theil 2015); open for the Lennard-Jones potential. Positive temperature: orientational order shown for some planar models with defects (Aumann 2015) [verify]; open for continuum particles.

title: Fixation of zero-temperature Glauber dynamics for the Ising model
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: Run zero-temperature Glauber dynamics of the Ising model on Z^d from iid spins that are + with probability p. (a) For every d ≥ 2 and every p > 1/2, every site is eventually + forever. (b) For p = 1/2 and d ≥ 3, every site flips infinitely often.
source: L. R. Fontes, R. H. Schonmann and V. Sidoravicius, Stretched exponential fixation in stochastic Ising models at zero temperature, Comm. Math. Phys. 228 (2002); S. Nanda, C. M. Newman and D. L. Stein, Dynamics of Ising spin systems at zero temperature, in On Dobrushin's Way (AMS, 2000)
why_important: The basic question of coarsening after a quench: whether the majority phase wins from any bias, and whether a symmetric quench ever freezes.
where_it_stands: For p = 1/2 and d = 2 every site flips infinitely often (Nanda–Newman–Stein 2000). Fixation at + for p close to 1 (Fontes–Schonmann–Sidoravicius 2002) and for p > 1/2 + ε_d with ε_d → 0 as d → ∞ (Morris 2011). Open for p slightly above 1/2 in fixed d, and (b) is open.

title: Lifshitz law for the low-temperature Ising Glauber dynamics
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: For continuous-time Glauber dynamics (each site updated at rate one) of the two-dimensional Ising model at any temperature below T_c, in an L × L box with + boundary conditions, the mixing time is of order L^2 (up to constants depending on the temperature).
source: I. M. Lifshitz, Kinetics of ordering during second-order phase transitions, Sov. Phys. JETP 15 (1962); D. S. Fisher and D. A. Huse, Dynamics of droplet fluctuations in pure and random Ising systems, Phys. Rev. B 36 (1987); F. Martinelli, Lectures on Glauber dynamics for discrete spin models, Saint-Flour 1997 (Lecture Notes in Math. 1717, 1999)
why_important: Motion by mean curvature of the interface is the predicted mechanism; proving it at positive temperature needs control of the interface over long times.
where_it_stands: At zero temperature: order L^2 in d = 2 (Lacoin–Simenhaus–Toninelli 2014) and up to logarithms in all d (Lacoin 2014) [verify]. Below T_c in d = 2: quasi-polynomial bound L^{O(log L)} (Lubetzky–Martinelli–Sly–Toninelli 2013). Gheissari–Sly (arXiv:2605.08052) prove rapid phase ordering from sufficiently biased iid initial states for every β > β_c in two dimensions; their proof still uses the quasi-polynomial plus-boundary bound. A polynomial bound at positive temperature is open.

title: Recurrence and transience of once-reinforced random walk
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Once-reinforced random walk on Z^d (an edge already crossed has weight 1 + δ, an uncrossed edge weight 1) is recurrent on Z^2 for every δ > 0; on Z^d with d ≥ 3 it is transient for small δ and recurrent for large δ.
statement_caveat: The precise conjectured picture in d ≥ 3 is to verify.
source: B. Davis, Reinforced random walk, Probab. Theory Related Fields 84 (1990); R. Pemantle, A survey of random processes with reinforcement, Probab. Surv. 4 (2007)
why_important: The simplest self-interacting walk whose long-time behaviour is unknown on the plane; the methods that settled the linearly reinforced walk (through the VRJP) do not apply.
where_it_stands: Recurrent on Z (Davis 1990) and on ladders (Sellke 2006; Vervoort) [verify]; a recurrence/transience phase transition on trees and on Z^d-like trees (Kious–Sidoravicius 2018; Collevecchio–Kious–Sidoravicius 2020). Transient and diffusive for d ≥ 6 and small reinforcement (Elboim–Kozma, arXiv:2601.17972, Jan 2026); the expected range is at least of order n^{d/(d+1)} for every d ≥ 2 and every reinforcement (Bou-Rabee–Peres, arXiv:2610.00090, Sep 2026), the order predicted for large reinforcement. Open on Z^2, for d = 3, 4, 5, and for large reinforcement in every d ≥ 3.

title: Monotonicity of the speed of biased random walk on Galton–Watson trees
domain_name: Branching processes, trees and genealogies
statement: For λ-biased random walk on a supercritical Galton–Watson tree with no leaves and mean offspring m > 1 (bias λ toward the root, transient for λ < m), the speed is strictly decreasing in λ on (0, m).
source: R. Lyons, R. Pemantle and Y. Peres, Biased random walks on Galton–Watson trees, Probab. Theory Related Fields 106 (1996); R. Lyons and Y. Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks (Cambridge, 2016)
why_important: A natural monotonicity that fails on trees with leaves (traps make the speed zero for strong bias) and should hold without them, yet resists every coupling.
where_it_stands: Proved for λ ≤ 1/2 (Aïdékon 2014) and for λ near 0 (Ben Arous–Fribergh–Sidoravicius 2014); the derivative at λ = 1 is known through the Einstein relation (Ben Arous–Hu–Olla–Zeitouni 2013) [verify]. Also known for λ ≤ m_1/(1 + √(1 − 1/m_1)) when every vertex has at least m_1 ≥ 2 children [verify attribution]; with computer assistance, strictly decreasing on [0, 1.755] for offspring uniform on {2, 3} (Mandarapu–Kunkunuru, arXiv:2609.29894, Sep 2026). Open on the rest of (0, m).

title: Number of components of the minimal spanning forest on Z^d
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: The minimal spanning forest of Z^d with iid uniform edge weights (free and wired coincide on Z^d) is a single tree for d < 8 and has infinitely many components for d > 8.
source: C. M. Newman and D. L. Stein, Spin-glass model with dimension-dependent ground state multiplicity, Phys. Rev. Lett. 72 (1994); R. Lyons, Y. Peres and O. Schramm, Minimal spanning forests, Ann. Probab. 34 (2006)
why_important: It is the zero-temperature limit of a disordered system and is tied to invasion percolation and the critical percolation two-point function; the predicted switch at d = 8 comes from the critical exponents.
where_it_stands: A single tree on Z^2 (Alexander 1995). On amenable transitive graphs the free and wired forests agree (Lyons–Peres–Schramm 2006). Open for every d ≥ 3 [verify high d].

title: Strict convexity of the limit shape in first-passage percolation
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For first-passage percolation on Z^d, d ≥ 2, with iid continuous edge weights satisfying E min(t_1, …, t_{2d})^d < ∞ (so that the shape theorem holds), the limit shape (the asymptotic shape of the ball of passage time t, scaled by t) is strictly convex.
statement_caveat: Weights with an atom at their minimum of mass above the directed-percolation threshold give flat edges (Durrett–Liggett 1981), hence the continuity assumption.
source: H. Kesten, Aspects of first passage percolation, École d'Été de Saint-Flour XIV (Lecture Notes in Math. 1180, 1986); A. Auffinger, M. Damron and J. Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017)
why_important: Almost every deeper result on geodesics and fluctuations in first-passage percolation assumes strict convexity or curvature of the limit shape, which is unproved for any continuous distribution.
where_it_stands: The limit shape is compact and convex (Cox–Durrett 1981); examples of non-polygonal shapes (Damron–Hochman 2013). Strict convexity is unknown for every continuous distribution, including exponential weights.

title: Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the SK model with no external field at inverse temperature β > 1, the Parisi measure (the unique minimiser in the Parisi formula) is full-RSB: its support is an interval [0, q_*] and it has an absolutely continuous part, rather than finitely many atoms.
source: G. Parisi, A sequence of approximated solutions to the S-K model for spin glasses, J. Phys. A 13 (1980); M. Talagrand, Mean Field Models for Spin Glasses, Vol. II (Springer, 2011)
why_important: Full RSB is the central prediction of Parisi's theory beyond the free energy, and at zero temperature it implies the no-overlap-gap property that makes near-optimal ground states findable in polynomial time (Montanari 2019).
where_it_stands: Proved: Lopatto (arXiv:2607.11756, v4), for zero external field and every β > 1, with Zhou (arXiv:2504.00269) first just past the critical temperature. Before that: the Parisi formula (Guerra 2003; Talagrand 2006), ultrametricity (Panchenko 2013), uniqueness of the minimiser (Auffinger–Chen 2015) and infinitely many steps of RSB at zero temperature (Auffinger–Chen–Zeng 2020). The external-field transition is T020.
retired_reason: SOLVED: full replica symmetry breaking at zero external field for every β > 1 (P. Lopatto, arXiv:2607.11756, v4): the Parisi measure has support [0, q_β], a smooth density there and an atom at q_β. Zhou (arXiv:2504.00269) had covered temperatures slightly below the critical one. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged by the w672 audit.

title: Uniqueness of the ground-state pair of the two-dimensional Edwards–Anderson spin glass
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the Edwards–Anderson spin glass on Z^2 with iid continuous couplings, every metastate built from boundary conditions independent of the couplings is supported on a single pair (σ, −σ) of infinite-volume ground states. The stronger statement, that almost surely there is only one such pair among all infinite-volume ground states, is a separate conjecture.
source: C. M. Newman and D. L. Stein, Ordering and broken symmetry in short-ranged spin glasses, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 15 (2003); D. S. Fisher and D. A. Huse, Ordered phase of short-range Ising spin-glasses, Phys. Rev. Lett. 56 (1986)
why_important: The number of ground states is where the droplet and replica-symmetry-breaking pictures of short-range spin glasses first disagree, and two dimensions is the case where every method can be tried.
where_it_stands: Proved (claimed): Newman and Stein (arXiv:2510.27507v2, October 2025, revised 2026) show that a critical droplet with space-filling boundary cannot occur in ground states generated by coupling-independent boundary conditions, deduce that incongruent ground states would have energy differences with variance of the order of the volume, and use this to prove that in two dimensions the metastate generated by, for example, periodic boundary conditions is unique and supported on a single pair of spin-reversed ground states (abstract read 14 Oct). Before that: uniqueness of the ground-state pair in the half-plane (Arguin–Damron–Newman–Stein 2010); restrictions on incongruent states in Z^d (Arguin–Newman–Stein, later papers) [verify]. The stronger statement, one pair among all infinite-volume ground states, and every higher dimension remain open.
retired_reason: SOLVED as stated (claim): Newman and Stein, arXiv:2510.27507v2 (revised 2026), prove that in two dimensions the metastate generated by coupling-independent boundary conditions, periodic ones being the example the abstract names, is unique and supported on a single pair of spin-reversed ground states (abstract read 14 Oct; flagged by w673). A preprint claim, not independently checked. The stronger all-ground-states statement is not claimed and is not listed separately.

title: Diffusion in the random Lorentz gas at fixed density
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: A point particle moving at unit speed with specular reflection among fixed hard balls of radius r centred at the points of a Poisson process in R^d (d ≥ 2, fixed density and radius below the threshold at which the vacant set stops percolating, the particle started with a random direction in the unbounded component of the vacant set) behaves diffusively: X_t/√t converges to a non-degenerate Gaussian. In d = 2 the motion is recurrent.
statement_caveat: Started anywhere outside the balls the statement is false: with positive probability the origin lies in a bounded vacant cavity and the particle stays bounded (w672 audit, 14 Oct). Annealed or quenched limit to be fixed.
source: H. A. Lorentz, The motion of electrons in metallic bodies, Proc. Amsterdam Acad. 7 (1905); H. Spohn, Large Scale Dynamics of Interacting Particles (Springer, 1991)
why_important: The simplest deterministic dynamics in a random medium; diffusion has been derived only through limits that make the scatterers sparse, and the fixed-density gas is the honest version of the question.
where_it_stands: In the Boltzmann–Grad limit the motion becomes a Markov flight process (Gallavotti 1969; Spohn 1978; Boldrighini–Bunimovich–Sinai 1983); diffusion under a joint Boltzmann–Grad and diffusive scaling, past the kinetic time scale (Lutsko–Tóth 2020) [verify]. Periodic scatterers: CLT with finite horizon (Bunimovich–Sinai 1981), √(t log t) with infinite horizon (Szász–Varjú 2007). Open at fixed density, including recurrence in d = 2.

title: Bulk universality and quantum unique ergodicity for random regular graphs of fixed degree
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For fixed d ≥ 3, the adjacency eigenvalues of a uniform random d-regular graph on N vertices have GOE local statistics in the bulk of the Kesten–McKay law as N → ∞, and the eigenvectors are delocalized and satisfy quantum unique ergodicity.
statement_caveat: Bulk statistics at fixed d were proved in October 2026 (He–Huang–Wang, arXiv:2610.08127); the open part is quantum unique ergodicity, whose precise form (which observables, which rate) must be fixed before work on it.
source: D. Jakobson, S. D. Miller, I. Rivin and Z. Rudnick, Eigenvalue spacings for regular graphs, in Emerging Applications of Number Theory (IMA Vol. 109, 1999)
why_important: The discrete analogue of the Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture for chaotic billiards, for a model with no independent matrix entries and bounded degree.
where_it_stands: Bulk GOE statistics for degree growing with N (Bauerschmidt–Huang–Knowles–Yau 2017, 2020); local Kesten–McKay law and delocalization for fixed large d (Bauerschmidt–Huang–Yau 2019); edge Tracy–Widom statistics and the Ramanujan property with probability about 0.69 for fixed d (Huang–McKenzie–Yau 2024) [verify]. He–Huang–Wang (arXiv:2610.08127) prove Sine_1 bulk universality (point process, gaps and fixed-energy correlations) for every fixed d ≥ 3. Quantum unique ergodicity at fixed d is open.

title: Dimensional reduction for lattice trees and lattice animals
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The critical exponents of lattice trees and lattice animals in Z^d equal those of the Yang–Lee edge singularity in dimension d − 2 (Parisi–Sourlas); in particular the number of lattice animals of size n grows like λ^n n^{−θ} with θ = 1 in d = 2 and θ = 3/2 in d = 3.
source: G. Parisi and N. Sourlas, Critical behavior of branched polymers and the Lee–Yang edge singularity, Phys. Rev. Lett. 46 (1981); D. C. Brydges and J. Z. Imbrie, Branched polymers and dimensional reduction, Ann. of Math. 158 (2003)
why_important: A supersymmetry argument predicts exact exponents for branched polymers in low dimension; the continuum version is a theorem, and the lattice version would make it a fact about counting clusters.
where_it_stands: Proved for a continuum model of branched polymers in d = 2, 3 (Brydges–Imbrie 2003). Lattice trees and animals are mean-field in high dimension (Hara–Slade 1990). Open for lattice models in d = 2, 3.

title: Gaboriau's fixed price problem
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: Every countable group Γ has fixed price: all free probability-measure-preserving actions of Γ have the same cost.
source: D. Gaboriau, Coût des relations d'équivalence et des groupes, Invent. Math. 139 (2000)
why_important: Cost is the measured analogue of the rank of a group, and fixed price is the main open problem of measured group theory; it is tied to percolation and spanning forests on Cayley graphs (Lyons) and to rank gradient (Abért–Nikolov).
where_it_stands: Fixed price holds for amenable groups (cost 1), free groups, and many classes closed under products and commensurability (Gaboriau 2000); higher-rank semisimple Lie groups and their lattices have fixed price 1 (Fraczyk–Mellick–Wilkens 2023, via Poisson–Voronoi tessellations) [verify]. Open in general.
note: Fame borderline in the w672 audit (14 Oct); kept for now.

title: Is the Liouville property of a group independent of the generating set?
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For a finitely generated group Γ, simple random walk on the Cayley graph Cay(Γ, S) has trivial Poisson boundary (no non-constant bounded harmonic functions) either for every finite symmetric generating set S or for none.
statement_caveat: The analogue for quasi-isometric graphs is false (T. Lyons 1987), and for quasi-isometric groups as well (Erschler 2004) [verify]; the question here is for one group with different generating sets.
source: V. A. Kaimanovich and A. M. Vershik, Random walks on discrete groups: boundary and entropy, Ann. Probab. 11 (1983)
why_important: Whether the Poisson boundary is a property of the group or of the walk is the basic question of the entropy theory of random walks on groups.
where_it_stands: True for groups where every measure is Liouville (the Choquet–Deny groups, characterised by Frisch–Hartman–Tamuz–Vahidi Ferdowsi 2019) and for groups with no Liouville measure at all; lamplighter boundaries identified (Erschler; Lyons–Peres 2021). Open in general [verify].

title: Concentration of the chromatic number of G(n, 1/2)
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: Determine the width of concentration of χ(G(n, 1/2)): conjecturally, for a set of n of density one, the shortest interval containing χ(G(n, 1/2)) with probability tending to 1 has length n^{1/2+o(1)}.
statement_caveat: The exact form of the conjecture (most n versus all n) is to verify.
source: E. Shamir and J. Spencer, Sharp concentration of the chromatic number on random graphs G_{n,p}, Combinatorica 7 (1987); B. Bollobás, How sharp is the concentration of the chromatic number?, Combin. Probab. Comput. 13 (2004); A. Heckel and O. Riordan, How does the chromatic number of a random graph vary?, J. London Math. Soc. 108 (2023) [verify]
why_important: Concentration of the chromatic number is a classical showcase of martingale methods; whether the √n window is the truth was open for thirty years.
where_it_stands: Concentration on an interval of length about √n (Shamir–Spencer 1987); not concentrated on fewer than n^{1/4−ε} values for infinitely many n (Heckel 2021), improved to n^{1/2−ε} (Heckel–Riordan 2023) [verify]. The behaviour for typical n is open.

title: Robbins' problem: minimising the expected rank with full information
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Observe iid Uniform(0, 1) values X_1, …, X_n one at a time, seeing their values; choose a stopping time τ to minimise the expected rank of X_τ among all n values. Determine V = lim V_n, and the form of an optimal rule.
source: F. T. Bruss and T. S. Ferguson, Minimizing the expected rank with full information, J. Appl. Probab. 30 (1993); F. T. Bruss, What is known about Robbins' problem?, J. Appl. Probab. 42 (2005)
why_important: The best-known open problem of optimal stopping: an innocent extension of the secretary problem whose optimal rule depends on the whole history.
where_it_stands: The limit V exists and lies roughly between 1.908 and 2.33 (Bruss–Ferguson 1993; later improvements of the upper bound) [verify bounds]; memoryless threshold rules are not optimal (Bruss–Ferguson). Brice–Bruss–Majumdar–Raskin (arXiv:2608.27419) give near-optimal strategies and improved values for n = 5 to 100 through finite-state abstractions; exact values are known only for n ≤ 4.
