The no-information version has value about 3.8695 (Chow–Moriguti–Robbins–Samuels 1964). V is unknown.

title: The Haldane conjecture for integer-spin chains
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The spin-1 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain H = Σ_x S_x·S_{x+1} has a unique infinite-volume ground state, a spectral gap above it, and exponentially decaying correlations; more generally antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains are gapped for integer spin and gapless for half-integer spin.
source: F. D. M. Haldane, Nonlinear field theory of large-spin Heisenberg antiferromagnets, Phys. Lett. A 93 (1983); F. D. M. Haldane, Continuum dynamics of the 1-D Heisenberg antiferromagnet, Phys. Rev. Lett. 50 (1983)
why_important: A Nobel-cited prediction about the simplest quantum many-body system; probabilists meet it through the loop representations of Tóth and Aizenman–Nachtergaele.
where_it_stands: The AKLT chain, a different spin-1 Hamiltonian, is gapped (Affleck–Kennedy–Lieb–Tasaki 1987); half-integer chains cannot have a unique gapped ground state (Lieb–Schultz–Mattis 1961; Affleck–Lieb 1986); a loop-model reformulation (Aizenman–Nachtergaele 1994). Open for the spin-1 Heisenberg chain.

title: Feige's 1/e conjecture and Samuels' conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: If X_1, …, X_n are independent nonnegative random variables each with mean at most 1 and S = X_1 + ⋯ + X_n, then P(S < E S + 1) ≥ 1/e, attained in the limit by X_i = (n + 1)·Bernoulli(1/(n + 1)). (Samuels' conjecture, which implies it, identifies the extremal laws for P(S ≥ a) given the means.)
statement_caveat: Whether Feige's form is P(S < E S + 1) or P(S < n + 1) is to verify; the two agree when every mean is 1.
source: U. Feige, On sums of independent random variables with unbounded variance and estimating the average degree in a graph, SIAM J. Comput. 35 (2006); S. M. Samuels, On a Chebyshev-type inequality for sums of independent random variables, Ann. Math. Statist. 37 (1966)
why_important: A bound for sums with no variance assumption that appears in algorithm analysis; the constant 1/e would be sharp, and the known proofs reach less than a fifth.
where_it_stands: Proved: Samuels' formula (Ling, arXiv:2608.18392), with Feige's 1/e as the equal-means case; a reformulation of the proof (Han, arXiv:2608.22816) and a short proof of Feige's bound (Milojević–Sudakov, arXiv:2610.10380). Before that: 1/13 (Feige), 1/8 (He–Zhang–Zhang 2010), about 0.14 (Garnett 2020), about 0.18 (Guo–He–Ling–Liu 2021); Samuels' conjecture for n ≤ 4 (Samuels 1966, 1968).
retired_reason: SOLVED: Samuels' conjecture is proved by Ling (arXiv:2608.18392), and Feige's 1/e bound follows from its equal-means case; Han (arXiv:2608.22816) recasts the proof as a cap-move argument and Milojević–Sudakov (arXiv:2610.10380) give a short proof of Feige's inequality. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged by the w672 audit.

title: Sylvester's problem in dimension three and higher
domain_name: Stochastic and geometric probability
statement: For a convex body K ⊂ R^d let v(K) be the expected volume of the convex hull of d + 1 independent uniform points of K, divided by vol(K). For d ≥ 3, v(K) is maximised by the simplex.
source: W. Blaschke, Über affine Geometrie XI: Lösung des 'Vierpunktproblems' von Sylvester aus der Theorie der geometrischen Wahrscheinlichkeiten, Ber. Verh. Sächs. Akad. Leipzig 69 (1917); V. Klee, What is the expected volume of a simplex whose vertices are chosen at random from a given convex body?, Amer. Math. Monthly 76 (1969)
why_important: Sylvester's four-point problem is the founding question of geometric probability; the upper bound in high dimension is linked to the isotropic constant (Milman–Pajor).
where_it_stands: d = 2 solved (Blaschke 1917: triangles maximise, ellipses minimise); ellipsoids minimise in every dimension (Groemer 1973); maximisers are known to be polytopes in some classes (Campi–Colesanti–Gronchi 1999) [verify]. The maximum is open for d ≥ 3.

title: Gaussian free field limit of the six-vertex height function
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: For the six-vertex model on Z^2 with weights a = b = 1 and c ∈ (0, 2), so that Δ = 1 − c²/2 ∈ (−1, 1), the height function converges in the scaling limit to a Gaussian free field whose variance is an explicit function of Δ.
source: R. J. Baxter, Exactly Solved Models in Statistical Mechanics (Academic Press, 1982); B. Nienhuis, Critical behavior of two-dimensional spin models and charge asymmetry in the Coulomb gas, J. Stat. Phys. 34 (1984)
why_important: The six-vertex model contains square ice, the uniform three-colourings and (through the BKW correspondence) the critical FK and Potts models; a GFF limit is the Coulomb-gas prediction behind their exponents.
where_it_stands: Δ = 0 is the dimer model, with GFF limit (Kenyon 2001); small perturbations of it by interacting-dimer methods (Giuliani–Mastropietro–Toninelli) [verify]. Logarithmic variance (delocalization) for c ∈ [1, 2] (Duminil-Copin–Karrila–Manolescu–Oulamara 2020) and further ranges (Lis 2021; Glazman–Peled) [verify ranges]. Averous–Duminil-Copin–He–Lammers–Manolescu (arXiv:2610.07454) prove convergence to the GFF in simply connected domains with piecewise constant boundary conditions for a wide range of Δ, including Δ near 0 and Δ between −1 and −1/2. The whole range Δ ∈ (−1, 1) is open.

title: Percolation description of the nodal lines of random waves (Bogomolny–Schmit)
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: The nodal set of the random plane wave (the centred Gaussian field on R^2 with covariance J_0(|x − y|)), and conjecturally of high-energy eigenfunctions of chaotic billiards, has the large-scale behaviour of critical percolation: crossing probabilities of nodal domains converge to Cardy's formula and nodal lines to SLE(6).
statement_caveat: The predicted number of nodal domains per unit area, (3√3 − 5)/π times a normalisation, is off by a few percent in numerics (Nastasescu 2011; Beliaev–Kereta 2013), so the conjecture is the scaling-limit statement, not that constant.
source: E. Bogomolny and C. Schmit, Percolation model for nodal domains of chaotic wave functions, Phys. Rev. Lett. 88 (2002); M. V. Berry, Regular and irregular semiclassical wavefunctions, J. Phys. A 10 (1977)
why_important: It ties quantum chaos (Berry's random wave model) to the universality of planar critical percolation, and it is the main test of percolation universality for strongly correlated fields.
where_it_stands: The number of nodal domains grows like a constant times the area (Nazarov–Sodin 2009, 2016). Russo–Seymour–Welsh bounds and sharp thresholds hold for positively correlated planar Gaussian fields with fast decay (Beffara–Gayet 2017; Rivera–Vanneuville 2019; Muirhead–Vanneuville 2020). The random plane wave correlates slowly and changes sign, so none of this applies; open.

title: Hydrodynamic limit of deterministic Hamiltonian dynamics
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: For classical particles in R^3 evolving under Newtonian dynamics with a fixed smooth short-range pair potential (or for a non-integrable chain of anharmonic oscillators), started from a local equilibrium state, the conserved fields evolve under Euler scaling by the compressible Euler equations up to the first shock.
statement_caveat: Integrable systems (hard rods, the Toda chain, harmonic chains) are excluded: their hydrodynamics is generalised, not Euler. The class of potentials is to fix.
source: C. B. Morrey, On the derivation of the equations of hydrodynamics from statistical mechanics, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 8 (1955); S. Olla, S. R. S. Varadhan and H.-T. Yau, Hydrodynamical limit for a Hamiltonian system with weak noise, Comm. Math. Phys. 155 (1993); H. Spohn, Large Scale Dynamics of Interacting Particles (Springer, 1991)
why_important: The derivation of fluid equations from mechanics is the core of Hilbert's sixth problem; every proof so far adds noise to the dynamics to obtain the ergodicity it needs.
where_it_stands: Proved with a small conservative noise (Olla–Varadhan–Yau 1993) and for several stochastic or noise-perturbed chains (Even–Olla 2014 and others) [verify]; derivations through the Boltzmann equation for dilute gases are a separate line (Lanford 1975 and later). Open for deterministic dynamics. See also T033 (Fourier's law).

title: The Komlós conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: There is an absolute constant K such that for all vectors v_1, …, v_n ∈ R^m of Euclidean norm at most 1 there are signs ε_i ∈ {−1, 1} with ‖ε_1 v_1 + ⋯ + ε_n v_n‖_∞ ≤ K.
source: J. Spencer, Ten Lectures on the Probabilistic Method (SIAM, 1987), where it is attributed to J. Komlós
why_important: The central open problem of discrepancy theory; it implies the Beck–Fiala conjecture, and its best bounds come from Gaussian measure and random-walk arguments.
where_it_stands: Proved: K = 3√(2π) (Guo–Fang–Lu, arXiv:2609.11189), improved to below 6.9013 with a deterministic algorithm (Akbas–Sra, arXiv:2609.27172). Before that: O(√(log n)) (Banaszczyk 1998), algorithmic since 2010 (Bansal; Bansal–Dadush–Garg–Lovett), and roughly (log n)^{1/4} (Bansal–Jiang 2025) [verify].
retired_reason: SOLVED: Guo–Fang–Lu (arXiv:2609.11189) prove the Komlós conjecture with K = 3√(2π), which also gives the O(√t) Beck–Fiala bound; Akbas–Sra (arXiv:2609.27172) reach 3π, then a constant below 6.9013, with a deterministic algorithm; Bansal (arXiv:2609.33215) is an exposition of the Guo–Fang–Lu algorithm. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged by the w672 audit.

title: Tightness of the Kesten–Stigum bound for reconstruction on trees
domain_name: Branching processes, trees and genealogies
statement: For the broadcast process on the d-ary tree (or a Galton–Watson tree with mean d) through the symmetric ferromagnetic q-state Potts channel with second eigenvalue λ > 0, the root can be reconstructed from the far leaves exactly when d λ² > 1 (the Kesten–Stigum bound is tight) for q = 3 and q = 4 and every d; for q ≥ 5 it is not tight.
statement_caveat: The channel must be ferromagnetic: the proper 4-colouring channel (λ = −1/3) on the 9-ary tree has d λ² = 1 and still reconstructs, by the forcing recursion p ↦ 1 − 3(1 − p/3)^9 + 3(1 − 2p/3)^9 − (1 − p)^9, which maps [3/4, 1] into itself (w672 audit, 14 Oct; arithmetic rechecked).
source: E. Mossel, Survey: information flow on trees, in Graphs, Morphisms and Statistical Physics (DIMACS Ser. 63, AMS, 2004); A. Sly, Reconstruction for the Potts model, Ann. Probab. 39 (2011)
why_important: Reconstruction thresholds govern phylogenetic reconstruction, Glauber mixing on trees, and the detection thresholds of the stochastic block model, where they separate easy from hard inference.
where_it_stands: q = 2: tight (Bleher–Ruiz–Zagrebnov 1995; Evans–Kenyon–Peres–Schulman 2000). Sly (arXiv:0811.1208) proves tightness for q = 3 on regular trees of large degree and non-tightness for every q ≥ 5. Mossel, Sly and Sohn (arXiv:2212.03362, Theorem 1.12) prove tightness for q = 3 and q = 4 at large mean degree, on regular trees and on Galton–Watson trees whose offspring law satisfies their concentration assumptions. Open for q = 3 and q = 4 at small degree, the binary tree included, and for general Galton–Watson trees.

title: Karp's problem: finding cliques of size (1 + ε) log₂ n in G(n, 1/2)
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: For every ε > 0, no polynomial-time algorithm finds a clique of size (1 + ε) log₂ n in G(n, 1/2) with probability bounded away from zero; equivalently, the greedy algorithm's size log₂ n is the algorithmic threshold, half the clique number 2 log₂ n.
statement_caveat: Proving it unconditionally would separate P from NP, so the working form asks for proofs against broad algorithm classes.
source: R. M. Karp, The probabilistic analysis of some combinatorial search algorithms, in Algorithms and Complexity: New Directions and Recent Results (Academic Press, 1976)
why_important: The founding example of a statistical-computational gap: a factor of two between what exists and what any known efficient method finds, open since 1976.
where_it_stands: The Metropolis process fails (Jerrum 1992); overlap-gap and low-degree barriers rule out large classes of algorithms beyond log₂ n for this and related problems (Gamarnik–Sudan 2017; Gamarnik–Zadik; Wein 2022) [verify]. Open.

title: The storage capacity of the binary perceptron (Krauth–Mézard)
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: For the binary perceptron, find σ ∈ {−1, 1}^N with ⟨g_a, σ⟩ ≥ 0 for M = αN iid standard Gaussian vectors g_a; the satisfiability threshold is α_c ≈ 0.833, the value of the Krauth–Mézard replica formula.
source: W. Krauth and M. Mézard, Storage capacity of memory networks with binary couplings, J. Phys. France 50 (1989); E. Gardner and B. Derrida, Optimal storage properties of neural network models, J. Phys. A 21 (1988)
why_important: The classical capacity question for neural networks with discrete weights, and a test case for replica predictions in a model with frozen, isolated solutions.
where_it_stands: Claimed proof: Y. Shmalo (arXiv:2607.11010), computer-assisted, Gaussian and subgaussian disorder, awaiting independent reproduction. Before that: the lower bound matching Krauth–Mézard (Ding–Sun 2019), a sharp threshold sequence (Xu 2021), the threshold under a numerical hypothesis (Huang 2024); the symmetric binary perceptron threshold (Perkins–Xu 2021; Abbe–Li–Sly 2022).
retired_reason: SOLVED (claimed): Y. Shmalo (arXiv:2607.11010) gives a computer-assisted proof, at κ = 0, that the capacity satisfies M_N/N → α_⋆ ∈ [0.833078599, 0.833078600], verifying the Ding–Sun and Huang conditions in Arb interval arithmetic, for Gaussian disorder and for every fixed iid mean-zero unit-variance subgaussian law, Bernoulli included. Reproduced internally and audited by a second system; not yet independently reproduced or peer reviewed (brain memory ising_perceptron_release_verified_2026_07_13). Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct.

title: The density conjecture for activated random walk
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: For activated random walk on Z^d with sleep rate λ, the critical density ζ_c(λ) of the infinite-volume fixation transition equals the limiting density of the driven-dissipative system run on growing boxes (and of a single-source aggregate), so that the model is self-organised critical at ζ_c.
statement_caveat: The exact list of densities claimed equal is to verify.
source: R. Dickman, M. A. Muñoz, A. Vespignani and S. Zapperi, Paths to self-organized criticality, Braz. J. Phys. 30 (2000); L. Levine and V. Silvestri, How far do activated random walkers spread from a single source?, J. Stat. Phys. 185 (2021); L. T. Rolla, Activated random walks on Z^d, Probab. Surv. 17 (2020)
why_important: Activated random walk is the probabilists' model of self-organised criticality, and the density conjecture is the precise form of the claim that a driven-dissipative system tunes itself to the critical point.
where_it_stands: 0 < ζ_c < 1 for every λ in every dimension (Rolla–Sidoravicius 2012; Stauffer–Taggi 2018; Hoffman–Richey–Rolla 2023; Forien–Gaudillière 2024) [verify]. In d = 1, Hoffman–Johnson–Junge–Meisel (arXiv:2605.00207) prove self-organised criticality, power-law avalanches and equality with the fixed-energy critical density. Open in d ≥ 2.

title: Branching Brownian motion with selection: the Bolthausen–Sznitman genealogy of N-BBM
domain_name: Branching processes, trees and genealogies
statement: For N-BBM (branching Brownian motion in which, at each branching, the leftmost particle is removed to keep N particles), the genealogy on time scale (log N)³ converges to the Bolthausen–Sznitman coalescent. The Brunet–Derrida speed v_N = v_∞ − c/(log N)² + o((log N)^{−2}) is proved; see where it stands.
source: É. Brunet and B. Derrida, Shift in the velocity of a front due to a cutoff, Phys. Rev. E 56 (1997); É. Brunet, B. Derrida, A. H. Mueller and S. Munier, Noisy traveling waves: effect of selection on genealogies, Europhys. Lett. 76 (2006)
why_important: A predicted universality class for populations under selection (and for noisy FKPP fronts), in which the coalescent is not Kingman's.
where_it_stands: Speed: proved for N-BBM (Maillard, arXiv:1304.0562, published 2016) and recovered in a time-inhomogeneous joint limit, log N ≪ T^{1/3} (Legrand–Maillard, arXiv:2402.04917 v4, Theorem 1.1(i) and Corollary 2.1); also for N-branching random walk (Bérard–Gouéré 2010) and noisy FKPP (Mueller–Mytnik–Quastel 2011). Genealogy: proved for BBM with absorption at a moving barrier (Berestycki–Berestycki–Schweinsberg 2013); for N-BBM itself it is open (the w672 audit read Legrand–Maillard in full; no genealogy theorem there).

title: The planted clique conjecture
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: For every fixed ε ∈ (0, 1/2) and k = n^{1/2−ε}, no polynomial-time algorithm distinguishes G(n, 1/2) from G(n, 1/2) with a planted clique of size k with advantage bounded away from zero, and none recovers the planted clique with probability bounded away from zero.
statement_caveat: A proof would imply P ≠ NP, so the realistic targets are restricted models: low-degree polynomials, sum-of-squares, statistical queries, Markov chains.
source: M. Jerrum, Large cliques elude the Metropolis process, Random Structures Algorithms 3 (1992); L. Kučera, Expected complexity of graph partitioning problems, Discrete Appl. Math. 57 (1995)
why_important: The reference hypothesis for statistical-computational gaps; hardness for sparse PCA, community detection and many testing problems is proved by reduction from it.
where_it_stands: Solvable for k ≥ c√n (Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov 1998). Lower bounds for the Metropolis process (Jerrum 1992), statistical-query algorithms (Feldman et al. 2013), sum-of-squares (Barak et al. 2016) and low-degree polynomials (Hopkins 2018). Open, and see T068.

title: Phase transition of the noisy majority vote process on Z^2
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: In the majority vote process on Z^2 (each site, at rate one, adopts the majority opinion of its four neighbours with probability 1 − ε and the minority with probability ε, ties broken at random), for ε small enough there are at least two distinct stationary measures.
statement_caveat: The exact update rule used in the literature (neighbourhood, tie-breaking) is to verify.
source: T. M. Liggett, Interacting Particle Systems (Springer, 1985); L. F. Gray, The positive rates problem for attractive nearest neighbor spin systems on Z, Z. Wahrsch. Verw. Gebiete 61 (1982)
why_important: A non-reversible relative of the Ising model whose low-noise order is never in doubt in simulations, but whose stationary measures have no Gibbs structure to argue with.
where_it_stands: In one dimension attractive nearest-neighbour systems with positive rates are ergodic (Gray 1982). Toom's anisotropic north-east-centre rule is non-ergodic at low noise (Toom 1980). The general positive-rates conjecture fails (Gács 2001). Open for the symmetric majority rule on Z^2 [verify].
note: Fame borderline in the w672 audit (14 Oct); kept for now.

title: Complete monotonicity of entropy along the heat flow (McKean; Cheng–Geng)
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: For a real random variable X with finite variance and an independent standard Gaussian Z, the function t ↦ h(X + √t Z) satisfies (−1)^{k+1} (d/dt)^k h(X + √t Z) ≥ 0 for every k ≥ 1; and for fixed variance the Gaussian X minimises each of these derivatives in absolute value (McKean's conjecture).
source: H. P. McKean, Speed of approach to equilibrium for Kac's caricature of a Maxwellian gas, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 21 (1966); F. Cheng and Y. Geng, Higher order derivatives in Costa's entropy power inequality, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 61 (2015)
why_important: It would give the whole hierarchy of inequalities of which de Bruijn's identity, Stam's inequality and Costa's concavity of entropy power are the first terms.
where_it_stands: Disproved at k = 5 (Gu–Sellke, arXiv:2605.11656), with log-concave counterexamples in every dimension (Zou–Fan–Gao–Wang, arXiv:2608.30275). Before that: true for k ≤ 4 in one dimension (Cheng–Geng 2015) and for some classes such as Gaussian mixtures.
retired_reason: DISPROVED: Gu–Sellke (arXiv:2605.11656) give an explicit measure whose fifth entropy derivative along the heat flow has the wrong sign, which also refutes the McKean and Toscani conjectures; Zou–Fan–Gao–Wang (arXiv:2608.30275) give log-concave counterexamples in every dimension. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged by the w672 audit.

title: Absolute continuity of Bernoulli convolutions at transcendental parameters
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: For every transcendental λ ∈ (1/2, 1), the Bernoulli convolution ν_λ (the law of Σ_{n≥0} ±λ^n with independent fair signs) is absolutely continuous.
statement_caveat: Asked as a question rather than a named conjecture [verify locator]; it is the form of Erdős's problem that the 2026 Salem counterexamples (T026, retired) leave untouched.
source: P. Erdős, On a family of symmetric Bernoulli convolutions, Amer. J. Math. 61 (1939); P. P. Varjú, Recent progress on Bernoulli convolutions, in European Congress of Mathematics (EMS, 2018) [verify]
why_important: The model case of self-similar measures with overlaps; the recent dimension theory (Hochman, Shmerkin, Varjú) settles dimension but not absolute continuity.
where_it_stands: Dimension one for every transcendental λ (Varjú 2019); absolutely continuous for almost every λ (Solomyak 1995) and outside a set of Hausdorff dimension zero (Shmerkin 2014); for algebraic non-Pisot λ close to 1 in terms of the Mahler measure (Varjú 2019; Kittle [verify]). Pisot reciprocals (Erdős 1939) and quartic Salem reciprocals (Cheng–Fang–Ma–Zhang, arXiv:2610.12072, Oct 2026) give singular measures. Open.

title: Random band matrices in dimensions two and three
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For random band matrices indexed by the box {1, …, L}^d, with independent centred entries (up to symmetry) in a fixed symmetry class, H_xy = 0 unless |x − y| ≤ W, and a regular variance profile, bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with Wigner–Dyson local statistics when W ≫ √(log L) in d = 2, and for every W ≥ W_0 with W_0 fixed in d = 3; in d = 2 the localization length is of order exp(cW²).
source: Y. V. Fyodorov and A. D. Mirlin, Scaling properties of localization in random band matrices: a σ-model approach, Phys. Rev. Lett. 67 (1991); P. Bourgade, Random band matrices, Proc. ICM 2018
why_important: Band matrices in d ≥ 2 interpolate between Wigner matrices and the Anderson model; d = 3 delocalization at bounded W is the matrix analogue of the extended-states conjecture (T009).
where_it_stands: d = 1 is settled (T035, retired). Delocalization when W is a power of L: d ≥ 7 (Xu–Yang–Yau–Yin 2022) [verify], d = 2 with W ≥ N^c (Dubova–Yang–Yau–Yin, arXiv:2503.07606) and d ≥ 3 with W ≥ N^c (Dubova–Yang–Yau–Yin, arXiv:2507.20274). In d = 2, Lai–Yang (arXiv:2609.24426) reach W ≥ (log N)^7 with localization length at least exp(W^{1/7}). The predicted exp(cW²) scale in d = 2 and bounded W in d = 3 are open.

title: Coexistence in the two-type Richardson model only at equal rates
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: In the two-type Richardson model on Z^d, d ≥ 2 (two infections spread from single sites at rates λ_1 and λ_2, and each site is taken by the first type to reach it), both types grow without bound with positive probability only when λ_1 = λ_2.
source: O. Häggström and R. Pemantle, First passage percolation and a model for competing spatial growth, J. Appl. Probab. 35 (1998); O. Häggström and R. Pemantle, Absence of mutual unbounded growth for almost all parameter values in the two-type Richardson model, Stochastic Process. Appl. 90 (2000)
why_important: The basic model of competing spatial growth; the answer depends on how one first-passage front can surround another, which ties it to the shape and geodesics of first-passage percolation.
where_it_stands: Coexistence with equal rates: d = 2 (Häggström–Pemantle 1998), every d ≥ 2 (Garet–Marchand 2005; Hoffman 2005). For unequal rates coexistence has probability zero for all but countably many ratios (Häggström–Pemantle 2000). Open for every given ratio other than 1.

title: Long-range order in the three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The spin-S quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on Z^d, d ≥ 3 (H = −Σ_{x∼y} S_x · S_y), has spontaneous magnetization at low positive temperature, for every S ∈ {1/2, 1, 3/2, …}.
source: F. J. Dyson, E. H. Lieb and B. Simon, Phase transitions in quantum spin systems with isotropic and nonisotropic interactions, J. Stat. Phys. 18 (1978); B. Simon, Fifteen problems in mathematical physics, in Perspectives in Mathematics (Birkhäuser, 1984) [verify]
why_important: The textbook case of spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry in quantum statistical mechanics; reflection positivity, which handles the classical model and the antiferromagnet, fails for the quantum ferromagnet. For S = 1/2 it is the cycle-weighted relative of Tóth's interchange problem (T012).
where_it_stands: Proved for the classical Heisenberg model (Fröhlich–Simon–Spencer 1976) and for quantum antiferromagnets (Dyson–Lieb–Simon 1978, S ≥ 1; Kennedy–Lieb–Shastry 1988, S = 1/2) [verify ranges]. For the ferromagnet: low-temperature free energy given by spin-wave theory (Conlon–Solovej 1991; Correggi–Giuliani–Seiringer 2015) [verify]; order on the complete graph and on trees through the interchange representation (Tóth; Björnberg; Hammond) [verify]. Open on Z^3.

title: The continuum limit of lattice Yang–Mills theory in three and four dimensions
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: Lattice Yang–Mills theory with a compact non-abelian gauge group (for example SU(2)) on εZ^d, d = 3 or 4, with the coupling tuned as ε → 0, has a nontrivial continuum limit satisfying the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms; in d = 4 the limit has a mass gap.
statement_caveat: The d = 4 statement with a mass gap is the Clay Millennium problem; its probabilistic content is the construction of the limiting random field.
source: A. Jaffe and E. Witten, Quantum Yang–Mills theory, Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Problem description (2000); S. Chatterjee, Yang–Mills for probabilists, in Probability and Analysis in Interacting Physical Systems (Springer, 2019)
why_important: Constructing a four-dimensional non-abelian gauge theory is the central open problem of constructive quantum field theory; confinement on the lattice (T011) is its companion.
where_it_stands: Solved in two dimensions (Gross–King–Sengupta; Driver; Sengupta; Lévy). Balaban's renormalization-group programme gives ultraviolet stability in finite volume for d = 3, 4 [verify]. Stochastic quantization of Yang–Mills in d = 2, 3 locally in time (Chandra–Chevyrev–Hairer–Shen 2022–24) [verify]. Open.

title: The freezing transition of hard spheres
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: The hard-sphere gas in R^d, d ≥ 2, has a phase transition as the density increases: close enough to close packing its infinite-volume Gibbs measures break translational symmetry when d ≥ 3, and have long-range orientational order when d = 2 (hard disks).
source: B. J. Alder and T. E. Wainwright, Phase transition for a hard sphere system, J. Chem. Phys. 27 (1957); E. P. Bernard and W. Krauth, Two-step melting in two dimensions: first-order liquid–hexatic transition, Phys. Rev. Lett. 107 (2011)
why_important: Freezing of hard spheres is the simplest entropy-driven phase transition, seen in every simulation since 1957 and in colloids, and nothing comparable is proved for any continuum particle system at positive temperature.
where_it_stands: Hard-core lattice gases order at high activity (Dobrushin 1968). In the continuum: uniqueness at low density by cluster expansion; hard disks cannot break translational symmetry (Richthammer 2007) [verify]; the densest packings are known in d = 3 (Hales 2005) and in d = 8, 24 (Viazovska; Cohn–Kumar–Miller–Radchenko–Viazovska 2017). No phase transition is proved at any density below close packing [verify]. See also T044.

title: The liquid–vapour transition for continuum particles with pair interactions
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: Classical point particles in R^d, d ≥ 2, interacting through a fixed stable, translation-invariant pair potential with a short-range repulsion and a finite-range attraction (of Lennard-Jones type) have a liquid–vapour transition: for some temperature and chemical potential there are two infinite-volume Gibbs measures with different densities.
statement_caveat: The class of potentials must be fixed; the known proofs add Kac scaling, a four-body repulsion or an attraction tied to a fixed partition of space.
source: J. L. Lebowitz, A. Mazel and E. Presutti, Liquid–vapor phase transitions for systems with finite-range interactions, J. Stat. Phys. 94 (1999); D. Ruelle, Existence of a phase transition in a continuous classical system, Phys. Rev. Lett. 27 (1971)
why_important: Liquid–gas coexistence is the oldest phase transition in physics (van der Waals 1873) and is still unproved for any finite-range pair potential in the continuum.
where_it_stands: Proved with Kac potentials at small scale parameter and a four-body repulsion (Lebowitz–Mazel–Presutti 1999), for the Widom–Rowlinson model (Ruelle 1971) and the continuum Potts model (Chayes–Chayes–Kotecký 1995) [verify]. With pair interactions only, He–Jauslin–Lebowitz–Peled (arXiv:2510.24825) prove it at a fixed small Kac parameter in a boxed model whose attraction follows a fixed partition into cubes, so not translation invariant. Open for translation-invariant pair potentials.

title: The Boltzmann–Sinai ergodic hypothesis for hard balls
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: N ≥ 2 hard balls of radius r on the flat torus T^d, d ≥ 2, moving freely and colliding elastically, form an ergodic (indeed Bernoulli) system on each component of the energy surface once total momentum and centre of mass are fixed, for every N and every admissible r.
source: Ya. G. Sinai, On the foundations of the ergodic hypothesis for a dynamical system of statistical mechanics, Soviet Math. Dokl. 4 (1963); D. Szász (ed.), Hard Ball Systems and the Lorentz Gas (Springer, 2000)
why_important: Boltzmann's ergodic hypothesis in its cleanest mathematical form; it is the justification of equilibrium statistical mechanics for the hard-sphere gas.
where_it_stands: Proved: Simányi (arXiv:1205.0061, 2012; published 2013), after N = 2 (Sinai 1970), N = 3 (Krámli–Simányi–Szász 1991) and almost every choice of masses or radii (Simányi–Szász 1999; Simányi 2003, 2004, 2009).
retired_reason: SOLVED: Simányi (arXiv:1205.0061, 2012; published 2013) completes the proof for every N ≥ 2, every d ≥ 2 and every admissible radius; the survey arXiv:1512.08272 treats the hypothesis as proved. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged by the w672 audit.

title: Pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: For a measure-preserving system (X, μ, T), k ≥ 3 and f_1, …, f_k ∈ L^∞(μ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n<N} f_1(T^n x) f_2(T^{2n} x) ⋯ f_k(T^{kn} x) converge for μ-almost every x.
statement_caveat: The commuting version, with f_i(T_i^n x) for commuting T_1, …, T_k, is the natural extension.
source: H. Furstenberg, Recurrence in Ergodic Theory and Combinatorial Number Theory (Princeton, 1981); J. Bourgain, Double recurrence and almost sure convergence, J. Reine Angew. Math. 404 (1990)
why_important: Norm convergence (Host–Kra 2005; Ziegler 2007) underlies the ergodic route to Szemerédi's theorem, but almost-everywhere convergence beyond two terms has resisted every method.
where_it_stands: k = 2 (Bourgain 1990). Norm convergence for every k (Host–Kra 2005; Ziegler 2007) and for commuting transformations (Tao 2008). Pointwise results for special systems such as nilsystems and distal systems, and for polynomial pairs (Krause–Mirek–Tao 2022) [verify]. Open for k = 3.

title: Negative correlation for uniform forests and for random-cluster measures with q < 1
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For every finite graph G and distinct edges e, f, a uniformly random spanning forest (acyclic subgraph) F of G satisfies P(e ∈ F, f ∈ F) ≤ P(e ∈ F) P(f ∈ F). More generally, random-cluster measures with 0 < q ≤ 1, whose limits include uniform forests and uniform connected subgraphs, are conjectured to have this pairwise negative correlation; negative association is a stronger, separate conjecture.
source: R. Pemantle, Towards a theory of negative dependence, J. Math. Phys. 41 (2000); G. R. Grimmett and S. N. Winkler, Negative association in uniform forests and connected graphs, Random Structures Algorithms 24 (2004)
why_important: Spanning trees are negatively correlated (Kirchhoff; Feder–Mihail), and forests are the next case; negative association would give the q < 1 random-cluster model a theory comparable to the FKG theory for q ≥ 1.
where_it_stands: Spanning trees and balanced matroids (Feder–Mihail 1992); checked by computer on small graphs (Grimmett–Winkler 2004); a bound with factor 2, P(e, f ∈ F) ≤ 2 P(e ∈ F) P(f ∈ F), from Lorentzian polynomials (Huh–Schröter–Wang 2021) [verify]. Pairwise negative correlation is proved for uniform forests of every complete graph K_n, n ≥ 2 (Gupta, arXiv:2609.26134); for the weighted forest measure on any graph at large enough fugacity, provided one of the two leading coefficients of the Rayleigh difference is nonzero, and for the q < 1 random-cluster model on K_n with all edge weights at least 2, or all equal and at least 1 (Çiçeksiz–Ravichandran, arXiv:2610.00549); and for 0 ≤ q < 1 on high-degree regular graphs satisfying a two-scale edge-isoperimetric condition, where the pairwise conjecture is also shown equivalent to its restriction to regular graphs of diverging degree (Tang–Zhang, arXiv:2609.11578). Open for uniform forests on general graphs.

title: Random Cayley graphs of the symmetric group are expanders
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: There is ε > 0 such that, for two independent uniformly random permutations σ, τ ∈ S_n, the Cayley graph of the group they generate, with generators σ^{±1}, τ^{±1}, is an ε-expander with probability tending to one as n → ∞.
statement_caveat: Two random permutations generate A_n or S_n with probability tending to one (Dixon 1969). Both are even with probability 1/4, and then the Cayley graph of S_n is disconnected, so the statement must be made on the generated group (w672 audit, 14 Oct, T085_parity_counterexample.md).
source: A. Lubotzky, Expander graphs in pure and applied mathematics, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 49 (2012) [verify problem number]; A. Lubotzky, Discrete Groups, Expanding Graphs and Invariant Measures (Birkhäuser, 1994)
why_important: Random generators give expanders for finite simple groups of Lie type of bounded rank (Breuillard–Green–Guralnick–Tao 2015); the symmetric group is the main case left, and it governs how fast a random walk with random generators mixes.
where_it_stands: S_n has bounded-size expanding generating sets (Kassabov 2007). For random generators: diameter O(n²(log n)^c) with high probability (Helfgott–Seress–Zuk 2015) [verify]; the known spectral gaps are only polynomial in 1/n [verify]. Open.

title: Small ball probabilities for the Brownian sheet in dimension three and higher
domain_name: Brownian motion, stochastic analysis and SPDE
statement: For the Brownian sheet W on [0, 1]^d with d ≥ 3, −log P(sup_{t ∈ [0,1]^d} |W(t)| ≤ ε) is of order ε^{−2} (log(1/ε))^{2d−1} as ε → 0.
statement_caveat: The exponent 2d − 1 is the conjectured one; it matches Talagrand's d = 2 answer.
source: M. Talagrand, The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet, Ann. Probab. 22 (1994); D. Bilyk, M. Lacey and A. Vagharshakyan, On the small ball inequality in all dimensions, J. Funct. Anal. 254 (2008)
why_important: It is tied to the small ball inequality for hyperbolic Haar sums and so to lower bounds for the discrepancy of point sets in dimension three and above, a central open problem of irregularities of distribution.
where_it_stands: d = 2: ε^{−2}(log 1/ε)^3 (Talagrand 1994). For d ≥ 3 an upper bound with exponent 2d − 1 and a lower bound with exponent 2d − 2 (Dunker–Kühn–Lifshits–Linde 1998) [verify], the lower bound improved by a small power of the logarithm (Bilyk–Lacey–Vagharshakyan 2008). Open.

title: Existence and values of the critical exponents of three-dimensional percolation
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^3 the critical exponents exist: θ(p) = (p − p_c)^{β+o(1)} as p ↓ p_c, the mean cluster size is (p_c − p)^{−γ+o(1)} as p ↑ p_c, the correlation length is |p − p_c|^{−ν+o(1)}, and at p_c the one-arm probability P(0 ↔ ∂B_n) is n^{−1/ρ+o(1)} and the two-point function decays like |x|^{−(1+η)+o(1)}; and they satisfy the scaling and hyperscaling relations, for example γ = ν(2 − η) and 3ν = γ + 2β.
statement_caveat: Existence of the exponents is part of the problem. Their values are known only numerically (β ≈ 0.418, ν ≈ 0.876, η ≈ −0.046 [verify]); no exact values are conjectured. Continuity at p_c (T001) would be a first step.
source: H. Kesten, Scaling relations for 2D-percolation, Comm. Math. Phys. 109 (1987); G. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed. (Springer, 1999)
locator: Grimmett 1999, Chapters 9 and 10 [verify]
why_important: Critical exponents are the central quantitative prediction of the theory of phase transitions. In three dimensions there is no exact solution and no lace expansion, so the problem tests whether any method reaches genuinely three-dimensional criticality.
where_it_stands: In d = 2 the exponents are known for site percolation on the triangular lattice (Smirnov 2001; Lawler–Schramm–Werner 2002; Smirnov–Werner 2001, through Kesten's scaling relations). Mean-field values (β = γ = 1, ν = 1/2) hold for d ≥ 11 (Hara–Slade 1990; Fitzner–van der Hofstad 2017) and for spread-out models with d > 6. For 3 ≤ d ≤ 6 no exponent is known to exist, and θ(p_c) = 0 is open for 3 ≤ d ≤ 10 (T001). Some inequalities hold in every dimension, for example β ≤ 1 and γ ≥ 1 (Aizenman–Newman 1984; Aizenman–Barsky 1987) [verify].

title: The chemical-distance exponent of planar critical percolation
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, let S_n be the length of the shortest open left-right crossing of an n × n box, on the event that one exists, so that S_n = n^{d_min+o(1)}. Determine d_min (numerically d_min ≈ 1.1306), and prove that the same exponent governs critical bond percolation on Z^2.
statement_caveat: Existence of d_min on the triangular lattice, through convergence of the intrinsic metric, is proved in arXiv:2604.14122 (2026, Corollary 1.2, for the conditional mean and the quantiles of S_n). No closed form is conjectured; unlike the other planar percolation exponents, d_min is not expected to come out of SLE(6) by a known computation.
source: O. Schramm, Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems, Proc. ICM 2006, vol. I [verify]; M. Aizenman and A. Burchard, Hölder regularity and dimension bounds for random curves, Duke Math. J. 99 (1999)
locator: Schramm 2006, problem list [verify locator]
why_important: The graph metric of the critical cluster is the intrinsic geometry of percolation; it governs random walk on the incipient cluster and first-passage times at criticality, and it is the most prominent planar percolation exponent that SLE has not delivered.
where_it_stands: S_n ≥ n^{1+ε} with high probability (Aizenman–Burchard 1999). The lowest crossing has length n^{4/3+o(1)} (Morrow–Zhang 2005), and E S_n ≤ n^{−δ} E L_n for the lowest crossing L_n, so the exponent is below 4/3 (Damron–Hanson–Sosoe, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 2021) [verify]. Dankovic, Markering, Miller and Yuan (arXiv:2604.14122) prove convergence of the intrinsic metric and of random walk on triangular-lattice critical clusters, and existence of d_min. The value and universality across lattices are open. Numerical estimate d_min ≈ 1.1306 (Zhou–Yang–Deng–Ziff 2012) [verify].
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For a classically chaotic quantum system, for example the Dirichlet Laplacian on a planar billiard Ω whose billiard flow is ergodic and hyperbolic (the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard), restricted to one symmetry class and with time-reversal symmetry, let x_j = |Ω|λ_j/4π be the eigenvalues unfolded by Weyl's law. As Λ → ∞, the x_j with λ_j in [Λ, 2Λ] have the local statistics of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble; in particular the nearest-neighbour spacing distribution converges to the GOE (Gaudin) law.
statement_caveat: Arithmetic examples (hyperbolic surfaces from quaternion algebras) have Poisson-like statistics, so a theorem needs a genericity hypothesis, and there is no agreed form of one. Bohigas, Giannoni and Schmit (doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1) state the conjecture from numerics on the Sinai billiard.
source: O. Bohigas, M.-J. Giannoni and C. Schmit, Characterization of chaotic quantum spectra and universality of level fluctuation laws, Phys. Rev. Lett. 52 (1984), 1–4
why_important: BGS is the founding conjecture of quantum chaos and the reason random-matrix statistics are expected in physical spectra; it is the deterministic counterpart of Wigner–Dyson universality.
where_it_stands: GOE statistics are not proved for any chaotic billiard or manifold. Support comes from periodic-orbit expansions of the spectral form factor (Berry 1985; Sieber–Richter 2001; Müller–Heusler–Braun–Haake–Altland 2004) and from numerics. Rigorous results concern eigenfunctions rather than eigenvalues: quantum ergodicity (Shnirelman 1974; Zelditch 1987; Colin de Verdière 1985) and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity (Lindenstrauss 2006). Arithmetic exceptions: Bogomolny–Georgeot–Giannoni–Schmit 1992; Luo–Sarnak 1994 [verify].
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: Kardar–Parisi–Zhang growth in 2+1 dimensions
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: Random surface growth in 2+1 dimensions in the isotropic KPZ class (the KPZ equation ∂_t h = Δh + λ|∇h|² + ξ in two space dimensions with spatially smoothed noise and fixed λ ≠ 0, or ballistic deposition and the Eden model) has nontrivial universal exponents: the height variance grows like t^{2β} with β ≈ 0.24, the roughness exponent is α ≈ 0.39, and the rescaled height has a non-Gaussian limit.
statement_caveat: The exponents are known only numerically. Isotropy matters: for anisotropic growth (AKPZ) fluctuations are predicted to be logarithmic (Wolf 1991).
source: M. Kardar, G. Parisi and Y.-C. Zhang, Dynamic scaling of growing interfaces, Phys. Rev. Lett. 56 (1986); T. Halpin-Healy and Y.-C. Zhang, Kinetic roughening phenomena, stochastic growth, directed polymers and all that, Phys. Rep. 254 (1995)
why_important: Two space dimensions is the physical case of surface growth and the critical dimension of the KPZ nonlinearity; no integrable model is known in the isotropic class, so any progress needs a new method. See T005 for 1+1 dimensions.
where_it_stands: When the coupling is sent to zero like 1/√log of the mollification scale, the limit is the Gaussian Edwards–Wilkinson equation (Chatterjee–Dunlap 2020; Caravenna–Sun–Zygouras, arXiv:1812.03911; Gu 2020), and at the critical coupling the critical 2D stochastic heat flow appears (Caravenna–Sun–Zygouras 2023; see also arXiv:2412.10311 and arXiv:2609.15832). Anisotropic models: logarithmic fluctuations for integrable AKPZ growth (Borodin–Ferrari 2014) and logarithmic superdiffusivity of the stationary AKPZ equation (Cannizzaro–Erhard–Toninelli, arXiv:2009.12934). In the isotropic strong-coupling regime nothing rigorous is known about the exponents, or even about the existence of a non-Gaussian universality class.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Uniqueness and regularity for the three-dimensional stochastic Navier–Stokes equations
domain_name: Brownian motion, stochastic analysis and SPDE
statement: For the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus driven by additive Gaussian noise, white in time and smooth in space, prove (a) that Leray–Hopf martingale solutions are unique in law, or (b) that for smooth initial data a global strong solution exists almost surely.
statement_caveat: With smooth additive noise the problem contains the difficulty of deterministic global regularity; the hope behind it, regularization by noise, is that noise of the right structure (for example transport noise) rules out singularities.
source: F. Flandoli, An introduction to 3D stochastic fluid dynamics, in SPDE in Hydrodynamic: Recent Progress and Prospects, Lecture Notes in Math. 1942 (Springer, 2008) [verify]; F. Flandoli and D. Gatarek, Martingale and stationary solutions for stochastic Navier–Stokes equations, Probab. Theory Related Fields 102 (1995)
why_important: This is the stochastic form of the Navier–Stokes Millennium problem, where Markov selections, the strong Feller property, ergodicity and convex integration in law meet the question of turbulence.
where_it_stands: Martingale solutions exist (Flandoli–Gatarek 1995). Markov selections with the strong Feller property and unique invariant measures exist (Da Prato–Debussche 2003; Flandoli–Romito 2008) [verify]. Non-uniqueness in law holds for solutions that fail the energy inequality, by convex integration (Hofmanová–Zhu–Zhu, arXiv:1912.11841), and for Leray solutions on R^3 when a suitable deterministic force is added (Brué–Jin–Li–Zhang, arXiv:2309.09753); neither is the unforced Leray–Hopf case on the torus. Global solutions exist with positive probability for small data (Lin–Wang, arXiv:2407.00722). Transport noise delays blow-up with high probability in vorticity form (Flandoli–Luo 2021) [verify]. Both (a) and (b) are open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Simple Lebesgue spectrum for a transformation of a probability space (Banach's problem, finite-measure form)
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: Is there an invertible measure-preserving transformation T of a probability space (X, μ) whose Koopman operator f ↦ f∘T, restricted to the orthocomplement of the constants in L²(μ), has simple Lebesgue spectrum, that is, is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by z on L²(S¹, Lebesgue measure)?
statement_caveat: Banach's question as recorded by Ulam is for the real line with Lebesgue measure, an infinite measure; for that version el Abdalaoui claims positive answers with conservative maps (arXiv:1508.06439; arXiv:2210.15480). The finite-measure version, which el Abdalaoui attributes to Rokhlin, is the open one (arXiv:2210.15480v2, introduction).
source: S. M. Ulam, A Collection of Mathematical Problems (Interscience, 1960) [verify]; A. Katok and J.-P. Thouvenot, Spectral properties and combinatorial constructions in ergodic theory, in Handbook of Dynamical Systems, vol. 1B (Elsevier, 2006); E. H. el Abdalaoui, L¹-flat polynomials and simple Lebesgue spectrum for conservative maps exist: a simple proof, arXiv:2210.15480
locator: el Abdalaoui, arXiv:2210.15480v2, Introduction, pp. 2–3 (distinguishes the two versions)
why_important: Every known transformation with Lebesgue spectrum (Bernoulli and K-automorphisms, Gaussian systems with absolutely continuous spectral measure, horocycle flows) has it with infinite multiplicity; the problem asks whether the spectral type of a chaotic system can be as small as possible, and it is the oldest open question of spectral ergodic theory.
where_it_stands: For probability-preserving transformations, Lebesgue spectrum of finite multiplicity is not known to occur. A Lebesgue component of multiplicity two occurs (Mathew–Nadkarni 1984; Kamae 1982) [verify], and constructions of rank-one type realize many other spectral multiplicities (Ageev; Danilenko; Ryzhikov) [verify]; a Lebesgue component is not pure simple Lebesgue spectrum. Open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The colourability threshold of sparse random graphs
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: For each fixed q ≥ 3 there is a constant c_q such that G(n, c/n) is q-colourable with probability tending to one when c < c_q and to zero when c > c_q; and c_q equals the value given by the one-step replica-symmetry-breaking cavity method (for example c_3 ≈ 4.687).
statement_caveat: A sharp threshold sequence c_q(n) exists (Achlioptas–Friedgut 1999); its convergence is part of the problem. The analogous question for random d-regular graphs with small d is also open [verify].
source: R. Mulet, A. Pagnani, M. Weigt and R. Zecchina, Coloring random graphs, Phys. Rev. Lett. 89 (2002), 268701; F. Krzakała, A. Montanari, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, G. Semerjian and L. Zdeborová, Gibbs states and the set of solutions of random constraint satisfaction problems, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 104 (2007)
why_important: Colouring is the canonical sparse random constraint satisfaction problem; with k-SAT (T017) it is the test of whether cavity-method thresholds are exact at small parameter values.
where_it_stands: c_q lies between 2q log q − log q − 2 log 2 + o_q(1) and 2q log q − log q − 1 + o_q(1) (Coja-Oghlan–Vilenchik, arXiv:1304.1063; Coja-Oghlan, arXiv:1305.0177; both 2013), after Achlioptas–Naor (2005). The condensation threshold, found for large q by Bapst–Coja-Oghlan–Hetterich–Rassmann–Vilenchik (2016) [verify], is determined for every q ≥ 3 (Coja-Oghlan–Krzakala–Perkins–Zdeborová, arXiv:1611.00814). For q = 3 only bounds are known, 4.03 < c_3 < 4.69 (Achlioptas–Moore 2003; Dubois–Mandler 2002) [verify]; existence of the limit is open for every fixed q.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The number of pure states of the three-dimensional Edwards–Anderson spin glass
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the Edwards–Anderson Ising spin glass on Z^3 with iid symmetric Gaussian couplings at low temperature, determine the structure of the periodic-boundary-condition metastate: whether it is trivial and supported on a single pair of flip-related pure states (the scaling-droplet and trivial–nontrivial pictures), nontrivial with each sampled Gibbs state a single flip-related pair (chaotic pairs), or nontrivial with each sampled Gibbs state a mixture of infinitely many pure-state pairs with a nontrivial overlap distribution (replica symmetry breaking).
statement_caveat: The pictures are those of Fisher–Huse, of Parisi and of Newman–Stein. Newman and Stein showed that the naive form of replica symmetry breaking cannot hold and proposed metastates as the framework, so the question is stated for metastates; the number of pure states in the support of the metastate and the decomposition of a single sampled Gibbs state are different questions.
source: C. M. Newman and D. L. Stein, Spin Glasses and Complexity (Princeton Univ. Press, 2013); D. S. Fisher and D. A. Huse, Equilibrium behavior of the spin-glass ordered phase, Phys. Rev. B 38 (1988)
locator: Newman–Read–Stein, Metastates and replica symmetry breaking, arXiv:2204.10345, Section 3, p. 13
why_important: The number of pure states is the defining question about short-range spin glasses and the point where the solved mean-field theory and finite-dimensional physics part ways.
where_it_stands: Metastates exist (Aizenman–Wehr 1990; Newman–Stein 1997) [verify], and the naive replica-symmetry-breaking scenario with a non-self-averaging overlap distribution in a single state is ruled out (Newman–Stein 1996) [verify]. Results on ground states concern two-dimensional half-planes (Arguin–Damron–Newman–Stein 2010) [verify]; see T052 for the planar ground-state problem. Even the existence of a low-temperature spin-glass phase is open (T025); arXiv:2407.17506 proves bounds on free-energy fluctuations and records that phase existence and the number of states remain open. Nothing decides the structure of the metastate in any dimension d ≥ 3.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Differentiability of the limit shape in first-passage percolation
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For first-passage percolation on Z^2 with iid nonnegative edge weights whose law is continuous and satisfies E min(τ_1, …, τ_4)² < ∞ (the Cox–Durrett condition for the shape theorem; τ_1, …, τ_4 are independent copies), the boundary of the limit shape is differentiable at every point.
statement_caveat: For weights with an atom at the infimum of the support, of mass above the oriented percolation threshold, the shape has flat edges, so some condition on the law is needed; flat edges do not give corners, since the boundary is differentiable at the endpoints of the flat edge (Auffinger–Damron 2013). Uniformly positive curvature is a separate conjecture, part of T050.
source: H. Kesten, Aspects of first passage percolation, École d'Été de Probabilités de Saint-Flour XIV, Lecture Notes in Math. 1180 (1986) [verify]; A. Auffinger, M. Damron and J. Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, University Lecture Series 68 (AMS, 2017)
locator: Auffinger–Damron–Hanson, arXiv:1511.03262, Sections 2.5–2.8
why_important: Differentiability and curvature of the limit shape are the hypotheses under which most results on geodesics, Busemann functions and fluctuation exponents are proved (Newman 1995; Damron–Hanson 2014); a proof would make them unconditional.
where_it_stands: The shape is compact and convex (Cox–Durrett 1981). Flat edges occur for atoms at the infimum (Durrett–Liggett 1981), with differentiability at the endpoints of the flat segment (Auffinger–Damron 2013; Auffinger–Damron–Hanson, arXiv:1511.03262, Theorem 2.25). No continuous weight distribution is known to give a differentiable boundary; strict convexity is open too (T050).
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model up to β = 1
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with an arbitrary external field at inverse temperature β < 1, single-site heat-bath Glauber dynamics mixes in time polynomial in n (conjecturally of order n log n) from every starting configuration, with probability tending to one over the disorder.
statement_caveat: β = 1 is the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold of the zero-field model; for β < 1 the Almeida–Thouless condition holds whatever the field, so the whole range is replica symmetric, but it lies outside any Dobrushin-type high-temperature regime.
source: A. S. Bandeira, A. Kireeva, A. Maillard and A. Rödder, Randomstrasse101: open problems of 2024, arXiv:2504.20539
locator: Bandeira–Kireeva–Maillard–Rödder 2025, Open Problem 15
why_important: SK is the model case of a disordered system with a complex energy landscape; rapid mixing up to β = 1 would show that the whole replica-symmetric phase is easy for the simplest local dynamics, matching the static picture.
where_it_stands: Spectral gap and modified log-Sobolev bounds give rapid mixing for β < 1/4 (Bauerschmidt–Bodineau 2019; Eldan–Koehler–Zeitouni 2022; Anari–Jain–Koehler–Pham–Vuong 2021) [verify], extended to β < 0.295 (Anari–Koehler–Vuong 2024). Wang (arXiv:2608.22159v2) proves mixing in O_β(n log(n/ε)) steps from every start for β < 1/2, uniformly over external fields, and Boban, Li and Oveis Gharan (arXiv:2609.13138) prove polynomial mixing for β ≤ 1/2 + ε with an absolute ε > 0 (no field is mentioned in the abstract). Other samplers go further but are not fixed-temperature Glauber dynamics: stochastic localization, in Wasserstein distance, for β < 1/2 (El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke 2022) and β < 1 (Celentano 2024), and simulated annealing with an increasing temperature schedule for all β < 1 (arXiv:2610.09882) [verify]. At low temperature, mixing from a worst-case start is exponentially slow (arXiv:2511.22621). Open between about 1/2 and 1.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Critical behaviour of level-set percolation of the three-dimensional Gaussian free field
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: For the discrete Gaussian free field φ on Z^3, the excursion set {φ ≥ h} has an infinite cluster for h < h_* and none for h > h_*. Determine its behaviour at and near h_*: whether the percolation probability, the correlation length and the one-arm probability at h_* follow power laws, with which exponents, and whether these agree with those of the cable-system field.
statement_caveat: On the metric graph (cable system) the critical level is 0 and several exponents are known exactly; the lattice field has h_* > 0 and is not covered by those results.
source: A. Drewitz, A. Prévost and P.-F. Rodriguez, Critical exponents for a percolation model on transient graphs, Invent. Math. 232 (2023) [verify]; H. Duminil-Copin, S. Goswami, P.-F. Rodriguez and F. Severo, Equality of critical parameters for percolation of Gaussian free field level sets, Duke Math. J. 172 (2023)
why_important: GFF level sets are the canonical percolation model with power-law correlations; their criticality tests the Harris–Weinrib criterion for correlated percolation, and isomorphism theorems tie them to random interlacements and loop soups.
where_it_stands: The transition is sharp, h_* = h_** = h̄ (Duminil-Copin–Goswami–Rodriguez–Severo, arXiv:2002.07735), and h_* > 0 on Z^d for every d ≥ 3 (Drewitz–Prévost–Rodriguez, arXiv:1708.03285). On the cable system h_* = 0 (Lupu 2016) and critical exponents are computed in low dimensions (Ding–Wirth 2020; Drewitz–Prévost–Rodriguez 2023; Cai–Ding 2024) [verify]; the recent arXiv:2406.02397 and arXiv:2610.03703 are also about the cable system. For the lattice field no critical exponent is known to exist.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: Stability of many-body localization
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For a one-dimensional spin chain with iid random fields, such as the Ising chain with transverse field H = Σ_i h_i σ_i^z + Σ_i γ_i σ_i^x + Σ_i J_i σ_i^z σ_{i+1}^z with weak transverse terms, at strong disorder every eigenstate is many-body localized in Imbrie's sense: there is a quasi-local unitary that turns H into a function of commuting integrals of motion (l-bits), where quasi-locality is probabilistic, holding away from rare resonant blocks whose probabilities decay with their size, with bounds uniform in the chain length.
statement_caveat: The quantifiers are part of the problem: the statement is for all eigenstates (infinite temperature), not only low energies. Exponential localization at every site, uniformly, is too strong a target, because resonant regions occur with positive density.
source: D. M. Basko, I. L. Aleiner and B. L. Altshuler, Metal–insulator transition in a weakly interacting many-electron system with localized single-particle states, Ann. Physics 321 (2006); J. Z. Imbrie, On many-body localization for quantum spin chains, J. Stat. Phys. 163 (2016)
why_important: Many-body localization would be a robust failure of thermalization in an isolated interacting quantum system, a counterexample to the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis; it is the main open problem joining random operators and quantum statistical mechanics.
where_it_stands: Imbrie (J. Stat. Phys. 163 (2016), arXiv:1403.7837) proved it for the random Ising chain with transverse field under an unproved assumption of limited level attraction. Avalanche arguments (De Roeck–Huveneers 2017) indicate instability in dimension two and higher, and numerics have raised doubts about the 1D transition (Šuntajs–Bonča–Prosen–Vidmar 2020) [verify]. Localization at low energies for the random XXZ chain is known (Elgart–Klein–Stolz 2018) [verify], with logarithmic light cones at the bottom of the XXZ spectrum (Elgart–Klein, arXiv:2602.01441). Huveneers (arXiv:2609.39462) reviews the state of the question. An unconditional proof at positive energy density is open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Critical exponents of the contact process and the universality of directed percolation
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: For the nearest-neighbour contact process on Z with recovery rate 1 and infection rate λ, the critical exponents exist: the stationary density satisfies ρ(λ) = (λ − λ_c)^{β+o(1)} as λ ↓ λ_c, and the spatial and temporal correlation lengths diverge like (λ − λ_c)^{−ν_⊥+o(1)} and (λ − λ_c)^{−ν_∥+o(1)}. Moreover the same exponents govern oriented bond and site percolation on the two-dimensional oriented lattice and every finite-range contact process on Z.
statement_caveat: The general form, the Janssen–Grassberger conjecture, puts every model with a single absorbing state, short-range interactions and no extra symmetry or conservation law in this class; it has no agreed mathematical definition, so the row names models. Numerical values in 1+1 dimensions are β ≈ 0.2765, ν_⊥ ≈ 1.0969, ν_∥ ≈ 1.7339 (Jensen 1999) [verify]; no exact values are conjectured.
source: H. K. Janssen, On the nonequilibrium phase transition in reaction–diffusion systems with an absorbing stationary state, Z. Phys. B 42 (1981); P. Grassberger, On phase transitions in Schlögl's second model, Z. Phys. B 47 (1982); T. M. Liggett, Stochastic Interacting Systems: Contact, Voter and Exclusion Processes (Springer, 1999)
why_important: Directed percolation is the canonical non-equilibrium phase transition, the absorbing-state counterpart of the Ising model. It has been seen in experiments (turbulent liquid crystals, Takeuchi–Kuroda–Chaté–Sano 2007), and nothing about its low-dimensional exponents is proved.
where_it_stands: The critical contact process dies out (Bezuidenhout–Grimmett 1990). Mean-field behaviour holds above the upper critical dimension 4, for spread-out oriented percolation (Nguyen–Yang 1993; van der Hofstad–Slade 2003) and for the spread-out contact process (Sakai 2001) [verify]. In 1+1 dimensions no exponent is known to exist, and a scaling limit near criticality has not been constructed.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Avalanche exponents of the two-dimensional abelian sandpile
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: For the abelian sandpile on Z^2 in its stationary measure (the infinite-volume limit of the uniform measure on recurrent configurations), add a grain at the origin and stabilize. Prove that the number S of topplings satisfies P(S ≥ s) = s^{1−τ+o(1)} for an exponent τ, prove the corresponding power laws for the radius (the largest distance from the origin of a toppled site) and the duration (the number of rounds of parallel toppling, in which every unstable site topples at once), and identify the exponents.
statement_caveat: Priezzhev, Ktitarev and Ivashkevich predicted τ = 6/5 from a decomposition of avalanches into waves of topplings [verify]. Numerical studies find multifractal rather than simple finite-size scaling of the avalanche size (Tebaldi–De Menech–Stella 1999), so whether a single exponent exists is part of the question.
source: P. Bak, C. Tang and K. Wiesenfeld, Self-organized criticality: an explanation of 1/f noise, Phys. Rev. Lett. 59 (1987); D. Dhar, Self-organized critical state of sandpile automaton models, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64 (1990); A. A. Járai, Sandpile models, Probab. Surv. 15 (2018)
locator: Járai 2018, open problems [verify locator]
why_important: The sandpile is the model of self-organized criticality, and its avalanche exponents are the predictions that theory was built to make. Dhar's burning bijection ties them to uniform spanning trees and loop-erased walk.
where_it_stands: The infinite-volume stationary measure exists on Z^2 (Athreya–Járai 2004). Avalanches on Z^2 are finite almost surely, with a bound on the tail of the radius by a negative power of its logarithm (arXiv:2610.13940). In three dimensions the tail exponents of the radius, the number of distinct toppled vertices and the total number of topplings are found in arXiv:2605.19419. The two-dimensional exponents are open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Closed orbits in the Lorentz mirror model
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: At each vertex of Z^2 place, independently, a two-sided mirror along one of the two diagonals, each with probability p/2, or no mirror, with probability 1 − p. A light ray moving along the edges is reflected by mirrors and passes straight through empty vertices. Prove that for every p ∈ (0, 1) every orbit is periodic almost surely.
statement_caveat: For p = 1 the statement follows from critical bond percolation on Z^2. In three dimensions the opposite is expected at small p: infinite orbits with positive probability.
source: T. W. Ruijgrok and E. G. D. Cohen, Deterministic lattice gas models, Phys. Lett. A 133 (1988); G. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed. (Springer, 1999)
locator: Grimmett 1999, Section 13.3 [verify]; current statement in arXiv:2610.12460 (2026), abstract
why_important: The mirror model is the simplest deterministic walk in a random environment. Whether randomness forces the trajectory to be trapped in the plane, even when almost every site is empty, is a basic question about the line between deterministic and diffusive transport.
where_it_stands: For p = 1 every orbit is closed, through critical bond percolation [verify]. Kozma and Sidoravicius showed that the probability that the ray reaches distance n is at least of order 1/n for every p [verify]. arXiv:2610.12460 (2026) states that finiteness of all orbits on Z^2 is still a conjecture and builds infinite rays on other decorated planar graphs; arXiv:2609.14949 is a numerical study. Open for 0 < p < 1.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Random walk on the two-dimensional incipient infinite cluster
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For simple random walk on Kesten's incipient infinite cluster of two-dimensional critical percolation, the quenched return probability is p_{2n}(0,0) = n^{−d_s/2+o(1)} and the mean exit time from the ball of radius r is r^{d_w+o(1)}. Determine the spectral dimension d_s and the walk dimension d_w; in particular decide whether the Alexander–Orbach value d_s = 4/3 holds.
statement_caveat: Alexander and Orbach conjectured d_s = 4/3 in every dimension; the value is believed to fail in low dimensions, with numerical estimates near 1.31 in two dimensions [verify]. By the Einstein relation d_w = d_f + β_res with d_f = 91/48, so the question is the resistance exponent β_res; the Alexander–Orbach value would need β_res = 91/96.
source: S. Alexander and R. Orbach, Density of states on fractals: fractons, J. Physique Lett. 43 (1982); H. Kesten, Subdiffusive behavior of random walk on a random cluster, Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Statist. 22 (1986)
why_important: Random walk on critical clusters is the model case of anomalous diffusion on random fractals. In two dimensions every geometric exponent of the cluster is known exactly but the walk exponent is not, so the problem tests whether conformal methods can reach the walk.
where_it_stands: Kesten (1986) proved subdiffusivity on the 2D incipient infinite cluster. The Alexander–Orbach value holds in high dimensions (Kozma–Nachmias 2009), and for the critical level set of the cable-system Gaussian free field in high dimensions (Ganguly–Nam, arXiv:2403.02318) [verify]. For the incipient infinite cluster of critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, Dankovic, Markering, Miller and Yuan (arXiv:2604.14122, Corollaries 1.3–1.4) prove that the exponents exist: 2(91/48)/(91/48 + β_res) for the almost-sure return probability and 91/48 + β_res for the mean exit time, with β_res not identified. The values are open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Let β be the growth exponent of loop-erased random walk on Z^3: the loop-erasure of simple random walk stopped on leaving the ball of radius n has n^{β+o(1)} steps. Determine β, which is also the Hausdorff dimension of the scaling limit.
statement_caveat: Numerically β ≈ 1.624 (Wilson 2010) [verify]; no closed form is conjectured.
source: G. F. Lawler, Intersections of Random Walks (Birkhäuser, 1991); G. Kozma, The scaling limit of loop-erased random walk in three dimensions, Acta Math. 199 (2007)
why_important: Loop-erased walk gives the branches of the uniform spanning tree through Wilson's algorithm and is the simplest self-avoiding path with a scaling limit in three dimensions; β is the three-dimensional counterpart of the planar value 5/4 that comes from SLE(2).
where_it_stands: In two dimensions β = 5/4 (Kenyon 2000; Masson 2009) [verify]. In three dimensions the scaling limit exists (Kozma 2007), β exists (Shiraishi 2018) and equals the Hausdorff dimension of the limit (Shiraishi 2019) [verify]; β ∈ (1, 5/3], the upper bound due to Lawler [verify], and the scaling limit has a Minkowski content (arXiv:2403.07256). An explicit β ≥ 1.0001 is proved in arXiv:2609.18643, and arXiv:2610.12047 characterizes the scaling limit, which gives its inversion invariance. The value is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Oliveira's conjecture on the mixing time of the interchange process
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: There is a universal constant C such that for every finite connected graph G on n vertices with nonnegative edge rates and every ε ∈ (0, 1/2), the total-variation mixing time of the interchange process on G satisfies t_mix^{IP}(ε) ≤ C log(n/ε) t_mix^{RW}(1/4), where t_mix^{RW} is the mixing time of a single random walk on G with the same rates.
statement_caveat: The logarithm cannot be dropped: on the complete graph with rate 1/(n − 1) on each edge one walk mixes in time O(1), while the interchange process (random transpositions) needs time of order log n. The reverse inequality t_mix^{IP} ≥ t_mix^{RW} holds because the interchange process projects onto one walk. The conjecture is the mixing-time analogue of Aldous's spectral gap conjecture.
source: R. I. Oliveira, Mixing of the symmetric exclusion processes in terms of the corresponding single-particle random walk, Ann. Probab. 41 (2013)
locator: Oliveira, arXiv:1007.2669, Sections 1.1–1.2, pp. 2–3
why_important: The interchange process is the basic random walk on the symmetric group driven by a graph. Comparing its mixing with that of one particle is the natural way to carry single-particle bounds over to many-particle systems, and the spectral version became a well-known theorem.
where_it_stands: Aldous's spectral gap conjecture was proved by Caputo, Liggett and Richthammer (2010). Oliveira (Ann. Probab. 41 (2013), arXiv:1007.2669) proved the bound for the exclusion process with any number of particles, and for the interchange process when a positive fraction of the sites is empty; the full interchange process, with every site labelled, is the open case. Hermon and Pymar compared k-particle exclusion with k independent walks up to lower-order terms [verify].
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The Berry–Tabor conjecture
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For a generic completely integrable quantum system, for example the Laplacian on a flat torus R^2/L with a generic lattice L, the eigenvalues counted once for each pair ±v of dual-lattice vectors and unfolded have the local statistics of a Poisson process: every k-point correlation function and the nearest-neighbour spacing distribution converge to the Poisson ones.
statement_caveat: The spectrum of a flat torus is symmetric under v ↦ −v, so without this identification every positive eigenvalue has even multiplicity and the spacing law has an atom at zero. Arithmetic tori such as the square torus have further multiplicities and are exceptions, so a theorem needs an explicit genericity (Diophantine) condition and must cover every local statistic, not only the pair correlation.
source: M. V. Berry and M. Tabor, Level clustering in the regular spectrum, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 356 (1977)
locator: Blomer–Bourgain–Radziwiłł–Rudnick, arXiv:1809.07881, Sections 1.1–1.2
why_important: Berry–Tabor is the integrable counterpart of the Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture (T089); together they say which spectra look random and how. For tori it becomes a question about the values of quadratic forms at integer points.
where_it_stands: The pair correlation is Poisson for almost every flat 2-torus (Sarnak 1997) and for explicit Diophantine tori (Eskin–Margulis–Mozes 2005) [verify]; some higher correlations are known for almost every torus (VanderKam) [verify]; Blomer, Bourgain, Radziwiłł and Rudnick (arXiv:1809.07881) obtain the triple correlation on average over tori and long gaps, and Marklof proved pair-correlation results for related integrable models [verify]. The spacing distribution is open for every individual torus.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Berry's random wave conjecture
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: High-energy eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on a manifold or billiard with chaotic (ergodic and hyperbolic) dynamics behave locally like the isotropic Gaussian monochromatic wave: along a density-one subsequence, the eigenfunction φ_j viewed at the wavelength scale around a uniformly chosen point converges in law to the Gaussian field whose covariance in dimension two is J_0(|x − y|).
statement_caveat: Precise formulations use local weak limits of eigenfunctions, normalized in L² by the volume and rescaled by the wavelength (a modern formulation is in arXiv:2305.14906); a density-one subsequence is needed because of exceptional modes (bouncing-ball modes of the stadium).
source: M. V. Berry, Regular and irregular semiclassical wavefunctions, J. Phys. A 10 (1977)
why_important: The random wave model underlies the predictions for nodal sets, L^p norms and value distributions of chaotic eigenfunctions, including the Bogomolny–Schmit percolation picture (T064). A proof would put the Gaussian picture of quantum chaos on firm ground.
where_it_stands: Quantum ergodicity gives equidistribution of |φ_j|^2 at fixed scales along a density-one subsequence (Shnirelman 1974; Zelditch 1987; Colin de Verdière 1985), and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity holds (Lindenstrauss 2006). Gaussian local statistics are not proved for any chaotic system; analogues are known for eigenvectors of random regular graphs (Backhausz–Szegedy 2019) [verify].
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: Let τ be uniform on [T, 2T]. Then max_{|h|≤1} log|ζ(1/2 + i(τ + h))| − (log log T − (3/4) log log log T) converges in distribution as T → ∞ to the limit law predicted by Fyodorov, Hiary and Keating.
statement_caveat: The predicted limit is that of a log-correlated field: a Gumbel variable shifted by an independent random variable. The random-matrix analogue, for the characteristic polynomial of a Haar unitary matrix and more generally for the circular β-ensembles, is proved (Paquette–Zeitouni, arXiv:2209.06743).
source: Y. V. Fyodorov, G. A. Hiary and J. P. Keating, Freezing transition, characteristic polynomials of random matrices, and the Riemann zeta function, Phys. Rev. Lett. 108 (2012); Y. V. Fyodorov and J. P. Keating, Freezing transitions and extreme values: random matrix theory, ζ(1/2+it) and disordered landscapes, Philos. Trans. R. Soc. A 372 (2014)
why_important: It joins three subjects: extreme values of log-correlated fields, characteristic polynomials of random matrices, and the local maxima of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line. Its zeta form is a probabilistic statement about a number-theoretic object.
where_it_stands: For circular β-ensembles the maximum is log N − (3/4) log log N + O_P(1) (Arguin–Belius–Bourgade 2017; Paquette–Zeitouni 2018; Chhaibi–Madaule–Najnudel 2018), and it converges in law to a Gumbel variable shifted by a derivative-martingale term (Paquette–Zeitouni, arXiv:2209.06743). For zeta, tightness of the recentred maximum and the order of its right tail are proved (Najnudel 2018; Arguin–Bourgade–Radziwiłł, arXiv:2007.00988 and arXiv:2307.00982). Convergence in law for zeta is open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The universal jump at the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the nearest-neighbour XY model on Z^2 (spins on the circle, energy −Σ cos(θ_x − θ_y)), (a) the helicity modulus Υ(β) exists in the thermodynamic limit, vanishes for β < β_BKT and jumps at the transition: β_BKT Υ(β_BKT+) = 2/π; and (b) at β_BKT the spin–spin correlation decays as |x|^{−1/4+o(1)}.
statement_caveat: The two predictions are linked through Kosterlitz's renormalization picture, but neither is known to imply the other; logarithmic corrections are expected in the correlation at β_BKT.
source: D. R. Nelson and J. M. Kosterlitz, Universal jump in the superfluid density of two-dimensional superfluids, Phys. Rev. Lett. 39 (1977); J. Fröhlich and T. Spencer, The Kosterlitz–Thouless transition in two-dimensional abelian spin systems and the Coulomb gas, Comm. Math. Phys. 81 (1981)
why_important: BKT is the model of a topological phase transition, and the universal jump is its sharpest quantitative prediction, confirmed in helium films (Bishop–Reppy 1978). The rigorous theory establishes the transition but none of its universal features.
