where_it_stands: Power-law decay at low temperature (Fröhlich–Spencer 1981) and exponential decay at high temperature give the transition; newer proofs go through delocalization of height functions (Lammers 2022 [verify]; van Engelenburg–Lis, arXiv:2110.09465; Aizenman–Harel–Peled–Shapiro 2021 [verify]), and arXiv:2608.04972 extends phase-existence results to disordered and generalized XY models. For the Villain model Aizenman–Harel–Peled–Shapiro bound the decay at the transition by |x|^{−1/4} from one side [verify]. Both (a) and (b) are open for the XY model.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: A single phase transition for the hard-core model on Z^2
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the hard-core lattice gas on Z^2 (independent sets weighted by λ^{|I|}) there is a critical activity λ_c such that the Gibbs measure is unique for λ < λ_c and there are two distinct checkerboard Gibbs measures for λ > λ_c; numerically λ_c ≈ 3.7962.
statement_caveat: The model is not known to be monotone in λ, so uniqueness at one activity does not give uniqueness below it; a single transition point is part of the claim.
source: D. S. Gaunt and M. E. Fisher, Hard-sphere lattice gases. I. Plane-square lattice, J. Chem. Phys. 43 (1965); R. J. Baxter, I. G. Enting and S. K. Tsang, Hard-square lattice gas, J. Stat. Phys. 22 (1980)
why_important: Hard squares is the simplest lattice model of a freezing transition (compare hard spheres, T080) and a standard test case for sampling algorithms; the gap between the proved uniqueness and coexistence regimes has resisted many methods. Baxter's exact solution covers hard hexagons, not hard squares.
where_it_stands: Uniqueness is proved for λ < 2.538 (Sinclair–Srivastava–Štefankovič–Yin 2017) and coexistence for λ > 5.3506 (Blanca–Galvin–Randall–Tetali) [verify both values]; coexistence at large λ goes back to Peierls arguments (Dobrushin 1968). Absence of complex zeros of the partition function up to the connective-constant threshold λ_c(σ) is proved in arXiv:2604.02746. The high-dimensional critical fugacity d^{−1+o(1)} (Hadas–Peled, arXiv:2603.27144; T140, retired) does not bear on Z^2. A single transition and the value of λ_c are open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Long-range order for proper 3-colourings of Z^3 (Kotecký's conjecture)
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For a uniformly random proper 3-colouring of the box {−L, …, L}^3 in Z^3 whose even boundary vertices are coloured 0 (the zero-temperature antiferromagnetic 3-state Potts model), there is c > 0 such that every even vertex far from the boundary has colour 0 with probability at least 1/3 + c, uniformly in L: the boundary's sublattice order survives in the bulk.
statement_caveat: In two dimensions the model maps to a height function and is expected to be disordered; the conjecture is that three dimensions is already ordered. Classifying the extremal Gibbs measures of maximal entropy (six are expected) would be a further step.
source: Kotecký's conjecture as reported in D. Galvin, J. Kahn, D. Randall and G. B. Sorkin, Phase coexistence and torpid mixing in the 3-coloring model on Z^d, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 29 (2015) [verify]
why_important: It is the cleanest open case of order created by entropy alone at zero temperature in a physical dimension, and it decides whether Glauber dynamics for 3-colourings of Z^3 mixes slowly.
where_it_stands: Long-range order is proved in high dimensions, with an error exp(−cd) controlled by the dimension rather than the box size (Galvin–Kahn–Randall–Sorkin, arXiv:1210.4232; Peled, High-dimensional Lipschitz functions are typically flat, Ann. Probab. 45 (2017)), and for q-colourings in high dimensions (Peled–Spinka 2018) [verify]. Three dimensions is open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: The optimal constant in the Berry–Esseen inequality
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Determine the least constant C_0 such that for every n and every iid sequence with E X = 0, E X² = 1 and E|X|³ = ρ < ∞, sup_x |P((X_1 + … + X_n)/√n ≤ x) − Φ(x)| ≤ C_0 ρ/√n. Esseen conjectured C_0 = (√10 + 3)/(6√(2π)) ≈ 0.4097, the value approached by a two-point distribution.
statement_caveat: Esseen (1956) showed that no smaller constant works even as n → ∞ [verify]; the conjecture is that his value suffices for every n.
source: C.-G. Esseen, A moment inequality with an application to the central limit theorem, Skand. Aktuarietidskr. 39 (1956)
why_important: The Berry–Esseen bound is the basic quantitative form of the central limit theorem and is used throughout statistics; the sharp constant has been pursued for over eighty years, and each improvement has needed new analytic ideas.
where_it_stands: Upper bounds went from 7.59 (Esseen 1942) through 0.7975 (van Beek 1972) to 0.4748 (Shevtsova 2011) [verify]. He and Cheng (arXiv:2609.06358v3) prove that Esseen's constant suffices for every n ≥ 2⌈exp(10^17)⌉, uniformly in the law. The constant for all n is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The 1/3–2/3 conjecture for linear extensions
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Every finite partially ordered set that is not a chain has two incomparable elements x and y such that a uniformly random linear extension places x before y with probability between 1/3 and 2/3.
statement_caveat: The bounds are attained by the three-element poset with a single relation. The conjecture is usually credited to Kislitsyn (1968) and, independently, to Fredman (1976) and Linial (1984) [verify].
source: S. S. Kislitsyn, Finite partially ordered sets and their associated sets of permutations, Mat. Zametki 4 (1968); M. L. Fredman, How good is the information theory bound in sorting?, Theoret. Comput. Sci. 1 (1976); N. Linial, The information-theoretic bound is good for merging, SIAM J. Comput. 13 (1984)
why_important: It is the best-known open problem about the uniform measure on linear extensions and has direct consequences for sorting with partial information.
where_it_stands: Kahn and Saks (1984) found a pair with probability in [3/11, 8/11]; Brightwell, Felsner and Trotter (1995) improved this to [(5 − √5)/10, (5 + √5)/10] ≈ [0.276, 0.724], which is optimal for some infinite posets, and Aires, Chan, Pak and Panova (arXiv:2609.30888) improve that bound by a small ε > 0, the first general improvement since 1995. The conjecture holds for posets of width two (Linial 1984), semiorders (Brightwell 1989) and posets of height two (Trotter–Gehrlein–Fishburn 1992) [verify]. Open in general.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The Gaussian product inequality
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For every centred Gaussian vector (X_1, …, X_m) and all positive integers k_1, …, k_m, E ∏ X_i^{2k_i} ≥ ∏ E X_i^{2k_i}.
statement_caveat: The case k_1 = … = k_m = 1 is equivalent to the real polarization problem for products of linear forms (Frenkel 2008; Malicet–Nourdin–Peccati–Poly 2016) [verify].
source: W. V. Li and A. Wei, A Gaussian inequality for expected absolute products, J. Theoret. Probab. 25 (2012) [verify]
why_important: It is the moment form of a family of Gaussian correlation inequalities, tied to the real polarization constant and to permanents of positive semidefinite matrices. It is easy to state and has resisted the methods that proved the Gaussian correlation inequality.
where_it_stands: Proved (claimed) for all positive exponents by Ouimet–Greaves (arXiv:2609.20234). Before that: m = 2, m = 3 with k_i = 1 (Frenkel 2008), three variables with even exponents (Herry–Malicet–Poly, arXiv:2211.07314) [verify], some three-dimensional cases with larger exponents (Russell–Sun 2022) [verify], and nonnegative covariances [verify].
retired_reason: SOLVED (claimed): Ouimet and Greaves, A proof of the strong Gaussian product inequality conjecture (arXiv:2609.20234, 2026, unrefereed), prove E ∏|X_i|^{α_i} ≥ ∏ E|X_i|^{α_i} for every centred Gaussian vector, degenerate ones included, and all positive exponents α_i, with equality exactly for independent coordinates when the variances are positive; the even-integer form in this row is the case α_i = 2k_i. Through Frenkel's hafnian formulation it also gives the real linear polarization constant. Herry, Malicet and Poly (arXiv:2211.07314) had already settled three variables with even exponents [verify]. Read from the paper 14 Oct by the w673 audit.

title: The B-conjecture for Gaussian measure
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For the standard Gaussian measure γ on R^n and every origin-symmetric convex body K, the function t ↦ γ(e^t K) is log-concave on R.
statement_caveat: Posed by Banaszczyk and popularized by Latała (Cordero-Erausquin–Fradelizi–Maurey 2004, p. 410).
source: R. Latała, On some inequalities for Gaussian measures, Proc. ICM 2002, vol. II [verify]; D. Cordero-Erausquin, M. Fradelizi and B. Maurey, The (B) conjecture for the Gaussian measure of dilates of symmetric convex sets and related problems, J. Funct. Anal. 214 (2004)
why_important: It is a central open problem on Gaussian measure and convex bodies, in the same family as the Gaussian correlation inequality (proved by Royen in 2014) and the log-Brunn–Minkowski conjecture.
where_it_stands: Proved for every symmetric convex set in every dimension, in the stronger diagonal form (Cordero-Erausquin–Fradelizi–Maurey 2004, Theorem 1). Related to the log-Brunn–Minkowski conjecture of Böröczky–Lutwak–Yang–Zhang (2012) [verify].
retired_reason: SOLVED in 2004: Cordero-Erausquin, Fradelizi and Maurey (J. Funct. Anal. 214 (2004) 410–427, doi:10.1016/j.jfa.2003.12.001) prove that t ↦ γ(e^t K) is log-concave for every symmetric convex set K in every dimension; their Theorem 1 is the stronger statement that (t_1, …, t_n) ↦ γ(e^{D(t_1, …, t_n)} K) is log-concave for diagonal D. The row's 'open for n ≥ 3' was wrong. The B-property for other symmetric log-concave measures is a different question. Read from the paper (pp. 410–411) 14 Oct by the w673 audit.

title: The Gotsman–Linial bound on the sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Every degree-d polynomial threshold function f = sign(p) on {−1, 1}^n has total influence (average sensitivity) at most C d √n, for an absolute constant C.
statement_caveat: Gotsman and Linial conjectured the exact maximizer: the symmetric function that changes sign on the d middle layers. That exact form is false (Chapman, arXiv:2108.02288, 2021); this row is the weaker asymptotic form, the O(d√n) bound.
source: C. Gotsman and N. Linial, Spectral properties of threshold functions, Combinatorica 14 (1994)
why_important: Sensitivity bounds for threshold functions control learning, noise sensitivity and pseudorandom generators for polynomial threshold functions. The Gaussian analogue is known, so the problem is about passing from Gaussian space to the cube.
where_it_stands: True for d = 1. Kane proved √n (log n)^{O(d log d)} 2^{O(d² log d)} (2014) [verify]; earlier bounds of the form n^{1 − 1/O(2^d)} are due to Diakonikolas–Harsha–Klivans–Meka–Raghavendra–Servedio–Tan and Harsha–Klivans–Meka (2010) [verify]. The Gaussian surface area of degree-d threshold functions is O(d) (Kane 2011). arXiv:2604.08095 bounds E√s_f, the mean square root of the sensitivity, not the total influence. Open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Worst-case trace reconstruction
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: An unknown binary string x of length n is observed through independent traces, each obtained by deleting every bit independently with probability q ∈ (0, 1). Determine the order of the number of traces needed to reconstruct every x with high probability; in particular decide whether polynomially many traces suffice.
statement_caveat: For a uniformly random x far fewer traces are needed, exp(O(log^{1/3} n)) (Holden–Pemantle–Peres–Zhai 2020); for the worst case the gap is now between polynomial and quasipolynomial bounds.
source: T. Batu, S. Kannan, S. Khanna and A. McGregor, Reconstructing strings from random traces, Proc. SODA 2004; F. Nazarov and Y. Peres, Trace reconstruction with exp(O(n^{1/3})) samples, Proc. STOC 2017
why_important: Trace reconstruction is the cleanest model of recovering a sequence from noisy copies (sequence alignment, DNA storage), and its gap between upper and lower bounds is among the widest in probability.
where_it_stands: exp(O(n^{1/3})) traces suffice (De–O'Donnell–Servedio 2017; Nazarov–Peres 2017), improved to exp(Õ(n^{1/5})) (Chase 2021) and then to quasipolynomially many, for every retention probability at least 1/polylog n (Burudgunte–Valiant–Wang, arXiv:2607.04073). The best lower bound is Ω̃(n^{3/2}) (Chase 2021), after n^{5/4} (Holden–Lyons 2020) [verify]. Whether polynomially many traces suffice is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The capacity of the binary deletion channel
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Determine the Shannon capacity C(d) of the binary deletion channel, in which each transmitted bit is deleted independently with probability d ∈ (0, 1) and the receiver sees the remaining bits in order.
statement_caveat: No closed form is conjectured; the problem is to find one, or a characterization that determines C(d).
source: R. L. Dobrushin, Shannon's theorems for channels with synchronization errors, Problems Inform. Transmission 3 (1967); M. Mitzenmacher, A survey of results for deletion channels and related synchronization channels, Probab. Surv. 6 (2009)
why_important: It is the simplest channel with synchronization errors and the basic binary channel whose capacity is unknown; it is the information-theoretic side of trace reconstruction (T116).
where_it_stands: The capacity exists as a limit of normalized mutual informations (Dobrushin 1967). C(d) ≥ (1 − d)/9 for every d (Mitzenmacher–Drinea 2006) [verify], with constructive lower bounds improved in arXiv:2609.24908; the expansion for small d is known to second order (Kanoria–Montanari 2013; Kalai–Mitzenmacher–Sudan 2010) [verify]; upper bounds of the form c(1 − d) with c < 1 hold for large d (Rahmati–Duman 2015) [verify]. arXiv:2609.19412 computes C(d) to within 0.0095 bits for every d and states that the exact capacity is unknown. Open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Computational hardness in the stochastic block model with five or more communities
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: For the symmetric stochastic block model with q ≥ 5 balanced communities and edge probabilities a/n and b/n, there is a nonempty region below the Kesten–Stigum bound (a − b)² = q(a + (q − 1)b) where weak recovery is information-theoretically possible but no polynomial-time algorithm achieves it.
statement_caveat: A full proof would separate complexity classes; realistic targets are lower bounds for restricted algorithm classes (low-degree polynomials, message passing, local algorithms) and the exact location of the information-theoretic threshold.
source: A. Decelle, F. Krzakala, C. Moore and L. Zdeborová, Asymptotic analysis of the stochastic block model for modular networks and its algorithmic applications, Phys. Rev. E 84 (2011); E. Abbe, Community detection and stochastic block models: recent developments, J. Mach. Learn. Res. 18 (2018)
locator: Abbe, arXiv:1703.10146, Section 10, Conjecture 2, p. 114
why_important: It is the leading example, with planted clique (T072), of a statistical–computational gap predicted by the cavity method; reconstruction on trees at the Kesten–Stigum bound (T067) is its local counterpart.
where_it_stands: Above the Kesten–Stigum bound weak recovery is achieved in polynomial time (Massoulié 2014; Mossel–Neeman–Sly for q = 2; Abbe–Sandon 2018 for general q) [verify]. For q ≥ 5 recovery below the bound is information-theoretically possible in part of the region (Banks–Moore–Neeman–Netrapalli 2016; Abbe–Sandon 2018) [verify]. For detection with q fixed, low-degree polynomials fail below the bound (Hopkins–Steurer 2017) [verify]; arXiv:2610.08872 adds lower bounds for low-degree rules, cycle statistics and belief propagation, and arXiv:2503.03047 treats a growing number of communities. For q = 2 the two thresholds coincide (Mossel–Neeman–Sly); for q = 3 and 4 whether they coincide is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The independence ratio of random cubic graphs
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: Determine the constant α_3 such that the independence number of a uniformly random 3-regular graph on n vertices, divided by n, converges in probability to α_3.
statement_caveat: The limit exists (Bayati–Gamarnik–Tetali 2013). The one-step replica-symmetry-breaking prediction is α_3 ≈ 0.4509 (Barbier–Krzakala–Zdeborová–Zhang 2013) [verify].
source: N. C. Wormald, Models of random regular graphs, in Surveys in Combinatorics 1999 (Cambridge Univ. Press, 1999) [verify]; J. Ding, A. Sly and N. Sun, Maximum independent sets on random regular graphs, Acta Math. 217 (2016)
why_important: Independent sets in random regular graphs are the test case for the cavity method at small degree. Ding, Sly and Sun proved the one-step formula for large degree; small degrees are where the method has not been confirmed.
where_it_stands: Bounds: α_3 ≥ 0.44533 (Csóka 2016) [verify] and α_3 ≤ 0.45537 (McKay 1987) [verify]. The one-step formula is proved for all d ≥ d_0 with d_0 large (Ding–Sly–Sun, arXiv:1310.4787), which does not reach d = 3. d = 3 is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: Finding large independent sets in sparse random graphs
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: In G(n, d/n) with d large, the independence number is (2 + o_d(1))(log d/d)n, while simple greedy algorithms find independent sets of size (1 + o_d(1))(log d/d)n. Prove that no polynomial-time algorithm finds an independent set of size (1 + ε)(log d/d)n with high probability, for fixed ε > 0 and all large d, or find one.
statement_caveat: As for planted clique (T072), the full statement is a hardness conjecture; lower bounds are proved for restricted classes of algorithms.
source: D. Gamarnik and M. Sudan, Limits of local algorithms over sparse random graphs, Ann. Probab. 45 (2017); A. M. Frieze, On the independence number of random graphs, Discrete Math. 81 (1990)
why_important: It is the sparse analogue of Karp's question on cliques in G(n, 1/2) (T068) and the main test of the overlap gap property as an explanation of algorithmic hardness in random structures.
where_it_stands: Local algorithms (factors of iid) cannot exceed (1 + 1/√2 + o(1))(log d/d)n (Gamarnik–Sudan 2017), and in fact (1 + o(1))(log d/d)n (Rahman–Virág 2017). The same limit holds for low-degree polynomial algorithms (Wein, arXiv:2010.06563; stronger low-degree hardness by Huang–Sellke, arXiv:2501.06427v2) and for stable algorithms through the overlap gap property (Gamarnik–Jagannath–Wein) [verify]. Unrestricted polynomial-time algorithms are open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Positive metric entropy of the Chirikov standard map
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: For the standard map f_K(x, y) = (x + y + K sin x, y + K sin x) on the 2-torus, prove that for some K, or for a set of K of positive measure, f_K has positive metric entropy with respect to Lebesgue measure, that is, a positive Lyapunov exponent on a set of positive area.
statement_caveat: Usually attributed to Sinai [verify]. For large K the entropy is expected to be about log(K/2). The difficulty is coexistence with elliptic islands, which exist for a residual set of large K (Duarte 1994).
source: B. V. Chirikov, A universal instability of many-dimensional oscillator systems, Phys. Rep. 52 (1979); Ya. G. Sinai, Topics in Ergodic Theory (Princeton Univ. Press, 1994) [verify]
why_important: The standard map is the basic model of area-preserving chaos (kicked rotors, particle accelerators); positive entropy for it would be the first proof of observable chaos for a natural conservative system without uniform hyperbolicity.
where_it_stands: Elliptic islands exist for a residual set of large K (Duarte 1994), so the map is not uniformly hyperbolic. Positive Lyapunov exponents are proved for random perturbations (Blumenthal–Xue–Young, Ann. Math. 185, 2017) and for modified standard maps (Berger–Carrasco 2014). Positive topological entropy for every K ≠ 0 is proved (arXiv:2404.02209), and arXiv:2003.00236 studies the measure of maximal entropy, which may be singular; neither gives positive entropy for Lebesgue measure. Positive metric entropy is not known for any K.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The maximum cut of sparse random graphs
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: For fixed d > 1, determine the limit of MaxCut(G)/n for G = G(n, d/n), or for a uniformly random d-regular graph, and prove that it equals the zero-temperature value predicted by the cavity method for the diluted antiferromagnet.
statement_caveat: For d ≤ 1, MaxCut/n → d/2 in G(n, d/n), since almost every edge lies in a tree component. As d → ∞ the answer is n(d/4 + P_*√(d/4) + o(√d)) with P_* ≈ 0.7632 the Parisi constant. For fixed d the prediction is the full replica-symmetry-breaking (Mézard–Parisi) cavity functional on a sparse graph, for which no rigorous variational formula is known.
source: M. Mézard and G. Parisi, The Bethe lattice spin glass revisited, Eur. Phys. J. B 20 (2001); A. Dembo, A. Montanari and S. Sen, Extremal cuts of sparse random graphs, Ann. Probab. 45 (2017)
why_important: MaxCut of a sparse random graph is the zero-temperature limit of the Viana–Bray diluted spin glass; a fixed-degree formula would carry the Parisi theory, proved in the dense mean-field case, over to sparse graphs, where most random optimization problems live.
where_it_stands: The limit exists (Bayati–Gamarnik–Tetali 2013). The large-d asymptotics are due to Dembo–Montanari–Sen (arXiv:1503.03923). For diluted spin glasses the Parisi-type formula gives upper bounds (Franz–Leone 2003; Panchenko–Talagrand 2004) [verify]; Harangi (arXiv:2506.21296) proves 2-RSB upper bounds that beat 1-RSB, and Aronow and Lopatto (arXiv:2609.19057) show that max-cut and max-bisection have the same limit at every fixed degree of a random regular graph. The exact value for fixed d > 1 is open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Mean-field critical behaviour of percolation on every nonamenable transitive graph
domain_name: Percolation and spatial random graphs
statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on any connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive nonamenable graph, the triangle condition holds at p_c, Σ_{x,y} τ_{p_c}(o,x) τ_{p_c}(x,y) τ_{p_c}(y,o) < ∞, and consequently the critical exponents take their mean-field values (β = γ = 1, δ = 2).
statement_caveat: Usually credited to Schramm [verify]. A stronger form asks for p_c < p_{2→2}, the threshold at which the percolation operator stops being bounded on ℓ², which implies the triangle condition (Hutchcroft).
source: O. Schramm, conjecture recorded in T. Hutchcroft, Percolation on hyperbolic graphs, Geom. Funct. Anal. 29 (2019) [verify]; I. Benjamini and O. Schramm, Percolation beyond Z^d, many questions and a few answers, Electron. Comm. Probab. 1 (1996)
why_important: Nonamenability is expected to make percolation behave like percolation on a tree at criticality in every dimension; together with p_c < p_u (T004) this is the central conjecture of percolation beyond Euclidean lattices.
where_it_stands: Proved for highly nonamenable graphs (Schonmann 2001; Pak–Smirnova-Nagnibeda 2000), for products of trees (Kozma 2011), for nonunimodular transitive graphs (Hutchcroft, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2020) [verify] and for Gromov-hyperbolic graphs (Hutchcroft, arXiv:1804.10191). Continuity θ(p_c) = 0 holds on all unimodular nonamenable transitive graphs (Benjamini–Lyons–Peres–Schramm 1999). Open in general, for example for many Cayley graphs of nonamenable groups with amenable-looking geometry.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Uniform expansion of SL_2(F_p) for all generating sets
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: There is ε > 0 such that for every prime p and every pair of elements generating SL_2(F_p), the Cayley graph of SL_2(F_p) with respect to that pair and its inverses has spectral gap at least ε; equivalently, the lazy random walk mixes in O(log p) steps uniformly over generating pairs.
statement_caveat: Lubotzky's question; the generators are allowed to depend on p, which is what makes uniformity hard.
source: A. Lubotzky, Discrete Groups, Expanding Graphs and Invariant Measures (Birkhäuser, 1994) [verify locator]
why_important: Expansion of Cayley graphs of finite simple groups is the meeting point of random walks, additive combinatorics and number theory (affine sieve, superstrong approximation); uniformity over generators asks whether expansion is a property of the group alone.
where_it_stands: Bourgain and Gamburd (Ann. Math. 2008) proved expansion for fixed generators in SL_2(Z) generating a non-elementary subgroup, reduced mod p. Breuillard and Gamburd (arXiv:0911.3022) proved uniform expansion over all generating pairs for a set of primes of density one, and random pairs give expanders with probability tending to one (Breuillard–Green–Guralnick–Tao 2015) [verify]. Uniform expansion over all primes is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Superdiffusivity of the two-dimensional self-repelling Brownian polymer
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For the self-repelling Brownian polymer in two dimensions (a Brownian particle pushed down the gradient of its own occupation measure smoothed by a fixed smooth, positive-definite potential V), with fixed coupling and started from its stationary environment (Tóth–Valkó), E|X(t)|² is of order t (log t)^{1/2}.
statement_caveat: The (log t)^{1/2} correction comes from a renormalization-group argument; the discrete true self-avoiding walk is a separate model with the same prediction. In one dimension the exponent is 2/3 and in three or more dimensions the motion is diffusive. Cannizzaro and Giles (arXiv:2403.06730) state the fixed-coupling exponent as unknown.
source: D. J. Amit, G. Parisi and L. Peliti, Asymptotic behavior of the 'true' self-avoiding walk, Phys. Rev. B 27 (1983); S. P. Obukhov and L. Peliti, Renormalisation of the 'true' self-avoiding walk, J. Phys. A 16 (1983)
why_important: Self-repelling motion is the simplest model of a walk interacting with its own past, and two dimensions is its critical dimension; the same logarithmic superdiffusivity is predicted for diffusion in random divergence-free fields and for the anisotropic KPZ equation.
where_it_stands: Tóth and Valkó (J. Stat. Phys. 2012) proved superdiffusive bounds between t log log t and t log t for the self-repelling Brownian polymer. The (log t)^{1/2} law is proved for a Brownian particle in the curl of the two-dimensional Gaussian free field (Cannizzaro–Haunschmid-Sibitz–Toninelli 2022) [verify], and in the weak-coupling limit of the polymer, with an explicit diffusivity (Cannizzaro–Giles, arXiv:2403.06730). The fixed-coupling (log t)^{1/2} law is open. In one dimension the scaling limit of the true self-repelling motion is known (Tóth–Werner 1998).
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Anomalous heat conduction in one-dimensional anharmonic chains
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: For a one-dimensional chain of anharmonic oscillators with nearest-neighbour interactions conserving energy, momentum and stretch, with a generic potential (an FPUT chain with nonzero cubic coupling, at nonzero pressure), the heat conductivity of a chain of length L between Langevin reservoirs grows like L^{1/3}, and in equilibrium the heat mode of the energy correlations spreads as a 5/3-stable Lévy process, while the two sound modes, moving at ±c, have KPZ scaling.
statement_caveat: These are predictions of Spohn's nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics (arXiv:1305.6412, eqs. (3.14) and (4.11)–(4.13)) and of mode coupling, not theorems; chains with special symmetry (for instance zero pressure) are predicted to fall into other classes.
source: S. Lepri, R. Livi and A. Politi, Heat conduction in chains of nonlinear oscillators, Phys. Rev. Lett. 78 (1997); H. Spohn, Nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics for anharmonic chains, J. Stat. Phys. 154 (2014)
why_important: Anomalous conduction is the one-dimensional face of the problem of deriving Fourier's law (T033); it is observed in simulations and in nanotubes, and it is the cleanest prediction of KPZ physics in a deterministic Hamiltonian system.
where_it_stands: For harmonic chains with momentum-conserving noise the conductivity grows like L^{1/2} (Basile–Bernardin–Olla 2006, 2009), and energy fluctuations follow a 3/4-fractional heat equation (Jara–Komorowski–Olla 2015; Bernardin–Gonçalves–Jara 2016) [verify]. For anharmonic chains, deterministic or with noise, the L^{1/3} law and the 5/3-Lévy heat mode are open. Normal conduction for pinned chains is T033.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Recurrence of the frog model on 3-ary and 4-ary trees
domain_name: Branching processes, trees and genealogies
statement: On the rooted d-ary tree, place one sleeping frog at each vertex and an active frog at the root; active frogs perform independent simple random walks and wake every frog they visit. Decide for d = 3 and d = 4 whether the root is visited infinitely often almost surely (recurrence) or finitely often (transience).
statement_caveat: Hoffman, Johnson and Junge settled d = 2 and d ≥ 5 and left the two middle cases; the problem is to find the transition.
source: C. Hoffman, T. Johnson and M. Junge, Recurrence and transience for the frog model on trees, Ann. Probab. 45 (2017)
why_important: The frog model is the basic model of a self-amplifying spread of random walkers (rumour and infection models); on trees the competition between branching of the walkers and transience of each walk is sharp, and the open cases sit exactly at the phase transition.
where_it_stands: Recurrent for d = 2 and transient for d ≥ 5 (Hoffman–Johnson–Junge, arXiv:1404.6238); with Poisson(μ) sleeping frogs per site the critical μ is known to grow linearly in d (Hoffman–Johnson–Junge 2016; Johnson–Junge 2016) [verify]. Mathews (arXiv:2309.14443) still treats d = 3 and d = 4 as known only from simulation. With one frog per site, d = 3 and d = 4 are open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: Random band matrices at the critical bandwidth
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: Let H be the real symmetric N × N band matrix with independent centred Gaussian entries h_ij (i ≤ j) of variance 1/(2W + 1) when the periodic distance |i − j|_N is at most W, and zero otherwise, and take W = c√N with c fixed. For every energy E in (−2, 2), the eigenvalues near E, unfolded by the semicircle density, converge as N → ∞ to a point process that depends on c and E through a single crossover parameter and interpolates between Poisson (c → 0) and GOE (c → ∞), as predicted by the supersymmetric sigma model.
statement_caveat: The localized (W ≪ √N) and delocalized (W ≫ √N) sides are now known; this row asks only for the critical regime, which the retired row T035 does not cover.
source: Y. V. Fyodorov and A. D. Mirlin, Scaling properties of localization in random band matrices: a σ-model approach, Phys. Rev. Lett. 67 (1991)
why_important: It is the one-dimensional model case of the Anderson transition in finite volume: a one-parameter family of critical statistics between localization and random-matrix behaviour.
where_it_stands: Both sides of the transition are proved (T035, retired): delocalization with Wigner–Dyson statistics for W ≫ √N (Yau–Yin, arXiv:2501.01718; Erdős–Riabov, arXiv:2506.06441) and localization at scale W² for W² ≪ N (Drogin, arXiv:2508.05802), with Poisson bulk statistics for real Gaussian band matrices when W² ≪ N/log N (Fan–Zou, arXiv:2609.23389). In a sigma-model approximation of Gaussian block band matrices the crossover at W ~ √N has been studied by M. Shcherbina and T. Shcherbina [verify]. The limiting statistics at W = c√N for the standard model are open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The singularity probability of random symmetric sign matrices
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: Let A_n be a uniformly random symmetric n × n matrix with independent ±1 entries on and above the diagonal. Then P(A_n is singular) = (1/2 + o(1))^n.
statement_caveat: The non-symmetric analogue, P(singular) = (1/2 + o(1))^n for ±1 matrices, is Tikhomirov's theorem; the symmetric case loses the independence between a row and its column that the non-symmetric proofs use. A sharper form, that two equal or opposite rows are the dominant cause, so that the probability is of order n² 2^{−n}, is a stronger target that needs its own source.
source: K. P. Costello, T. Tao and V. Vu, Random symmetric matrices are almost surely nonsingular, Duke Math. J. 135 (2006); V. H. Vu, Recent progress in combinatorial random matrix theory, Probab. Surv. 18 (2021) [verify]
locator: Vu, Probab. Surv. 18 (2021), arXiv:2005.02797, Conjecture 3.3
why_important: Invertibility of random discrete matrices is the core of non-asymptotic random matrix theory and of Littlewood–Offord theory; the symmetric case is the natural test because the dependence breaks the methods that solved the non-symmetric problem.
where_it_stands: Costello–Tao–Vu (2006) proved o(1); the bound was improved to n^{−C} (Nguyen 2012), exp(−n^c) (Vershynin 2014), exp(−c√n) (Campos–Mattos–Morris–Morrison 2021) and further [verify], and exponentially small probability exp(−cn) was proved by Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe (arXiv:2105.11384), who also bound the least singular value by Cε + exp(−cn) and the probability of a repeated eigenvalue by exp(−Ω(n)) (arXiv:2203.06141); corank estimates are in arXiv:2506.01155. The base 1/2 is open. For non-symmetric ±1 matrices the base 1/2 is proved (Tikhomirov, Ann. Math. 2020), with sharper forms for general discrete entries by Jain, Sah and Sawhney [verify].
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The dynamic critical exponent of the two-dimensional Ising model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For continuous-time heat-bath Glauber dynamics (each site updated at rate 1) of the Ising model on the L × L torus at the critical temperature, the inverse spectral gap and the mixing time are L^{z+o(1)} for an exponent z, numerically z ≈ 2.17. Prove that z exists, determine it, and show it is the same for every local reversible single-spin dynamics whose rates are bounded above and below uniformly.
statement_caveat: This is the dynamic exponent of model A in the Hohenberg–Halperin classification; no closed form is predicted.
source: P. C. Hohenberg and B. I. Halperin, Theory of dynamic critical phenomena, Rev. Mod. Phys. 49 (1977); E. Lubetzky and A. Sly, Critical Ising on the square lattice mixes in polynomial time, Comm. Math. Phys. 313 (2012)
why_important: z is the basic exponent of critical slowing down, which controls the cost of simulating critical systems; in two dimensions every static exponent is known exactly but the dynamic one is not.
where_it_stands: Lubetzky and Sly (2012) proved polynomial mixing at criticality, L^C for some C. The lower bound z ≥ 2 is proved (Masaoka–Soejima–Watanabe, arXiv:2502.09908), improving z ≥ 7/4 = 2 − η. Numerical estimates give z ≈ 2.1667 (Nightingale–Blöte 1996) [verify]. Existence and value are open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The Coulomb phase of the three-dimensional dimer model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For uniformly random dimer coverings (perfect matchings) of large boxes or tori in Z^3, dimer–dimer correlations decay like |x|^{−3} with a dipolar angular dependence, and the associated flux field converges to a Gaussian (Coulomb) field.
statement_caveat: In two dimensions the analogous statement follows from Kasteleyn's determinantal solution; in three dimensions there is no such solution.
source: D. A. Huse, W. Krauth, R. Moessner and S. L. Sondhi, Coulomb and liquid dimer models in three dimensions, Phys. Rev. Lett. 91 (2003)
why_important: The Coulomb phase is the basic example of an emergent gauge field in classical statistical mechanics (spin ice, frustrated magnets), and the three-dimensional dimer model is its simplest lattice instance.
where_it_stands: A variational principle and large deviations for the height-like flux of three-dimensional dimers are proved (Chandgotia–Sheffield–Wolfram, arXiv:2304.08468), and macroscopic loops in related three-dimensional loop and double-dimer models are known (Quitmann–Taggi) [verify]. The power-law correlations and the Gaussian limit are open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: Metric scaling limits of decorated random planar maps
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: Random planar maps weighted by a critical FK model with 0 ≤ q < 4 (q = 0 is the map decorated by a uniform spanning tree, q = 1 the uniform map, q = 2 the critical Ising map), with distances rescaled by n^{−1/d_γ+o(1)}, converge in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology to the γ-Liouville quantum gravity metric sphere, where q = 2 + 2cos(πγ²/2) (γ = √2, √(8/3), √3 in the three cases).
statement_caveat: Only the uniform case γ = √(8/3) (the Brownian map) is known; the exponent d_γ for other γ is itself unknown (T037). For q > 4 the maps are in another phase, with a continuum-random-tree limit (Feng, arXiv:2311.06235). This row asks for metric convergence, while T023 asks for convergence under conformal embedding.
source: J. Miller and S. Sheffield, Liouville quantum gravity and the Brownian map I, Invent. Math. 219 (2020) [verify]; J. Ding, J. Dubédat, A. Dunlap and H. Falconet, Tightness of Liouville first passage percolation for γ ∈ (0,2), Publ. Math. IHÉS 132 (2020)
why_important: It would identify the geometry of random surfaces carrying the main critical models with LQG, the continuum theory physicists use for two-dimensional quantum gravity, and would make d_γ a measurable growth exponent of discrete maps.
where_it_stands: Uniform maps converge to the Brownian map (Le Gall 2013; Miermont 2013), identified with √(8/3)-LQG (Miller–Sheffield). The γ-LQG metric exists and is unique for every γ ∈ (0,2) (Ding–Dubédat–Dunlap–Falconet 2020; Gwynne–Miller 2021). For decorated maps only distance-exponent bounds are known (Ding–Gwynne; Gwynne–Holden–Sun) [verify]; for spanning-tree-decorated maps a directed distance scales as n^{1/3} (arXiv:2609.22514), which is not the graph distance. Open for every γ ≠ √(8/3).
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The arctic curve of the six-vertex model with domain-wall boundary conditions
domain_name: SLE, Gaussian fields, Liouville quantum gravity and random planar maps
statement: For the six-vertex model with domain-wall boundary conditions on an n × n square, in the disordered regime −1 < Δ < 1, the boundary between the frozen and disordered regions converges after rescaling by n to the curve predicted by Colomo and Pronko, and recovered by the tangent method of Colomo and Sportiello; the analogous prediction holds in the antiferroelectric regime Δ < −1.
statement_caveat: The predictions are explicit algebraic or transcendental curves depending on the weights; at Δ = 0 (free fermions) the curve is an ellipse, the arctic circle of domino tilings for equal weights.
source: F. Colomo and A. G. Pronko, The limit shape of large alternating sign matrices, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 24 (2010); F. Colomo and A. Sportiello, Arctic curves of the six-vertex model on generic domains: the tangent method, J. Stat. Phys. 164 (2016)
why_important: The six-vertex model is the basic integrable model outside free fermions; its limit shapes test whether the variational and tangent-method predictions hold beyond the determinantal case, and uniformly random alternating sign matrices are a special case.
where_it_stands: At Δ = 0 the arctic circle is known (Jockusch–Propp–Shor 1995). At the ice point Δ = 1/2, which includes uniformly random alternating sign matrices, Aggarwal (arXiv:1812.03847, 2020) proved the Colomo–Pronko arctic curve for domain-wall boundary conditions, and the predicted boundaries for more general three-bundle domains. Other values of Δ are open; fluctuations of the height function are T063.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: An exponential improvement of the random-graph lower bound for diagonal Ramsey numbers
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: Is there ε > 0 such that R(k, k) ≥ (√2 + ε)^k for all large k? Equivalently, are there graphs on (√2 + ε)^k vertices with no clique and no independent set of size k?
statement_caveat: Erdős's 1947 bound comes from the random graph G(n, 1/2), and no construction, random or explicit, has beaten its exponential rate. Erdős offered prizes for the existence and the value of lim R(k, k)^{1/k} [verify].
source: P. Erdős, Some remarks on the theory of graphs, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 53 (1947)
why_important: This is the founding problem of the probabilistic method: the random graph is the best known Ramsey graph, and an exponential improvement would need a genuinely new source of structure or randomness.
where_it_stands: The lower bound R(k, k) ≥ (1 + o(1)) (√2 k/e) 2^{k/2} (Spencer 1975, by the local lemma) is a factor 2 over Erdős's. The upper bound was improved exponentially to (4 − ε)^k (Campos–Griffiths–Morris–Sahasrabudhe 2023), then to about 3.8^k (Gupta–Ndiaye–Norin–Wei) [verify], and arXiv:2609.14525 claims 3.69507^k. No exponential improvement of the lower bound is known; explicit constructions are far weaker.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Singularity of harmonic measure for random walks on cocompact Fuchsian groups (Kaimanovich–Le Prince)
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Let Γ be a cocompact lattice in PSL_2(R), for example the fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic surface, and μ a finitely supported probability measure whose support generates Γ as a semigroup. The harmonic (hitting) measure on the boundary circle of the random walk with step law μ is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure.
statement_caveat: Kaimanovich and Le Prince conjectured singularity for every finitely supported random walk on a discrete subgroup of a semisimple Lie group; the cocompact Fuchsian case is the test case, because there the boundary circle carries both measures naturally.
source: V. A. Kaimanovich and V. Le Prince, Matrix random products with singular harmonic measure, Geom. Dedicata 150 (2011)
why_important: It asks whether the stationary measure of a random walk, which can be made smooth by spreading the steps out (Furstenberg), can be absolutely continuous when the steps are finitely supported; the answer ties the entropy, drift and growth of a random walk to the geometry of the group.
where_it_stands: Kaimanovich and Le Prince showed that every such group carries finitely supported walks with singular harmonic measure. Singularity is proved for every finitely supported walk on non-cocompact lattices (Guivarc'h–Le Jan 1990; Gadre–Maher–Tiozzo 2017) [verify] and for nearest-neighbour walks with respect to certain generating sets of cocompact Fuchsian groups (Kosenko–Tiozzo 2022) [verify]. Bourgain (2012) constructed finitely supported measures on SL_2(R), generating non-discrete groups, whose stationary measure is absolutely continuous. Open for general finitely supported walks on cocompact lattices.
retired_reason: SOLVED (claimed): Kosenko and Tiozzo, Singularity of harmonic measure for finitely supported random walks (arXiv:2609.19115, 16 Sep 2026, unrefereed), resolve the singularity conjecture affirmatively for finitely supported non-degenerate random walks on cocompact Fuchsian groups, which is this row. The proof builds one geodesic current from Lebesgue measure and one from the harmonic measure and shows with Fourier analysis on the boundary that they differ. The Kaimanovich–Le Prince conjecture for discrete subgroups of other semisimple groups is a separate question. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged by the w673 audit.

title: Free-energy and ground-state fluctuations of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model at low temperature
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the Ising SK model H_N(σ) = N^{−1/2} Σ_{i<j} g_ij σ_i σ_j with iid standard Gaussian couplings, determine the order and the limiting law of the fluctuations of log Z_N(β) at each fixed β > 1, and of the ground-state energy max_σ H_N(σ). Physics predicts a standard deviation of order N^{1/6}.
statement_caveat: Order N^{1/4} has also been proposed; the survey of Collins-Woodfin and Le records the competing predictions. In the spherical SK model the low-temperature fluctuations are of order N^{1/3} with a Tracy–Widom law (Baik–Lee 2016), which is no guide to the Ising case.
source: A. Crisanti, G. Paladin, H.-J. Sommers and A. Vulpiani, Replica trick and fluctuations in disordered systems, J. Phys. I France 2 (1992) [verify]; E. Collins-Woodfin and H. T. Le, Free energy fluctuations in SK and related spin glass models: a literature survey, arXiv:2510.26960 (2025), Section 2
why_important: The Parisi formula fixes the limit of the free energy, but nothing fixes the next order; the order of fluctuations is the basic quantitative question about a disordered system beyond its limit, and the ground-state version is the fluctuation question for a random quadratic optimisation problem.
where_it_stands: For β < 1 the fluctuations are of order one and Gaussian (Aizenman–Lebowitz–Ruelle 1987). For β > 1 superconcentration gives variance O(N/log N) (Chatterjee) [verify]. Aronow and Lopatto (arXiv:2609.09103, 2026) prove that at zero external field and every fixed β > 1 the variance of log Z_N(β) lies between the orders N^{4/15} and N^{7/15}, with the same exponents for the ground-state energy; the predicted standard deviation N^{1/6}, a variance of order N^{1/3}, lies inside that range. The competing predictions are surveyed by Collins-Woodfin and Le (arXiv:2510.26960). The exponent and the limit law are open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the Viana–Bray model, N Ising spins in which each pair interacts, independently with probability c/N, through an independent coupling with the symmetric law ±1 (or the standard Gaussian law), prove that lim (1/N) E log Z_N(β) equals the Mézard–Parisi variational formula at every β > 0, with full replica symmetry breaking where the model needs it. The same question is posed for the diluted K-spin model with K even and for random K-SAT at positive temperature.
statement_caveat: The Mézard–Parisi formula is a hierarchy of distributions over distributions of cavity fields, much heavier than the SK formula. The model, the coupling law and the trial functional have to be fixed; for heavy-tailed couplings the expected free energy need not even be finite. The zero-temperature MaxCut case on sparse random graphs is T122.
source: M. Mézard and G. Parisi, The Bethe lattice spin glass revisited, Eur. Phys. J. B 20 (2001); D. Panchenko, Structure of finite-RSB asymptotic Gibbs measures in the diluted spin glass models, arXiv:1406.4702 (2014)
why_important: Sparse random constraint satisfaction problems, MaxCut and colouring of sparse random graphs are diluted spin glasses at zero temperature; the formula would give their ground-state values and would put the cavity method, which predicts their phase transitions, on a rigorous footing.
where_it_stands: The formula is an upper bound for the diluted K-spin model with K even, which includes Viana–Bray, and for random K-SAT (Franz–Leone 2003; Panchenko–Talagrand 2004), and it is proved in replica-symmetric regimes such as high temperature [verify]. Panchenko showed that 1-RSB asymptotic Gibbs measures of the diluted p-spin models satisfy the Mézard–Parisi ansatz (arXiv:1308.1944), and that after a small modification of the Hamiltonian so do all finite-RSB ones (arXiv:1406.4702); the full-RSB case and the removal of the modification are missing. The satisfiability threshold of random K-SAT at large K is proved to be the one-step value (Ding–Sly–Sun 2015), but that is a zero-temperature statement, not the free energy. The formula at every temperature is open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The algorithmic threshold of random k-SAT
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: For random k-SAT with n variables and ⌊αn⌋ independent uniformly random k-clauses, characterise the densities α at which some randomized polynomial-time algorithm finds a satisfying assignment with high probability. Conjecturally the threshold is (1 + o_k(1)) 2^k ln k / k, far below the satisfiability threshold 2^k ln 2 − (1 + ln 2)/2 + o_k(1).
statement_caveat: Hardness for every polynomial-time algorithm cannot be proved without a complexity assumption, so the question as usually posed is to locate the threshold and to prove that broad classes of algorithms (local, low-degree, stable) fail above it. The limits are taken with k fixed and n → ∞, and then k large.
source: D. Achlioptas and A. Coja-Oghlan, Algorithmic barriers from phase transitions, FOCS 2008; A. Coja-Oghlan, A better algorithm for random k-SAT, SIAM J. Comput. 39 (2010); D. Gamarnik, The overlap gap property, arXiv:2109.14409 (2021)
why_important: Random k-SAT is the model case of a gap between existence and efficient construction: solutions exist at densities about k/ln k times larger than any known algorithm reaches, and the gap begins where the solution space shatters into clusters.
where_it_stands: Coja-Oghlan's algorithm succeeds up to (1 − ε) 2^k ln k / k, where the solution space shatters (Achlioptas–Coja-Oghlan 2008); the satisfiability threshold for large k is known (Ding–Sly–Sun 2015). Low-degree polynomial algorithms fail above about 4.91 · 2^k ln k / k (Bresler–Huang 2021) [verify], with stronger low-degree hardness by Huang and Sellke (arXiv:2501.06427), and He, Li and Yang (arXiv:2610.10474) sample solutions almost uniformly for α ≤ 2^k/k^16 at large k. Whether any polynomial-time algorithm succeeds above (1 + ε) 2^k ln k / k is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Mansour's conjecture on the Fourier spectrum of DNF formulas
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: There is a constant C such that for every t ≥ 2 and ε ∈ (0, 1), every Boolean function f on {−1,1}^n computed by a DNF formula with t terms has a polynomial p with at most t^{C log(1/ε)} monomials and E (f − p)² ≤ ε; equivalently, all but ε of the Fourier weight of f lies on that many coefficients.
statement_caveat: With t = 1 the bound would allow a single monomial, which fails for a conjunction of a few literals, hence t ≥ 2. It follows from the Fourier entropy–influence conjecture (T021). Through Gopalan, Kalai and Klivans (2008) it would give a polynomial-time agnostic learning algorithm for DNF formulas under the uniform distribution with membership queries [verify]; the non-agnostic case is already Jackson's Harmonic Sieve (1997).
source: Y. Mansour, An O(n^{log log n}) learning algorithm for DNF under the uniform distribution, J. Comput. System Sci. 50 (1995)
why_important: DNF formulas are the basic class of computational learning theory, and the conjecture is the cleanest statement that their Fourier spectrum is as sparse as their size suggests.
where_it_stands: Mansour proved the bound t^{O(log log t · log(1/ε))}. The conjecture holds for random DNF formulas (Klivans–Lee–Wan 2010) [verify]. For DNFs of read number k, Lecomte and Tan (arXiv:2109.04525) prove concentration on t^{O(log log k)} coefficients for constant ε, improving the earlier t^{O(k^{3/2})}, and the optimal poly(t) for k up to about log log t. Open in general.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: The hard-core model on Z^d in high dimension (Galvin–Kahn)
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For every ε > 0 and all large enough d, the hard-core model on Z^d (the random independent set I weighted by λ^{|I|}) has more than one Gibbs measure, the states favouring the even and the odd sublattice being different, at every fugacity λ ≥ d^{−1+ε}.
statement_caveat: Uniqueness holds for λ below a constant times 1/d, by comparison with the regular tree [verify], so the conjecture puts the transition at d^{−1+o(1)}. Monotonicity in λ is not known, so the threshold need not be a single number. T109 asks whether there is a single transition on Z^2.
source: D. Galvin and J. Kahn, On phase transition in the hard-core model on Z^d, Combin. Probab. Comput. 13 (2004) (exact form of the conjecture to verify)
why_important: The hard-core model is the basic lattice gas with exclusion; its high-dimensional behaviour tests whether lattice phase transitions approach their tree (mean-field) values, and the proofs drove the combinatorics of odd cutsets and containers.
where_it_stands: Phase coexistence for λ ≥ C d^{−1/4} log^{3/4} d (Galvin–Kahn 2004) and λ ≥ C d^{−1/3} log² d (Peled–Samotij 2014) [verify], then for λ ≥ C log d/d (Hadas–Peled, arXiv:2603.27144).
retired_reason: SOLVED (claimed): Hadas and Peled, On the critical fugacity of the hard-core model on regular bipartite graphs (arXiv:2603.27144, 28 Mar 2026), prove long-range order on finite regular bipartite graphs above a threshold set by expansion parameters; on the hypercube and on fixed-side tori this is λ ≥ Ω(log d/d), and reflection positivity carries it to Z^d, so the critical fugacity on Z^d is d^{−1+o(1)}. Read from the arXiv abstract 14 Oct; flagged by the w673 audit.

title: The oriented Kesten–McKay law for random regular digraphs
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For fixed d ≥ 3, the empirical distribution of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of a uniformly random simple d-regular directed graph on n vertices (no loops, in- and out-degree d at every vertex) converges weakly in probability as n → ∞ to the rotation-invariant law on the disc |z| < √d with density d²(d − 1) / (π (d² − |z|²)²), the Brown measure of the free sum of d Haar unitaries.
statement_caveat: Rescaled by √d, the conjectured law tends to the circular law as d → ∞; the conjecture is the fixed-degree counterpart of the Kesten–McKay law for undirected random regular graphs.
source: C. Bordenave and D. Chafaï, Around the circular law, Probab. Surv. 9 (2012) [verify locator]
why_important: It is the basic spectral question for sparse non-Hermitian random matrices; at fixed degree the method behind the circular law, control of the least singular value of the shifted matrix, breaks down.
where_it_stands: The circular law, after rescaling by √d, is proved when d grows at least polylogarithmically in n (Cook 2019; Litvak–Lytova–Tikhomirov–Tomczak-Jaegermann–Youssef 2021) and for sums of d independent uniform permutation matrices with d growing (Basak–Cook–Zeitouni 2018) [verify]. At fixed d ≥ 3 even the nonsingularity of the adjacency matrix was proved only recently (J. Huang) [verify]. Adhikari and Dembo (arXiv:2310.14132) reduce the conjecture to a bound on the probability that the smallest singular values of the shifted matrices are tiny, and leave that bound open. Coste, Lambert and Zhu (arXiv:2204.00524) find the limit of the characteristic polynomial inside the unit disc for sums of random permutation matrices, which does not give the eigenvalue law. Convergence to the oriented Kesten–McKay law is open.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: The variance of the longest common subsequence of two random words (Waterman's conjecture)
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Let L_n be the length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary words of length n. Then Var(L_n) is of order n: there are constants 0 < c < C with c n ≤ Var(L_n) ≤ C n for all large n.
statement_caveat: E L_n / n converges to the Chvátal–Sankoff constant γ_2 ≈ 0.812, whose exact value is unknown; Steele's guess γ_2 = 2/(1 + √2) is ruled out by Lueker's bounds (J. ACM 2009). The upper bound is elementary, so the conjecture is the matching lower bound.
source: V. Chvátal and D. Sankoff, Longest common subsequences of two random sequences, J. Appl. Probab. 12 (1975); M. S. Waterman, Estimating statistical significance of sequence alignments, Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. B 344 (1994) [verify]
why_important: The longest common subsequence is the basic score for comparing two sequences (in DNA alignment among others), and its fluctuations decide when an alignment score is significant. It is a directed last-passage percolation problem with dependent weights; independent weights would give variance of order n^{2/3}, so the conjecture says the dependence changes the universality class.
where_it_stands: Steele (1986) proved Var(L_n) ≤ n with the Efron–Stein inequality; Chvátal and Sankoff had conjectured a variance of order o(n^{2/3}), which Waterman's simulations contradict. A linear lower bound is proved when one letter has very small probability (Lember–Matzinger, Ann. Probab. 2009) and in other strongly biased models (Houdré–Ma 2016) [verify]. Houdré and Işlak (arXiv:1408.1559) prove a central limit theorem for L_n assuming a lower bound of the right order on the variance, so the conjecture would also give the fluctuations. Open for uniform binary words.
note: Status updated after the w673 audit (14 Oct). Fame borderline in that audit; kept for now.

title: The limit law of the cover time of the two-dimensional torus
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Let C_n be the time simple random walk on the discrete torus (Z/nZ)² takes to visit every vertex. There are deterministic a_n such that √(C_n)/n − a_n converges in distribution, conjecturally to a randomly shifted Gumbel law.
statement_caveat: The first-order asymptotics C_n ~ (4/π) n² (log n)² are due to Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni; the conjecture is the analogue, for cover times, of the convergence in law of the maximum of the two-dimensional Gaussian free field.
source: A. Dembo, Y. Peres, J. Rosen and O. Zeitouni, Cover times for Brownian motion and random walks in two dimensions, Ann. Math. 160 (2004); D. Belius, J. Rosen and O. Zeitouni, Tightness for the cover time of the two dimensional sphere, Probab. Theory Related Fields 176 (2020)
why_important: Two-dimensional cover times are governed by the same log-correlated structure as the maximum of the Gaussian free field and of branching random walk; the limit law is the piece still missing from that picture.
where_it_stands: First order: Dembo–Peres–Rosen–Zeitouni (2004). Second-order terms: Belius–Kistler (2017) and Abe (2021) [verify]. Tightness of the centred square root is proved for Brownian motion on the two-sphere (Belius–Rosen–Zeitouni 2020), and convergence to a randomly shifted Gumbel law for the cover time of the binary tree (Cortines–Louidor–Saglietti 2021) [verify]. Convergence in law on the discrete torus is open (whether tightness is proved there is to verify).
retired_reason: SOLVED (claimed): Yechi Zhou, A limit law for the cover time of the two-dimensional discrete torus (arXiv:2610.01852, 1 Oct 2026, unrefereed), proves for the walk with jump rate one on (Z/NZ)² that T_N/((2/π) N² log N) − 2 log N + log log N converges in law to G + log(κZ), with G a standard Gumbel variable, Z the total mass of the critical Gaussian multiplicative chaos of the zero-average Gaussian free field on the unit torus, independent of G, and κ > 0 deterministic; the paper transfers this to discrete time. In the row's form, √(C_N)/N − (2/√π) log N + (1/(2√π)) log log N converges to (G + log(κZ))/(2√π). It answers the question of Aldous recorded by Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni. Read from the arXiv abstract and the paper's introduction 14 Oct; flagged by the w673 audit.

title: Wigner–Dyson level statistics for the three-dimensional Anderson model at weak disorder
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For the Anderson model H = −Δ + λV on Z^3, with V_x iid with a bounded density (for example uniform on [−1, 1]) and small λ > 0, restricted to the box [−L, L]^3 with periodic boundary conditions, take an energy E in the bulk of the spectrum where the states are extended. The eigenvalues near E, rescaled by the integrated density of states, converge as L → ∞ to the bulk sine-kernel process of the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (H is real symmetric).
statement_caveat: A genuinely random potential is needed: a constant potential gives the free Laplacian, whose spectrum has degenerate deterministic spacings. In the localized regime the corresponding limit is Poisson. Absolutely continuous spectrum, the subject of T009, would not by itself give GOE statistics.
source: B. I. Shklovskii, B. Shapiro, B. R. Sears, P. Lambrianides and H. B. Shore, Statistics of spectra of disordered systems near the metal–insulator transition, Phys. Rev. B 47 (1993); M. Aizenman and S. Warzel, Random Operators (AMS, 2015) [verify locator]
why_important: Level statistics are the observable signature of the metal–insulator transition and the bridge between random Schrödinger operators and random matrix theory.
where_it_stands: Poisson statistics in the localized regime are proved (Minami 1996; for Hölder single-site laws Dolai–Krishna, arXiv:1408.4251). On the delocalized side GOE statistics are proved for random band matrices of large enough width (T128) but for no Schrödinger operator on Z^d. For uniform potentials at weak disorder, absolutely continuous spectrum near the bottom of the band in every d ≥ 3 is claimed in an unrefereed 2026 preprint (T009, retired); the level statistics are open.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Equality of the microstates and non-microstates free entropies
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For every n-tuple of self-adjoint elements X_1, …, X_n of a tracial von Neumann algebra that embeds in an ultrapower of the hyperfinite II_1 factor (a Connes-embeddable tuple), Voiculescu's microstates free entropy χ(X_1, …, X_n), defined through the volume of the set of n-tuples of matrices whose joint moments approximate those of the X_i, equals his non-microstates free entropy χ*(X_1, …, X_n), defined through free Fisher information.
statement_caveat: Without the embeddability assumption the equality fails: since Connes's embedding problem has a negative answer (Ji–Natarajan–Vidick–Wright–Yuen, MIP* = RE), there are tuples with no microstates, so χ = −∞, and χ* > −∞ (Jekel–Pi, arXiv:2305.02574, introduction). Up to Gaussian normalisation, χ is the exponential rate (a lim sup) at which independent GUE matrices have joint moments near those of the X_i, so equality would identify a large-deviation quantity for random matrices with an entropy defined intrinsically, much as classical entropy is recovered from Fisher information along the heat flow. Whether the corresponding large deviation principle holds is itself open.
source: D. Voiculescu, The analogues of entropy and of Fisher's information measure in free probability theory V: noncommutative Hilbert transforms, Invent. Math. 132 (1998) [verify]
why_important: It is the central open problem of free entropy, the theory that connects random matrix large deviations with the structure of operator algebras.
where_it_stands: χ ≤ χ* is proved (Biane–Capitaine–Guionnet 2003, through large deviations for Hermitian Brownian motion), with an elementary proof, extended to conditional free entropies, by Jekel and Pi (arXiv:2305.02574). Equality holds for a single variable and for free families [verify]. Open for Connes-embeddable tuples.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Universality of the critical two-dimensional Ising model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For every ferromagnetic Ising model on Z^2 with finite-range, translation-invariant pair couplings that are invariant under the symmetries of Z^2 and whose interaction graph is connected, at its critical temperature the spin–spin correlation decays like |x|^{−1/4}, the correlation-length exponent is ν = 1, and the rescaled spin and energy fields converge to the same conformally invariant limits as for the nearest-neighbour model.
statement_caveat: Onsager's exact solution and the fermionic methods behind the scaling limits need a planar nearest-neighbour model; a finite-range model is not planar. Connectivity is needed: couplings only between sites at distance 2 along the axes split Z^2 into four independent Ising models on sublattices.
source: Standard renormalisation-group prediction; see H. Duminil-Copin, 100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice, Proc. ICM 2022 [verify]
why_important: Universality is the central prediction of the renormalisation group, and the two-dimensional Ising model is the one case where the universal limit is completely known; the question is purely whether non-integrable models reach it.
where_it_stands: Proved for the nearest-neighbour model, also on isoradial graphs (Smirnov 2010; Chelkak–Smirnov 2012; Chelkak–Hongler–Izyurov 2015), and for energy correlations of small finite-range perturbations of it (Giuliani–Greenblatt–Mastropietro 2012) [verify]. For general finite-range models with a connected interaction graph, Aizenman, Duminil-Copin, Tassion and Warzel (arXiv:1801.04960, Theorem 1.2) proved that the boundary spin correlations at criticality are asymptotically Pfaffian; this concerns boundary correlations, not the bulk scaling limits. Open in general.
note: Statement revised after the w673 audit (14 Oct).

title: Sidorenko's conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For every bipartite graph H and every graph G, the homomorphism densities satisfy t(H, G) ≥ t(K_2, G)^{e(H)}; more generally t(H, W) ≥ (∫W)^{e(H)} for every graphon W. In probabilistic form: if the vertices of H are mapped independently and uniformly at random to vertices of G, the probability that every edge of H lands on an edge of G is at least p^{e(H)}, where p = 2e(G)/|V(G)|² is the edge density of G.
statement_caveat: Bipartiteness is necessary: an odd cycle has density 0 in a bipartite G of positive edge density. Sidorenko stated the conjecture as a correlation inequality for integrals of products of a nonnegative kernel along the edges of H; Erdős and Simonovits made an equivalent conjecture in graph language [verify].
source: A. F. Sidorenko, A correlation inequality for bipartite graphs, Graphs Combin. 9 (1993) 201–204 [verify]; M. Simonovits, Extremal graph problems, degenerate extremal problems, and supersaturated graphs, in Progress in Graph Theory, Academic Press (1984) [verify]
why_important: It says that among all graphs of a given edge density the random graph has the fewest copies of every bipartite graph, a correlation inequality for products of a kernel along the edges of a bipartite graph. Its strengthening, the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma, would characterise quasirandom graphs by the count of any bipartite graph with a cycle [verify]; it is a central question about extremal problems for graph limits.
where_it_stands: Proved for trees and even cycles, complete bipartite graphs, hypercubes (Hatami 2010), bipartite graphs with a vertex joined to every vertex of the other side (Conlon–Fox–Sudakov 2010), and wider classes closed under certain gluing operations (Szegedy; Kim–Lee–Lee 2016; Conlon–Kim–Lee–Lee 2018) [verify]. The smallest open case is usually given as K_{5,5} with a Hamiltonian cycle removed [verify]. Zhao (arXiv:2606.23018, arXiv:2607.02260, 2026) proves the inequality for special classes of host kernels, such as two-sided correlation kernels on finite groups. Open.

title: Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: If F is a finite family of subsets of a finite set, closed under unions and containing a nonempty set, then some element belongs to at least half of the members of F. Equivalently, if A is a uniformly random member of F, then P(x ∈ A) ≥ 1/2 for some element x.
statement_caveat: The power set shows that 1/2 cannot be improved. Since 2022 the probabilistic form has been attacked with entropy inequalities for two independent random members of F.
source: Usually attributed to P. Frankl (1979); stated in print in I. Rival (ed.), Graphs and Order, Reidel (1985) [verify]; survey: H. Bruhn and O. Schaudt, The journey of the union-closed sets conjecture, Graphs Combin. 31 (2015) 2043–2074 [verify]
why_important: It is one of the best-known elementary questions in combinatorics, and Gilmer's entropy argument turned it into a question about entropy and couplings of random sets; the best constants now come from information inequalities, and the gap between them and 1/2 measures how far those methods reach.
where_it_stands: Gilmer (arXiv:2211.09055, 2022) proved that some element lies in at least a 0.01 fraction of the members, by an entropy argument; Alweiss–Huang–Sellke, Chase–Lovett and Sawin raised the fraction to (3 − √5)/2 ≈ 0.382 [verify], and later work went slightly beyond. The best bound is now about 0.38289 (Jiang, arXiv:2609.08291, computer-assisted; Costa–Sadhu, arXiv:2610.02295, 0.3828852549…). The conjecture is known for small ground sets and small families, and for families containing at least two thirds of all subsets of the ground set (Balla–Bollobás–Eccles 2013) [verify]. Open.

title: The asymptotics of the Ramsey number R(3,k)
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: The Ramsey number R(3,k), the least n such that every graph on n vertices contains a triangle or an independent set of k vertices, satisfies R(3,k) = (1/2 + o(1)) k²/log k as k → ∞.
statement_caveat: Erdős asked for an asymptotic formula for R(3,k). The bounds are now (1/2 + o(1)) k²/log k ≤ R(3,k) ≤ (1 + o(1)) k²/log k, so the question is the constant. The constant 1/2 was conjectured by Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe and is recorded as Conjecture 1.1 by Hefty, Horn, King and Pfender; an earlier conjecture that the triangle-free process is optimal, with constant 1/4, was disproved in 2025.
source: P. Erdős, Erdős problem #165 (erdosproblems.com/165) [verify]; J. H. Kim, The Ramsey number R(3,t) has order of magnitude t²/log t, Random Structures Algorithms 7 (1995) 173–207; R. Hefty, P. Horn, D. King and F. Pfender, arXiv:2510.19718 (2025)
locator: Hefty–Horn–King–Pfender, arXiv:2510.19718, Conjecture 1.1 (the constant 1/2) and Theorem 1.2 (the lower bound)
why_important: R(3,k) is the founding example of the probabilistic method in Ramsey theory: its lower bounds come from random greedy processes (the semi-random nibble and the triangle-free process) and its upper bound from Shearer's bound on the independence number of triangle-free graphs. Matching the constants would show which random construction is optimal.
where_it_stands: Order of magnitude: Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi (1980) above and Kim (1995) below. Shearer (1983) gives the upper constant 1. Bohman–Keevash and Fiz Pontiveros–Griffiths–Morris (2013) gave the lower constant 1/4 through the triangle-free process; Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe (arXiv:2505.13371, 2025) gave 1/3, disproving the conjecture that 1/4 is the truth; Hefty, Horn, King and Pfender (arXiv:2510.19718, 2025) gave 1/2. The constant is open.

title: Temperature chaos in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the SK model H_N(σ) = N^{−1/2} Σ_{i<j} g_ij σ_i σ_j with iid standard Gaussian couplings and no external field, fix 1 < β < β′. Sample σ from the Gibbs measure at inverse temperature β and τ independently from the Gibbs measure at β′, both with the same couplings. Then the overlap R(σ, τ) = N^{−1} Σ_i σ_i τ_i tends to 0 in probability as N → ∞.
statement_caveat: With an external field h ≠ 0 the overlap should concentrate at a constant depending on β and β′ instead. Physics predicts that temperature chaos in the SK model is very weak, appearing only at high order in perturbation theory (Rizzo–Crisanti 2003) [verify]; the proofs so far use the extra structure of models with many p-spin terms.
source: A. J. Bray and M. A. Moore, Chaotic nature of the spin-glass phase, Phys. Rev. Lett. 58 (1987) 57–60 [verify]; D. Panchenko, Chaos in temperature in generic 2p-spin models, Comm. Math. Phys. 346 (2016), arXiv:1502.03801
why_important: Chaos, the extreme sensitivity of the low-temperature Gibbs measure to small changes of the parameters, is a defining feature of the spin-glass phase in the Parisi picture and is invoked to explain rejuvenation and memory in experiments; for temperature it means that the pure states at two different low temperatures are unrelated.
where_it_stands: Proved (claimed): Aronow and Lopatto (arXiv:2609.17442, September 2026), in identifying the limiting overlap structure of mixed even p-spin models, prove temperature chaos for the zero-field SK model at every pair of distinct nonnegative inverse temperatures (abstract read 14 Oct; the SK case is Corollary 9.2). Before that: disorder chaos was proved for the SK model, without an external field (Chatterjee 2009) and with one (Chen 2013) [verify]; temperature chaos was proved for generic mixed even p-spin models that contain sufficiently many p-spin terms (Panchenko, arXiv:1502.03801) and for some spherical mixed models (Chen–Panchenko, arXiv:1608.02478), and it fails for spherical pure p-spin models with p ≥ 3 (Ben Arous–Subag–Zeitouni, arXiv:1804.10573).
retired_reason: SOLVED: Aronow and Lopatto (arXiv:2609.17442, 15 Sep 2026) prove temperature chaos for the zero-field SK model at every pair of distinct nonnegative inverse temperatures (abstract read 14 Oct; w673 opened Corollary 9.2). A preprint claim, not independently checked.

title: Zamolodchikov's E8 particle spectrum for the critical Ising model in a magnetic field
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: Take the nearest-neighbour Ising model on aZ² at its critical temperature with external field h a^{15/8}, h > 0, and let a → 0. The massive field theory obtained in the limit has eight particles, with masses proportional to the components of the positive (Perron–Frobenius) eigenvector of the adjacency matrix of the E8 Dynkin diagram, equivalently the eigenvector of the E8 Cartan matrix for its smallest eigenvalue; in particular m_2/m_1 = 2 cos(π/5), the golden ratio, and three of the eight masses lie below the two-particle threshold 2m_1.
statement_caveat: In probabilistic terms the masses are exponential decay rates of truncated correlations of the scaling limit Φ^h of the magnetization field, and the statement concerns the spectrum of the relativistic quantum field theory reconstructed from Φ^h (Osterwalder–Schrader); Camia, Jiang and Newman describe the masses through a stationary Gaussian process built from Φ^h. In the form they pose it, the truncated two-point function of Φ^h along a line decays as a sum of three exponentials with rates m_1, m_2, m_3 below the threshold 2m_1, with the E8 ratios, plus a continuum; a positive mass gap alone does not give even the first isolated mass.
source: A. B. Zamolodchikov, Integrals of motion and S-matrix of the (scaled) T = T_c Ising model with magnetic field, Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 4 (1989) 4235–4248 [verify]; F. Camia, J. Jiang and C. M. Newman, The Gaussian process for particle masses in the near-critical Ising model, arXiv:2111.05134 (2021)
locator: Camia–Jiang–Newman, arXiv:2111.05134, Section 1.2, equation (3)
why_important: It is the most celebrated prediction of integrable field theory for a lattice model of probability: a hidden E8 structure in the simplest perturbation of the critical Ising model, with the golden ratio as a mass ratio, later seen in neutron scattering on cobalt niobate (Coldea et al., Science 327 (2010)). A proof would derive an interacting massive particle spectrum from a lattice model.
where_it_stands: The scaling limits of the critical magnetization field and of the near-critical model in a field exist (Camia–Garban–Newman 2015, 2016) [verify]; the near-critical limit has exponentially decaying correlations, so a positive lowest mass (Camia–Jiang–Newman, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 2020) [verify]; and the masses are tied to a Gaussian process recovered from the lattice magnetization along a line (Camia–Jiang–Newman, arXiv:2111.05134). A second particle, the mass ratios and the E8 structure are open.

title: Spectral gap for random walks on SU(2) (Gamburd–Jakobson–Sarnak)
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: For every n ≥ 2 and Haar-almost every n-tuple (g_1, …, g_n) in SU(2), the averaging operator T f(x) = (2n)^{−1} Σ_i (f(g_i x) + f(g_i^{−1} x)) on L²(SU(2)) has norm strictly less than 1 on the functions of mean zero. Equivalently, for every f in L²(SU(2)) the averages T^k f converge to the Haar mean of f exponentially fast in L²; the law of the walk at time k is atomic, so the equidistribution is in this weak sense, not in total variation.
statement_caveat: The stronger statement, that every finite symmetric set generating a dense subgroup of SU(2) has a spectral gap, is also open [verify attribution]. Density is needed: a set generating a finite group has no gap.
source: A. Gamburd, D. Jakobson and P. Sarnak, Spectra of elements in the group ring of SU(2), J. Eur. Math. Soc. 1 (1999) 51–85
