Other self-similar sets (rational product Cantor sets, the Sierpinski gasket) raise the same question.
source: F. Nazarov, Y. Peres and A. Volberg, The power law for the Buffon needle probability of the four-corner Cantor set, Algebra i Analiz 22 (2010) 82–97 [verify]
locator: Nazarov–Peres–Volberg, arXiv:0801.2942, abstract: 'A classical theorem of Besicovitch implies that the Favard length of K_n tends to zero. It is still an open problem to determine its exact rate of decay.' Introduction: 'A lower bound Fav(K_n) ≥ c/n for some c > 0 follows from Mattila [8, 1.4].' and, after Theorem 1, 'a bound decaying faster than O(n^{−1/4}) would require new ideas.'
why_important: The four-corner Cantor set is the canonical purely unrectifiable set, and the decay of its Favard length is the model problem for making Besicovitch's projection theorem quantitative. The question links harmonic analysis (zeros of trigonometric mask polynomials), additive combinatorics and geometric measure theory, and it is closely tied to analytic capacity and Vitushkin's conjecture.
where_it_stands: Peres and Solomyak proved Fav(K_n) ≤ C exp(−a log* n). Nazarov, Peres and Volberg (arXiv:0801.2942) proved Fav(K_n) ≤ C n^{−1/6+δ}. Bateman and Volberg improved the lower bound to c log n / n [verify]. Łaba and Zhai (arXiv:0902.0964), Bond, Łaba and Volberg (arXiv:1109.1031) and Łaba and Marshall (arXiv:2202.07555) extended power-law bounds to rational product Cantor sets, and Marshall (arXiv:2509.02882) obtained N^{−1/5+u} for the four-corner set. Random variants have exact rates (arXiv:2609.33557). The gap between log n / n and n^{−1/5} remains. Open.
note: Fame: a well-known problem in geometric measure theory, posed explicitly by Nazarov, Peres and Volberg and the subject of a sustained line of work.

title: Sarnak's Möbius disjointness conjecture
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: Let μ be the Möbius function. Sarnak conjectured that for every continuous map T of a compact metric space X with zero topological entropy, every f ∈ C(X) and every x ∈ X, (1/N) Σ_{n ≤ N} f(T^n x) μ(n) → 0 as N → ∞.
statement_caveat: The conjecture is implied by Chowla's conjecture on the vanishing of correlations of the Möbius (or Liouville) function, open since 1965. Tao showed that the logarithmically averaged versions of the two conjectures are equivalent. Zero entropy is necessary in general, since μ² itself is a point of a positive-entropy system. Compare T029 (Furstenberg's ×2 ×3 conjecture), a different rigidity question in the same area.
source: P. Sarnak, Three lectures on the Möbius function, randomness and dynamics (2010); status as in S. Ferenczi, J. Kułaga-Przymus and M. Lemańczyk, Sarnak's conjecture: what's new, in Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems in their Interactions with Arithmetics and Combinatorics, Lecture Notes in Math. 2213 (2018) 163–235 [verify]
locator: Ferenczi–Kułaga-Przymus–Lemańczyk, arXiv:1710.04039, Introduction: 'In 2010, Sarnak [148, 149] formulated the following conjecture: (2) Each zero entropy continuous map T of a compact metric space X is Möbius disjoint.' and 'Chowla conjecture ⇒ Sarnak's conjecture'.
why_important: The conjecture expresses the principle that the Möbius function does not correlate with any deterministic sequence, which is the form of randomness of the primes needed in many problems of analytic number theory. It has organised a large body of work joining ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis and multiplicative number theory since 2010.
where_it_stands: Möbius disjointness is known for many classes: rotations (Davenport), nilsystems (Green–Tao), horocycle flows (Bourgain–Sarnak–Ziegler), and various classes of interval exchange transformations and rank-one systems surveyed in arXiv:1710.04039 [verify each attribution]. Matomäki and Radziwiłł's theorem on multiplicative functions in short intervals gave the averaged form of two-point Chowla (Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao); Tao proved the logarithmic two-point Chowla conjecture and the equivalence of logarithmic Chowla and logarithmic Sarnak; Tao and Teräväinen proved logarithmic Chowla for odd order; Frantzikinakis and Host proved the logarithmic Sarnak conjecture for zero-entropy systems with countably many ergodic invariant measures [verify]. The conjecture in its original Cesàro form remains open in general. Open.
note: Fame: one of the central conjectures linking dynamics and number theory.

title: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: Assume the Riemann hypothesis and write the nontrivial zeros as 1/2 + iγ. Montgomery conjectured that for fixed 0 < a < b, #{(γ, γ′): 0 < γ, γ′ ≤ T, 2πa/log T ≤ γ − γ′ ≤ 2πb/log T} ~ (T log T / 2π) ∫_a^b (1 − (sin πu/πu)²) du as T → ∞, equivalently that his function F(α) equals 1 for all |α| ≥ 1. This is the pair correlation of the eigenvalues of large random matrices from the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble.
statement_caveat: Montgomery proved, under the Riemann hypothesis, that F(α) = |α| + T^{−2|α|} log T (1 + o(1)) for |α| ≤ 1, which determines the pair correlation against test functions with Fourier transform supported in (−1, 1); the conjecture is the extension to all α. Gallagher and Mueller showed that the conjecture implies that almost all zeros are simple. Compare T107 (the Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture), T089 (Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit) and T105 (Berry–Tabor), which concern other random-matrix predictions; T184 concerns moments of zeta.
source: H. L. Montgomery, The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function, in Analytic Number Theory, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 24, Amer. Math. Soc. (1973) 181–193
locator: Goldston–Lee–Schettler–Suriajaya, arXiv:2503.15449, abstract: 'Montgomery in 1973 introduced the Pair Correlation Conjecture (PCC) for zeros of the Riemann zeta-function. He also conjectured that asymptotically 100% of the zeros are simple.'
why_important: The conjecture is the original link between the zeros of the zeta function and random matrix theory, and the agreement with GUE statistics found numerically by Odlyzko is one of the most striking pieces of evidence for the Hilbert–Pólya philosophy. It is equivalent, through Goldston and Montgomery, to an asymptotic for the variance of primes in short intervals.
where_it_stands: Montgomery (1973) proved the conjecture for test functions with Fourier support in (−1, 1) under the Riemann hypothesis. Rudnick and Sarnak (Duke Math. J. 81 (1996)) proved the analogous result for all n-level correlations with restricted support; Goldston and Montgomery related the conjecture to primes in short intervals; Odlyzko's computations of zeros near the 10^20-th and later zeros agree closely with the GUE prediction [verify]. Goldston, Lee, Schettler and Suriajaya (arXiv:2503.15449) showed that the conjecture implies that almost all zeros are simple and on the critical line. No extension of the support beyond (−1, 1) is known. Open.
note: Fame: one of the best-known conjectures in analytic number theory and the founding conjecture of the random-matrix model of L-functions.

title: The Keating–Snaith conjecture for the moments of the Riemann zeta function
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For k > −1/2, Keating and Snaith conjectured that (1/T) ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2 + it)|^{2k} dt ~ a_k g_k/Γ(k² + 1) (log T)^{k²} as T → ∞, where a_k is the arithmetic factor Π_p (1 − 1/p)^{k²} Σ_{m≥0} (Γ(m + k)/(m! Γ(k)))² p^{−m} and g_k/Γ(k² + 1) = G(k + 1)²/G(2k + 1), with G the Barnes G-function. The constant is obtained from the moments of characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices.
statement_caveat: The cases k = 1 (Hardy–Littlewood) and k = 2 (Ingham) are classical; the conjectured constants for k = 3 (g_3 = 42, Conrey–Ghosh) and k = 4 (g_4 = 24024, Conrey–Gonek) predate the random-matrix derivation, which gave the constant for all k. The conjecture is open for every k other than 1 and 2, already for k = 3. The lower-order terms are predicted by the recipe of Conrey, Farmer, Keating, Rubinstein and Snaith. Compare T183 (pair correlation) and T107 (the maximum of zeta on short intervals).
source: J. P. Keating and N. C. Snaith, Random matrix theory and ζ(1/2 + it), Comm. Math. Phys. 214 (2000) 57–89
locator: Bui–Gonek–Milinovich, arXiv:1302.5032, abstract: 'Keating and Snaith modeled the Riemann zeta-function ζ(s) by characteristic polynomials of random NxN unitary matrices, and used this to conjecture the asymptotic main term for the 2k-th moment of ζ(1/2+it) when k>-1/2.'
why_important: The moments of the zeta function on the critical line are a classical object of analytic number theory, and the Keating–Snaith formula was the first derivation of the leading constant for all k, using a probabilistic model rather than number theory. It made the moments of characteristic polynomials of random matrices a standard tool and connected the problem to log-correlated fields and Gaussian multiplicative chaos.
where_it_stands: The order of magnitude (log T)^{k²} is known in several ranges: Radziwiłł and Soundararajan, and Heap and Soundararajan, proved matching lower bounds for all k > 0; under the Riemann hypothesis Harper proved the sharp upper bound for all k > 0; unconditionally Heap, Radziwiłł and Soundararajan proved the sharp upper bound for 0 ≤ k ≤ 1 [verify each range]. The asymptotic with the conjectured constant is known only for k = 1 and k = 2 (with lower-order terms for k = 2). Moments of moments over short intervals were studied by Bailey and Keating (arXiv:2006.04503). Open.
note: Fame: a central conjecture of analytic number theory and the best-known application of random matrix theory to L-functions.

title: Stability of α-fair bandwidth sharing networks with general file-size distributions
domain_name: Queueing and stochastic networks
statement: In the connection-level model of Massoulié and Roberts, flows on each route arrive as a Poisson (or renewal) process and bring a random amount of work with a general distribution, and the link capacities are shared among the flows present according to the weighted α-fair allocation. Prove that whenever the network is subcritical (the offered load on every link is below its capacity) the process describing the flows and their residual work is positive recurrent.
statement_caveat: For exponential file sizes the number of flows per route is a Markov chain and stability under α-fair policies for all α > 0 is known (de Veciana–Lee–Konstantopoulos, Bonald–Massoulié). For general file sizes the state must include residual work, and the Markov-chain arguments for the exponential case do not transfer. A standard route is to prove stability of the fluid model and then deduce stability of the stochastic model; Fu and Williams treat the first step.
source: M. Bramson, Network stability under max–min fair bandwidth sharing, Ann. Appl. Probab. 20 (2010) 1126–1176; status as in Y. Fu and R. J. Williams, Stability of a subcritical fluid model for fair bandwidth sharing with general file size distributions, Stoch. Syst. 10 (2020) 251–273
locator: Fu–Williams, Stoch. Syst. 10 (2020) 251–273, doi:10.1287/stsy.2019.0058, abstract: 'Since the year 2000, it has been a standing problem to prove stability of the data communications network model of Massoulié and Roberts [...], with general file sizes and operating under fair bandwidth sharing policies, when the offered load is less than capacity (subcritical conditions). A crucial step in an approach to this problem is to prove stability of subcritical fluid model solutions.'
why_important: Bandwidth sharing networks are the standard flow-level model of Internet congestion control, and the α-fair family contains proportional fairness and TCP-like allocations. Stability under general file sizes is the basic sanity property of such a protocol, and it is a test case for the fluid-model method of proving positive recurrence in networks where the state includes residual service times.
where_it_stands: Bramson (arXiv:1010.3142) proved stability of weighted max–min fair sharing for general interarrival and service distributions with 2 + δ moments. Massoulié (arXiv:0707.4542) treated proportional fairness with exponential-type assumptions [verify the scope]. Gromoll and Williams (Ann. Appl. Probab. 2009) established fluid limits. Paganini, Tang, Ferragut and Andrew (IEEE Trans. Automat. Control 57 (2012) 579–591) gave a Lyapunov function for the fluid model under smoothness assumptions, and Fu and Williams proved stability of subcritical fluid model solutions for general file sizes. Positive recurrence of the stochastic model for α-fair policies with general file sizes has not been established [verify whether later work completed this step]. Open.
note: Fame borderline (my judgment): a recognised standing problem in stochastic networks since 2000; known mainly within applied probability and networking.

title: A scaling limit for the circumference of G(n, c/n) for every c > 1
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: Let L_n(c) be the length of the longest cycle (the circumference) of the Erdős–Rényi graph G(n, c/n). Prove that for every c > 1 there is a constant f(c) such that L_n(c)/n → f(c) in probability (or almost surely) as n → ∞.
statement_caveat: The existence of cycles of linear length for every c > 1, conjectured by Erdős, was proved by Ajtai, Komlós and Szemerédi and independently by Fernandez de la Vega. Subadditivity arguments do not apply directly, so even the existence of the limit is nontrivial. In the weakly supercritical regime c = 1 + ε the best bounds are 1.581ε² ≤ ℓ_min(1 + ε) ≤ 1.7395ε² (Anastos; Kemkes–Wormald), so the asymptotic constant of the circumference near criticality is also unknown. For large c the longest path has the same first-order limit (Anastos–Frieze).
source: M. Anastos and A. Frieze, A scaling limit for the length of the longest cycle in a sparse random graph, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 148 (2021) 184–208 [verify]; status as in M. Anastos, J. Erde, M. Kang and V. Pfenninger, arXiv:2503.14336
locator: Anastos–Erde–Kang–Pfenninger, arXiv:2503.14336, Section 1: 'the bound on c in Theorem 1.1 was not made explicit, but parts of the arguments require that c ≥ 10^6. However, the result was later shown to hold for all c ≥ 20 by the first author [3, Theorem 1].' Section 8: 'whilst the distribution of the circumference of a sparse random graph G(n, c/n) is well understood now when c is large, there is still a large gap in our knowledge for smaller c, where even a scaling limit has not yet been established.'
why_important: The circumference is one of the basic global parameters of the sparse random graph, and the problem goes back to Erdős's question about long cycles. Unlike the giant component or the k-core, it has no known local description for small c, so a scaling limit would require new structural understanding of the giant component just above criticality.
where_it_stands: Ajtai, Komlós and Szemerédi proved L_n(c) ≥ ℓ(c)n w.h.p. for every c > 1. Frieze determined 1 − ℓ_min(c) up to a factor 1 + o_c(1) as c → ∞. Anastos and Frieze (arXiv:1907.03657) proved that L_n(c)/n → f(c) almost surely for sufficiently large c, with f computable to any precision; Anastos (arXiv:2105.13828) extended this to c ≥ 20; Anastos, Erde, Kang and Pfenninger (arXiv:2503.14336) proved a central limit theorem for c ≥ 20. Below c = 20, and in particular below the threshold for the strong 4-core (numerically c* ≈ 9.2), no scaling limit is known. Open.
note: Fame borderline (my judgment): a natural open question about the most studied random graph model, stated by the authors working on it; known to random-graph specialists.

title: Quantum unique ergodicity on negatively curved manifolds (Rudnick–Sarnak)
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: Let (M, g) be a compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary and with negative sectional curvature, and let (u_n) be any orthonormal basis of L²(M) consisting of Laplace eigenfunctions, −Δu_n = λ_n u_n with λ_n → ∞. Rudnick and Sarnak conjecture that the whole sequence equidistributes: the only semiclassical measure is the Liouville measure on the unit cosphere bundle S*M, and in particular the probability measures |u_n(x)|² dvol(x) converge weakly to the normalised Riemannian volume.
statement_caveat: Quantum ergodicity (Shnirelman, Zelditch, Colin de Verdière) gives the same conclusion along a density-one subsequence for any manifold with ergodic geodesic flow; the conjecture says there are no exceptional subsequences when the flow is Anosov. Ergodicity of the flow alone is not enough: Hassell (Ann. of Math. 171 (2010)) showed that generic Bunimovich stadia are not quantum uniquely ergodic. Compare T054 (the analogue for eigenvectors of random regular graphs) and T106 (Berry's random-wave model for the same eigenfunctions).
source: Z. Rudnick and P. Sarnak, The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds, Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994) 195–213
locator: S. Nonnenmacher, Quantum ergodicity and semiclassical measures: mathematical results, arXiv:2606.12098, Section 4: 'In 1994, Rudnick and Sarnak stated a conjecture specific to the manifolds of negative curvature (on which the geodesic flow is Anosov). Conjecture 1 (Quantum Unique Ergodicity). Take (M, g) a compact manifold of negative curvature (without boundary). Then there exist no exceptional eigemodes of the Laplacian ... In other words, for these manifolds there exists a unique semiclassical measure, which is the Liouville measure'; Section 4.1: 'The conjecture remains open, even in the case of manifolds of constant negative curvature.'
why_important: QUE is the sharpest form of the correspondence between classical chaos and the high-energy behaviour of quantum states, and it is the template for delocalisation questions about eigenvectors throughout random matrix theory and spectral graph theory. The partial results have required new ideas from measure rigidity, entropy theory and harmonic analysis.
where_it_stands: For joint eigenfunctions of the Laplacian and the Hecke operators on arithmetic surfaces, Lindenstrauss (Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 165–219) proved arithmetic QUE, completed for the modular surface by Soundararajan's escape-of-mass bound (Ann. of Math. 172 (2010)); Brooks and Lindenstrauss (Invent. Math. 2014) need only one Hecke operator [verify]. Without arithmetic structure, Anantharaman (Ann. of Math. 168 (2008)) showed every semiclassical measure has positive entropy, Anantharaman and Nonnenmacher (math-ph/0610019) at least half the maximal entropy in constant curvature, Dyatlov and Jin (arXiv:1705.05019) that semiclassical measures on hyperbolic surfaces have full support, and Dyatlov, Jin and Nonnenmacher (arXiv:1906.08923) the same for surfaces of variable negative curvature. Uniqueness of the semiclassical measure is not known for any compact negatively curved manifold without arithmetic symmetry. Open.
note: Fame: among the best-known problems of mathematical physics and spectral geometry; Lindenstrauss's Fields Medal citation names arithmetic QUE.

title: Irreducibility of random 0–1 polynomials (Odlyzko–Poonen)
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Let P_d(x) = x^d + A_{d−1}x^{d−1} + ⋯ + A_1 x + 1, where A_1, …, A_{d−1} are independent and uniform on {0, 1}. Odlyzko and Poonen conjectured that P(P_d is irreducible in Z[x]) → 1 as d → ∞.
statement_caveat: The same question is asked for other coefficient laws, for instance independent uniform coefficients in {−1, 1} or in a fixed finite set, and is usually strengthened to the statement that the Galois group is the full symmetric group with probability tending to one. A related problem is van der Waerden's conjecture on the Galois groups of polynomials with coefficients in a growing box (Anderson, Chow, Dietmann and Hokken, arXiv:2608.22297), where the degree is fixed and the height grows; here the height is fixed and the degree grows.
source: A. M. Odlyzko and B. Poonen, Zeros of polynomials with 0,1 coefficients, Enseign. Math. (2) 39 (1993) 317–348
locator: E. Breuillard and P. P. Varjú, Irreducibility of random polynomials of large degree, arXiv:1810.13360, Section 1: 'Let P(x) = x^d + A_{d−1}x^{d−1} + ... + A_1x + 1 ∈ Z[x] be a random polynomial with independent coefficients A_1, ..., A_{d−1} taking values in 0 and 1 with equal probability. Odlyzko and Poonen [31] conjectured that the probability that P is irreducible in Z[x] converges to 1 as d → ∞. The best known lower bound in this problem is due to Konyagin [26] who proved that P(P is irreducible) > c/log d'.
why_important: The problem asks whether algebraic structure in a random object of large size is as rare as it looks, and its solution seems to need probabilistic input (equidistribution of random walks modulo primes) and arithmetic input at the same time. It has become a test case for combining random walks on finite fields with sieve methods.
where_it_stands: Konyagin (Acta Arith. 88 (1999) 333–350) proved a lower bound c/log d. Breuillard and Varjú (arXiv:1810.13360, Acta Math. 2019 [verify]) proved the conjecture, with Galois group containing A_d, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions. Unconditionally, Bary-Soroker and Kozma (arXiv:1710.05165) proved irreducibility with probability tending to one for coefficients uniform on {1, …, L} for suitable L such as 210, and Bary-Soroker, Koukoulopoulos and Kozma (arXiv:2007.14567) for coefficients uniform on at least 35 consecutive integers, together with a positive lower bound for any arithmetic progression of at least two terms. Klurman and Matei (arXiv:2511.10359) treat random multiplicative signs. The 0–1 case itself is proved only under GRH. Open.
note: Fame borderline (my judgment): well known in probabilistic number theory and among probabilists working on random polynomials; the GRH-conditional solution and the unconditional large-alphabet results are recent and widely cited.

title: An FPRAS for counting perfect matchings in general graphs
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Is there a fully polynomial randomised approximation scheme for the number of perfect matchings of an arbitrary finite graph? Equivalently, given a graph G on n vertices and ε > 0, can one output with probability at least 3/4 a number within a factor 1 ± ε of the number of perfect matchings of G in time polynomial in n and 1/ε, without assuming G bipartite?
statement_caveat: For bipartite graphs this is the permanent of a 0–1 matrix, solved by Jerrum, Sinclair and Vigoda; for planar graphs the count is exact in polynomial time by Kasteleyn's Pfaffian method. Exact counting is #P-complete (Valiant 1979). The problem is the main open case of the Markov chain Monte Carlo programme for matchings.
source: M. Jerrum, A. Sinclair and E. Vigoda, A polynomial-time approximation algorithm for the permanent of a matrix with nonnegative entries, J. ACM 51 (2004) 671–697
locator: D. Štefankovič, E. Vigoda and J. Wilmes, On counting perfect matchings in general graphs, arXiv:1712.07504, abstract: 'it has remained an open question whether there exists an FPRAS for counting perfect matchings in general graphs. In fact, it was unresolved whether the same Markov chain defined by JSV is rapidly mixing in general. In this paper, we show that it is not.'
why_important: Approximate counting of perfect matchings is the problem that created the canonical-path and Markov-chain technology of the 1980s, and the bipartite solution is one of the landmark results of the area. Whether non-bipartite graphs are equally tractable decides whether the Gallai–Edmonds structure of factor-critical subgraphs is a genuine obstruction to rapid mixing or only to current proofs.
where_it_stands: Jerrum and Sinclair handled graphs whose ratio of near-perfect to perfect matchings is polynomially bounded, including dense graphs. Štefankovič, Vigoda and Wilmes (arXiv:1712.07504) proved torpid mixing of the Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda chain on general graphs for every weighting of hole patterns and gave an FPRAS for graphs close to bipartite, fixed-parameter in the largest order of a factor-critical subgraph. Alimohammadi, Anari, Shiragur and Vuong (arXiv:2102.02708) count matchings of given size in planar graphs via fractional log-concavity. For the permanent, Chen, Vigoda and Yang (arXiv:2608.26599) give a faster FPRAS. No FPRAS and no hardness result is known for general graphs. Open.
note: Fame: a standard open problem in the theory of approximate counting and Markov chain Monte Carlo, listed alongside #BIS (T195) in surveys of the area.

title: Anomalous dissipation for stationary solutions of the stochastically forced 3D Navier–Stokes equations
domain_name: Brownian motion, stochastic analysis and SPDE
statement: Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on T³ with viscosity ν and additive Gaussian forcing, white in time and smooth in space, with energy input ε fixed. Show that there exist statistically stationary martingale solutions u^ν with lim_{ν→0} ν E‖u^ν‖²_{L²} = 0 (weak anomalous dissipation, WAD); Bedrossian, Coti Zelati, Punshon-Smith and Weber conjecture that WAD holds whenever the forcing satisfies a suitable Hörmander bracket condition.
statement_caveat: By the theorem of the same authors, WAD implies Kolmogorov's 4/5 law for the third-order longitudinal structure function, averaged over directions and over an inertial range; the row is therefore the open hypothesis under which the 4/5 law is a theorem. WAD fails for some degenerate forcings (a single forced mode gives an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck solution), so a non-degeneracy condition is needed. Distinct from T091 (uniqueness and regularity of the same equations).
source: J. Bedrossian, M. Coti Zelati, S. Punshon-Smith and F. Weber, A sufficient condition for the Kolmogorov 4/5 law for stationary martingale solutions to the 3D Navier–Stokes equations, Comm. Math. Phys. 367 (2019) 1045–1075 [verify], arXiv:1803.09695
locator: arXiv:1803.09695, Definition 1.1: 'We say that a sequence {u}ν>0 of stationary martingale solutions satisfies weak anomalous dissipation if lim_{ν→0} νE‖u‖²_{L²_x} = 0. (WAD)'; Remark 1.6: 'It is an open problem to prove existence of solutions satisfying (WAD) ... It is natural to conjecture that (WAD) holds whenever the stochastic forcing satisfies some suitable Hörmander bracket condition'; list of open problems: 'By far, the most important question is the existence of suitable stationary martingale solutions that satisfy (WAD) (at least).'
why_important: Anomalous dissipation is the founding assumption of Kolmogorov's theory of turbulence, and the 4/5 law is the only exact result that theory predicts. A proof of WAD for randomly forced Navier–Stokes would give the first derivation of the 4/5 law from the equations for a natural class of flows.
where_it_stands: Onsager's conjecture on energy conservation for Euler is resolved (Isett; Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol), and Bruè, Colombo, Crippa and De Lellis (arXiv:2212.08413) construct deterministic forcings for which forced 3D Navier–Stokes solutions dissipate anomalously, with Onsager-critical bounds. For stochastic forcing, the 4/5 law is proved conditionally on WAD (arXiv:1803.09695); the analogous laws are proved for passive scalars advected by stochastic Navier–Stokes (Bedrossian, Blumenthal and Punshon-Smith) and for stochastic Burgers (Gao and Kuksin, arXiv:2209.14288 [verify]), and Hofmanová, Pappalettera, Zhu and Zhu (arXiv:2305.08090) obtain anomalous dissipation of a passive scalar. WAD itself has not been established for any non-degenerate stochastic forcing. Open.
note: Fame borderline (my judgment): the precise WAD formulation is recent, but it is the rigorous form of anomalous dissipation, which is the central unproved hypothesis of turbulence theory.

title: Polynomial diameter of every Cayley graph of the symmetric group (Babai's conjecture)
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Show that there is an absolute constant C such that for every n and every generating set A of the symmetric group Sym(n) or the alternating group Alt(n), every element is a product of at most n^C elements of A ∪ A^{−1}; that is, the diameter of every connected Cayley graph of these groups is polynomial in n. This is the case of Babai's conjecture that diam Cay(G, A) ≤ (log |G|)^C for every non-abelian finite simple group G.
statement_caveat: By standard comparison arguments a polynomial diameter bound gives a polynomial bound on the mixing time of the lazy random walk on every Cayley graph of Sym(n) up to a factor depending on |A|, which is how the problem enters random walks on groups. Compare T085 (random Cayley graphs of Sym(n) are expanders) and T124 (uniform expansion of SL_2(F_p)), which ask for spectral gaps rather than diameters.
source: L. Babai and Á. Seress, On the diameter of permutation groups, European J. Combin. 13 (1992) 231–243 [verify]
locator: H. A. Helfgott and Á. Seress, On the diameter of permutation groups, arXiv:1109.3550, abstract: 'It has long been conjectured that the diameter of the symmetric group of degree n is polynomially bounded in n, but the best previously known upper bound was exponential in √(n log n). We give a quasipolynomial upper bound, namely, diam(G) = exp(O((log n)^4 log log n)) ... This addresses a key open case of Babai's conjecture on diameters of simple groups.'
why_important: The diameter of a Cayley graph governs how fast any generating set mixes the group, and the symmetric group is the case where character-theoretic tools give the least. For simple groups of Lie type of bounded rank the conjecture is a theorem (Helfgott; Breuillard, Green and Tao; Pyber and Szabó), so the symmetric and alternating groups are the main remaining family.
where_it_stands: Babai and Seress (1988) proved exp((1 + o(1))√(n log n)); Helfgott and Seress (Ann. of Math. 179 (2014) 611–658, arXiv:1109.3550) proved the quasipolynomial bound exp(O((log n)^4 log log n)). For two random generators the diameter is polynomial with high probability (Babai and Hetyei; Schlage-Puchta; Helfgott, Seress and Zuk give O(n²(log n)^c) [verify]). Keevash and Lifshitz (arXiv:2307.15030) obtain essentially sharp diameter estimates for generating sets of density at least exponential in −n. Computations of Chervov, Fedoriaka, Konstantinova and Naumov (arXiv:2509.19162) suggest that the largest diameters for two generators are of order n²/2. No polynomial bound is known for general generating sets. Open.
note: Fame: a central conjecture in the combinatorics of finite groups, with a long line of work by Babai, Seress, Helfgott and others; known well beyond group theory through its links with expansion and mixing.

title: Deterministic matrices with the restricted isometry property beyond the square-root bottleneck
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Construct, deterministically and in time polynomial in N, a family of m × N matrices Φ with N/m → ∞ that satisfy the restricted isometry property of order k with a fixed constant δ < 1 (that is, (1 − δ)‖x‖² ≤ ‖Φx‖² ≤ (1 + δ)‖x‖² for all k-sparse x) with k ≥ m^{1−o(1)}, as random Gaussian or Bernoulli matrices do with high probability for k of order m/log(N/m). Even k ≥ m^{1/2+γ} for a fixed γ that is not tiny is open.
statement_caveat: Coherence-based arguments, which bound inner products of pairs of columns, cannot give k beyond order √m: this is the square-root bottleneck. The problem is a derandomisation question for a high-dimensional probabilistic property, closely related to bounding clique numbers of Paley-type graphs; certifying RIP of a given matrix is NP-hard (Bandeira, Dobriban, Mixon and Sawin, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 59 (2013) [verify]).
source: J. Bourgain, S. Dilworth, K. Ford, S. Konyagin and D. Kutzarova, Explicit constructions of RIP matrices and related problems, Duke Math. J. 159 (2011) 145–185; T. Tao, Open question: deterministic UUP matrices, blog post, 2007 [verify]
locator: S. Satake and Y. Gu, On compressed sensing matrices breaking the square-root bottleneck, arXiv:2010.11179, abstract: 'One of challenging problems in compressed sensing is to construct deterministic matrices having restricted isometry property (RIP). So far, there are only a few publications providing deterministic RIP matrices beating the square-root bottleneck on the sparsity level.' Bandeira, Fickus, Mixon and Wong, arXiv:1202.1234, abstract: 'While random matrices are known to satisfy this property with high probability, deterministic constructions have found less success.'
why_important: The restricted isometry property is the standard sufficient condition for exact sparse recovery, and random matrices achieve the optimal sparsity level. Whether the same can be done without randomness is a clean test of how much of high-dimensional probability can be derandomised, and progress has required additive combinatorics.
where_it_stands: Bourgain, Dilworth, Ford, Konyagin and Kutzarova (Duke 2011) gave the only unconditional construction beating the bottleneck, with k = m^{1/2+ε_0} for a very small ε_0, later increased slightly by Mixon [verify]. Bandeira, Fickus, Mixon and Wong (arXiv:1202.1234) conjectured that Paley equiangular tight frames are RIP; Bandeira, Mixon and Moreira obtained a construction conditional on a clique-number bound for Paley graphs [verify], and Satake and Gu (arXiv:2010.11179) one conditional on the generalized Paley graph conjecture. No unconditional deterministic construction reaches k = m^{1/2+γ} for moderate γ. Open.
note: Fame borderline (my judgment): well known in compressed sensing, applied harmonic analysis and high-dimensional probability since Tao's 2007 formulation; less known in pure probability.

title: Exponential improvement of Minkowski's lower bound for sphere packing in high dimensions
domain_name: Stochastic and geometric probability
statement: Let Δ_d be the largest density of a packing of congruent balls in R^d. Is liminf_{d→∞} (1/d) log₂ Δ_d > −1, that is, can the lower bound Δ_d ≥ 2^{−d} (up to polynomial factors) of Minkowski and Hlawka be improved by an exponential factor? Torquato and Stillinger conjecture that disordered packings achieve Δ_d ≥ 2^{−(0.7786…+o(1))d}.
statement_caveat: The best upper bound is Kabatiansky and Levenshtein's Δ_d ≤ 2^{−(0.599…+o(1))d}, so the exponent of Δ_d is known only to lie in [0.599, 1]. All lower bounds come from probabilistic constructions: random lattices, random sequential addition, independent sets in random graphs and random ellipsoids. The analogous question for binary codes, whether the Gilbert–Varshamov bound is asymptotically tight, is also open.
source: S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density of sphere packings, Experiment. Math. 15 (2006) 307–331 [verify], arXiv:math/0508381
locator: Torquato and Stillinger, arXiv:math/0508381, abstract: 'Remarkably, no one has been able to provide exponential improvement on a 100-year-old lower bound on the maximal packing density due to Minkowski in d-dimensional Euclidean space ... we obtain a provisional lower bound on the density whose asymptotic behavior is controlled by 2^{−0.7786... d}, thus providing the putative exponential improvement of Minkowski's bound.'
why_important: Sphere packing in high dimension is the geometric counterpart of channel coding, and the exponential rate of the optimal density is unknown at both ends. The lower-bound side is a question about how well a random or random-greedy construction can be beaten, which is why probabilistic methods have produced every improvement since Rogers.
where_it_stands: Lower bounds have improved only by polynomial factors: Rogers (c d 2^{−d}), Ball, Vance, Venkatesh (an extra log log d along a sparse sequence of dimensions), Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe (arXiv:2312.10026, (1 − o(1)) d log d / 2^{d+1}), and Klartag (arXiv:2504.05042, a lattice packing of density c d² 2^{−d} from a stochastically evolving ellipsoid). Vanoni, Guo and Torquato (arXiv:2608.00920) show that, conditional on the Torquato–Stillinger realizability conjecture, hyperuniform pair correlations give rates down to 2^{−(0.6226…+o(1))d}, and that the unrestricted pair-correlation programme matches the Cohn–Elkies rate. No exponential improvement is proved. Open.
note: Fame: one of the oldest open problems in the geometry of numbers and discrete geometry, prominent in Conway and Sloane and in the recent literature on high-dimensional packings.

title: Fire lanes in the two-dimensional Drossel–Schwabl forest-fire process
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: In the Drossel–Schwabl forest-fire process on Z² (or on the triangular lattice), all sites are vacant at time 0, each vacant site becomes occupied at rate 1, each site is hit by lightning at rate ζ > 0, and a lightning strike burns its entire occupied cluster instantly. Let t_c be the time at which an infinite cluster would first appear without fires. Show that there is δ > 0 such that, as ζ → 0, the probability that the origin burns before time t_c + δ tends to zero, as van den Berg and Nolin proved for the volume-threshold version of the model and expect for the Drossel–Schwabl model.
statement_caveat: The Drossel–Schwabl model is the standard example of self-organised criticality, and physicists predicted that its ζ → 0 limit is critical at all large times; rigorous work suggests a more complicated picture, with recurrent near-critical and off-critical behaviour. Van den Berg and Brouwer (Comm. Math. Phys. 2006) asked whether the origin burns before t_c + δ; for the model with a volume threshold N in place of lightning the answer is negative because of the emergence of fire lanes. Compare T100 (avalanche exponents of the abelian sandpile), another self-organised critical model.
source: B. Drossel and F. Schwabl, Self-organized critical forest-fire model, Phys. Rev. Lett. 69 (1992) 1629–1632; J. van den Berg and R. Brouwer, Self-organized forest-fires near the critical time, Comm. Math. Phys. 267 (2006) 265–277 [verify]
locator: J. van den Berg and P. Nolin, A 2D forest fire process beyond the critical time, arXiv:2210.05642, abstract: 'we prove a somewhat counterintuitive result: there exists δ > 0 such that with high probability, the origin does not burn before time t_c + δ. This provides a negative answer to Open Problem 4.1 of van den Berg and Brouwer [Comm. Math. Phys., 2006] ... We expect that such a behavior also holds for the classical Drossel-Schwabl model.'
why_important: Forest fires are the model through which self-organised criticality entered probability, and the question of what the ζ → 0 limit looks like in two dimensions has resisted rigorous analysis since the 1990s. The fire-lane phenomenon contradicts the simplest physical picture, and proving it for the Drossel–Schwabl dynamics would settle the behaviour near the critical time.
where_it_stands: Kiss, Manolescu and Sidoravicius (Ann. Probab. 2015) analysed planar forest fires near the critical time; van den Berg, Kiss and Nolin proved deconcentration and mesoscopic clusters for volume-frozen percolation; van den Berg and Nolin (arXiv:2210.05642) proved the fire-lane statement for the volume-threshold model and (arXiv:2407.13652) studied fires ignited from the boundary. The infinite-volume Drossel–Schwabl process for fixed ζ exists (Dürre) [verify], but its ζ → 0 behaviour beyond the critical time is not understood. Open.
note: Fame borderline (my judgment): the forest-fire model is very well known in statistical physics, and the rigorous problem is a standard open question among specialists in planar percolation; the specific fire-lane formulation is recent.

title: The complexity of approximately counting independent sets in bipartite graphs (#BIS)
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Is there a fully polynomial randomised approximation scheme for the number of independent sets of a bipartite graph? Dyer, Goldberg, Greenhill and Jerrum conjectured that there is none, while #BIS is also not known to be as hard as approximately counting satisfying assignments of a Boolean formula (#SAT); the problem is to resolve its complexity in either direction.
statement_caveat: #BIS is complete under approximation-preserving reductions for the logically defined class #RHΠ1, so its status decides the approximability of many problems shown to be #BIS-equivalent, among them the ferromagnetic Potts and random-cluster partition functions and counting stable matchings. In the language of Gibbs measures it is the hard-core model at fugacity 1 on bipartite graphs, where Glauber dynamics can mix slowly because of the two sublattice phases.
source: M. Dyer, L. A. Goldberg, C. Greenhill and M. Jerrum, The relative complexity of approximate counting problems, Algorithmica 38 (2004) 471–500
locator: X. Chen, M. Dyer, L. A. Goldberg, M. Jerrum, P. Lu, C. McQuillan and D. Richerby, The complexity of approximating conservative counting CSPs, arXiv:1208.1783, abstract: '#BIS, the problem of counting independent sets in bipartite graphs. #BIS is complete with respect to approximation-preserving reductions for a logically-defined complexity class #RHPi1, and is believed to be intractable.'
why_important: #BIS sits at the centre of the complexity classification of approximate counting: a large family of natural problems is equivalent to it, and none of the standard techniques (Markov chains, correlation decay, polynomial interpolation) is known either to solve it or to prove hardness. It is also the cleanest instance of the question whether phase coexistence in a statistical-mechanics model is a genuine algorithmic barrier.
where_it_stands: Algorithms exist for restricted classes: bipartite expanders and unbalanced bounded-degree bipartite graphs via cluster expansions and Markov chains (Jenssen, Keevash and Perkins; Liao, Lin, Lu and Mao; Chen, Galanis, Štefankovič and Vigoda; Cannon and Perkins) [verify list]. Cai, Galanis, Goldberg, Guo, Jerrum, Štefankovič and Vigoda proved #BIS-hardness for antiferromagnetic two-spin systems on bounded-degree bipartite graphs in the non-uniqueness region [verify]. Neither an FPRAS nor NP-hardness is known for #BIS. Open.
note: Fame: the best-known open problem in the complexity of approximate counting; Goldberg and Jerrum's work over two decades is organised around it.

title: Linear-size sample compression (Littlestone–Warmuth)
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Does every binary concept class C contained in {0,1}^X of finite VC dimension d admit a labelled sample compression scheme of size O(d)? The compressor must retain at most Cd labelled examples from every finite sample realizable by C, with a universal constant C, and the fixed reconstruction map must recover a hypothesis consistent with the whole sample.
statement_caveat: The size bound is independent of the sample size. The original size-d conjecture is stronger; this row asks the customary linear-size version. Finite compression of size exponential in d is known, so merely obtaining a sample-size-independent bound is not the problem. Regression, multiclass learning and approximate or randomized reconstructions are different formulations.
source: J. H. Rubinstein and B. I. P. Rubinstein, Unlabelled Sample Compression Schemes for Intersection-Closed Classes and Extremal Classes, arXiv:2210.05455 (2022); see also Attias, Hanneke and Ramaswami, arXiv:2410.13012
locator: Rubinstein–Rubinstein, Introduction, PDF p. 1: 'This conjecture, for size O(d), remains open now more than 35 years later'. The preceding sentence specifies labelled schemes for VC-d classes.
why_important: Compression would explain finite-VC statistical learnability through a uniformly small set of retained observations. It is one of the oldest structural questions behind distribution-free learning and generalisation bounds.
where_it_stands: Rubinstein and Rubinstein obtain unlabelled schemes of size at most 11d for intersection-closed classes and describe earlier size-d schemes for maximum classes. Attias, Hanneke and Ramaswami (arXiv:2410.13012) still use the binary linear-size conjecture as a hypothesis for reductions to other learning settings. The 2026 agnostic squared-loss compression result arXiv:2609.29696 concerns an accuracy-dependent regression guarantee and does not prove this exact binary reconstruction statement. Open.
note: Fame: the opened introduction calls it one of the oldest open problems in learning theory and traces it to Littlestone and Warmuth (1986).

title: The free group factor isomorphism problem (Murray–von Neumann)
domain_name: Random matrices and random operators
statement: For the free groups F_m and F_n on distinct finite numbers m,n >= 2 of generators, are the tracial von Neumann algebras L(F_m) and L(F_n) isomorphic? In particular, decide whether L(F_2) is isomorphic to L(F_3). Here L(F_n) is generated by the left regular representation on l²(F_n), with its canonical trace.
statement_caveat: These are separable II_1 factors. The nonseparable analogue is a different problem. Equality of first-order theories is weaker than isomorphism. T145 asks equality of two free-entropy constructions, a potential source of invariants, rather than this classification question.
source: I. Goldbring and J. Pi, On the First-Order Free Group Factor Alternative, arXiv:2305.08168v2 (2025), Introduction and Theorem 1.1
locator: Introduction, PDF p. 1: 'A long-standing question regarding the free group factors'; the following displayed question asks whether L(F_m) is isomorphic to L(F_n) for distinct m,n >= 2.
why_important: Free group factors are the basic operator algebras of free probability, generated by freely independent Haar unitaries. Distinguishing their number of generators is a central motivation for free entropy and its random-matrix models.
where_it_stands: Goldbring and Pi recall the Dykema–Radulescu dichotomy: all interpolated free group factors are isomorphic or all their distinct parameters give nonisomorphic factors. Their new results concern elementary equivalence and do not choose between these alternatives. Boutonnet, Drimbe, Ioana and Popa (arXiv:2308.05671) settle a nonseparable analogue, which does not settle the separable question. Newer papers inspected in the status ledger concern embeddings and other group factors. Open.
note: Fame: the opened source attributes the problem to Murray and von Neumann; it is a standard foundational problem of free probability and II_1-factor theory.

title: Falconer's distance set conjecture in the plane
domain_name: Stochastic and geometric probability
statement: Let E be a compact subset of R² with Hausdorff dimension greater than 1. Must its Euclidean distance set Delta(E) = {|x-y| : x,y in E} have positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure?
statement_caveat: The threshold 1 is half the ambient dimension. Full Hausdorff dimension of the distance set is a weaker conclusion than positive Lebesgue measure. Pinned distance sets fix one endpoint and pose a stronger question. Finite-field and integer-lattice distance problems are separate variants; none is counted here as another row. T181 concerns projections of a fixed Cantor set rather than its distance set.
source: A. Iosevich and A. Yavicoli, Improved dimension bounds for Falconer's distance problem in the plane, arXiv:2610.05500 (2026), Introduction
locator: Introduction, PDF p. 5: 'Falconer conjectured that' the distance set 'has positive Lebesgue measure whenever' the source dimension exceeds 1. The next sentence says even the weaker full-dimension conclusion remains open near 1.
why_important: This is a central question about how a nonlinear map transforms fractal probability measures. Frostman measures, Fourier decay, energy integrals and probabilistic constructions are fundamental to both its positive results and its obstructions.
where_it_stands: Iosevich and Yavicoli (October 2026) improve lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of distance sets when the source dimension is just above 1. Those bounds do not give positive Lebesgue measure. Gan, Liu and Wu (arXiv:2610.05015) revisit the 5/4 positive-measure result; the full threshold 1 remains out of reach in the opened current literature. Open.
note: Fame: a named four-decade conjecture central to geometric measure theory and its interaction with probability; the October 2026 source describes it as one of the field's most intriguing problems.

title: The capacity region of the general two-receiver broadcast channel
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Given a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless channel p(y,z|x) with one sender and two receivers, determine the capacity region of achievable rate triples (R_0,R_1,R_2), where the common message is decoded by both receivers and receiver i also decodes its own private message, with error probability tending to zero as block length tends to infinity.
statement_caveat: The target is a general characterization beyond the regularized block-coding definition. Degraded, deterministic and Gaussian subclasses have special solutions. It is no longer appropriate to identify the capacity region with the one-letter Marton inner bound: a 2026 paper reports a counterexample. T166 concerns two interfering senders, a different channel model.
source: M. Huang, Y. Liu and Y. Liu, Sub-optimality of Marton's Inner Bound for the Two-Receiver Broadcast Channel, arXiv:2608.19869 (2026), Introduction; original model attributed there to Cover (1972)
locator: Introduction, PDF p. 1: 'the full characterization of the capacity region remains one of the most fundamental open problems in information theory for decades'. Figure 1 specifies common and private messages.
why_important: The model isolates how one random channel input can carry different information to different receivers. Its unresolved capacity is a basic obstruction to a general theory of multiuser communication and has motivated random coding, auxiliary-variable and entropy methods since Cover's formulation.
where_it_stands: Huang, Liu and Liu, Theorem 5, construct a finite two-receiver channel for which the complete one-letter Marton region is strictly below capacity, by proving a two-letter gain. This refutes the optimality conjecture for that bound, not the existence of an as-yet unknown capacity characterization. The opened 2026 source still identifies the general capacity problem as open; subsequent searched results concern subclasses or assisted channels. Open.
note: Fame: one of the classical unsolved problems of Shannon theory, explicitly described as fundamental in the opened 2026 paper.

title: Exact intersection exponents of three-dimensional Brownian motion
domain_name: Brownian motion, stochastic analysis and SPDE
statement: Determine the three-dimensional Brownian intersection exponents xi_3(k,lambda), for integers k >= 1 and real lambda > 0. In the standard definition, k independent Brownian paths start at 0 and another starts at (1,0,0); Z_n is the conditional probability that the latter path avoids the first k until all have reached the sphere of radius exp(n), given the first k paths. Then xi_3(k,lambda) = -lim n^(-1) log E[Z_n^lambda]. In particular, determine xi_3(1,1).
statement_caveat: This is a question about exact values, not existence or analyticity of the exponents. The special value xi_3(1,2)=1 is known. T103 concerns loop-erased random walk and its growth exponent; Brownian intersection exponents describe avoidance of independent un-erased paths and a whole moment family.
source: Y. Gao, X. Li, Y. Li, R. Liu and X. Liu, A boundary Harnack principle and its application to analyticity of 3D Brownian intersection exponents, arXiv:2411.14921 (2024), Section 1.1
locator: Section 1.1, PDF p. 3: 'Although determining all values of' xi_3(k,lambda) 'is still out of reach'. Equation (1.1), PDF p. 2, defines the exponents.
why_important: These exponents govern nonintersection probabilities and the fractal geometry of Brownian cut points. Their planar analogues were landmark applications of SLE; three dimensions lack the conformal tools that produced those exact answers.
where_it_stands: Gao and collaborators prove real analyticity in lambda for every positive integer k (Theorem 1.1); this does not identify the values. Liu (arXiv:2609.18643) proves the explicit bound xi_3(1,1)<0.9999. Shi, Liu, Li, Li and Deng (arXiv:2609.25968) give numerical estimates for several packet sizes and continuous moments, explicitly describing them as numerical. No general exact expression is known. Open.
note: Fame: a classical Brownian critical-exponent problem, treated in Lawler's work and in the literature surrounding the Lawler–Schramm–Werner planar intersection-exponent theorems.

title: A nontrivial traffic transition in the Biham–Middleton–Levine model
domain_name: Interacting particle systems, growth and KPZ
statement: Initially each site of Z² independently contains a northbound car with probability p/2, an eastbound car with probability p/2, or a vacancy with probability 1-p. At odd steps all northbound cars with an empty site immediately north move simultaneously, and at even steps eastbound cars do likewise eastward. Is there p_c in (0,1) such that for p>p_c almost surely no car moves infinitely often, whereas for p<p_c almost surely every car moves infinitely often?
statement_caveat: This is the infinite-lattice conjecture, with positive-density independent initial data. A theorem for finitely many cars, or for a vanishing density on finite tori, does not establish its low-density phase. The stronger assertion of asymptotic free-flow speed 1/2 is discussed separately in the posing paper. Intermediate periodic states on finite tori need not contradict the infinite-volume statement.
source: O. Angel, A. E. Holroyd and J. B. Martin, The Jammed Phase of the Biham–Middleton–Levine Traffic Model, arXiv:math/0504001 (2005)
locator: PDF p. 3, unnumbered Conjecture: 'There exists' a critical density in (0,1); below it 'almost surely all cars move infinitely often'. The same paragraph states the jammed conclusion above it.
why_important: This is a standard example of collective self-organisation arising from deterministic dynamics with random initial conditions. Even proving flow at a fixed sufficiently small positive density would require overcoming persistent long-range blocking dependencies.
where_it_stands: Angel, Holroyd and Martin prove that sufficiently high density gives jamming, on Z² and on large tori of bounded aspect ratio. Rabinovich, Biham and Katzav (arXiv:2601.01180v2, 2026) still describe only a few rigorous results and study low-density torus dynamics through geometric observables and simulations. Their analysis does not prove the infinite-lattice conjecture at positive low density. Open.
note: Fame borderline: the BML model is a widely studied foundational traffic cellular automaton; the posing paper notes its appearance as an unsolved puzzle.

title: Mahler's minimum volume-product conjecture in dimension four and higher
domain_name: Stochastic and geometric probability
statement: For every convex body K in R^n, n>=4, let P(K)=min over z in the interior of K of vol_n(K) vol_n((K-z)^polar), where A^polar={y: <x,y><=1 for every x in A}. Prove P(K)>=(n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)², the value for a simplex, with equality only for simplices.
statement_caveat: This is the general, nonsymmetric conjecture. The centrally symmetric version predicts the different minimum 4^n/n!, attained by Hanner polytopes. Both belong to one volume-product programme and are not counted as separate rows. The three-dimensional general case now has a reported solution and is excluded from the open range.
source: M. Fradelizi, M. Meyer and A. Zvavitch, Volume Product, arXiv:2301.06131 (2023), Section 3, Conjecture 1
locator: Section 3, PDF p. 15, Conjecture 1: 'For every convex body K in' R^n; the displayed inequality gives the simplex value, 'with equality if and only if' K is a simplex.
why_important: The volume product measures a convex body together with its dual. It connects log-concave probability, entropy and transport inequalities with asymptotic convex geometry. Sharp lower bounds would determine the extremal geometry behind inverse Santalo inequalities.
where_it_stands: The 2023 survey records the planar general case and the three-dimensional symmetric case. Chen, Li, Xi and Xu (arXiv:2605.09334v3) report a proof for all three-dimensional convex bodies, including the equality case, using shadow flow. This does not cover n>=4. The current search also found special-symmetry and functional results rather than a general higher-dimensional solution. Open.
note: Fame: a classical named conjecture dating to 1938, central to convex geometry and routinely connected to log-concave probability.

title: The Shannon capacity of the seven-cycle
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Determine Theta(C_7)=lim as k tends to infinity of alpha(C_7 strong-product ... strong-product C_7)^(1/k), where the product has k factors and alpha denotes its independence number. Equivalently, determine the optimal zero-error communication rate log_2 Theta(C_7) for a channel whose confusability graph is the seven-cycle.
statement_caveat: The strong product joins two distinct tuples when every coordinate agrees or is adjacent in C_7. The five-cycle has capacity sqrt(5), but the analogous exact value for the seven-cycle remains unknown. Finite-product independence numbers and improved lower bounds do not identify the limit. T117 concerns a stochastic deletion channel rather than zero-error capacity of a fixed confusability graph.
source: N. Lavi and I. Sason, Advances in the Shannon Capacity of Graphs, arXiv:2509.24600v3 (2026); Y. Gao, A Recursive Construction Improving the Lower Bound on the Shannon Capacity of C7, arXiv:2607.27869 (2026)
locator: Lavi–Sason, Example 4.1, PDF p. 26, equation (120), displays a strict interval for Theta(C_7). Gao, abstract, PDF p. 1: 'We give a recursive reformulation and extension' of a large independent set in a power of C_7.
why_important: The smallest unresolved odd cycle is a landmark test case for zero-error information theory. Its capacity captures the advantage of long block codes over a single use and has driven semidefinite bounds and probabilistic-combinatorial constructions.
where_it_stands: The Lovasz theta upper bound is 7 cos(pi/7)/(1+cos(pi/7)), about 3.31767. The opened January 2026 survey gives a strict lower/upper gap; July 2026 papers improve lower bounds using larger independent sets and recursive constructions, including Gao's explicit set in C_7^200. Those constructions leave a gap to the upper bound and do not determine capacity. Open.
note: Fame: the canonical next case after Lovasz's celebrated solution for C_5; a decades-old problem in zero-error information theory and probabilistic combinatorics.

title: Pólya's eigenvalue conjecture for arbitrary Euclidean domains
domain_name: Brownian motion, stochastic analysis and SPDE
statement: Let Omega be a bounded connected domain in R^d, d>=2, with piecewise smooth boundary and volume V. Write lambda_k for its Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues, starting at k=1, and mu_k for its Neumann eigenvalues, starting with mu_0=0. If omega_d is the unit-ball volume, prove mu_k <= 4 pi² (k/(omega_d V))^(2/d) <= lambda_k for every k>=1.
statement_caveat: The conjecture asks that every eigenvalue lie on the prescribed side of the leading Weyl term. Weyl asymptotics alone do not imply it. The Neumann indexing convention is explicit. Counterexamples for curved ambient manifolds do not refute the conjecture for Euclidean domains. T030 concerns locations of extrema of Neumann eigenfunctions, a different question.
source: G. Dai and Y. Sun, Pólya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of annuli, arXiv:2610.05146 (2026), Introduction
locator: Introduction, PDF p. 2: 'Pólya’s conjecture asks for considerably more'; the immediately following display is mu_k(Omega)<=W_k(Omega)<=lambda_k(Omega), k>=1.
why_important: The spectra govern killed and reflected Brownian semigroups. The conjecture would turn the asymptotic relation between volume and spectral density into sharp bounds at every frequency, using only volume.
where_it_stands: Pólya's tiling-domain argument proves important special cases. Dai and Sun prove the Neumann inequality for all circular annuli and obtain product and sector extensions. Other 2025–2026 papers treat balls, thin products and Dirichlet annuli; none covers arbitrary Euclidean domains. The sphere counterexample in arXiv:2209.12671 concerns a different ambient geometry. Open.
note: Fame: a classical named spectral conjecture formulated in 1954, central to geometric spectral theory and closely connected to Brownian heat kernels.

title: The Kakeya Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in dimensions four and higher
domain_name: Stochastic and geometric probability
statement: For each n>=4, prove that every Borel set in R^n containing a unit line segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension n.
statement_caveat: Positive Lebesgue measure is not asserted: Kakeya sets of measure zero exist. Hausdorff dimension, Minkowski dimension and maximal-function estimates are different versions of the problem. The three-dimensional Hausdorff-dimension conjecture is now proved, so the open range starts at four. T198 concerns distance sets rather than segments in all directions.
source: L. Guth, The Kakeya conjecture, after Wang and Zahl, arXiv:2604.03416 (2026), opening page
locator: PDF p. 1: 'In dimension n ≥ 4, the conjecture is currently open.' The preceding paragraph states the full Hausdorff-dimension conjecture and records Wang–Zahl's three-dimensional theorem.
why_important: This is a central extremal problem about overlapping thin tubes and fractal sets. It connects geometric probability and incidence methods with Fourier restriction; constructions based on random and multiscale geometry have shaped the subject.
where_it_stands: Guth's 2026 Bourbaki survey explains Wang and Zahl's resolution in dimension three and explicitly leaves dimensions at least four open. Choudhuri (arXiv:2610.12480) reports an improved four-dimensional Hausdorff-dimension lower bound of 3.073, below the required 4. New zero-measure constructions in arbitrary dimension do not contradict full Hausdorff dimension. Open.
note: Fame: one of the best-known geometric-measure conjectures; the opened current source is a Bourbaki exposition of its recent three-dimensional breakthrough.

title: Characterizing the almost-entropic cone of four random variables
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Characterize the closure of the set of vectors (H(X_A)) indexed by nonempty subsets A of {1,2,3,4}, where (X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4) ranges over jointly distributed finite-valued random variables and X_A denotes the tuple with indices in A. Equivalently, characterize all linear information inequalities valid for four random variables.
statement_caveat: The closure is the almost-entropic cone; exact entropic representability on its boundary is a different, stronger question. The cone is not described by the Shannon inequalities alone and is not polyhedral. Thus the problem does not ask for an impossible finite list of linear inequalities. The completeness of iterated Copy Lemma methods is one possible route, not an established characterization.
source: L. Csirmaz, Exploring the entropic region, arXiv:2509.12439v2, Sections 1, 3.4 and 9
locator: Introduction, PDF p. 2: 'it is also unknown whether any of these methods captures the complete entropy region'. Section 3.4 treats two, three and four variables and distinguishes entropy regions from their closures.
why_important: The entropy vector records every marginal dependence in a finite probability law. Knowing its feasible region would settle the universal constraints behind network coding, secret sharing and many information-theoretic optimization problems.
where_it_stands: The opened survey reviews the Zhang–Yeung non-Shannon inequality, infinite families of further inequalities, and copy and maximum-entropy methods, while explicitly leaving completeness unknown. Recent five-variable inequalities extend outer bounds in a larger problem and do not give a complete four-variable characterization. Open.
note: Fame: a foundational information-theoretic probability problem, established by the non-Shannon-inequality literature since Zhang and Yeung's work.

title: The Erdős–Hajnal conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For every fixed finite graph H, does there exist c(H)>0 such that every n-vertex graph with no induced copy of H contains a clique or an independent set with at least n^c(H) vertices?
statement_caveat: The exclusion is induced: both edges and nonedges of H must be respected. The exponent may depend on H. This is a polynomial homogeneous-set statement for a restricted family, whereas unrestricted random graphs typically have only logarithmic cliques and independent sets. T134 and T149 concern quantitative unrestricted Ramsey numbers.
source: S. Huang, Y. Ju and Y. Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal conjecture beyond five-vertex graphs, arXiv:2606.06258, revised 2026
locator: Abstract, PDF p. 1: 'a central open problem in combinatorics'; its preceding sentence states exactly the polynomial clique-or-independent-set assertion for every fixed forbidden induced graph.
why_important: The conjecture says that a local forbidden pattern forces global structure far stronger than random-graph behaviour. It is one of the central interfaces between Ramsey theory, structural graph theory and the probabilistic method.
where_it_stands: The opened 2026 paper records the five-vertex breakthrough, including the five-vertex path, and develops further six-vertex cases. Other current papers address bounded-VC families, specified forbidden graphs or hypergraph versions. These do not establish the assertion for arbitrary H. Open.
note: Fame: the opened current paper calls it central and records its inclusion among the leading Erdős problems; a standard named conjecture of probabilistic combinatorics.

title: Almost all graphs are determined by their adjacency spectrum (Haemers)
domain_name: Random graphs and random constraint satisfaction
statement: Let G be sampled from G(n,1/2). Does the probability tend to one that every simple n-vertex graph with the same multiset of adjacency-matrix eigenvalues as G is isomorphic to G?
statement_caveat: Only the ordinary adjacency spectrum is supplied. Supplying the spectra of both G and its complement gives the generalized spectrum, a strictly stronger data set; that variant now has a reported solution. Simple eigenvalues or nonsingular adjacency matrices do not suffice to prove reconstruction. T054 and T129 ask different random-matrix questions.
source: Z. Xiang, Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, arXiv:2610.11047 (2026), Introduction
locator: Introduction, PDF p. 1: Haemers' ordinary-spectrum conjecture 'is still open'. The abstract and the next paragraph explicitly distinguish the generalized-spectrum variant proved in this paper.
why_important: The spectrum gives all closed-walk counts but forgets the vertex labels and eigenvectors. Whether these statistics identify a typical graph is a basic inverse problem linking random symmetric matrices, random graphs and spectral reconstruction.
where_it_stands: Koval and Kwan prove that exponentially many graphs are determined by their spectrum, as recorded in the opened source. Xiang (October 2026) proves that G(n,1/2) is determined by its generalized spectrum with probability tending to one, using arithmetic and inverse Littlewood–Offord methods. The same paper explicitly leaves ordinary-spectrum reconstruction unresolved. Open.
note: Fame borderline: a long-standing named conjecture in spectral and random graph theory, prominent in van Dam–Haemers surveys and current random-matrix work.

title: The exact real Grothendieck constant
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Determine the smallest universal constant K_G such that, for every finite real matrix (a_ij) and every choice of real unit vectors u_i,v_j in a common Euclidean space, sum a_ij<u_i,v_j> <= K_G max over signs epsilon_i,delta_j in {-1,1} of sum a_ij epsilon_i delta_j.
statement_caveat: The matrix dimensions and vector dimension are unrestricted. This is the real constant, not its complex or fixed-vector-dimension variants. Krivine's proposed exact value was disproved; asking for that value to be proved would be a retired conjecture, whereas determining the actual optimum remains open.
source: M. Braverman, K. Makarychev, Y. Makarychev and A. Naor, The Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than Krivine's bound, arXiv:1103.6161; S. Heilman, C. Jones and G. Malavolta, arXiv:2610.10477 (2026)
locator: Braverman et al., abstract, PDF p. 1: 'the exact value of the Grothendieck constant' remains unknown. The opening display specifies the constant without any restriction on matrix dimensions.
why_important: The optimal constant compares vector correlations with correlations of signs. Gaussian rounding makes it fundamental in probabilistic inequalities, approximation algorithms and the analysis of classical versus quantum correlations.
where_it_stands: The 2011 paper strictly improves Krivine's bound. Several 2026 papers produce certified upper or lower bounds rather than an exact value. Heilman, Jones and Malavolta (arXiv:2610.10477) prove 1.773 <= K_G <= 1.7799 and give a numerical heuristic near 1.779; the certified interval is not an exact evaluation. Open.
note: Fame: the canonical unknown sharp constant in Grothendieck's inequality, central to the probabilistic and algorithmic uses of that theorem.

title: Ryser's odd-order Latin-square transversal conjecture
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: Does every Latin square of odd order n have a transversal: a set of n cells containing exactly one cell from each row, exactly one from each column, and exactly one occurrence of each symbol?
statement_caveat: This is the odd-order full-transversal part of the Ryser–Brualdi–Stein programme. Partial transversals of size n-1 and almost-sure results for random Latin squares are weaker conclusions. Ryser's conjecture on covers of multipartite hypergraphs is a different conjecture with the same name; no result about it is used as a status check for this row.
source: R. Montgomery, Transversals in Latin Squares, arXiv:2406.19873 (2024), Section 3, Conjecture 3.2
locator: Conjecture 3.2, PDF p. 9: 'a full transversal if n is odd'. The preceding page attributes the odd-order conjecture to Ryser in 1967.
why_important: The problem asks whether local row and column constraints force a perfect rainbow matching. It is a classical test case for random greedy constructions, absorption and the probabilistic method in highly dependent combinatorial structures.
where_it_stands: Montgomery's survey distinguishes almost-all Latin-square results, the solved Hall–Paige problem for group tables and progress on near-perfect transversals from the odd-order full-transversal conjecture. The 2026 paper on Latin squares generated by particular cellular automata treats a subclass. Current papers on hypergraph Ryser conjectures do not answer this question. Open.
note: Fame: a classical 1967 conjecture on Latin squares, a central problem of modern probabilistic combinatorics and the subject of major conference surveys.

title: Existence of Hadamard matrices in every order divisible by four
domain_name: Boolean functions, concentration and probabilistic inequalities
statement: For every positive integer m, does there exist a real 4m by 4m matrix H with entries in {-1,1} and HH^T=4m I?
statement_caveat: This concerns unrestricted real Hadamard matrices. Circulant, skew and complex Hadamard matrices impose different conditions; the status of those variants does not settle this conjecture. The arithmetic necessary condition, apart from orders 1 and 2, is divisibility by four. T192 asks for explicit restricted-isometry matrices, a different dimension and sparsity problem.
source: M. Cati and D. V. Pasechnik, A database of constructions of Hadamard matrices, arXiv:2411.18897, abstract and Section 1
locator: Abstract, PDF p. 1: 'Hadamard matrices of order n are conjectured to exist whenever n is 1, 2, or a multiple of 4'.
why_important: These are extremal sign matrices with perfectly orthogonal rows. They give optimal experimental designs, codes and discrete substitutes for independent coordinates, making the existence question basic to statistics and the combinatorial side of random matrix theory.
where_it_stands: Cati and Pasechnik implement and audit many existing constructions and document remaining gaps; checking finitely many orders does not prove existence for every multiple of four. Recent search results concern approximate matrices, complex order-six classification or restricted symmetry classes, rather than the unrestricted all-orders assertion. Open.
note: Fame: one of the best-known existence conjectures for sign matrices, familiar throughout combinatorics, coding, experimental design and random matrix theory.

title: The computational gap for tensor principal component analysis
domain_name: Statistics, optimal transport and information inequalities
statement: Fix an integer k>=3. Observe Y=lambda sqrt(N) theta^tensor(k)+G, where x is uniform on {−1,+1}^N, theta=x/sqrt(N), and G is the symmetrization of a tensor of independent standard Gaussian entries. Prove the conjectured computational lower bound: when lambda is below N^((k−2)/4) by a fixed polynomial factor, no randomized polynomial-time estimator weakly recovers x, meaning correlation bounded away from zero, with absolute correlation used for even k.
statement_caveat: The normalization of the signal and noise is essential. Information-theoretic weak recovery is possible at a constant signal strength, whereas the conjectured computational scale is polynomial in N. Lower bounds for low-degree polynomials, sum of squares, statistical queries or specified Markov chains are not lower bounds for every polynomial-time algorithm. T072 concerns a graph-based planted-clique problem, not this Gaussian tensor observation model.
source: A. Das and T. Schramm, Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics, arXiv:2610.16705 (2026), Section 1
locator: Introduction, PDF p.4, equation (1) and its following paragraph: 'While this longstanding conjecture remains open'. The paragraph defines the statistical-computational gap and the N^((k−2)/4) scale.
why_important: Tensor PCA is a canonical example of an inference problem that is statistically solvable but apparently computationally inaccessible. A general algorithm below the conjectured scale, or a convincing hardness theory at that scale, would reshape the interpretation of computational barriers in high-dimensional probability.
where_it_stands: Das and Schramm obtain polynomial-time strong recovery at the established algorithmic scale using annealing and ergodic averaging of Glauber dynamics. This closes a proposed gap between local and global methods, while their Introduction explicitly retains the main statistical-computational gap. New 2026 low-degree bounds and average-case reductions address restricted computational models or conditional hardness. Open.
note: Fame: the opened source calls tensor PCA a canonical planted problem and documents its extensive probability, spin-glass, statistics and average-case-complexity literature since Richard–Montanari.

title: The quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel
domain_name: Queueing and stochastic networks
statement: Determine the unassisted quantum capacity Q(D_p) of D_p(rho)=(1−3p)rho+p(X rho X+Y rho Y+Z rho Z), where X,Y,Z are the Pauli matrices and 0<=p<=1/3. In particular, determine the exact noise threshold at which its quantum capacity becomes zero.
statement_caveat: The parameter p is the probability of each nonidentity Pauli error; the total error probability is 3p. Quantum capacity concerns faithful transmission of unknown quantum states without entanglement assistance. The classical capacity, entanglement-assisted capacity, and performance threshold of a particular quantum code are different quantities. A coherent-information lower bound from one input state is not a capacity formula.
source: A. Krohn-Grimberghe, A certified lower bound on the quantum-capacity threshold of the depolarizing channel, arXiv:2608.15870v2 (2026), Sections 2, 7 and 8
locator: Section 7, PDF p.4: 'No family-wide or all-state statement, and no capacity formula.' Section 8 states that the gap to the no-cloning ceiling remains large; Section 2 fixes the channel convention.
why_important: This is the simplest symmetric quantum noise model whose capacity still resists an explicit determination. Its obstruction is genuinely probabilistic and information-theoretic: correlated inputs across many uses can outperform single-use coding, making the regularization essential.
where_it_stands: The opened August 2026 paper certifies positive coherent information at per-Pauli p=16239/250000=0.064956 using an explicit 45-copy input. Antidegradability gives zero quantum capacity for p>=1/12. The exact capacity and threshold between these regimes remain undetermined. The September 2026 third-order classical-capacity result arXiv:2609.37240 concerns classical communication and does not close this quantum-capacity gap. Open.
note: Fame: a standard foundational quantum-information capacity problem studied since the 1990s; the current paper traces three decades of depolarizing-channel threshold bounds.

title: Is the free Ising measure on a regular tree a factor of IID up to reconstruction?
domain_name: Branching processes, trees and genealogies
statement: For the infinite d-regular tree, d>=3, let mu_beta be the zero-field ferromagnetic Ising Gibbs measure with free boundary condition. Is mu_beta an Aut(T_d)-equivariant measurable factor of independent identically distributed labels whenever tanh(beta)<=(d−1)^(−1/2)?
statement_caveat: The factor must commute with every tree automorphism. Equivalently, mu_beta is the fair-root binary broadcast process with adjacent-spin correlation tanh(beta). Above the reconstruction threshold it is not a factor of IID. Below that threshold, extremality or a trivial tail is not already a factor construction. T067 asks whether Kesten–Stigum is sharp for reconstruction; here the binary reconstruction threshold is known, and the issue is equivariant generation of the entire process.
source: D. Nam, A. Sly and L. Zhang, Ising model on trees and factors of IID, arXiv:2012.09484v2 (2022), Introduction and Theorem 1; R. Lyons, Factors of IID on Trees, arXiv:1401.4197
locator: Nam–Sly–Zhang, PDF p.2: 'we conjecture that the Ising model on T should be a factor of IID'; the sentence specifies every d>=3 and tanh(beta)<=(d−1)^(−1/2).
why_important: The question separates statistical nonreconstruction from generation by a local invariant rule.
