Factors of IID describe probabilistic processes compatible with symmetry and local algorithms on large sparse graphs, so identifying their limits is a central problem in probability on trees.
where_it_stands: The uniqueness range tanh(beta)<=1/(d−1) is known. Nam, Sly and Zhang extend the construction to tanh(beta)<=c/sqrt(d−1) for a universal c>0 and sufficiently large d, and explicitly conjecture the full nonreconstruction range. Later Ising factor results found for amenable graphs do not settle the nonamenable regular-tree gap. Open.
note: Fame: a question highlighted in Lyons's survey of factors of IID, with a substantial probability paper devoted to extending the known regime.

title: The universal critical slope of the random copolymer at a selective interface
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: Determine the exact weak-coupling critical slope m_(1/2)=lim_(lambda down to 0) h_c(lambda)/lambda for the standard disordered copolymer with simple-random-walk excursions. In the normalization Z_N=E exp(−2 lambda sum_(i=1)^N Delta_i(omega_i+h)), the omega_i are independent mean-zero variance-one Gaussian charges, Delta_i is constant on each walk excursion and independently chooses its side with probability 1/2, F=lim N^(−1)E log Z_N, and h_c(lambda)=sup{h:F(lambda,h)>0}.
statement_caveat: The excursion renewal exponent is alpha=1/2. The existence and universality of the slope are known; its exact value is the target. Some papers shift the annealed critical curve and consequently use 1−h_c(lambda)/lambda instead, so their notation must be translated. Monthus's proposed value 2/3 is not the current conjectured answer: its equality prediction has been ruled out. Pinning at renewal contacts is a different disorder model.
source: F. Caravenna, G. Giacomin and F. L. Toninelli, Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems, arXiv:1010.5587, Sections 1.2–1.4; Q. Berger, F. Caravenna, J. Poisat, R. Sun and N. Zygouras, arXiv:1301.5308
locator: The survey, PDF p.9: 'capturing the value of mα, for α ∈(0,1), is an important open problem.' Equations (4)–(6), (14) and Theorem 1 fix the model, critical curve and slope.
why_important: The slope is a universal quenched critical quantity for a basic disordered-polymer model. It is a particularly clean test of whether an exact prediction can be extracted from the energy–entropy competition at a random interface.
where_it_stands: The continuum weak-coupling limit proves that the slope exists and depends only on the renewal exponent. The opened later paper arXiv:1301.5308 records strictness of the Monthus lower bound and resolves the finite-mean alpha>1 slope, while retaining the distinct alpha=1/2 problem. Newer copolymer work located in the status searches treats correlated disorder, a reduced model, or other geometries rather than giving this exact slope. Open.
note: Fame: Bolthausen–den Hollander's continuum copolymer programme and the Caravenna–Giacomin–Toninelli survey identify this as a principal open problem, with longstanding competing physical predictions.

title: Global strong solutions of the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation for general large data
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: For the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation d_t F+v·grad_x F=Q(F,F) on T^3_x times R^3_v, prove global existence and uniqueness of a classical solution for arbitrary smooth strictly positive initial densities with finite mass, energy and entropy and sufficiently rapid velocity decay, without a smallness or near-equilibrium assumption.
statement_caveat: This is the spatially inhomogeneous, three-dimensional equation. Global renormalized solutions do not supply the uniqueness and regularity demanded here. Global homogeneous theory, near-Maxwellian theory, and one-dimensional models are not the general large-data result. T065 concerns deriving macroscopic hydrodynamics from deterministic particles; the present problem is global well-posedness of the kinetic probability-density equation itself.
source: L. He, J.-C. Jiang, J.-I. Kim, D. Lee and S. Park, A Kinetic Concentration criterion for Large-data Boltzmann Dynamics, arXiv:2610.12093 (2026), Introduction
locator: Introduction, PDF p.4: 'global well-posedness in a strong or mild class, uniqueness, and unconditional convergence to equilibrium'; the sentence identifies these as central open problems for general large data.
why_important: The distribution of a collisional gas should remain a well-defined density under its own nonlinear kinetic evolution. Establishing this beyond perturbative regimes is a foundational question linking probability, collision geometry and the kinetic explanation of thermodynamics.
where_it_stands: DiPerna–Lions theory gives global renormalized solutions, and perturbative theories give classical solutions near equilibrium. The opened October 2026 paper proves uniqueness, weighted bounds and convergence for global mild solutions satisfying an additional uniform velocity-tail criterion; it explicitly retains the unconditional large-data problem. Recent non-cutoff local classical and one-dimensional large-data results likewise do not resolve this three-dimensional target. Open.
note: Fame: a classical central problem of kinetic theory, explicitly identified as such in the opened current paper and situated between the landmark weak-solution and perturbative theories.

title: Monotonicity of the speed of once-excited random walk in low dimensions
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Consider once-excited nearest-neighbour random walk on Z^d. On the first departure from a site it steps in directions +e_1 and −e_1 with probabilities (1+beta)/(2d) and (1−beta)/(2d), and in each other coordinate direction with probability 1/(2d); on later departures it is simple symmetric. Is its limiting speed v_d(beta)=lim X_n·e_1/n nondecreasing in beta throughout [0,1], for each 2<=d<=8?
statement_caveat: There is one directional cookie per site. Higher excitement changes the subsequently visited set, so a direct ordered coupling of successive steps is not available. One-dimensional multi-cookie monotonicity is a different theorem. T048 concerns a biased walk on a random Galton–Watson tree; here the graph is deterministic and the memory is carried by visited sites.
source: R. van der Hofstad and M. Holmes, Monotonicity for excited random walk in high dimensions, arXiv:0803.1881; E. Kosygina and M. P. W. Zerner, Excited random walks: results, methods, open problems, arXiv:1204.1895, Remark 4.11; C.-D. Pham, arXiv:1501.04499
locator: Kosygina–Zerner, Remark4.11, PDF p.20: 'monotonically increasing in the drift parameter p if d ≥9'. Pham, PDF pp.1–3, defines the beta normalization and separates smoothness from monotonicity.
why_important: A stronger local directional preference need not transparently produce greater asymptotic speed in a self-interacting process. This basic test of monotonicity links geometric exploration of the range to regeneration and perturbation methods.
where_it_stands: Van der Hofstad and Holmes prove strict monotonicity in all dimensions d>=9, and on a small-bias interval in dimension 8. Pham proves smoothness for positive beta in every d>=2 and further partial monotonicity results for many-cookie variants; these do not establish the full once-excited low-dimensional assertion. The 2026 excited-walk shape results found in the searches concern different radial excitation rules. Open.
note: Fame: a standard speed question for the Benjamini–Wilson model, highlighted in the principal excited-walk survey and the subject of several dedicated monotonicity papers.

title: Almost-sure finite-range localization of linearly vertex-reinforced random walk
domain_name: Random walks, Markov chains and mixing
statement: Let G be an infinite connected graph of bounded degree. Starting at a fixed vertex, define Z_n(y)=1+sum_(j=0)^n 1{X_j=y}, and choose the next neighbour y of X_n with probability Z_n(y)/sum_(z adjacent to X_n) Z_n(z). Must the set of all visited vertices be finite almost surely? In particular, settle this for the usual nearest-neighbour graph Z^d, d>=2.
statement_caveat: The reinforcement is linear in visits to the destination vertex, with initial weight one. Neither the continuous-time vertex-reinforced jump process nor reciprocally summable superlinear weights are the same model. T047 concerns reinforcement of an edge once after its first traversal; that transition rule does not include this vertex-local-time process as a special case.
source: S. Volkov, Vertex-reinforced random walk on arbitrary graphs, arXiv:math/9907196 (1999), abstract; P. Tarrès, Localization of reinforced random walks, arXiv:1103.5536
locator: Volkov's original arXiv abstract: 'We conjecture that on all graphs of bounded degree, this happens a.s.' The preceding clause identifies visiting only finitely many vertices as the event.
why_important: Linear reinforcement balances escape into an infinite graph against the attraction of accumulated local time. Proving finite trapping on a multidimensional lattice would resolve one of the basic questions distinguishing reinforced motion from ordinary random walk.
where_it_stands: Volkov proves finite-range localization with positive probability on a broad class of graphs and almost surely on bounded-degree trees. The one-dimensional linear model has its much sharper five-site theorem. Cotar and Thacker, arXiv:1509.00807, prove eventual two-vertex trapping under superlinear summability assumptions, which exclude linear weights. New continuous-time, interacting-walk and tree-indexed models found in 2023–2026 do not settle the linear discrete-time conjecture. Open.
note: Fame: a longstanding Pemantle–Volkov/Tarrès reinforced-walk question, presented in the dedicated localization survey and explicitly conjectured in the original general-graph paper.

title: The cutoff-free three-dimensional Coulomb mean-field limit
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: Let N repelling particles in R^3 satisfy d_t X_i=V_i and d_t V_i=N^(−1)sum_(j not i) K(X_i−X_j), with the exact Coulomb force K(x)=x/|x|^3 and independent initial phase points of smooth compactly supported probability density f_0. Prove that, for each fixed T, their empirical phase-space measures converge in probability, uniformly for 0<=t<=T, to the classical solution of d_t f+v·grad_x f+(K*rho_f)·grad_v f=0, rho_f(x)=integral f(x,v)dv, without any microscopic regularization.
statement_caveat: The target is second-order Newtonian motion with no noise and no N-dependent cutoff. Results for first-order Coulomb gradient flows, for a linearization around equilibrium, or for stochastic Vlasov–Poisson–Fokker–Planck dynamics are different. T065 asks for a hydrodynamic limit; this is instead propagation of chaos toward a kinetic equation at fixed macroscopic time.
source: M. Feistl-Held and P. Pickl, On the mean-field limit for the Vlasov-Poisson system, arXiv:2504.01471 (2025), Section1.1; M. Duerinckx and P.-E. Jabin, arXiv:2608.04104 (2026)
locator: Feistl-Held–Pickl, Section1.1, PDF p.2: the discussion of microscopic derivation without a cutoff says it 'is still an open problem.' Equations(1.1)–(1.2) specify Newtonian dynamics and the Vlasov–Poisson equation.
why_important: The Coulomb singularity creates rare, very close encounters that must be controlled probabilistically without changing the physical interaction. A solution would derive collisionless plasma kinetics directly from the unmodified many-particle dynamics.
where_it_stands: Feistl-Held and Pickl allow a cutoff of order N^(−5/12+sigma). Duerinckx and Jabin (August2026) remove the cutoff for the two-dimensional Coulomb problem and forces locally in L^(2−eta); the three-dimensional Coulomb force is more singular and is not included. September2026 cutoff-free three-dimensional VPFP work adds velocity noise. First-order Coulomb flow and equilibrium-fluctuation advances also leave this nonlinear inertial deterministic problem unresolved. Open.
note: Fame: a classical central mean-field-limit problem for Coulomb/Newton interactions, highlighted in the opened current derivation papers and the propagation-of-chaos programme.

title: The critical free-energy asymptotics of marginal disordered pinning
domain_name: Lattice statistical mechanics (Ising, Potts, O(n), gauge fields, polymers, spin glasses)
statement: Let tau be a renewal process starting at 0 with interarrival law K(n)=n^(-3/2)/zeta(3/2), and let omega_n be independent standard Gaussians. Set Z_N(beta,h)=E_tau[exp(sum_(n=1)^N (beta omega_n+h-beta^2/2) 1_{n in tau}) 1_{N in tau}], F(beta,h)=lim_(N to infinity) N^(-1) E_omega log Z_N(beta,h), and h_c(beta)=inf{h:F(beta,h)>0}. For fixed beta>0, determine the sharp asymptotic order of F(beta,h_c(beta)+delta) as delta decreases to zero, including whether the transition has a finite critical exponent or is of infinite order.
statement_caveat: This is the marginal renewal exponent alpha=1/2 with IID disorder and beta held fixed. The weak-disorder critical-point shift h_c(beta) as beta tends to zero, and the scaling limit in an intermediate-disorder critical window, are different questions. A quadratic smoothing upper bound is not a matching asymptotic. T215 concerns a copolymer whose disorder rewards entire excursions rather than renewal contacts; T177 concerns a hierarchical recursive model.
source: Q. Berger and H. Lacoin, Pinning on a defect line: characterization of marginal disorder relevance and sharp asymptotics for the critical point shift, arXiv:1503.07315v2 (2015), Section 2.5
locator: Section 2.5, 'Open questions', PDF p.6, immediately after (2.22): 'there is no general agreement on what the critical exponent should be for the disordered system as soon as hc(β) > 0.' The preceding sentence singles out alpha=1/2; (2.1)-(2.5) define the model.
why_important: Disordered pinning is the standard renewal model for the effect of quenched randomness on a phase transition. In the marginal Harris case, the critical point is understood much more precisely than the singularity at that point. Determining the singularity would distinguish competing finite-order and infinite-order pictures of disorder smoothing.
where_it_stands: Berger and Lacoin settle the marginal critical-point shift and give its weak-disorder asymptotics, while explicitly leaving this free-energy question open. The smoothing inequality gives F(beta,h_c+delta)<=3 delta^2/(4 beta^2). Wei and Yu's critical disordered pinning measure, arXiv:2402.17642v3, concerns intermediate disorder and does not compute the fixed-beta singularity. The 2024 localized-phase regularity and fluctuation results likewise hold strictly above criticality. Open.
note: Fame: the Harris disorder-relevance programme for pinning, developed in standard monographs and surveys; the source devotes its open-questions section to this missing critical behavior.

title: Rokhlin entropy of Bernoulli shifts over arbitrary countable groups
domain_name: Ergodic theory and stationary processes
statement: For every countably infinite group G and every standard probability space (L,lambda), is h_Rok(G acting on (L^G,lambda^G))=H(L,lambda)? Here G acts by the Bernoulli shift, H is the Shannon entropy of the base, taken as infinity for a base without countable support, and h_Rok is the infimum of the Shannon entropies of countable generating partitions of this ergodic probability-preserving action.
statement_caveat: The conjecture, called RBS by Seward, includes infinite base entropy. The inequality h_Rok<=H is immediate from the coordinate partition; the opposite inequality is the issue. The equality is known for sofic groups. The existence of a non-sofic group does not itself prove either a positive or a negative answer. Isomorphism of Bernoulli shifts with unequal base entropies is a consequence-level question, not a second row here. T034 and T092 concern mixing and spectrum of a single transformation.
source: B. Seward, Krieger's finite generator theorem for actions of countable groups II, arXiv:1501.03367v4 (2019), Introduction, statement RBS and Theorem 1.12
locator: Introduction, PDF p.3, displayed statement RBS: equality of Rokhlin entropy for the Bernoulli shift and Shannon entropy for the base. The following sentence says it 'may be true for all countably infinite groups G.' Definitions are on PDF pp.1-2.
why_important: Bernoulli shifts are the basic probability-preserving systems of independent random labels. This asks whether independence has its expected intrinsic entropy even when no finite approximation of the acting group is available. A positive answer would preserve the information content of IID sources under every measurable equivariant recoding.
where_it_stands: Seward proves the equality conditionally on positive Rokhlin entropy actions existing for every countably infinite group and establishes it for sofic groups. The inspected 2025-2026 entropy papers concern particular classes of actions or consequences of positive entropy, rather than a proof of RBS for all groups. The 2026 non-sofic-group announcement removes a possible shortcut through universal soficity but does not resolve RBS. Open.
note: Fame: a foundational entropy problem in measurable dynamics, posed explicitly alongside the general Bernoulli isomorphism problem in Seward's finite-generator theorem series.

title: Steele's variance-limit conjecture for the planar Euclidean traveling salesman problem
domain_name: Stochastic and geometric probability
statement: Let X_1,...,X_n be independent uniform points in [0,1]^2 and let L_n be the length of the shortest closed Euclidean tour through them. Prove that Var(L_n) converges to a constant as n tends to infinity, and identify that constant if possible.
statement_caveat: The variance here is unscaled, for the total tour length in the fixed unit square. This is a fluctuation question, distinct from T156, which asks for the constant in the first-order law L_n/sqrt(n). It is not the mean-field traveling salesman model with independent edge costs, and it is not a variance statement about an approximation algorithm. A central limit theorem alone without variance control would not establish the assertion.
source: S. Chatterjee, A general method for lower bounds on fluctuations of random variables, arXiv:1706.04290, Section 3, open problem (2)
locator: Section 3, PDF p.27, item (2): 'prove that the variance of the length of the optimal tour converges to a constant'. The item specifies uniform points on [0,1]^2 and attributes the conjecture to Mike Steele.
why_important: The Euclidean traveling salesman tour is a basic stochastic optimization functional with a well-understood law of large numbers but an unresolved fluctuation theory. Even convergence of its variance would be a substantial step toward a distributional limit and would test the reach of stabilization methods beyond locally determined functionals.
where_it_stands: The opened source explains that upper fluctuation bounds are well understood and recalls Rhee's lower bound of the correct order in dimension two. It still poses variance convergence explicitly. The inspected recent papers on finite-temperature mean-field optimization, one-dimensional bipartite tours and neural tour solvers do not establish this planar zero-temperature variance limit. No closing theorem was found in the recorded current-status searches. Open.
note: Fame: Steele's conjecture in a classical probabilistic optimization model, singled out in Chatterjee's general fluctuation paper and connected there to Steele's standard monograph.

title: Global convergence of the mean-field gradient flow for two-layer networks
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Let f_rho(x) = ∫ a·sigma(<w,x>) rho(da,dw) be a two-layer network written as an integral over a measure rho of neurons, and let rho_t be the Wasserstein gradient flow of the population square loss R(rho), the limit of gradient descent on a width-m network as m → ∞ under mean-field scaling. Prove that for ReLU units, Gaussian inputs, a target realizable by finitely many neurons and an initialization rho_0 such as a Gaussian (unbounded support, with a stated convention for the flow at the ReLU kink), the flow rho_t is well posed, R(rho_t) → inf R as t → ∞ without entropic regularization, and rho_t converges in W2 (these are separate questions: risk convergence does not imply convergence of the parameter law); give a rate.
statement_caveat: Chizat–Bach prove that IF the flow converges in W2 then the limit is a global minimizer, under hypotheses that include an initialization whose support is bounded (in a ball B(0, r_b)) and separates the spheres, plus technical conditions (Theorems 3.3 and 3.5, auditor codex-w687, 16 Oct); a Gaussian initialization is outside that scope. The open part is convergence itself, for natural initializations, and any rate. With added noise (mean-field Langevin, T225) convergence is known but the rate degrades with the temperature.
source: L. Chizat and F. Bach, On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Over-parameterized Models using Optimal Transport, arXiv:1805.09545 (2018); S. Mei, A. Montanari and P.-M. Nguyen, A Mean Field View of the Landscape of Two-Layers Neural Networks, arXiv:1804.06561 (2018)
locator: 1805.09545 Section 3.1 Theorem 3.3 (PDF p6) and Section 3.2 Theorem 3.5 (PDF p7); 1804.06561 Section 3 Theorem 3 (PDF p12) and Section 4 (PDF p15). Read by codex-w687, 16 Oct.
why_important: The mean-field limit is the cleanest probabilistic model of feature learning in neural networks; global convergence of its gradient flow is the basic question behind 'overparameterized networks are trained to global minima'.
where_it_stands: Open in the stated generality. Known: global convergence under entropic regularization (Mei–Montanari–Nguyen 1804.06561; Hu et al. 1905.07769; Chizat 2202.01009), for special symmetric targets and one-dimensional settings, and the conditional theorem of Chizat–Bach. Not re-checked against 2025–26 literature.
note: Fame: the Chizat–Bach and Mei–Montanari–Nguyen papers are among the most cited in deep-learning theory; the convergence gap is stated in many surveys (e.g. Bartlett–Montanari–Rakhlin 2103.09177).

audit.status_ref: arXiv:1805.09545, Theorems 3.3 and 3.5; arXiv:2605.10775, abstract and Section 1.3 (2026)
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify convergence topology, moment hypotheses and solution convention at ReLU singularities; distinguish risk convergence from convergence of the parameter law
audit.replace_with: Specify a well-posed ReLU population gradient flow and ask separately about risk convergence, W2 convergence and a rate under explicit moment/support conditions.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 1805.09545 Section 3.1 Theorem 3.3, PDF p6; Section 3.2 Theorem 3.5, PDF p7; 1804.06561 Section 3 Theorem 3, PDF p12, and Section 4 Discussion, PDF p15

title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for noiseless training of two-layer networks
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Train a width-m two-layer network by gradient descent (or online SGD with step epsilon) under mean-field scaling, and let mu^m_t be the empirical measure of the m neurons. Prove that, in a setting where the mean-field flow converges to a global minimizer, the risk gap |R(mu^m_t) − R(rho_t)| is O(m^{-1/2}) (or O(1/m) in expectation) uniformly over all t ≥ 0, with constants polynomial in the dimension, for the noiseless dynamics; equivalently for weak errors E|∫φ d(mu^m_t − rho_t)| with fixed smooth test functions φ. (A dimension-free m^{-1/2} rate cannot hold for W_2(mu^m_t, rho_t) itself: already at t = 0 the empirical measure of m iid neurons in parameter dimension p > 2 is at W_2 distance of order m^{-1/p} from its law.)
statement_caveat: Finite-horizon propagation of chaos (constants exponential in t) is known. Uniform-in-time bounds are known with entropic regularization (noise). The noiseless case without a convexity mechanism is the open part.
source: S. Mei, A. Montanari and P.-M. Nguyen, arXiv:1804.06561 (2018); J. Sirignano and K. Spiliopoulos, Mean Field Analysis of Neural Networks: A Law of Large Numbers, arXiv:1805.01053 (2018); G. M. Rotskoff and E. Vanden-Eijnden, arXiv:1805.00915 (2018)
locator: to verify: Mei–Montanari–Nguyen, the finite-time approximation theorem and the discussion of its time dependence.
why_important: Without uniform-in-time control the mean-field theory says nothing about networks trained to convergence; this is the bridge from the infinite-width picture to the finite networks actually trained.
where_it_stands: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos is proved for mean-field Langevin dynamics (F. Chen, Z. Ren and S. Wang 2212.03050; Suzuki–Wu–Nitanda 2306.07221). The noiseless case is open as far as the writer knows, but M. Glasgow et al., Uniform-in-Time Weak Propagation-of-Chaos in Shallow Neural Networks, arXiv:2605.22010 (2026), addresses it directly: read its theorem and hypotheses before anyone works this row (flagged by codex-w687, 16 Oct).
note: Fame: a standard open question of the mean-field theory, raised in the founding papers.

audit.status_ref: Margalit Glasgow and Joan Bruna, arXiv:2605.22010 (2026), Theorem 2 and Corollary 6, PDF pp13-14; independent t=0 W2 obstruction

audit.replace_with: A precisely specified noiseless weak-output PoC rate beyond Glasgow-Bruna's regularity and loss-decay assumptions; separate empirical W2 sampling error from particle-coupling error.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: verify the deterministic t=0 quantization obstruction, then formulate an explicit scalar-output rate gap relative to 2605.22010; do not assign the false W2 statement.
audit.locator: 1804.06561 Theorem 3, PDF pp12-13; 1805.01053 Theorems 1.2 and 1.6, Section 1; 1805.00915 Section 3; new 2605.22010 Theorem 2, PDF p13

title: Convergence time of mean-field Langevin dynamics at low temperature
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Mean-field Langevin dynamics minimizes F_lambda(rho) = R(rho) + lambda·KL(rho || pi) for a two-layer network risk R, where pi is a confining reference measure (e.g. a Gaussian prior, equivalently an L2 weight penalty plus entropy; with Lebesgue entropy on unbounded parameters F_lambda is unbounded below: spreading the output weights a as N(0, s²) independently of w leaves f_rho = 0 and the risk fixed while the entropy goes to −∞). It converges exponentially at a rate set by a uniform log-Sobolev constant of the proximal Gibbs measures, which in general is exp(−C/lambda). For a realizable two-layer regression problem in dimension d (smooth activation, Gaussian inputs, a teacher with a bounded number of neurons and bounded weights, all of which the bound may depend on polynomially), decide whether the time for MFLD (with lambda tuned or annealed) to reach risk R ≤ inf R + epsilon is polynomial in d and 1/epsilon, or prove an exponential lower bound.
statement_caveat: The question is about the unregularized risk reached through small lambda, not the regularized objective at fixed lambda. Chizat's theorems exclude the vanilla unbounded two-layer parameterization and note a smoothness issue for ReLU, so they do not cover plain ReLU (auditor codex-w687, 16 Oct).
source: L. Chizat, Mean-Field Langevin Dynamics: Exponential Convergence and Annealing, arXiv:2202.01009 (2022); A. Nitanda, D. Wu and T. Suzuki, Convex Analysis of the Mean Field Langevin Dynamics, arXiv:2201.10469 (2022)
locator: 2202.01009 Theorem 3.2 (Section 3, PDF p6), Theorem 4.1 (Section 4, PDF p7), discussion of Eq. (22) (Section 5.2, PDF p11); 2201.10469 Theorem 1. Read by codex-w687, 16 Oct.
why_important: MFLD is the one setting where global convergence of neural-network training is fully proved; whether its guarantees are ever efficient decides whether that proof says anything quantitative.
where_it_stands: Open. Exponential-in-1/lambda LSI constants are what the general theory gives; annealing gives only logarithmic convergence. Some structured targets (e.g. single-index) have polynomial guarantees in later work (to verify).
note: Fame: central question of the MFLD line (Chizat; Nitanda–Wu–Suzuki; Suzuki et al.).

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2202.01009 Theorems 3.2 and 4.1; arXiv:2201.10469 Theorem 1; independent entropy obstruction
audit.statement_ok: NO: risk plus Lebesgue entropy on unbounded neuron parameters is unbounded below without confinement; specify reference measure/domain, teacher size and norm bounds, activation, input law, initialization, annealing schedule and runtime dependence
audit.replace_with: Specify a confining potential or prior and a normalized teacher/input class, then ask for polynomial low-temperature complexity with all model parameters included.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: prove the entropy nonexistence obstruction and repair the objective; the repaired polynomial-time problem is a programme.
audit.locator: 2202.01009 Theorem 3.2, Section 3; Theorem 4.1, Section 4; discussion of Eq.(22), PDF p11; 2201.10469 Theorem 1, Section 3

title: The edge of stability: why full-batch gradient descent hovers at sharpness 2/eta
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: For full-batch gradient descent with fixed step eta on a neural-network training loss, the top Hessian eigenvalue first rises to about 2/eta and then hovers there while the loss keeps decreasing non-monotonically (Cohen et al.). Fix a model (e.g. a smooth two-layer network of moderate width on Gaussian data with square loss, or a deep linear network), an initialization law and a range of eta. Prove that with probability bounded below over the initialization GD enters the edge-of-stability regime, stays there, and converges to a global minimizer whose sharpness is 2/eta + o(1) as eta → 0 (or show the event has small probability). Local theorems near a minimizing manifold (Gan 2026, Theorem 4.4, assumes a C4 loss and a nondegeneracy condition) leave open whether random initialization reaches their basin.
statement_caveat: Results that assume a specific cubic structure of the loss, or study two-parameter toy models, are partial. Divergence above the classical 2/L threshold is NOT what happens: the point is convergence without the descent-lemma condition.
source: J. M. Cohen, S. Kaur, Y. Li, J. Z. Kolter and A. Talwalkar, Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability, arXiv:2103.00065 (2021)
locator: 2103.00065 Sections 1-3 (empirical); E. Gan, arXiv:2606.15551 (2026), Theorem 4.4 (local convergence at the threshold). Read by codex-w687, 16 Oct.
why_important: Classical optimization theory says GD with step above 2/L diverges; every practical network is trained in exactly that regime. A theory of it is one of the main gaps between optimization theory and practice.
where_it_stands: Partial: self-stabilization under assumptions on third derivatives (Damian, Nichani and Lee 2209.15594); Arora, Li and Panigrahi 2205.09745 for normalized losses; Ahn et al. 2204.01050; analyses of two-layer and scalar toy models. Open for genuine networks (not re-checked against 2025–26).
note: Fame: one of the most discussed empirical phenomena of deep-learning optimization since 2021.

audit.status_ref: Eric Gan, arXiv:2606.15551 (2026), Theorem 4.4 (page locator checked separately)
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify network/data model, loss, initialization law, learning-rate range and asymptotic for o(1); generic initialization need not yield entry into an edge regime or exact limiting sharpness
audit.replace_with: Fix a smooth network and data law and ask whether random initialization enters the local basin covered by a stated edge-of-stability theorem, with a quantified probability and sharpness tolerance.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 2103.00065 Sections 1-3, progressive sharpening and edge-of-stability experiments; 2606.15551 Theorem 4.4 (local convergence at the threshold)

title: The catapult phase of large-learning-rate training
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Lewkowycz et al. observe for wide networks three regimes in the step eta relative to lambda_0, the top eigenvalue of the neural tangent kernel at initialization: lazy for eta < 2/lambda_0, a catapult phase for 2/lambda_0 < eta < eta_max ≈ c/lambda_0 in which the loss first grows, the curvature drops, and training then converges, and divergence above eta_max. Prove the existence of the catapult phase and identify eta_max for a fixed deep nonlinear architecture of large finite width (stated activation, input and label law, normalization of the initialization), as an eta interval on which the loss rises and then converges with high probability.
statement_caveat: The two-layer linear 'uv' model is solved in the original paper; the question is about nonlinear and deep networks.
source: A. Lewkowycz, Y. Bahri, E. Dyer, J. Sohl-Dickstein and G. Gur-Ari, The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism, arXiv:2003.02218 (2020)
locator: 2003.02218 Sections 2-3 (the solvable uv model, eta_max = 4/lambda_0 there) and the Figure 3 discussion, PDF p7: for the ReLU networks of the experiments, 'eta_max ≈ 12/lambda_0 is a good predictor' (an empirical value with that paper's normalization). Corrected by codex-w687, 16 Oct.
why_important: Explains why large learning rates give flatter minima and better generalization; it is the infinite-width counterpart of the edge of stability (T226).
where_it_stands: Proved for the uv model and some quadratic models (Zhu et al. 2022-23, to verify). Open for deep nonlinear networks.
note: Fame: widely cited (catapult mechanism), a standard example in large-learning-rate theory.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2003.02218 Sections 2-3; arXiv:2607.04993 (2026), opened source describes solvable finite-step models

audit.replace_with: Fix a finite-width nonlinear network and normalized input/label law; define an eta interval and a high-probability loss-growth-then-convergence event, and bound its endpoints.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 2003.02218 Sections 2-3, solvable uv dynamics and Figure 3 discussion, PDF p7

title: Heavy-tailed stationary behaviour of SGD on neural-network losses
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Simsekli et al. observed that SGD gradient noise in deep networks is heavy-tailed, and Gurbuzbalaban, Simsekli and Zhu proved for linear regression that the SGD iterates converge to a stationary law with power-law tails whose index alpha decreases as eta/b (step over batch) grows. The same paper states a criterion for nonlinear recursions (its Theorem 1, Mirek-type asymptotically linear random maps). Verify it for a concrete nonlinear model: e.g. constant-step SGD with batch b on a generalized linear model or a two-layer network with a smooth bounded activation, Gaussian inputs and persistent label noise. Prove that the iterates have a stationary law, that the recursion contracts on average and is asymptotically linear with a non-arithmetic multiplier and a nonzero tail constant, so that the stationary tail is a power law with index given by the Lyapunov equation, with alpha < 2 in a nonempty range of (eta, b).
statement_caveat: For linear regression the result follows from Kesten's theory of random affine recursions; nonlinear networks give non-affine random iterations. Monotonicity of the index in eta/b is proved under Gaussian data (assumption A3) and alpha >= 1 (auditor codex-w687, 16 Oct).
source: M. Gurbuzbalaban, U. Simsekli and L. Zhu, The Heavy-Tail Phenomenon in SGD, arXiv:2006.04740 (2020); U. Simsekli, L. Sagun and M. Gurbuzbalaban, A Tail-Index Analysis of Stochastic Gradient Noise in Deep Neural Networks, arXiv:1901.06053 (2019)
locator: 2006.04740 Theorem 1 (PDF p4); Theorems 2-4 and Proposition 5 (PDF pp7-8). Read by codex-w687, 16 Oct.
why_important: Heavy tails change what 'SGD finds' (Lévy-driven rather than Brownian exploration) and have been tied to generalization; a theorem for nonlinear models would turn an empirical claim into probability.
where_it_stands: Linear case proved; nonlinear results under strong assumptions only (to verify). Open in general.
note: Fame: connects SGD to Kesten's random recursion theory; widely cited line.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2006.04740, Theorem 1 (Mirek-type nonlinear recursions), PDF p4; Theorems 2-4 and Proposition 5, PDF pp7-8

audit.replace_with: Choose a concrete nonlinear regression law and prove average contraction, asymptotic linearity, a nonarithmetic multiplier and a nondegenerate tail constant before asking for the tail index.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: a scalar smooth bounded perturbation of linear regression may satisfy the already-stated Mirek criterion; verify all recurrence and tail-nondegeneracy hypotheses explicitly.
audit.locator: 2006.04740 Section 3.1 Theorem 1, PDF p4; Section 3.2 Theorems 2-4 and Proposition 5, PDF pp7-8; 1901.06053 Section 5 Conclusion and Open Problems, PDF pp10-11

title: Where label-noise SGD goes on the manifold of interpolating minima
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: For an overparameterized loss whose zero set is a manifold Gamma, SGD with label noise and small step eta, run for time of order eta^{-2}, follows in the limit eta → 0 a deterministic flow on Gamma that decreases tr(∇²L) (Blanc et al.; Damian et al.; Li, Wang and Arora). Gatmiry, Li, Reddi and Jegelka (arXiv:2410.16401, Theorem 3.5) prove that the flow reaches a global minimizer of the sharpness for an explicit class of smooth two-layer networks under their Assumptions 3.1, 3.2 and 3.4. Prove the same for a class outside those assumptions (two-layer ReLU networks, or networks of depth L >= 3) on generic data, or give a non-asymptotic bound on the distance to the sharpness minimizer at finite eta.
statement_caveat: The limit theorem is known under smoothness and manifold assumptions; the open parts are the global behaviour of the limiting flow and finite-eta control.
source: Z. Li, T. Wang and S. Arora, What Happens after SGD Reaches Zero Loss? A Mathematical Framework, arXiv:2110.06914 (2021); A. Damian, T. Ma and J. D. Lee, Label Noise SGD Provably Prefers Flat Global Minimizers, arXiv:2106.06530 (2021); G. Blanc et al., arXiv:1904.09080 (2019)
locator: to verify: Li–Wang–Arora, the limiting-flow theorem and the open directions in the conclusion.
why_important: This is the cleanest mechanism proposed for the implicit regularization of SGD noise toward flat minima.
where_it_stands: Limiting flow proved (Li–Wang–Arora, Corollary 5.2); convergence to stationary points of a regularized loss (Damian–Ma–Lee); global sharpness minimization for an explicit smooth two-layer class (Gatmiry et al. 2024). Open for ReLU and deeper networks and at finite eta (auditor codex-w687, 16 Oct).
note: Fame: well known line on SGD implicit regularization (Blanc et al.; HaoChen et al.; Damian et al.; Li et al.).

audit.replace_with: State a specific ReLU or deeper-network class outside the activation/data assumptions of 2410.16401, or request a precise finite-eta rate beyond its small-step theorem.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME

title: Sample complexity of gradient descent with sample reuse for single-index models
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Let y = g(<w*,x>) + noise with x ~ N(0, I_d) and unknown unit w*. Online SGD on a two-layer network needs n ≍ d^{max(1, k*−1)} samples, k* the information exponent of g (Ben Arous, Gheissari and Jagannath). Statistical-query lower bounds give n ≳ d^{max(1, k_gen/2)}, k_gen the generative exponent (Damian et al. 2024). Fix the class: g a polynomial link with label noise of a fixed law (the generative exponent depends on the conditional law of y), recovery of w* up to the link's symmetries, and a standard two-layer network with no preprocessing of the labels, trained by multi-pass SGD with a stated batch size, step-size schedule and number of passes over n samples. Determine whether it learns w* with n = d^{max(1, k_gen/2)+o(1)} samples, or prove it cannot.
statement_caveat: Algorithms that transform the labels before running a spectral or tensor method are known to reach the SQ bound; the question is about ordinary gradient training.
source: G. Ben Arous, R. Gheissari and A. Jagannath, Online stochastic gradient descent on non-convex losses from high-dimensional inference, arXiv:2003.10409 (2020); A. Damian, L. Pillaud-Vivien, J. D. Lee and J. Bruna, Computational-Statistical Gaps in Gaussian Single-Index Models, arXiv:2403.05529 (2024)
locator: to verify: Damian et al. 2403.05529, the introduction's open questions on whether gradient methods reach the generative-exponent bound.
why_important: Single-index models are the standard probe of what gradient training can learn in high dimension; this decides whether 'data reuse' changes the sample-complexity exponent of SGD.
where_it_stands: Partial: reuse and large steps already reach part of the range for specific algorithms (Lee, Oko, Suzuki and Wu, arXiv:2406.01581, Theorems 1-2; arXiv:2510.21020, Theorem 3.3, learning-rate phase transitions from the information to the generative exponent; full-batch GD versus one-pass SGD, arXiv:2602.02431, Theorem 3.1; Dandi et al. 2024). Smoothed online SGD matches the CSQ bound d^{k*/2} (Damian et al. 2305.10633). Full question open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: a central current question of high-dimensional learning theory (Ben Arous; Bruna; Lee; Krzakala–Zdeborová groups).

title: The leap-complexity conjecture for SGD on multi-index functions
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: For a function f(x) = h(x_1,...,x_P) of P coordinates of x uniform on {−1,1}^d (or Gaussian), Abbe, Boix-Adserà and Misiakiewicz define the leap complexity Leap(h). Their Conjecture 1: for fixed P = O_d(1), h outside a measure-zero set of coefficients, and a rotationally invariant initialization, online SGD on a two-layer network learns f with Θ̃(d^{max(Leap(h)−1, 1)}) samples (sample or iteration complexity; arithmetic time is separate). Prove the conjecture for standard joint training, or for a first finite family of supports not covered by their layer-wise theorem.
statement_caveat: The authors prove the upper bound for a modified layer-wise training procedure and a CSQ lower bound; the conjecture is about standard joint SGD training.
source: E. Abbe, E. Boix-Adserà and T. Misiakiewicz, SGD learning on neural networks: leap complexity and saddle-to-saddle dynamics, arXiv:2302.11055 (2023); The merged-staircase property, arXiv:2202.08658 (2022)
locator: 2302.11055 Conjecture 1 (PDF p6); Theorem 1 (PDF pp11-12) and Theorem 2. Corrected by codex-w687, 16 Oct: the conjecture carries genericity, fixed-P and initialization hypotheses, and does not assert one plateau per leap for every support.
why_important: Gives a single combinatorial quantity predicting what SGD can learn in polynomial time; proving it would be a structure theorem for feature learning.
where_it_stands: Open for standard training; proved for leap one (merged staircase, 2202.08658) under layer-wise training and in several special cases (to verify).
note: Fame: a named conjecture from a widely cited 2023 COLT paper.

title: Saddle-to-saddle dynamics of deep linear networks from small initialization
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Train a deep linear network W_L···W_1 by gradient flow on a square loss from initialization scale alpha → 0. Jacot et al. prove the escape from the saddle at the origin; the escape time is of order log(1/alpha) for L = 2 and of order alpha^{-(L-2)} for L > 2 (their Theorem 2). Their Conjecture 3: under genericity assumptions on the singular values of the data, the trajectory passes in the limit near a sequence of saddles that are local minima of the loss restricted to width k = 1, 2, ..., along translated paths. Prove the next step (the passage from the width-1 to the width-2 saddle) for general data and depth L ≥ 2 without commuting or diagonal assumptions, or the whole sequence.
statement_caveat: Pesme and Flammarion prove the analogous picture for diagonal linear networks.
source: A. Jacot, F. Ged, B. Simsek, C. Hongler and F. Gabriel, Saddle-to-Saddle Dynamics in Deep Linear Networks: Small Initialization Training, Symmetry, and Sparsity, arXiv:2106.15933 (2021); S. Pesme and N. Flammarion, Saddle-to-Saddle Dynamics in Diagonal Linear Networks, arXiv:2304.00488 (2023)
locator: 2106.15933 Theorem 2 and the paragraph after it (PDF p5), Conjecture 3 (PDF p6), Appendix C.5. Corrected by codex-w687, 16 Oct (the escape time is logarithmic only for L = 2).
why_important: Incremental learning (one feature at a time) is the mechanism behind low-rank implicit bias; this is the basic solvable case.
where_it_stands: Diagonal case proved; first steps for the general case proved by Jacot et al.; full sequence open (not re-checked).
note: Fame: a stated conjecture in a well-cited paper, part of the implicit-bias program.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2106.15933 Theorem 2 PDF p5, Conjecture 3 PDF p6, Appendix C.5; arXiv:2304.00488 Theorem 2
audit.statement_ok: NO: logarithmic escape time is wrong for L>2; original source gives alpha^(-(L-2)); exact ranks 0,1,2,... and final globally minimum rank are stronger than the source's local width-k saddle statement
audit.replace_with: State Conjecture 3 faithfully with the depth-dependent escape scaling, singular-value/genericity assumptions and width-k local minima; ask for a specific next-saddle theorem.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: rederive the scalar homogeneous escape scaling and correct the conjecture; full noncommuting saddle sequence remains a programme.
audit.locator: Jacot et al. Section 5 Theorem 2, PDF p5; Conjecture 3, PDF p6; Appendix C.5 for escape times; Pesme-Flammarion Theorem 2

title: Width needed for gradient descent on deep linear networks from random initialization
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Depth-L linear network f(x) = alpha W_L ... W_1 x, W_i with iid N(0,1) entries, hidden widths m, input dimension d_x, output dimension d_y, alpha = (m^(L-1) d_y)^(-1/2) (the normalization of Du and Hu, arXiv:1901.08572), square loss on data X of rank r and condition number kappa, gradient descent with step eta <= d_y/(2 L ||X||^2). Du and Hu prove polynomial-time convergence when m grows linearly with L (up to logs); Shamir (arXiv:1809.08587) shows that width independent of L fails (time exponential in L) for scalar output. Let T(L, m) be the number of steps to reach loss eps with probability 1 - delta. For fixed d_x, d_y, r, kappa, the target norm, delta and eps, prove that log T(L, m) = Theta(L/m) + O(log L) uniformly over d_x <= m <= L, so that the time is polynomial exactly when L/m = O(log L); in particular decide whether at m = c L the time is polynomial for every fixed c > 0.
statement_caveat: Narrow networks (width one) need time exponential in L (Shamir); Du and Hu show width growing linearly in L suffices; orthogonal initialization removes the L dependence (Hu, Xiao and Pennington 2020).
source: S. S. Du and W. Hu, Width Provably Matters in Optimization for Deep Linear Neural Networks, arXiv:1901.08572 (2019); O. Shamir, arXiv:1809.08587 (2018); S. Arora, N. Cohen, N. Golowich and W. Hu, arXiv:1810.02281 (2018)
locator: to verify: Du–Hu, introduction and conclusion on whether the linear-in-L width is necessary for Gaussian initialization.
why_important: Deep linear networks are the simplest model where depth makes optimization hard; the width-depth trade-off for random initialization is a basic question about products of random matrices in training.
where_it_stands: Open for Gaussian initialization as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: a standard open question of deep linear network theory.

audit.status_ref: Du-Hu arXiv:1901.08572 Theorem 4.1; Shamir arXiv:1809.08587
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify input and output dimensions, Gaussian variance/normalization, target operator norm, learning-rate choice, failure probability and conditioning; a function m(L,d) alone does not fix the problem
audit.replace_with: Fix scalar output, whitened bounded-norm data and the Du-Hu Gaussian normalization, then determine whether polynomial convergence needs width growing with depth, with explicit confidence dependence.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: test a fixed small width and scalar input/output via Gaussian matrix-product Lyapunov estimates, checking whether small initial prediction/gradients imply a depth-dependent lower bound.
audit.locator: 1901.08572 Section 4 Theorem 4.1 and its discussion; width lower/upper comparison in introduction/conclusion; 1809.08587 for scalar-depth obstruction

title: The implicit bias of gradient descent in matrix sensing with small initialization
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Matrix sensing: y_i = <A_i, M*> with symmetric Gaussian A_i, i <= n, and M* PSD of rank r in R^(d x d); fit M = U U^T with U in R^(d x d) by gradient flow from U_0 = alpha U_init. Jin, Li, Lyu, Du and Lee (arXiv:2301.11500, Theorem 4.1) prove that as alpha -> 0, with time of order log(1/alpha), the trajectory follows greedy low-rank learning and recovers M* when the measurements satisfy a restricted isometry property of the order they need; Gunasekar et al. (arXiv:1705.09280) conjecture convergence to the minimum nuclear norm solution. For n Gaussian measurements below what that RIP hypothesis requires but above the information-theoretic order d r, decide whether the alpha -> 0 limit of gradient flow is the minimum-rank solution, the minimum-nuclear-norm solution, or neither, and whether it equals M*; and state the same for gradient descent with a fixed small step, which can differ from the flow.
statement_caveat: Gunasekar et al. conjectured convergence to the minimum nuclear-norm solution; Razin and Cohen gave settings where gradient flow drives the nuclear norm to infinity and the bias is better read as rank minimization. The open problem is the full characterization.
source: S. Gunasekar, B. Woodworth, S. Bhojanapalli, B. Neyshabur and N. Srebro, Implicit Regularization in Matrix Factorization, arXiv:1705.09280 (2017); N. Razin and N. Cohen, Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning May Not Be Explainable by Norms, arXiv:2005.06398 (2020); S. Arora, N. Cohen, W. Hu and Y. Luo, arXiv:1905.13655 (2019)
locator: to verify: Gunasekar et al., the stated conjecture in Section 1; Razin–Cohen, the counterexample setting.
why_important: Matrix sensing is the model problem for implicit regularization; its answer decides whether 'gradient descent minimizes a norm' or 'gradient descent minimizes rank' is the right picture.
where_it_stands: Nuclear-norm form refuted in some settings (Razin–Cohen); greedy rank picture proved under assumptions (Li, Luo and Lyu 2021; later work — to verify). Full characterization open.
note: Fame: the Gunasekar conjecture is one of the best-known conjectures of implicit-bias theory.

audit.status_ref: Jin-Li-Lyu-Du-Lee arXiv:2301.11500 Theorem 4.1 PDF p7; Gunasekar et al. arXiv:1705.09280 Conjecture Section 3
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify measurement count/RIP regime, initialization, order of alpha-to-zero and long-time limits, the precise greedy algorithm and the asserted minimum-rank comparison; a request to characterize under unspecified conditions is a programme
audit.replace_with: Specify an underdetermined Gaussian PSD sensing regime outside the existing RIP/initialization results and ask for a definite trajectory or recovery statement, keeping GD and gradient flow distinct.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 1705.09280 Section 3 Conjecture; 2005.06398 Section 3 matrix-completion construction; 2301.11500 Theorem 4.1 PDF p7 and Assumptions 3.1-3.3

title: A proof of grokking for modular arithmetic under standard training
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Modular addition: inputs are the one-hot codes of (a, b) in Z_p x Z_p, a two-layer network of width m with a stated activation (quadratic or ReLU) and p output logits, Gaussian initialization of a stated scale, cross-entropy loss, a training set that is a uniformly random fraction rho of the p^2 pairs, full-batch gradient descent with step eta and weight decay lambda. Prove that for rho in a stated range, as p -> infinity, the training error reaches 0 by a time T_1 = O(log p / eta) while the test accuracy stays at chance + o(1) until a time c/(eta lambda), and exceeds 1 - o(1) after C log p/(eta lambda), and that the hidden weights then concentrate on Fourier features of Z_p. Lyu et al. (arXiv:2311.18817, Theorems 3.4-3.5) prove delayed generalization from a dichotomy of early (kernel) and late (small-norm) implicit biases for homogeneous networks with large initialization and small weight decay; the transformer and AdamW experiment of Power et al. (arXiv:2201.02177) is a different model.
statement_caveat: Theorems exist for modified settings (large initialization, homogeneous networks, specific losses); the question is the standard grokking setting of Power et al.
source: A. Power, Y. Burda, H. Edwards, I. Babuschkin and V. Misra, Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets, arXiv:2201.02177 (2022); K. Lyu, J. Jin, Z. Li, S. S. Du, J. D. Lee and W. Hu, Dichotomy of Early and Late Phase Implicit Biases Can Provably Induce Grokking, arXiv:2311.18817 (2023)
locator: to verify: Lyu et al., introduction (what is proved and what remains for standard settings).
why_important: Grokking is the most famous example of delayed generalization; a proof in its native setting would be a test case for any theory of training dynamics.
where_it_stands: Partial (Lyu et al. 2311.18817; Kumar et al. 2310.06110; max-margin features for modular addition, Morwani et al. 2311.07568). Native setting open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: grokking is a widely known phenomenon (2022 onward).

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2311.18817 Theorems 3.4-3.5 PDF p6; arXiv:2201.02177 Section 2 and Appendix A.1.2 PDF p6
audit.statement_ok: NO: fix p/width/split asymptotics, input encoding, activation, initialization law/scale, learning rate, test criterion and constants in the claimed times; a fraction of the table is not sufficient to guarantee grokking
audit.replace_with: Choose one precisely specified modular-addition architecture and split law, then formulate a quantified delayed-generalization statement; do not call it identical to Power et al.'s transformer/AdamW experiment.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 2201.02177 Section 2 Method PDF p2; Appendix A.1.2 Model and Optimization PDF p6; 2311.18817 Theorems 3.4-3.5 PDF p6

title: Mild overparameterization suffices to learn a planted ReLU teacher
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Inputs x ~ N(0, I_d); teacher y = sum_{j<=k} relu(v_j . x) with orthonormal v_j and output weights 1, the model in which Safran and Shamir (arXiv:1712.08968) find spurious local minima for an exactly matched student (k >= 6) and observe that mild over-parameterization helps. Student sum_{i<=k'} relu(w_i . x) with output weights fixed to 1, square loss, Gaussian initialization of a stated scale, online SGD (or gradient descent on the population loss) with a constant step. Prove that for k' = k + c with a fixed c, or k' = k polylog(k), the student reaches population loss epsilon with probability at least 1 - delta in time and samples poly(d, k, 1/epsilon, log(1/delta)); or show that a student of width k + c still fails with probability bounded below. The absence of bad local minima for the wider student is a separate, weaker question.
statement_caveat: With exactly k student units spurious local minima are common and GD often fails (Safran and Shamir). With k' polynomially larger than k, kernel-regime results apply but give poor sample complexity.
source: I. Safran and O. Shamir, Spurious Local Minima are Common in Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks, arXiv:1712.08968 (2017)
locator: to verify: Safran–Shamir, final section on the effect of overparameterization (stated as open).
why_important: Teacher-student learning is the simplest test of whether gradient descent can learn a network; the role of mild overparameterization is a long-standing question.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows; results for k' = k + 1 in restricted settings (Safran, Yehudai and Shamir 2021, to verify).
note: Fame: a well-known open question since Safran–Shamir 2017.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:1712.08968 Introduction PDF p2 and Theorem 1; current quantitative mild-width frontier not verified
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify teacher coefficient/norm bounds, separation/genericity, output-layer parametrization, student activation, loss, initialization scale, step schedule and error probability; polynomial dependence only on d,k,epsilon cannot cover unbounded conditioning
audit.replace_with: Fix the original positive-output orthogonal-teacher model, a normalized teacher and a specific mildly wider student; separate absence of bad minima from a high-probability polynomial SGD guarantee.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 1712.08968 Introduction, PDF p2, paragraph comparing n=k,k+1,k+2 and Eq.(2); experimental discussion Section 3

title: The minimal overparameterization for gradient descent to fit n samples
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Two-layer network f(x) = m^(-1/2) sum_{j<=m} a_j sigma(w_j . x / sqrt d) with a fixed smooth activation (or ReLU), output weights a_j = +-1 fixed, first layer trained, no biases, w_j iid N(0, I_d); n samples x_i iid uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt d with arbitrary labels bounded by 1; square loss; gradient descent with a stated step; n of order d^k for a fixed k >= 1. Prove that with probability at least 1 - delta gradient descent reaches training loss epsilon in poly(n, log(1/epsilon)) steps as soon as m d >= C n log^a(n) log(1/delta) for an absolute a (the counting bound up to logs), or show that more width is needed. The neural tangent kernel is well conditioned at m d of order n up to logs (Bombari, Amani and Mondelli, arXiv:2205.10217, Theorem 4; see T253), but the existing gradient-descent guarantees (Oymak and Soltanolkotabi, arXiv:1902.04674, Theorem 2.1) need more width.
statement_caveat: Neural-tangent-kernel proofs need m ≥ poly(n) (quadratic and later subquadratic in n); the conjectured optimum is linear in the number of samples.
source: S. Oymak and M. Soltanolkotabi, Towards moderate overparameterization: global convergence guarantees for training shallow neural networks, arXiv:1902.04674 (2019); C. Song, A. Ramezani-Kebrya, T. Pethick, A. Eftekhari and V. Cevher, Subquadratic Overparameterization for Shallow Neural Networks, arXiv:2111.01875 (2021); S. S. Du et al., arXiv:1810.02054 (2018)
locator: to verify: Oymak–Soltanolkotabi, discussion of the gap to md ≈ n.
why_important: Global convergence of GD is proved only for absurd widths; the natural conjecture that 'parameters ≈ samples' suffices would bring theory to the regime of practice.
where_it_stands: Open; best known bounds subquadratic in n (to verify current record).
note: Fame: stated as the key open problem in many overparameterization papers.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:1902.04674 Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2; arXiv:2111.01875; current optimality claim not certified; Bombari-Amani-Mondelli arXiv:2205.10217, Theorem 4 PDF p10
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify activation and trained layers, loss, label bound, biases, initialization/step scaling, dimension/sample regime, probability and numerical interpolation tolerance; a parameter count alone is not a universal GD guarantee
audit.replace_with: Choose a fixed smooth or ReLU two-layer architecture and specify all trained weights and dimension regimes; ask for a near-linear parameter GD theorem with an explicit failure probability.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 1902.04674 Theorem 2.1 PDF pp4-5, Corollary 2.2 and remaining-gap discussion PDF p5; 2111.01875 Introduction and network-specialization section

title: The transition between the lazy and the rich regime
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Single-index teacher y = g(v . x), x ~ N(0, I_d), |v| = 1; student f(x) = alpha m^(-1) sum_{j<=m} a_j relu(w_j . x) minus its value at initialization, with Gaussian initialization, square loss on n samples, gradient flow up to time T; limits m -> infinity first, then n, d -> infinity with n/d^k fixed. Chizat, Oyallon and Bach (arXiv:1812.07956) show lazy (linearized) training as alpha -> infinity; Woodworth et al. (arXiv:2002.09277) describe the transition for diagonal linear networks. Determine the window of alpha, as a function of d and n, across which the distance between the trained predictor and the linearized (kernel) predictor goes from o(1) to order 1, and the test error across that window.
statement_caveat: Woodworth et al. solve the analogous question for diagonal linear networks; Chizat, Oyallon and Bach establish the lazy regime for large alpha.
source: B. Woodworth et al., Kernel and Rich Regimes in Overparametrized Models, arXiv:2002.09277 (2020); L. Chizat, E. Oyallon and F. Bach, On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming, arXiv:1812.07956 (2018)
locator: to verify: Woodworth et al., discussion section (extension beyond diagonal linear networks posed as open).
why_important: Whether a trained network behaves like a kernel or learns features is the main dichotomy of deep-learning theory; the crossover is where real networks seem to live.
where_it_stands: Diagonal linear case solved; partial results for two-layer networks (to verify). Open.
note: Fame: the lazy/rich dichotomy is standard in the field.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2002.09277 Theorem 1 PDF p4 and Theorem 2; arXiv:1812.07956 Theorems 2.2-2.3
audit.statement_ok: NO: define architecture/activation, normalization of alpha, loss, target class, time horizon/order of limits, training algorithm and an observable/tolerance defining the lazy-rich boundary; 'natural target class' is not a fixed model
audit.replace_with: Fix a normalized two-layer teacher-student model and an order of m,n,d,alpha limits; quantify departure of predictions from the linearized model and test error across a specified scaling window.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 2002.09277 Section 4 Theorem 1, PDF p4, interpolation by hypentropy; 1812.07956 Section 2 Theorems 2.2-2.3, general finite-time lazy-training bounds; Woodworth et al. Section 7, PDF p9, nonlinear-model discussion

title: Dynamical mean-field theory for gradient descent on two-layer networks in the proportional regime
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Teacher y = sum_{j<=k} sigma(v_j . x / sqrt d) plus noise, x ~ N(0, I_d), n samples; student of width p with trained first layer and fixed readout scaled by 1/p; square loss with a stated ridge; full-batch gradient flow; n/d -> alpha. Rigorous dynamical mean-field (DMFT) limits of the training and test errors are known when the widths p and k stay fixed as d grows (Celentano, Cheng and Montanari; Gerbelot et al. arXiv:2302.05882, Theorems 3.1-3.5; arXiv:2602.06320, Theorem 3.2). Prove the finite-horizon DMFT limit, on every bounded time interval, in the extensive-width regime p/d -> beta and k/d -> beta_* with fixed beta, beta_* > 0. The long-time limit and its commutation with d -> infinity are a separate question (see T266).
statement_caveat: DMFT is proved for generalized linear models and fixed-width networks with many samples (Celentano, Cheng and Montanari 2021; Gerbelot et al.). The proportional-width case is open.
source: L. Arnaboldi, L. Stephan, F. Krzakala and B. Loureiro, From high-dimensional & mean-field dynamics to dimensionless ODEs, arXiv:2302.05882 (2023); S. Goldt, M. Advani, A. Saxe, F. Krzakala and L. Zdeborová, arXiv:1906.08632 (2019)
locator: to verify: open directions in Arnaboldi et al. (extensive width).
why_important: An exact, rigorous description of training curves in the regime where width, data and dimension are comparable would be the analogue of the random-features double-descent theory for trained networks.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows; physics-level predictions exist.
note: Fame: part of the statistical-physics program for learning dynamics.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:1906.08632 Theorem 1.1; arXiv:2302.05882 Theorems 3.1-3.5; arXiv:2602.06320 Theorem 3.2 PDF p7
audit.statement_ok: NO: fix student/teacher widths and scaling, activation, initialization, loss, noise and time normalization; specify finite-time versus long-time convergence and whether their limits commute
audit.replace_with: State a finite-horizon theorem for an explicit offline extensive-width model and keep the long-time error problem distinct from T266's final double-descent curve.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 2302.05882 Section 3 Theorems 3.1-3.5 (online-SGD overlap ODE approximations); 1906.08632 Theorem 1.1; new 2602.06320 Theorem 3.2 PDF p7

title: Escape from the symmetric plateau in teacher-student committee machines
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Soft committee machine with K = M = 2: student f(x) = g(w_1 . x/sqrt N) + g(w_2 . x/sqrt N), teacher y = g(v_1 . x/sqrt N) + g(v_2 . x/sqrt N), g(z) = erf(z/sqrt 2), output weights fixed to 1, v_n . v_m/N = delta_nm, x ~ N(0, I_N), noiseless labels; online SGD with one fresh sample per step and step eta/sqrt N, time t = steps/N; initialization iid uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt(N q0). For each eta in an interval where the symmetric fixed point of the Saad-Solla ODE is hyperbolic with one unstable direction (eigenvalue lambda(eta)), prove that the specialization time tau_N = inf{t : |R_11 - R_12| > delta} satisfies tau_N / log N -> 1/(2 lambda(eta)) in probability and that the generalization error tends to 0 after tau_N; then K > M >= 2 and other activations.
statement_caveat: The ODE limit itself is proved (Goldt et al. 2019); the global behaviour of the ODE system is the open part.
source: S. Goldt, M. Advani, A. M. Saxe, F. Krzakala and L. Zdeborová, Dynamics of stochastic gradient descent for two-layer neural networks in the teacher-student setup, arXiv:1906.08632 (2019)
locator: to verify: Section 2 (ODE theorem) and the discussion of plateaus.
why_important: Plateaus are the classic statistical-physics picture of learning (Saad–Solla 1995); proving them closes a thirty-year-old loop between physics and rigorous probability.
where_it_stands: Open in general; special cases (K = M = 1, 2) analysed (to verify).
note: Fame: Saad–Solla dynamics is a classic of the physics of learning.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:1906.08632 Theorem 1.1, PDF p4; Section 2 and supplementary Section C
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify activation, noiseless versus noisy labels, teacher Gram matrix, fixed/trained output weights, initialization, learning-rate range and the time normalization for O(log d); distinguish finite-d perturbations from an exactly symmetric limiting ODE state
audit.replace_with: For a fixed noiseless erf committee K=M=2 with a specified stable learning rate, compute the transverse unstable eigenvalue and prove logarithmic-time tracking from finite-d random perturbations.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: symbolically linearize the explicit small committee overlap ODE at its symmetric plateau and determine the symmetry-breaking eigenvalue; global convergence for every K>=M is a programme.
audit.locator: 1906.08632 Theorem 1.1 PDF p4; SCM plateau discussion PDF p5; supplementary Section C for eight-overlap reduction and perturbative fixed points

title: Global convergence of feature-learning infinite-width limits of deep networks
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Three-layer network of width m in the maximal-update parametrization of Yang and Hu (arXiv:2011.14522): f(x) = m^(-1) a . phi(W_2 phi(W_1 x)), W_1 entries N(0, 1/d), W_2 entries N(0, 1/m), a entries N(0, 1), learning rates scaled as in muP, a smooth activation phi; n fixed training points in a fixed dimension d with a regression target; square loss; gradient flow. As m -> infinity the dynamics converge to Yang and Hu's limiting equations, which learn features. Prove that for every target in a stated class and data in general position, the limiting gradient flow drives the training loss to 0 as t -> infinity (or converges to a global minimizer of a stated population risk), or exhibit an initialization-typical stationary point where it stalls. Compare with the three-layer mean-field limit of T367 first.
statement_caveat: For L = 2 this is the mean-field problem T223. For deeper networks even well-posedness of the mean-field dynamics needs care (Nguyen–Pham; Sirignano–Spiliopoulos).
source: G. Yang and E. J. Hu, Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks (Tensor Programs IV), arXiv:2011.14522 (2020)
locator: to verify: open problems in the conclusion of Tensor Programs IV.
why_important: muP is used to tune very large models; a convergence theorem for its limit would say that the training rule practitioners use has a well-behaved infinite-width limit.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows (results with special initializations for multilayer mean-field, Nguyen–Pham 2020, to verify).
note: Fame: Tensor Programs IV is one of the most cited theory papers of recent years.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2011.14522 Theorems 3.3-3.6 (stable parametrizations and feature learning), not a long-time global convergence theorem
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify architecture, activation, task/data law, initialization, exact muP normalization, optimized loss and convergence mode; 'a natural regression task' includes trivial/special cases and does not pose a fixed hard problem
audit.replace_with: Fix an explicit muP three-layer regression model and ask for a specified global-risk convergence theorem; compare its limiting equations with T367 before treating them as separate problems.
audit.solver_shape: PROGRAMME
audit.locator: 2011.14522 Section 3 Theorems 3.3-3.6; exact long-time-convergence open-problem locator not found

title: Commuting the depth and width limits of residual-network training
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: For ResNets with two-layer-perceptron blocks h^l = h^(l-1) + (ML)^(-1) V_l phi(D^(-1/2) U_l^T h^(l-1)) (depth L, hidden width M, embedding dimension D) in the maximal-local-update regime, Chaintron, Chizat and Maass prove that k steps of (clipped) gradient descent converge to a single large-scale limit at rate O(1/L + sqrt(D/(ML)) + 1/sqrt D) whenever log L <= D <= C M, so the depth and width limits commute when M is of order D. Prove convergence to the same limit when D/M → ∞ with D/(ML) → 0 (their constraint D = O(M) removed), or a bound with at most exponential dependence on the number of steps k (theirs is super-exponential); or prove the joint limit of training for depth-one residual blocks with branch multiplier 1/sqrt(L) and muP width scaling (Bordelon et al.; Yang et al.), where only the sequential limit and the first forward pass are rigorous.
statement_caveat: Repaired after audit (codex-w687, 16 Oct: the first version, 'jointly in any manner' for an unspecified model, is answered for depth-two blocks with M of order D by arXiv:2603.18168 Theorem 1.1). The authors believe only D/(ML) → 0 is necessary and leave the other shape constraints open (p 5). At initialization see also Li–Nica–Roy (T262).
source: L.-P. Chaintron, L. Chizat and J. Maass, ResNets of All Shapes and Sizes: Convergence of Training Dynamics in the Large-scale Limit, arXiv:2603.18168 (2026); B. Bordelon, L. Noci, M. B. Li, B. Hanin and C. Pehlevan, Depthwise Hyperparameter Transfer in Residual Networks: Dynamics and Scaling Limit, arXiv:2309.16620 (2023); G. Yang, D. Yu, C. Zhu and S. Hayou, Tensor Programs VI: Feature Learning in Infinite-Depth Neural Networks, arXiv:2310.02244 (2023)
locator: 2603.18168 Theorem 1.1 (p 4) and the shape-constraint remark (p 5); 2310.02244 Theorem 4.1; 2309.16620 Appendix F (p 30).
why_important: Depth-muP is how large residual models are scaled; a rigorous joint limit would justify transfer of hyperparameters across depth.
where_it_stands: Partly solved: joint limit for depth-two blocks with D = O(M) on fixed horizons (2603.18168, 2026); the shape, horizon and depth-one-block cases are open.
note: Fame: active 2023-26 topic at the boundary of SDE limits and training theory.

audit.status_ref: arXiv:2310.02244 Theorem 4.1; Chaintron-Chizat-Maass arXiv:2603.18168 (2026), Theorem 1.1 PDF p4 and shape-constraint discussion PDF p5

title: Optimal rates in the Gaussian-process limit of wide random networks
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Let f_n be a depth-L fully connected network with hidden widths n, iid N(0, C_W/fan-in) weights and a fixed Lipschitz activation, viewed as a random field on a compact input set K ⊂ R^d. f_n converges in law to the neural-network Gaussian process (NNGP) as n → ∞. Determine the optimal rate of this convergence in a functional metric (e.g. Wasserstein-2 distance between laws on C(K), or total variation of k-point marginals), including the dependence on L, k and the activation; in particular decide whether the rate is n^{-1/2} or n^{-1} for smooth test functions.
statement_caveat: Rates for a fixed finite set of inputs in Wasserstein distance are known (several 2022-24 papers); the question asks for functional (sup-norm) rates and sharp depth dependence.
source: J. Lee et al., Deep Neural Networks as Gaussian Processes, arXiv:1711.00165 (2017); A. G. de G. Matthews et al., Gaussian Process Behaviour in Wide Deep Neural Networks, arXiv:1804.11271 (2018); B. Hanin, Random Neural Networks in the Infinite Width Limit as Gaussian Processes, arXiv:2107.01562 (2021)
locator: to verify: Hanin 2107.01562, introduction (discussion of quantitative versions as open).
why_important: The NNGP limit is the starting point of infinite-width theory; how fast a real network approaches it decides when that theory is quantitatively useful.
where_it_stands: Finite-dimensional quantitative CLTs known (Basteri–Trevisan; Favaro et al.; Balasubramanian et al.; Trevisan 2023, to verify). Sharp functional rates open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the NNGP correspondence (Neal 1996; Lee et al.; Matthews et al.) is foundational.

title: A rigorous 1/width expansion of deep random networks with depth-to-width ratio as coupling
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Deep fully connected ReLU network at initialization, zero biases, critical weight variance 2/n, width n, depth L, a fixed finite set of inputs and output coordinates. Roberts and Yaida (The Principles of Deep Learning Theory) derive that the normalized connected 2k-point cumulants of the preactivations are of order (L/n)^(k-1), so that L/n acts as a coupling constant. For each fixed k, prove this with an explicit remainder uniform in L <= c n (constants may depend on k and on the inputs), stating whether the expansion variable is L/n or 1/n at fixed L. Since the normalized fourth cumulant stays bounded away from 0 when L/n tends to t > 0, the leading law there is not Gaussian: describe it (for one input the log-normal law of Li, Nica and Roy is the comparison) and the value of t beyond which the expansion stops being asymptotic. Compare exact single-input moments before the multi-input statement.
statement_caveat: Order-by-order statements at fixed L are easier; uniformity in depth is the content. The fourth cumulant at leading order is known rigorously (Hanin 2022, to verify).
source: D. A. Roberts, S. Yaida and B. Hanin, The Principles of Deep Learning Theory, arXiv:2106.10165 (2021)
locator: to verify: Chapters 4-5 (the 1/n expansion and the depth-to-width ratio as expansion parameter).
why_important: The effective-theory book is the most systematic physics account of finite-width networks; a rigorous version would turn it into probability theory.
where_it_stands: Leading-order corrections rigorous in several works; the all-orders expansion uniform in depth open.
note: Fame: 'The Principles of Deep Learning Theory' (Cambridge UP 2022) is widely read.

audit.status_ref: Roberts-Yaida-Hanin2106.10165 section3.4 equations3.53-3.57 PDF p77, fully read with footnote8, explicitly solves fixed-order deep-linear moments in the L/n double limit and warns that the approximation is not uniform in moment order. Sections4-5 discuss critical nonlinear finite-width expansions, but no deciding all-orders uniform nonlinear remainder theorem or current citing-graph clearance was established in this review. Exact scalar ReLU moments provide a diagnostic, not a new general theorem.
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify weight variance,bias,critical tuning,normalized cumulants,number of inputs and coordinates,truncation order,error metric and constants depending on that order. Fixed positive L/n leaves nonzero normalized fourth cumulant, so perturbatively close must not mean an asymptotically exact Gaussian leading law throughout L<=c*n. Tanh/ReLU cannot share a universal unstated critical parameter choice.
audit.replace_with: Fix critically normalized zero-bias ReLU, a finite input/coordinate set and fixed cumulant order2k. Seek explicit remainder uniform in L<=c*n after specifying expansion variable L/n versus1/n and permissible dependence on k. Compare exact single-input moments before a multi-input theorem.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: exact critical-ReLU second/fourth/sixth moment diagnostic completed in T244_ReLU_moments.md. The multi-input all-orders uniform programme remains unverified.
