title: Evolution of the neural tangent kernel when depth and width are comparable
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: For a depth-L network of width n trained by gradient descent, the NTK is deterministic and frozen during training in the limit n → ∞ at fixed L. Hanin and Nica show that at initialization its fluctuations are of order exp(c·L/n) − 1, so it is random when L/n is not small. Determine the law of the NTK and of its change over training in the joint limit L, n → ∞ with L/n → t > 0, and decide whether feature learning (a nontrivial change of the NTK) occurs at a rate set by t.
statement_caveat: Huang and Yau's neural tangent hierarchy gives the finite-width dynamics as an infinite hierarchy; the question is a closed description in the joint limit.
source: B. Hanin and M. Nica, Finite Depth and Width Corrections to the Neural Tangent Kernel, arXiv:1909.05989 (2019); J. Huang and H.-T. Yau, Dynamics of Deep Neural Networks and Neural Tangent Hierarchy, arXiv:1909.08156 (2019)
locator: to verify: Hanin–Nica, main theorem on NTK fluctuations and its concluding discussion.
why_important: The NTK picture is the main tractable theory of training; knowing exactly where it stops being valid in depth is a probability question about products of random matrices.
where_it_stands: Open (initialization fluctuations known; training-time behaviour in the joint limit not rigorous).
note: Fame: Hanin–Nica is the standard reference for NTK beyond infinite width.

title: The law of input-output Jacobians of deep random networks with general activations
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Hanin and Nica show that for ReLU networks with He initialization the squared norm of the input-output Jacobian (and of gradients) is approximately log-normal, with log-variance proportional to the sum of reciprocal widths Σ_l 1/n_l. Prove the analogue for smooth activations (tanh, GELU) at criticality, and determine the limiting law of the whole singular-value spectrum of the Jacobian when L and n tend to infinity with L/n → t.
statement_caveat: For ReLU the Jacobian reduces to a product of random matrices with random diagonal masks; smooth activations create dependence between forward and backward passes.
source: B. Hanin and M. Nica, Products of Many Large Random Matrices and Gradients in Deep Neural Networks, arXiv:1812.05994 (2018); Comm. Math. Phys. 376 (2020)
locator: to verify: main theorem (ReLU) and the closing discussion of other activations.
why_important: Exploding and vanishing gradients are the original obstacle to training deep networks; their exact law at finite width is a basic random-matrix question.
where_it_stands: ReLU case solved (Hanin); general activations and full spectrum in the joint limit open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: well cited, connects deep learning to Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products.

title: The singular-value spectrum of deep network Jacobians in the joint depth-width limit (dynamical isometry)
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Pennington, Schoenholz and Ganguli compute, via free probability, the limiting singular-value distribution of the input-output Jacobian J = Π D_l W_l of a depth-L network with orthogonal or Gaussian weights, assuming asymptotic freeness of the diagonal derivative matrices D_l and the weights W_l, and find 'dynamical isometry' at criticality for orthogonal weights and sigmoid-like activations. Prove the formula and the isometry claim when depth and width tend to infinity jointly (L = L(n) → ∞), not only at fixed depth.
statement_caveat: At fixed depth asymptotic freeness of the layer Jacobians has been proved (Pastur and Slavin; Collins and Hayase, to verify). The joint limit needs control of errors accumulated over L layers.
source: J. Pennington, S. S. Schoenholz and S. Ganguli, Resurrecting the sigmoid in deep learning through dynamical isometry: theory and practice, arXiv:1711.04735 (2017)
locator: to verify: Section 2 (the free-probability computation and its freeness assumption).
why_important: Dynamical isometry underlies orthogonal initialization of very deep networks; the joint limit is exactly the regime in which it is used.
where_it_stands: Fixed-depth freeness proved; joint limit open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: a widely cited free-probability application in deep learning.

title: Edge universality for the conjugate kernel of a random network
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Conjugate kernel of a one-layer random network: Y = sigma(W X / sqrt d), W m x d with iid N(0, 1) entries, X d x N with iid sub-Gaussian entries (or columns uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt d), m, d, N tending to infinity proportionally. Take sigma Lipschitz (or smooth), centred, with no linear part: E sigma(Z) = 0 and E Z sigma(Z) = 0 for Z ~ N(0, 1). Prove that lambda_max(Y Y^T / N) converges to the right edge of the limiting (Pennington-Worah) law, which is regular there, with Tracy-Widom (beta = 1) fluctuations on the n^(-2/3) scale. Then allow a linear component, which changes the bulk: state an explicit rule for any finite-rank spikes it or the input design creates and prove the same edge statement for the largest eigenvalue after them. For polynomial activations of degree at least 3 the top eigenvalue at widths below several thousand is an outlier made by the largest entry of Y, so the statement is asymptotic only.
statement_caveat: The global law is known; the edge and fluctuations are the open part. Outliers come from the mean and the linear Hermite component of sigma.
source: L. Benigni and S. Péché, Eigenvalue distribution of nonlinear models of random matrices, arXiv:1904.03090 (2019); Z. Fan and Z. Wang, Spectra of the Conjugate Kernel and Neural Tangent Kernel for linear-width neural networks, arXiv:2005.11879 (2020)
locator: to verify: open questions at the end of Fan–Wang and Benigni–Péché.
why_important: Nonlinear random matrices are a new class of random-matrix models born from neural networks; edge behaviour governs conditioning of random-feature regression.
where_it_stands: Global laws proved; edge results partial (to verify). Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: nonlinear random matrix theory is an active RMT topic since Pennington–Worah 2017.

audit.status_ref: Benigni-Peche1904.03090 Theorems2.2/2.3 PDF p5, fully read with iid-entry,strong-tail,analyticity and centering hypotheses p4, prove the global law. Remark2.5 p5 explicitly states that their method also gives largest-eigenvalue convergence for odd activations. Fan-Wang2005.11879 Assumption3.2/Theorem3.4 PDF p5, fully read with definition p4, proves CK bulk convergence and bounded norm under approximately orthogonal inputs and smooth centered normalized activation. Footnote2 p4 explicitly warns bulk weak convergence does not imply individual-edge convergence. Neither opened result proves the requested broad Tracy-Widom law.
audit.statement_ok: NO: iid columns alone do not imply the quoted global law or bounded edge. Specify input distribution/concentration,moments,activation regularity/normalization,aspect ratios,regular edge,scaling constant and a precise finite-rank spike rule. The linear Hermite component generally affects the bulk and cannot simply be labeled an outlier to discard.
audit.replace_with: Fix iid sub-Gaussian entries or a specified concentrated input design and a smooth centered activation, remove only explicitly identified finite-rank spikes, then ask edge rigidity/Tracy-Widom at a nondegenerate right edge. Compare later largest-eigenvalue results before claiming an open case.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: isotropic iid-column radial counterexample completed in T248_radial_diagnostic.md. A Gaussian polynomial-activation regular-edge special case is concrete, but no novelty clearance.
audit.locator: 1904.03090 Sec2 assumptions PDF p4;Theorems2.2/2.3 and Remark2.5 p5.2005.11879 Definition3.1/footnote2 p4;Assumption3.2 and Theorem3.4 p5;NTK extension Theorem3.7 p7. Exact generic Tracy-Widom conjecture is not located in these source passages.

title: Trainability depth at the edge of chaos
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: For a random tanh network with weight variance sigma_w² and bias variance sigma_b², mean-field signal propagation gives a correlation depth scale xi(sigma_w, sigma_b) that diverges on the order-to-chaos line. Schoenholz et al. conjecture from experiments that such networks can be trained by SGD exactly when depth L ≲ c·xi (c ≈ 6). Prove a rigorous version: for L ≫ xi, gradient descent from this initialization cannot reduce the loss on a nontrivial task in polynomial time, while for L ≪ xi it can.
statement_caveat: The mean-field recursions are exact as width → ∞ at fixed depth; the conjecture is about trainability, which needs both a negative and a positive statement.
source: S. S. Schoenholz, J. Gilmer, S. Ganguli and J. Sohl-Dickstein, Deep Information Propagation, arXiv:1611.01232 (2016); B. Poole et al., Exponential expressivity in deep neural networks through transient chaos, arXiv:1606.05340 (2016)
locator: to verify: Schoenholz et al., Section 5 (trainability experiments and the 6·xi rule).
why_important: Edge-of-chaos initialization is used in practice; whether information-propagation depth really controls trainability is the question it rests on.
where_it_stands: Open (empirical law; rigorous mean-field recursions only).
note: Fame: the edge-of-chaos papers are standard references for initialization.

title: Quantitative Tensor Programs: finite-width rates for any architecture
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Yang's Master Theorem (Tensor Programs) gives almost sure convergence of coordinate averages as the width n tends to infinity, and so the NNGP and NTK limits of many architectures. A quantitative version with rate n^(-1/2) is given in arXiv:2607.06290 (2026). Unrestricted constants polynomial in the program length are false (a program that repeatedly multiplies by a fixed factor above 1 amplifies the error exponentially). For a stable normalized subclass (for example critically initialized MLPs with normalized layers, Gaussian initialization), a stated class of test functions (pseudo-Lipschitz of fixed order) and stated nondegeneracy conditions, prove a rate n^(-1/2) with constants polynomial in the depth; and for attention, normalization or transpose (NTK) programs, identify the operations and hypotheses not covered by the 2026 theorem and prove a rate for them.
statement_caveat: Finite-width rates for specific MLPs are known; the question asks for the general program with explicit length dependence.
source: G. Yang, Tensor Programs I: Wide Feedforward or Recurrent Neural Networks of Any Architecture are Gaussian Processes, arXiv:1910.12478 (2019); G. Yang, Tensor Programs II: Neural Tangent Kernel for Any Architecture, arXiv:2006.14548 (2020)
locator: to verify: Tensor Programs I, the Master Theorem and the closing remarks on rates.
why_important: Tensor Programs give the infinite-width limit of everything in one theorem; a rate would make all those limits quantitative at once.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the Tensor Programs series is the main general theory of infinite-width limits.

audit.status_ref: Yang1910.12478 Theorem5.4 PDF p7, fully read, proves controlled-test empirical LLN for fixed NETSOR programs;Corollary5.6 p8 covers controlled/parameter-controlled architectures with extra assumptions. Yang2006.14548 Theorem7.2 PDF p10, fully read, proves BP-like transpose-program LLN with polynomially bounded nonlinearities/tests. Agazzi-Mosig Garcia-Trevisan2607.06290 Theorem1.2 and Corollary1.3 PDF p4, fully read, already give quantitative normalized-vector Wp coupling and empirical-kernel Lp errors bounded by c*sum_hidden_widths m^(-1/2), under Lipschitz NETSOR structural hypotheses.

Unrestricted polynomial-depth constants are false for unnormalized empirical averages of programs repeatedly multiplying by fixed a>1; each line can have the same finite Lipschitz constant while error amplifies exponentially.
audit.replace_with: Start from2607.06290 and ask polynomial-depth constants only for a stable normalized subclass, with a specified test class and quantitative conditioning assumptions. For attention/normalization or transpose/NTK programs, identify operations and hypotheses not already covered by the2026 theorem.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: exact exponential-amplification diagnostic completed in T250_amplification_diagnostic.md. A contractive finite-depth subclass with explicit structural constants is a concrete route; unrestricted any-architecture polynomial-depth theorem is not viable as stated.

title: Heavy-tailed spectra of trained weight matrices
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Martin and Mahoney observe that the empirical spectral distributions of weight matrices of well-trained deep networks develop power-law tails, with the tail exponent correlating with test accuracy, while at initialization they follow Marchenko–Pastur. Prove, for a tractable model (e.g. a two-layer network or a linear network trained by SGD with constant step), that SGD drives the singular-value distribution of a weight matrix from Marchenko–Pastur to a law with a power-law tail, and identify the exponent in terms of step size, batch size and data.
statement_caveat: Spiked (finite-rank) changes from training are understood in some models; the claim is about a heavy tail in the bulk.
source: C. H. Martin and M. W. Mahoney, Implicit Self-Regularization in Deep Neural Networks: Evidence from Random Matrix Theory and Implications for Learning, arXiv:1810.01075 (2018)
locator: to verify: Sections 1 and 5 (the 5+1 phases of training and the heavy-tailed phase).
why_important: Heavy-tailed self-regularization is used to diagnose trained models without test data; a mechanism in probability is lacking.
where_it_stands: Open (empirical; partial heuristics connecting it to heavy-tailed SGD, T228).
note: Fame: well known empirical theory with tools in wide use.

title: Bulk and outliers of the Hessian of a trained classifier
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Empirically the Hessian of the training loss of a C-class network near the end of training has a bulk near zero plus about C (or C(C−1)) outlier eigenvalues, with outliers explained by class-mean structure (Sagun et al.; Papyan; Ghorbani et al.). Prove, for a natural model (multinomial logistic regression or a two-layer network on a Gaussian mixture with C classes in high dimension), the limiting spectral law of the Hessian and the number and positions of its outliers.
statement_caveat: Results for linear models at initialization are easier; the question is about a network at or near a trained minimizer.
source: V. Papyan, The Full Spectrum of Deepnet Hessians at Scale, arXiv:1811.07062 (2018); L. Sagun, L. Bottou and Y. LeCun, Eigenvalues of the Hessian in Deep Learning: Singularity and Beyond, arXiv:1611.07476 (2016); B. Ghorbani, S. Krishnan and Y. Xiao, arXiv:1901.10159 (2019)
locator: to verify: Papyan, sections on the class-mean decomposition of the Hessian.
why_important: Hessian spectra govern the step-size limits (T226) and sharpness-based generalization arguments; the outlier structure is a precise random-matrix prediction.
where_it_stands: Partial results for mixture models (Ben Arous, Gheissari, Huang and Jagannath on 'effective dynamics' and outlier alignment, to verify). Open in general.
note: Fame: the bulk-plus-outliers picture is standard in deep-learning optimization.

title: The smallest eigenvalue of the neural tangent kernel Gram matrix
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Inputs x_1..x_n uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt d; two-layer ReLU network with m hidden units, first-layer weights iid N(0, I_d), output weights plus or minus 1/sqrt m, fixed; K the first-layer NTK Gram matrix, K_ij = (x_i.x_j / d)(1/m) sum_k 1{w_k.x_i > 0} 1{w_k.x_j > 0}, with diagonal about 1/2. The rank of K is at most m d, so lambda_min(K) = 0 when m d < n. With m d = gamma n, gamma > 1, and n = d^k (k >= 1), d tending to infinity, determine the high-probability limit or sharp order of lambda_min(K) as a function of gamma and k, compared with lambda_min of the infinite-width kernel (results of Montanari and Zhong give an order-one lower bound once the parameter count exceeds n by a polylog factor). Initialization only; the stability of the kernel during training is a separate question.
statement_caveat: Nguyen, Mondelli and Montúfar give tight bounds when n is polynomial in d with width conditions; the sharp width requirement is the open part.
source: Q. Nguyen, M. Mondelli and G. Montúfar, Tight Bounds on the Smallest Eigenvalue of the Neural Tangent Kernel for Deep ReLU Networks, arXiv:2012.11654 (2020)
locator: to verify: conclusion (width requirements as an open question).
why_important: Every NTK-based convergence and memorization proof runs through lambda_min(K); its sharp behaviour gives the minimal overparameterization (T237).
where_it_stands: Open in the sharp form as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: a central technical quantity of overparameterization theory.

Section8 p15 explicitly leaves optimization guarantees for single-linear-width-layer networks open. The source fixes input expected squared norm Theta(d); its d-scale eigenvalue result is not invariant under input/kernel parameterization.

Specify sphere radius,output/weight parameterization,trained layers,depth,normalization and probability. md>=N is a necessary rank condition in a two-layer model, not a universal sufficient minimal-width theorem.

title: Rank collapse in deep attention at initialization
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Dong, Cordonnier and Loukas show that pure self-attention (no skip connections or MLPs) collapses token representations to rank one doubly exponentially fast in depth. For transformers with residual connections, layer normalization and random initialization, determine the rate at which the token Gram matrix degenerates with depth L as width and the number of tokens grow, and the residual scaling (e.g. 1/sqrt(L)) at which it does not degenerate, with a rigorous limit theorem.
statement_caveat: Noci et al. analyse signal propagation and give conditions to avoid collapse; the question asks for a rigorous joint-limit theorem.
source: Y. Dong, J.-B. Cordonnier and A. Loukas, Attention is Not All You Need: Pure Attention Loses Rank Doubly Exponentially with Depth, arXiv:2103.03404 (2021); L. Noci et al., Signal Propagation in Transformers: Theoretical Perspectives and the Role of Rank Collapse, arXiv:2206.03126 (2022)
locator: to verify: Noci et al., the main propagation result and its assumptions.
why_important: Rank collapse is the transformer version of the vanishing-signal problem; it decides how deep attention models can be initialized.
where_it_stands: Partial; rigorous joint-limit description open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: rank collapse is a standard concern in transformer theory.

title: The covariance SDE of the shaped transformer
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: For the shaped-attention covariance SDE of Noci, Li, Li, He, Hofmann, Maddison and Roy (arXiv:2306.17759, Theorem 4.2; with shaped MLP blocks, Corollary 4.3), whose local convergence from the finite network is proved there, with m tokens, residual parameters lambda^2 + gamma^2 = 1, temperature tau0 and positive-definite initial covariance V_0: decide whether the solution exists for all t (no explosion) and stays positive definite. On the exchangeable ray V = a I + c 11^T the drift is cubic and the Feller test gives explosion iff (m - 1)^2 > 2 gamma^2; simulations of the exact covariance chain show explosion with probability strictly between 0 and 1 for m = 2, 3, 4, 8. Prove explosion with positive probability for m >= 3 from V_0 = s I with s large, then from every positive-definite V_0; settle m = 2 (the ray predicts explosion iff gamma^2 < 1/2); treat the attention-only and the attention-plus-MLP SDE separately.
statement_caveat: For shaped MLPs the neural covariance SDE is proved (Li, Nica and Roy 2206.02768); attention adds a softmax nonlinearity coupling all tokens.
source: L. Noci, C. Li, M. B. Li, B. He, T. Hofmann, C. J. Maddison and D. M. Roy, The Shaped Transformer: Attention Models in the Infinite Depth-and-Width Limit, arXiv:2306.17759 (2023); M. B. Li, M. Nica and D. M. Roy, The Neural Covariance SDE, arXiv:2206.02768 (2022)
locator: to verify: Noci et al., the main theorem and which steps are heuristic.
why_important: It would give the first rigorous infinite depth-and-width limit of a transformer, the architecture behind current large models.
where_it_stands: Open in full rigour as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: part of the infinite depth-and-width program (Li, Nica, Roy, Noci, Hanin).

Section4.4 pp10-11 explains lack of general global existence and numerical instabilities for large initial covariance. Standard softmax or unrestricted training is a different model.

title: The transition to chaos in random recurrent neural networks (Sompolinsky–Crisanti–Sommers)
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Consider dx_i/dt = −x_i + Σ_j J_ij tanh(x_j), i = 1..N, with J_ij iid N(0, g²/N). Sompolinsky, Crisanti and Sommers (1988) predict that for g < 1 the origin is globally attracting, while for g > 1 the dynamics is chaotic: the maximal Lyapunov exponent is positive and the autocorrelation follows a self-consistent mean-field equation. Prove that for g > 1 the maximal Lyapunov exponent is positive with high probability as N → ∞, and the dynamical mean-field equation for the autocorrelation.
statement_caveat: Ben Arous and Guionnet proved large deviations and the DMFT limit on finite time intervals; the positivity of the Lyapunov exponent in the long-time chaotic phase is the open part (to verify).
source: A. Crisanti and H. Sompolinsky, Path Integral Approach to Random Neural Networks, arXiv:1809.06042 (2018); H. Sompolinsky, A. Crisanti and H.-J. Sommers, Chaos in Random Neural Networks, Phys. Rev. Lett. 61 (1988) 259
locator: to verify: Crisanti–Sompolinsky 2018, the DMFT and Lyapunov-exponent sections.
why_important: The SCS model is the founding model of chaos in neural networks and of reservoir computing; its chaotic phase has resisted proof for more than thirty years.
where_it_stands: Finite-time DMFT rigorous (Ben Arous–Guionnet 1995); long-time chaos unproved as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the 1988 PRL is a classic (well over a thousand citations).

title: Complexity of critical points of the empirical risk of a two-layer network
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Choromanska et al. argued, by analogy with spherical p-spin glasses (Auffinger, Ben Arous and Černý), that critical points of the loss of large networks of low index concentrate in a narrow band above the global minimum. For a two-layer network with n Gaussian samples in dimension d (n/d → alpha) and a planted teacher, compute by the Kac–Rice formula the annealed and quenched complexity of critical points of the empirical risk at each loss level and index, and prove the band structure (or disprove it) without the independence assumptions used by Choromanska et al.
statement_caveat: Maillard, Ben Arous and Biroli compute the annealed complexity for generalized linear models (single neuron); networks with several neurons and the quenched complexity are open.
source: A. Choromanska, M. Henaff, M. Mathieu, G. Ben Arous and Y. LeCun, The Loss Surfaces of Multilayer Networks, arXiv:1412.0233 (2014); A. Auffinger, G. Ben Arous and J. Černý, Random Matrices and complexity of Spin Glasses, arXiv:1003.1129 (2010); A. Maillard, G. Ben Arous and G. Biroli, arXiv:1912.02143 (2019)
locator: to verify: Choromanska et al., the assumptions listed in Section 3 and the stated open problem in the discussion.
why_important: Whether the loss landscape of a network is glassy is the question behind 'local minima are good enough'.
where_it_stands: Open for multi-neuron networks as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the Choromanska et al. paper is among the most cited landscape papers; the spin-glass analogy is famous.

title: Basins of the symmetric spurious minima of two-layer ReLU teacher-student models
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: For a two-layer ReLU student with k units learning a ReLU teacher with k orthonormal units under Gaussian inputs, Arjevani and Field describe families of spurious minima with large isotropy (symmetry) groups and compute their Hessian spectra analytically. Determine the probability, under Gaussian initialization, that gradient flow converges to a spurious minimum, as a function of k (Safran–Shamir report failure rates growing with k), and prove its limit as k → ∞.
statement_caveat: The existence of the families and their Hessians are proved; the basin sizes under random initialization are the open part.
source: Y. Arjevani and M. Field, Analytic Characterization of the Hessian in Shallow ReLU Models: A Tale of Symmetry, arXiv:2008.01805 (2020); I. Safran and O. Shamir, arXiv:1712.08968 (2017)
locator: to verify: Arjevani–Field, concluding questions on basins of attraction.
why_important: It is the most detailed exact picture of a nonconvex network landscape; the basin question connects it to what training actually does.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: well known within landscape theory (symmetry-breaking analysis).

title: Bayesian deep networks in the proportional regime: kernel renormalization for nonlinear networks
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: For a Bayesian deep network (Gaussian prior on weights, Gaussian likelihood) with width n, depth L and P training samples, the posterior predictor converges to the NNGP predictor when n → ∞ at fixed P, losing feature learning. In the proportional regime P/n → alpha > 0 Li and Sompolinsky derive for deep linear networks a 'back-propagating kernel renormalization', and Hanin and Zlokapa prove exact formulas for deep linear networks. Prove a rigorous limit theorem for the posterior predictive of nonlinear (e.g. ReLU) Bayesian networks in this regime.
statement_caveat: The linear case is solved; nonlinear networks are open.
source: Q. Li and H. Sompolinsky, Statistical Mechanics of Deep Linear Neural Networks: The Back-Propagating Kernel Renormalization, arXiv:2012.04030 (2020); B. Hanin and A. Zlokapa, Bayesian Interpolation with Deep Linear Networks, arXiv:2212.14457 (2022)
locator: to verify: Hanin–Zlokapa, discussion of nonlinear networks as open.
why_important: This is the cleanest probabilistic model of representation learning at finite width: what Bayesian inference over network weights learns when data and width are comparable.
where_it_stands: Open for nonlinear activations (physics-level theories exist).
note: Fame: active line (Sompolinsky; Hanin; Pehlevan; Seroussi–Ringel).

title: Error universality for deep random-features regression
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Deep random features: inputs pass through L fixed random layers of widths proportional to d and only the last layer is trained by ridge regression on n ≍ d samples. Schröder, Cui, Dmitriev and Loureiro give a deterministic equivalent for the test error and claim universality (the error equals that of a Gaussian model with matched covariances). Prove this deterministic equivalent rigorously for all L ≥ 2 and general Lipschitz activations, including ridgeless limits.
statement_caveat: The one-layer case (Mei–Montanari; Hu–Lu Gaussian equivalence) is proved; the paper proves part of the multi-layer statement under assumptions (to verify).
source: D. Schröder, H. Cui, D. Dmitriev and B. Loureiro, Deterministic equivalent and error universality of deep random features learning, arXiv:2302.00401 (2023)
locator: to verify: which statements are theorems and which are conjectures (Section 3).
why_important: Deep random features are the solvable model of what depth does to representations before training.
where_it_stands: Partially proved; full statement open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: part of the Gaussian-equivalence program (Goldt, Loureiro, Krzakala, Zdeborová, Hu–Lu, Montanari).

title: Random-features regression beyond linear scaling
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Random-features ridge regression with N features sigma(<w_j, x>), n samples and dimension d, with N ≍ d^{k1} and n ≍ d^{k2} for real exponents, inputs on the sphere. Determine the exact asymptotic test error for every pair (k1, k2), including the multiple-descent peaks at integer exponents and at N ≍ n, and prove it.
statement_caveat: The proportional case (Mei–Montanari) and kernel ridge regression in polynomial scaling (Misiakiewicz; Xiao, Hu, Misiakiewicz and Pennington) are known; general (k1, k2) for random features was addressed in 2024 work (to verify whether fully settled).
source: S. Mei and A. Montanari, The generalization error of random features regression: Precise asymptotics and double descent curve, arXiv:1908.05355 (2019); T. Misiakiewicz, Spectrum of inner-product kernel matrices in the polynomial regime and multiple descent phenomenon in kernel ridge regression, arXiv:2204.10425 (2022)
locator: to verify: Misiakiewicz, final section (random features in polynomial regimes as an open question).
why_important: Random features are the main exactly solvable model of overparameterization; polynomial scalings are where learning beyond linear functions happens.
where_it_stands: Possibly settled for random features in 2024 (to verify); kept because the trained-network analogue is open.
note: Fame: double descent for random features is one of the best-known results of the field.

title: The infinite depth-and-width limit of unshaped ReLU networks
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Unshaped fully connected ReLU network without residual connections, zero biases, critical weight variance 2/n, width n, depth L with L/n tending to t > 0, and two inputs at a fixed angle theta_0. The correlation of the two hidden vectors tends to 1 and their angle theta_L is of order 1/n. Prove that n theta_(tn) converges in law to a nondegenerate random limit, jointly with the logs of the two radii (for one input the log-Gaussian law of Li, Nica and Roy), identify the limit, and state the topology in which the process in t converges. Simulations at n = 200 to 1600 show the law of n theta has converged in n and rule out the naive diffusion approximation. Then three or more inputs (the rescaled shape of the Gram matrix).
statement_caveat: For shaped activations a covariance SDE is proved (T255 cites it); the unshaped case degenerates (correlations tend to one) and needs a different scaling.
source: M. B. Li, M. Nica and D. M. Roy, The Future is Log-Gaussian: ResNets and Their Infinite-Depth-and-Width Limit at Initialization, arXiv:2106.04013 (2021)
locator: to verify: main theorem (norms) and the stated open questions on multiple inputs.
why_important: Real networks have depth comparable to width; this joint limit, not the Gaussian process, is what describes them at initialization.
where_it_stands: Single-input norm laws proved; multi-input joint law open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the founding paper of the depth-and-width program.

audit.status_ref: Li-Nica-Roy2106.04013 Theorem1 PDF pp4-5, fully opened, gives an exact Gaussian-times-random-radial representation for the stated residual architecture. Its asymptotic Gaussian radial-log conclusions explicitly assume Conjecture5 about hypoactivation/interlayer dependence. The source also introduces a separate balanced architecture. This is not an unconditional generic fully connected/smooth-activation multi-input covariance theorem, nor a Gaussian law for the log of a fixed-dimensional Gaussian-mixture output norm.
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify alpha=0 chain versus vanilla/balanced residual network,critical weight/bias scaling,activation and input covariance. Distinguish hidden radial log from log output norm, and terminal output law from the entire evolving Gram process. Define raw degenerate limit versus rescaled angular fluctuations and the requested topology.
audit.replace_with: Fix unshaped zero-bias critical ReLU with two inputs. Determine the appropriate rescaling of1-correlation and its joint radial/angular process when L/n tends to t, with explicit initial covariance and stopped/global topology. Check existing coupled-limit work before claiming novelty.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: deterministic two-input correlation expansion and readout/radial distinction completed in T262_correlation_diagnostic.md. This is a diagnostic from the sequential-width limit and cannot be transferred unproved to joint depth-width scaling.
audit.locator: 2106.04013 architecture Eq1 PDF p3;Conjecture5 informal and exact representation part of Theorem1 p4;conditional asymptotics and Proposition2 p5. Fully connected alpha=0 and balanced architecture must be read separately; no exact numbered general multi-input/smooth-activation posing located.

title: A tight generalization bound for gradient-trained overparameterized networks
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Networks trained by (S)GD to zero training error generalize although they can fit random labels (Zhang et al.), and Nagarajan and Kolter show that any bound by two-sided uniform convergence over a set of hypotheses containing the trained network can be vacuous. Give, for a natural setting (e.g. a two-layer ReLU network trained by gradient descent on a Gaussian-mixture or teacher-network distribution with n samples in dimension d), a bound on the test error of the trained network that is provably tight up to constant factors in its dependence on n and d.
statement_caveat: Non-vacuous numerical bounds (PAC-Bayes, compression) exist for specific trained networks; the question asks for a theorem whose rate is provably tight.
source: C. Zhang, S. Bengio, M. Hardt, B. Recht and O. Vinyals, Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization, arXiv:1611.03530 (2016); V. Nagarajan and J. Z. Kolter, Uniform convergence may be unable to explain generalization in deep learning, arXiv:1902.04742 (2019)
locator: to verify: Nagarajan–Kolter, Section 5 (the open question of non-uniform-convergence bounds).
why_important: This is the generalization puzzle of deep learning in its sharpest form.
where_it_stands: Open in the stated form as far as the writer knows; tight results exist for linear and kernel models and some two-layer settings in high dimension (benign overfitting line).
note: Fame: 'rethinking generalization' is among the most cited papers in machine learning.

title: Tempered overfitting of interpolating ReLU networks in fixed dimension
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Mallinar et al. propose a taxonomy (benign, tempered, catastrophic) of interpolation with noisy labels and conjecture that interpolating ReLU networks in fixed input dimension are tempered: the excess risk stays bounded but does not vanish as n → ∞. For minimum-norm (or GD-trained) interpolating two-layer ReLU networks with inputs in a fixed dimension d ≥ 2 and label noise, determine whether the limiting excess risk is zero, finite and positive, or infinite.
statement_caveat: For univariate inputs (d = 1) the question is settled: tempered for some losses/norms, catastrophic for others (Kornowski–Yehudai–Shamir; Joshi–Vardi–Srebro).
source: N. Mallinar et al., Benign, Tempered, or Catastrophic: A Taxonomy of Overfitting, arXiv:2207.06569 (2022); G. Kornowski, G. Yehudai and O. Shamir, arXiv:2305.15141 (2023); N. Joshi, G. Vardi and N. Srebro, arXiv:2307.15396 (2023)
locator: to verify: Mallinar et al., the conjecture on ReLU networks; Joshi et al., the open d ≥ 2 case in the conclusion.
why_important: Interpolation of noisy data is what large networks do; whether it costs a constant or nothing in low dimension is basic to the theory of overfitting.
where_it_stands: d = 1 settled; d ≥ 2 open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the benign/tempered taxonomy is now standard terminology.

title: Benign overfitting of two-layer networks outside the nearly orthogonal regime
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Gradient-descent-trained two-layer networks that interpolate noisy labels are known to generalize near-optimally (benign overfitting) when the dimension d is much larger than the sample size n, so that training points are nearly orthogonal (Frei, Chatterji and Bartlett; Cao, Chen, Belkin and Gu). Determine whether, and for which data distributions, benign overfitting of GD-trained two-layer ReLU networks holds when n ≥ d, for instance for a Gaussian mixture with n/d → infinity.
statement_caveat: With n ≫ d the near-orthogonality used by all current proofs fails; tempered behaviour is expected in fixed dimension (T264).
source: S. Frei, N. S. Chatterji and P. L. Bartlett, Benign Overfitting without Linearity, arXiv:2202.05928 (2022); Y. Cao, Z. Chen, M. Belkin and Q. Gu, Benign Overfitting in Two-layer Convolutional Neural Networks, arXiv:2202.06526 (2022); P. L. Bartlett, P. M. Long, G. Lugosi and A. Tsigler, Benign Overfitting in Linear Regression, arXiv:1906.11300 (2019)
locator: to verify: Frei et al., discussion of the high-dimensionality assumption.
why_important: Benign overfitting is the main rigorous explanation of noisy interpolation; extending it beyond the high-dimensional regime is necessary for it to explain practice.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the Bartlett–Long–Lugosi–Tsigler PNAS paper started a major line.

title: Double descent for trained two-layer networks in the proportional regime
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Let n samples x_i ~ N(0, I_d) with labels from a fixed target plus noise, and train all layers of a two-layer network with p hidden units by gradient descent (to convergence, with small or zero ridge). As n, d, p → ∞ proportionally, prove that the test error converges to a deterministic curve in p/n and d/n, and determine whether it has a peak at the interpolation threshold as random-features regression does.
statement_caveat: For random features (only the second layer trained) the curve is known exactly (Mei–Montanari). The question is about training both layers.
source: M. Belkin, D. Hsu, S. Ma and S. Mandal, Reconciling modern machine learning practice and the bias-variance trade-off, arXiv:1812.11118 (2018); P. Nakkiran et al., Deep Double Descent, arXiv:1912.02292 (2019); S. Mei and A. Montanari, arXiv:1908.05355 (2019)
locator: to verify: Mei–Montanari, final discussion (fully trained networks as open).
why_important: Double descent overturned the bias-variance picture taught for decades; an exact theorem for a trained network would settle what the phenomenon really is.
where_it_stands: Open for fully trained networks as far as the writer knows (physics-level results exist).
note: Fame: double descent (Belkin et al. PNAS 2019) is one of the best-known discoveries of modern ML.

title: Epoch-wise double descent
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Epoch-wise double descent for networks. Fix a two-layer network of width m with a stated activation, trained by full-batch gradient flow from a stated initialization on n samples, Gaussian inputs in dimension d, labels from a teacher plus noise of variance s^2 (or labels flipped with probability p), in a stated limit: proportional (n, m, d tending to infinity at fixed ratios) or lazy (m much larger than n). Compute the limiting test risk R(t), the actual risk and not an upper bound, and prove that with probability tending to one R has two local minima and an interior local maximum in t, with the peak time to leading order. Feature learning (both layers trained) and the lazy or random-features regime are separate statements. Linear models with features learned at different speeds already show the effect (Heckel and Yilmaz; Pezeshki et al.) and do not answer the question.
statement_caveat: Linear models with features of very different scales show the effect (Heckel and Yilmaz 2020, to verify); the question is for networks.
source: P. Nakkiran, G. Kaplun, Y. Bansal, T. Yang, B. Barak and I. Sutskever, Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt, arXiv:1912.02292 (2019)
locator: to verify: Section 6 (epoch-wise double descent).
why_important: It decides whether early stopping is ever the right rule in the overparameterized regime.
where_it_stands: Open for networks as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: 'Deep Double Descent' is widely cited.

audit.status_ref: Heckel-Yilmaz2007.10099 Theorem1 PDF p5 and Figure2 p6, fully read, establish the Gaussian-linear risk approximation and two-speed epoch-double-descent mechanism; Proposition1 pp6-7 aligns coordinate stopping minima by learning rates. Theorem2 p10, model pp8-9, already gives a wide two-layer ReLU GD risk upper bound as a superposition of spectral bias/variance terms; it is not a matching lower bound proving two actual neural-risk descents. Nakkiran1912.02292 is empirical. Recent2601.08316 is empirical and2605.27078 a representation/readout diagnostic; neither is used as a deciding theorem.
audit.statement_ok: NO: the statement explicitly permits a linear-model witness, already known, while c/st say networks only. Specify architecture, actual risk rather than an upper bound, training scale, noise/data law, probability event and what peak-location precision means. Feature-learning and lazy wide-network regimes must be distinguished.
audit.replace_with: Ask for two strict descents of actual population risk, with quantitative peak location, in one specified feature-learning two-layer teacher-student scaling. Exclude the published linear alternative and state whether the result is averaged over or high probability in the training sample.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: T267_two_mode_diagnostic.md derives an exact noise-averaged fixed-design two-mode risk and verifies derivative signs at0,1,10,100. This reproduces a known mechanism; it is not fresh progress on nonlinear feature learning.
audit.locator: 1912.02292 Sec6 epoch-wise double descent PDF pp7-8;Sec8 Conclusion and Discussion pp9-10 on optimal early stopping. Quote p10: fully understanding the optimal early stopping behavior.2007.10099 Theorem1 p5,Figure2 p6,Proposition1 pp6-7;Theorem2 p10 is a neural-risk upper bound.

title: Depth-independent sample complexity under spectral-norm constraints
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: For depth-L networks with 1-Lipschitz activations whose weight matrices have spectral norms at most M_l, Bartlett, Foster and Telgarsky bound the generalization gap by (Π_l M_l)·(Σ_l ‖W_l‖_{2,1}^{2/3}/M_l^{2/3})^{3/2}/sqrt(n) up to logs, and Golowich, Rakhlin and Shamir obtain depth-independent bounds under Frobenius-norm constraints. Decide whether, under spectral-norm constraints alone (plus a bound on Π_l M_l), the sample complexity can be bounded independently of depth and width.
statement_caveat: Golowich–Rakhlin–Shamir pose the spectral-norm version as open and give partial lower bounds.
source: N. Golowich, A. Rakhlin and O. Shamir, Size-Independent Sample Complexity of Neural Networks, arXiv:1712.06541 (2017); P. Bartlett, D. J. Foster and M. Telgarsky, Spectrally-normalized margin bounds for neural networks, arXiv:1706.08498 (2017)
locator: to verify: Golowich–Rakhlin–Shamir, the open questions at the end.
why_important: Norm-based capacity is the main classical route to generalization bounds for networks; this is its cleanest unresolved case.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows (later partial results, e.g. Vardi–Shamir–Srebro 2022 on sample complexity with spectral norms, to verify).
note: Fame: a well-known open question of statistical learning theory for networks.

title: Which margin does gradient descent find in homogeneous networks?
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: For homogeneous networks trained by gradient flow on the logistic loss over separable data, the parameter direction converges to a KKT point of the max-margin problem (Lyu–Li; Ji–Telgarsky). Vardi, Shamir and Srebro show that this KKT point need not even be a local maximizer of the margin. For two-layer ReLU networks with Gaussian initialization of width m on n generic separable points, determine whether with high probability the limit is a local (or global) margin maximizer.
statement_caveat: The worst-case negative answer is known; the question is about typical data and random initialization.
source: K. Lyu and J. Li, Gradient Descent Maximizes the Margin of Homogeneous Neural Networks, arXiv:1906.05890 (2019); Z. Ji and M. Telgarsky, Directional convergence and alignment in deep learning, arXiv:2006.06657 (2020); G. Vardi, O. Shamir and N. Srebro, On Margin Maximization in Linear and ReLU Networks, arXiv:2110.02732 (2021)
locator: to verify: Vardi–Shamir–Srebro, conclusion (typical-case question).
why_important: The max-margin implicit bias is the main theory of why GD-trained classifiers generalize; this decides whether it actually holds for networks.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: Lyu–Li and Ji–Telgarsky are standard theorems; Soudry et al. 1710.10345 started the line.

title: Max-margin implicit bias of infinitely wide two-layer networks without assuming convergence
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Chizat and Bach show that for infinitely wide two-layer networks with homogeneous activations trained on the logistic loss, if the Wasserstein gradient flow converges in direction then the limit is a max-margin classifier in the variation norm (the F1 space), which adapts to low-dimensional structure. Prove the directional convergence itself, and give a rate at which the normalized margin approaches its maximum.
statement_caveat: Same structure as T223: the theorem is conditional on convergence.
source: L. Chizat and F. Bach, Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent for Wide Two-layer Neural Networks Trained with the Logistic Loss, arXiv:2002.04486 (2020)
locator: to verify: main theorem and the remark on the convergence assumption.
why_important: It is the cleanest statement that GD on wide networks learns adaptively, unlike kernels; without the convergence step it remains conditional.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: well cited (COLT 2020).

title: Neural collapse under gradient training of an actual network
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Papyan, Han and Donoho observe that in the terminal phase of training, last-layer features of each class collapse to their class mean, the class means form a simplex equiangular tight frame, and the classifier aligns with them (neural collapse). Proofs exist for the 'unconstrained features model' in which features are free variables. Prove that neural collapse (or a quantified approximate version) emerges under gradient descent for a network whose features are produced by trained layers (e.g. a two- or three-layer network on a Gaussian-mixture model with C classes) with weight decay, as training time → ∞.
statement_caveat: Súkeník et al. show that in the deep unconstrained features model, deep neural collapse is optimal for two layers but not in general for more layers; the question is about emergence under GD for real architectures.
source: V. Papyan, X. Y. Han and D. L. Donoho, Prevalence of Neural Collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training, arXiv:2008.08186 (2020); D. G. Mixon, H. Parshall and J. Pi, arXiv:2011.11619 (2020); P. Súkeník, M. Mondelli and C. H. Lampert, arXiv:2405.14468 (2024)
locator: to verify: Papyan–Han–Donoho, final section (open theoretical questions).
why_important: Neural collapse is the most precise geometric regularity observed in trained networks.
where_it_stands: Open for constrained features as far as the writer knows; unconstrained models largely understood.
note: Fame: the PNAS 2020 paper is widely cited.

title: The permutation conjecture for linear mode connectivity
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Two two-layer networks of width m trained on the same data (Gaussian inputs, a teacher network) from independent initializations with a stated law, by online or full-batch SGD with stated step size and time T. Let B_m be the loss barrier on the straight segment between the two after the best permutation of the hidden units of one of them. Ferbach et al. (arXiv:2310.19103) prove a mean-field version; state exactly what it covers (finite-time two-layer SGD, at which width rate, with what probability). Prove the missing cases: B_m tends to 0 in probability with an explicit rate for SGD run to the end of training (T growing with m), and for three-layer networks with layerwise permutations. Keep the loss barrier separate from closeness of predictions, and keep a statement about typical SGD runs separate from one about every global minimum, which is not asked.
statement_caveat: Ferbach et al. prove a version for wide two-layer networks in the mean-field regime via optimal transport; deeper networks and finite-time SGD remain.
source: R. Entezari, H. Sedghi, O. Saukh and B. Neyshabur, The Role of Permutation Invariance in Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks, arXiv:2110.06296 (2021); D. Ferbach, B. Goujaud, G. Gidel and A. Dieuleveut, Proving Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks via Optimal Transport, arXiv:2310.19103 (2023); S. K. Ainsworth, J. Hayase and S. Srinivasa, Git Re-Basin, arXiv:2209.04836 (2022)
locator: to verify: Entezari et al., the conjecture stated in the introduction.
why_important: If true, SGD solutions form essentially one basin up to symmetry, which underlies model merging and weight averaging.
where_it_stands: Mean-field two-layer version proved (Ferbach et al.); general case open.
note: Fame: a named conjecture with large follow-up (Git Re-Basin, model merging).

audit.status_ref: Ferbach-Goujaud-Gidel-Dieuleveut2310.19103 Theorem3.1/Corollary3.2 PDF p4, fully opened with assumptions, already prove finite-time independent two-layer SGD mean-field prediction linearity after permutation and a population squared-loss barrier bound. Same initialization law and underlying time T, bounded-Lipschitz activation/data and regularity, sufficiently large width then sufficiently small step are essential. Assumption2 is unused for unregularized noiseless SGD. Deep Theorem5.2 p6 concerns Gaussian initialization, not trained deep solutions. Recent Zhan-Li-Wu2503.06001 Theorem6 p7 states O(m^-1/2) matching-barrier decay in its teacher-student setting under the assumed multinomial/simplex global-minimum sampling law (Assumption3 p4); it does not derive that law from SGD. The following rate calculation additionally introduces uniform-overlap approximation Eq10. No general trained-deep theorem certified.
audit.statement_ok: NO: c incorrectly lists finite-time SGD as unproved after citing a paper that proves a finite-time two-layer SGD result. Specify same data/task,initialization law,SGD time/step/width limit and a high-probability or typical-solution quantifier. Distinguish prediction interpolation,loss barrier,algorithmic matching and all global minima. A statement about every SGD solution is stronger than the source likely/most formulation.
audit.replace_with: Choose a trained depth>=3 model or a quantitative ReLU extension with explicit finite-time width/step requirements beyond2310.19103. Separate existence of a low-barrier permutation from finding it efficiently. Verify the common trained neuron-law assumption rather than assuming SGD uniformly samples global minima.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: T272_transport_diagnostic.md derives a bounded-neuron prediction-interpolation defect <=(D/2)W1 between matched empirical laws. The hard missing input is a suitable trained-law theorem; this deterministic reduction is already the published optimal-transport mechanism.
audit.locator: 2110.06296 introductory conjecture PDF p2 and Sec3,TheoremD1/3.1 p21 is initialization.2209.04836 Conjecture1 p1 says most SGD solutions;Lemma1 p4 is matching-complexity.2310.19103 Ass1/2,Theorem3.1 andCor3.2 p4;deep Theorem5.2 p6.2503.06001 Ass1/3 p4,Theorem6/Eq10 p7.

title: Low-loss paths between minima found by SGD
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Garipov et al. and Draxler et al. find that minima found by SGD in deep networks are connected by simple curves (polygonal chains or Bézier curves) of nearly constant low loss. Kuditipudi et al. prove connectivity for dropout-stable or noise-stable solutions. Prove that for a natural class of networks (e.g. two-layer ReLU networks of moderate width on generic data) any two minima reached by gradient descent from random initialization are joined by a path along which the training loss stays below epsilon, without assuming dropout stability.
statement_caveat: Statements for all global minima of very wide networks follow from overparameterization arguments; the question is about networks of moderate width.
source: T. Garipov et al., Loss Surfaces, Mode Connectivity, and Fast Ensembling of DNNs, arXiv:1802.10026 (2018); F. Draxler et al., Essentially No Barriers in Neural Network Energy Landscape, arXiv:1803.00885 (2018); R. Kuditipudi et al., Explaining Landscape Connectivity of Low-cost Solutions for Multilayer Nets, arXiv:1906.06247 (2019)
locator: to verify: Kuditipudi et al., discussion of removing the stability assumption.
why_important: Connectivity of the solution set is a basic geometric fact about loss landscapes, and is used in ensembling and fine-tuning.
where_it_stands: Open in the stated generality as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: mode connectivity is a well-known phenomenon (NeurIPS 2018 papers).

title: The lottery ticket hypothesis in its original (trainable subnetwork) form
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Frankle and Carbin conjecture that a dense randomly initialized network contains a sparse subnetwork that, trained in isolation from the same initial weights, reaches the test accuracy of the full network in at most the same number of steps. Prove, for a natural model (e.g. a two-layer network learning a sparse teacher), that such a subnetwork exists with a constant fraction of the weights removed, and that iterative magnitude pruning finds it.
statement_caveat: The 'strong' lottery ticket hypothesis (a subnetwork of a larger random network approximates a target without any training) is proved (Malach et al.; Pensia et al.; Orseau et al.). The original form involves training and is different.
source: J. Frankle and M. Carbin, The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks, arXiv:1803.03635 (2018); E. Malach, G. Yehudai, S. Shalev-Shwartz and O. Shamir, Proving the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Pruning is All You Need, arXiv:2002.00585 (2020)
locator: to verify: Frankle–Carbin, Section 1 (statement of the hypothesis).
why_important: The hypothesis motivated much of the pruning literature; a theorem would say what makes an initialization 'winning'.
where_it_stands: Strong form proved; original form open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICLR 2019 best paper; extremely widely cited.

title: Can gradient descent learn Barron-class functions at Monte Carlo rates?
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Functions with finite Barron norm are approximated by two-layer networks with m units at rate m^{-1/2} independently of dimension, and the minimum-Barron-norm estimator generalizes at a dimension-free rate (E, Ma and Wu). Determine whether gradient descent on two-layer networks trained from random initialization achieves test error O(n^{-1/2}) (up to logs, dimension-free constants) for every target of Barron norm ≤ 1, in time polynomial in d and n, or prove a lower bound for gradient methods.
statement_caveat: Computational lower bounds for learning some two-layer networks (statistical query, cryptographic) suggest the full class is hard; the question is whether gradient descent achieves the rate on the whole class or on a natural subclass, and which.
source: W. E, C. Ma and L. Wu, The Barron Space and the Flow-induced Function Spaces for Neural Network Models, arXiv:1906.08039 (2019); W. E, C. Ma, S. Wojtowytsch and L. Wu, Towards a Mathematical Understanding of Neural Network-Based Machine Learning: what we know and what we don't, arXiv:2009.10713 (2020)
locator: to verify: E et al. 2009.10713, the list of open problems (section on the gap between approximation, estimation and optimization).
why_important: Barron's theorem is the standard explanation of how networks beat the curse of dimensionality; whether training realizes it is the open half.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: Barron 1993 is classic; E et al. list this among the main open questions.

title: Deep networks learn low bottleneck rank: Jacot's conjectures
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Jacot (arXiv:2209.15055) defines the Jacobian rank Rank_J and the bottleneck rank Rank_BN of a piecewise-linear function and proves that the large-depth limit R_infinity of the normalized L2 representation cost of deep ReLU networks satisfies Rank_J <= R_infinity <= Rank_BN; the equality R_infinity = Rank_BN is his conjecture (Remark 4). (i) Prove or refute the equality for finite piecewise-linear functions on a bounded domain. (ii) For n iid samples from a law on a bounded domain labelled by a piecewise-linear f* of bottleneck rank k, and a stated depth L, weight decay lambda and initialization, prove that with high probability gradient descent on the regularized empirical loss reaches a network whose function has bottleneck rank k (population rank recovery), with explicit dependence on n, L and lambda.
statement_caveat: The rank characterization of the infinite-depth representation cost is proved; the claims about trained networks are conjectures.
source: A. Jacot, Implicit Bias of Large Depth Networks: a Notion of Rank for Nonlinear Functions, arXiv:2209.15055 (2022)
locator: to verify: the stated conjectures in Section 4-5.
why_important: It extends the low-rank implicit bias of linear networks (T232, T234) to nonlinear deep networks.
where_it_stands: Open (partial results by Jacot and coauthors, to verify).
note: Fame: ICLR 2023 paper; active line.

audit.status_ref: Jacot2209.15055 Theorem1 PDF p5, opened in full, proves Rank_J<=R_infinity<=Rank_BN, not equality. Remark4 on the same page conjectures R_infinity=Rank_BN. Propositions2-4 PDF pp5-6 establish finite-depth rank-one global-minimizer/representation bounds, Proposition5 p7 a true-function rank upper bound; these are not GD convergence guarantees.
audit.statement_ok: NO: the opening assertion says the infinite-depth normalized representation cost converges to bottleneck rank as a theorem; the cited source proves only a sandwich and explicitly conjectures equality. It also mixes global minimizers with the optimizer reached by GD, and finite-data rank-one interpolation with recovery of the population function rank.
audit.replace_with: Separate (i) R_infinity=Rank_BN for finite piecewise-linear functions on bounded domains and (ii) GD dynamics under a specified finite-data/noise/depth regime. For a probabilistic solver target, ask quantitative population-rank recovery from iid data under explicit assumptions.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: test a concrete piecewise-linear function with Rank_J<Rank_BN using the source construction and bound its representation cost. The already-proved rank-one interpolation/global-minimum statements are diagnostics, not new solver work.
audit.locator: 2209.15055 Theorem1 and Remark4 PDF p5; Propositions2-4 pp5-6; Proposition5 and Remark5 PDF p7. Remark5 says experiments did not observe GD underestimating true rank and discusses local rather than global minima.

title: Depth separation for gradient-trained networks on hierarchical targets
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Prove a natural target class (e.g. f(x) = g(h(x)) with h a low-degree polynomial feature) such that gradient descent on three-layer networks learns it to error epsilon with n = poly(d) samples and time, while gradient descent on two-layer networks (any width polynomial in d) needs n ≥ d^{omega(1)}, both from standard initializations.
statement_caveat: Separations exist for specific constructions and modified training (Allen-Zhu and Li; Nichani, Damian and Lee); a natural class with standard training on both sides is the open part.
source: Z. Allen-Zhu and Y. Li, Backward Feature Correction: How Deep Learning Performs Deep (Hierarchical) Learning, arXiv:2001.04413 (2020); E. Nichani, A. Damian and J. D. Lee, Provable Guarantees for Nonlinear Feature Learning in Three-Layer Neural Networks, arXiv:2305.06986 (2023); B. Ghorbani et al., When Do Neural Networks Outperform Kernel Methods?, arXiv:2006.13409 (2020)
locator: to verify: Nichani–Damian–Lee, conclusion.
why_important: Why depth helps learning (not just approximation) is one of the central questions of the field.
where_it_stands: Partial; natural-class separation with standard training open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: depth separation for learning is a long-standing goal (also T301).

title: Stability-based generalization bounds for SGD on overparameterized nonconvex networks
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Hardt, Recht and Singer bound the generalization gap of SGD by its uniform stability; for nonconvex losses the bound grows polynomially with the number of steps T, and becomes vacuous for training to interpolation. Prove, for a natural class of networks (e.g. two-layer ReLU networks of width polynomial in n) trained by SGD to near-zero training loss, a stability-based bound on the generalization gap that does not grow with T and is o(1) as n → ∞.
statement_caveat: Such bounds exist in the NTK regime and for convex problems; the question is beyond the kernel regime.
source: M. Hardt, B. Recht and Y. Singer, Train faster, generalize better: Stability of stochastic gradient descent, arXiv:1509.01240 (2015)
locator: to verify: Section 3 (nonconvex case) and the discussion of long training.
why_important: Stability is one of the few generalization tools that sees the algorithm; making it work for long training would explain why SGD can be run to interpolation.
where_it_stands: Open beyond the kernel regime as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: Hardt–Recht–Singer is a classic (ICML 2016).

title: A reparametrization-invariant flatness measure that controls generalization
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Sharp minima were proposed to generalize worse (Keskar et al.), but Dinh et al. show that sharpness is not invariant under reparametrizations that leave the network function unchanged, so it cannot by itself predict generalization. Find a measure of flatness invariant under the symmetries of ReLU networks (rescalings, permutations) and prove that, for minima reached by SGD on a natural model, the test error is bounded above by an increasing function of this measure that tends to the Bayes error as the measure → 0.
statement_caveat: Large-scale empirical studies (Jiang et al.) find many flatness measures correlate with test error; no theorem of the stated kind is known to the writer.
source: L. Dinh, R. Pascanu, S. Bengio and Y. Bengio, Sharp Minima Can Generalize For Deep Nets, arXiv:1703.04933 (2017); N. S. Keskar et al., arXiv:1609.04836 (2016); Y. Jiang et al., Fantastic Generalization Measures and Where to Find Them, arXiv:1912.02178 (2019)
locator: to verify: Dinh et al., conclusion.
why_important: 'Flat minima generalize' is one of the most repeated claims in deep learning; a precise version would be a theorem connecting optimization geometry and statistics.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the flat-minima debate (Hochreiter–Schmidhuber 1997; Keskar; Dinh) is widely known.

title: Spectral bias in the feature-learning regime
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Spectral bias with feature learning. On the sphere S^(d-1), a two-layer network f(x) = (1/m) sum_j a_j sigma(w_j . x + b_j) in mean-field scaling (both layers trained, gradient flow on the population square loss, m tending to infinity), from a stated rotation-invariant initialization, with sigma a fixed activation whose Gegenbauer coefficients are nonzero in every degree (ReLU without bias misses the odd degrees above 1). Let t_k be the first time the residual energy in degree k falls below half its initial value. (a) Fixed d, target a sum of one zonal harmonic of each degree 1..K along directions u_1..u_K: determine t_k, decide whether it increases in k for generic directions, and how it depends on the angles between the u_k; compare with the lazy (NTK) times, which are set by the kernel's eigenvalues and are increasing in k. (b) d tending to infinity: express t_k through the leap complexity of the target. A theorem that t_k is increasing in k for every target is not expected: a degree-k component along an already learned direction can be learned earlier than a lower degree along a new one.
statement_caveat: Non-uniform input densities change the ordering (Basri et al.); the question is for uniform inputs first.
source: N. Rahaman et al., On the Spectral Bias of Neural Networks, arXiv:1806.08734 (2018); Z.-Q. J. Xu, Y. Zhang and Y. Xiao, Frequency Principle, arXiv:1901.06523 (2019); R. Basri et al., arXiv:2003.04560 (2020)
locator: to verify: Rahaman et al., discussion section.
why_important: Spectral bias is one of the most widely invoked explanations of good generalization of networks.
where_it_stands: NTK-regime versions proved (Cao et al. 2019; Basri et al.); feature-learning regime open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: widely cited empirical principle.

audit.status_ref: Rahaman1806.08734 Theorem1 PDF p2, fully read, describes Fourier decay of a fixed ReLU representation, not a feature-learning harmonic hitting-time theorem. Xu-Zhang-Luo-Xiao-Ma1901.06523 Theorem1 p11, fully read, gives a small-weight one-dimensional tanh per-frequency gradient comparison on a1-C exp(-c/delta) fraction of a small ball, not global training-time ordering. Basri et al.2003.04560 Theorem1 p6 gives ~O(kappa^2/p_min) in the stated S1 fixed-kernel setting;Theorem2 p7 controls finite-wide deep training by NTK eigendecomposition under its width/init/step assumptions. No theorem settling the requested nonlinear mean-field harmonic times certified.
audit.statement_ok: NO: choose activation,biases,initialization law,mean-field parametrization,target class and absolute/relative error hitting time. Increasing times for every k cannot be assumed merely from eigenvalue decay, and some harmonics are not representable in a bias-free two-layer ReLU model. Training-time harmonic coupling is absent from the proposed definition.
audit.replace_with: Fix a biased two-layer model and a finite representable harmonic target, define relative mode-error hitting times and a small initialization regime. First ask a two-mode quantitative order theorem with all assumptions explicit, checking existing mean-field analyses.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: T280_parity_diagnostic.md proves odd harmonic degrees>=3 identically vanish for bias-free two-layer ReLU at every training time. This repairs the architecture/target scope; it does not settle a biased feature-learning ordering theorem.
audit.locator: 1806.08734 Thm1 p2,Sec3 p3,Sec6 p8 (future Fourier/sensitivity analysis, no numbered proposed harmonic-order conjecture).1901.06523 Thm1 p11 and setup p10.2003.04560 Thm1/Section4.3 p6,Thm2 p7. Basri higher-dimensional conjecture p6 concerns its kernel setting.

title: A separation between SGD and full-batch gradient descent for neural networks
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Amir, Koren and Livni construct stochastic convex optimization problems on which one-pass SGD generalizes while full-batch gradient descent with the same number of steps (and any regularization) overfits. Prove an analogous separation on a natural neural-network learning problem: a data distribution and architecture on which small-batch SGD reaches test error epsilon with n samples, while full-batch GD (any step size and iteration count in a polynomial range) has test error bounded away from epsilon.
statement_caveat: Empirically the gap between small and large batch is often closed by tuning (learning-rate scaling); a theorem for a natural problem is the question.
source: I. Amir, T. Koren and R. Livni, SGD Generalizes Better Than GD (And Regularization Doesn't Help), arXiv:2102.01117 (2021); N. S. Keskar et al., On Large-Batch Training for Deep Learning: Generalization Gap and Sharp Minima, arXiv:1609.04836 (2016)
locator: to verify: Amir–Koren–Livni, conclusion (beyond convex problems).
why_important: Whether stochasticity itself is a source of generalization is a basic question about why SGD works.
where_it_stands: Open for natural nonconvex problems as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the large-batch generalization gap is a standard topic.

title: Gaussian universality for nonconvex learning problems and learned features
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Gaussian universality for empirical risk minimization on features phi(x) says that training and test errors match those of Gaussian features with the same first two moments. Montanari and Saeed (arXiv:2202.08832) prove it for nonconvex losses over compact constraint sets when the features lie in a domain of Gaussianity (low-dimensional projections close to Gaussian), for the minimal training error and, under extra conditions, for the test error of selected near-minimizers; matching two moments alone is not enough (a localized coordinate breaks it). Open: (a) test-error universality for the minimizer an algorithm actually reaches, for example gradient descent on a two-layer network, without assuming a selected or unique minimizer; (b) for features after one gradient step on the first layer with step size eta of order n^a, the readout fitted on a sample independent of the one used for the step, determine the range of a for which the features stay in a domain of Gaussianity, and the test error outside it.
statement_caveat: Universality fails for features that have learned a spike after one large gradient step in some regimes (Ba et al.; Cui et al.); the question is to delimit exactly when it holds.
source: A. Montanari and B. Saeed, Universality of empirical risk minimization, arXiv:2202.08832 (2022); H. Hu and Y. M. Lu, Universality Laws for High-Dimensional Learning with Random Features, arXiv:2009.07669 (2020); S. Goldt et al., The Gaussian equivalence of generative models for learning with shallow neural networks, arXiv:2006.14709 (2020)
locator: to verify: Montanari–Saeed, conclusion (nonconvex case as open).
why_important: Gaussian equivalence is the engine behind most exact asymptotics of learning; knowing exactly where it holds decides which predictions transfer to real data.
where_it_stands: Convex case proved; nonconvex and learned-feature cases open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: central tool in high-dimensional learning theory.

audit.status_ref: Montanari-Saeed2202.08832 Theorem1 PDF p4, with Assumptions1-5/Definition1 pp3-4 opened in full, already proves nonconvex ERM-value universality for compact constraints in a domain of Gaussianity, fixed projection count and proportional dimensions. Theorem3 and Corollary1 PDF p11 give conditional universality of extremal test error over near-interpolators; Theorem4 p12 gives selected-minimizer test universality under its convexity, gap, or differentiable-perturbation alternatives. These deciding statements were opened, and none is an unrestricted learned-feature SGD theorem.
audit.statement_ok: NO: cited Montanari-Saeed is not limited to convex losses/penalties. Matching first two moments alone is insufficient: a localized coordinate can distinguish Rademacher from Gaussian features with a bounded Lipschitz nonconvex loss. State projection-Gaussianity/delocalization, data independence, width scaling and minimizer-selection assumptions. Features learned from the same observations require an explicit dependence model.
audit.replace_with: Fix a one-step learned-feature model with a specified step size and independent evaluation sample; determine a domain of Gaussianity and a test-risk selection criterion beyond current hypotheses. Remove the blanket convex-only baseline.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: completed bounded-Lipschitz localized-coordinate counterexample in T282_projection_obstruction.md. A sample-split one-step feature model with explicit spike strength is a possible narrow research target; novelty/status remain to check.
audit.locator: 2202.08832 Definition1/Assumptions1-5 pp3-4,Theorem1 p4,Theorem3/Corollary1 p11,Theorem4 p12;2009.07669 Theorem1 and assumptions;2006.14709 Conjecture1 and Theorem2 (projection Gaussian equivalence). Claimed conclusion posing all nonconvex cases as open was not found.

title: The low-degree conjecture
domain_name: Deep learning: high-dimensional learning, statistical physics and computational limits
statement: For a planted high-dimensional testing problem (planted distribution P_n against null Q_n), the low-degree heuristic predicts that if every polynomial of degree D = polylog(n) (or D = n^{δ}) fails to distinguish P_n from Q_n in the sense that the low-degree likelihood ratio has bounded norm, then no polynomial-time algorithm distinguishes them. Find a formulation of this conjecture, for a natural class of noise-robust, symmetric problems, that survives the known counterexamples, and prove it for some class, or prove it implies a standard complexity-theoretic assumption.
statement_caveat: The original form (Hopkins) has counterexamples: Holmgren and Wein construct problems where low-degree fails but an efficient algorithm succeeds; lattice-based algorithms beat low-degree predictions in noiseless clustering (Zadik, Song, Wein and Bruna). The question is the right statement, then its proof.
source: S. B. Hopkins, P. K. Kothari, A. Potechin, P. Raghavendra, T. Schramm and D. Steurer, The power of sum-of-squares for detecting hidden structures, arXiv:1710.05017 (2017); D. Kunisky, A. S. Wein and A. S. Bandeira, Notes on Computational Hardness of Hypothesis Testing: Predictions using the Low-Degree Likelihood Ratio, arXiv:1907.11636 (2019); J. Holmgren and A. S. Wein, Counterexamples to the Low-Degree Conjecture, arXiv:2004.08454 (2020)
locator: to verify: Kunisky–Wein–Bandeira, Section 4 (the conjecture as stated, with its caveats).
why_important: Almost every statistical-computational gap claimed in high-dimensional learning (planted clique, tensor PCA, single-index models, community detection) rests on low-degree evidence; whether that evidence is a proof of hardness is the biggest foundational question of the area.
where_it_stands: Open; original form refuted for contrived and noiseless problems.
note: Fame: the central conjecture of average-case computational complexity for statistics.

title: Does the overlap gap property imply algorithmic hardness?
domain_name: Deep learning: high-dimensional learning, statistical physics and computational limits
statement: For random optimization problems (spin-glass ground states, independent sets in sparse random graphs, the binary perceptron, random k-SAT), the overlap gap property (OGP) — the absence of pairs (or tuples) of near-optimal solutions at intermediate overlaps — is proved to obstruct stable algorithms (approximate message passing, low-degree polynomials, Langevin dynamics on bounded time). Prove that in some such problem the onset of the multi-OGP coincides with failure of every polynomial-time algorithm, under a standard assumption, or exhibit a polynomial-time algorithm that crosses an OGP threshold.
statement_caveat: OGP lower bounds are for classes of stable algorithms; non-stable algorithms (e.g. lattice reduction, Gaussian elimination) can beat them in structured problems.
source: D. Gamarnik, The Overlap Gap Property: a Geometric Barrier to Optimizing over Random Structures, arXiv:2109.14409 (2021)
locator: to verify: the survey's concluding open problems.
why_important: OGP is the main geometric explanation of algorithmic hardness in random structures, including the landscapes of learning problems such as the perceptron.
where_it_stands: Open (hardness proved only against stable algorithm classes).
note: Fame: OGP (Gamarnik–Sudan 2014 onward) is a central tool; the survey is in PNAS.

title: The statistical-computational gap of the committee machine with many hidden units
domain_name: Deep learning: high-dimensional learning, statistical physics and computational limits
statement: In the teacher-student committee machine (a two-layer network with K hidden sign units and fixed second layer) with n = alpha·d samples, Aubin et al. prove the replica formula for the Bayes-optimal error at fixed K and find, as K grows, a specialization transition at alpha_IT of order K, while approximate message passing needs alpha of order K² to beat a trivial non-specialized solution. Prove the large-K asymptotics of both thresholds rigorously and prove that no polynomial-time algorithm (or no low-degree algorithm) achieves specialization below order K² samples per dimension.
statement_caveat: The finite-K replica formula is proved; the K → ∞ scaling and computational lower bounds are open.
source: B. Aubin, A. Maillard, J. Barbier, F. Krzakala, N. Macris and L. Zdeborová, The committee machine: Computational to statistical gaps in learning a two-layers neural network, arXiv:1806.05451 (2018)
locator: to verify: Section 4 (large-K analysis) and the conclusion.
