note: Fame: induction heads (Olsson et al. 2022) are a central object in mechanistic interpretability.

title: Implicit bias of softmax attention: max-margin token selection
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Tarzanagh, Li, Zhang and Oymak show that gradient descent on the key-query matrix of a single softmax attention layer (with logistic-type loss and separable data) converges in direction to the solution of a hard-margin SVM that separates optimal from non-optimal tokens, under conditions (locally, or globally for some initializations). Prove global directional convergence for general data and initialization, and extend to joint training of the value/prediction head and to several heads.
statement_caveat: Local convergence and global convergence under extra assumptions are known; the general case and joint training are posed as open.
source: D. A. Tarzanagh, Y. Li, X. Zhang and S. Oymak, Max-Margin Token Selection in Attention Mechanism, arXiv:2306.13596 (2023)
locator: to verify: the conclusion's open problems.
why_important: It is the attention analogue of the max-margin implicit bias of linear classifiers (Soudry et al.), the cleanest description of what attention learns to attend to.
where_it_stands: Open in general.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2023; a well-cited line ('transformers as support vector machines').

title: The optimal memorization capacity of ReLU networks with bounded bit complexity
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Vardi, Yehudai and Shamir (arXiv:2110.03187) prove that n points in R^d with norm at most r, pairwise separation delta and C classes can be memorized by a ReLU network with O~(sqrt n) parameters plus terms in d and log(r/delta), using weights of O~(sqrt n) bits; that W parameters of B bits give VC dimension O(W B + W log W) (Theorem 6.1); and a precision-depth tradeoff (Theorem 6.2). The logarithmic gaps are posed in their Conclusion. With d, r/delta and C fixed and the architecture counted in the bit budget, determine up to constant factors the minimal number of parameters W(n, B) that memorizes every allowed n-point dataset with B-bit weights; in particular, does W = O(n / log n) suffice when B = O(log n), or is the true requirement larger than the counting bound Omega(n / log n)?
statement_caveat: With unbounded precision, O(sqrt n) neurons suffice for arbitrary points (Yun, Sra and Jadbabaie for width-depth trade-offs); the role of precision is the open part.
source: G. Vardi, G. Yehudai and O. Shamir, On the Optimal Memorization Power of ReLU Neural Networks, arXiv:2110.03187 (2021); C. Yun, S. Sra and A. Jadbabaie, Small ReLU networks are powerful memorizers: a tight analysis of memorization capacity, arXiv:1810.07770 (2018)
locator: to verify: Vardi et al., discussion of bit complexity and open questions.
why_important: Memorization capacity bounds how much of its training data an overparameterized model can store, which is the counting side of the generalization puzzle.
where_it_stands: Open (logarithmic gaps and bounded-precision regime).
note: Fame: ICLR 2022 spotlight (to verify).

audit.status_ref: Vardi-Yehudai-Shamir2110.03187 Theorem3.1/Remark3.2 PDF p5,Theorem6.1 p8 and Theorem6.2 p9, all opened in full, already provide parameter/bit-complexity upper and lower bounds up to logarithms. Theorem6.1 is VCdim=O(WB+W logW), including architecture encoding. Theorem6.2 gives a constructive precision-depth tradeoff. Exact logarithmic gaps are explicitly posed in Conclusion p9, but their current status remains uncleared.
audit.statement_ok: NO: the claimed sqrt(n)-parameter baseline suppresses an additive input dimension d and logarithmic dependence on norm/separation/classes. The precision role is already studied by the cited source, not an untouched regime. O(logn)-bit and o(n) parameters is finer than the n^(1-epsilon) impossibility: the counting bound only forces W=Omega(n/logn) for polynomially bounded W, so it alone does not answer the logarithmic saving question.
audit.replace_with: Fix d, norm/separation/class count and a total bit encoding including graph structure. Ask whether W=O(n/logn) with B=O(logn) suffices for every allowed dataset, or give a matching lower bound, tracking actual rather than tilde precision.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: specialize source Theorem6.2 to polylogarithmic bit budgets and compare exact logarithms against Theorem6.1. This is a concrete gap calculation, not a new counting theorem.
audit.locator: 2110.03187 Theorem3.1/Remark3.2 PDF p5,Theorem6.1 p8,Theorem6.2 and Conclusion p9;1810.07770 Section3 shallow-width memorization. Exact source posing of logarithmic gaps is Conclusion p9.

title: Depth separation for functions approximable to inverse-polynomial accuracy
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Known depth-2 versus depth-3 separations (Eldan and Shamir, arXiv:1512.03965; Daniely; Safran and Shamir) use functions whose Lipschitz constant grows polynomially in d, or highly oscillatory ones. Safran, Eldan and Shamir (arXiv:1904.06984, Theorem 1) show that every 1-Lipschitz radial function on the unit ball is uniformly approximable to accuracy epsilon by depth 2 with width exp(O(epsilon^-9 log(d/epsilon))), polynomial in d at fixed accuracy. Find an explicit O(1)-Lipschitz function on the unit ball of R^d, computed by a depth-3 network of size poly(d), that depth-2 networks cannot approximate within a fixed constant in L2(mu), for a natural law mu, unless their width is super-polynomial in d (the function must be non-radial), or prove that no such separation exists for a stated natural class; and sharpen the dependence on epsilon of the radial upper bound.
statement_caveat: Safran, Eldan and Shamir give separations of a different (approximation versus 1/poly accuracy) type and pose the Lipschitz version.
source: I. Safran, R. Eldan and O. Shamir, Depth Separations in Neural Networks: What is Actually Being Separated?, arXiv:1904.06984 (2019); R. Eldan and O. Shamir, The Power of Depth for Feedforward Neural Networks, arXiv:1512.03965 (2015)
locator: to verify: Safran–Eldan–Shamir, the open question in the conclusion.
why_important: It asks whether depth separations concern functions anyone would want to learn, or only pathological ones (compare T277 and T301).
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: COLT 2019.

audit.status_ref: Safran-Eldan-Shamir1904.06984 Theorem1 PDF p5 with Assumption1 p4, opened in full, gives uniform unit-ball approximation of every1-Lipschitz radial function by depth2 width exp(O(epsilon^-9 log(d/epsilon))). Hence fixed-accuracy width polynomial in d is already proved for this normalized radial class. The source Introduction pp1-3 explicitly distinguishes already-known polynomial-Lipschitz separations from the intended O(1)-Lipschitz, bounded-radius, fixed-accuracy question.
audit.statement_ok: NO: requesting only poly(d)-Lipschitz separating functions repeats the stated known regime; the genuinely normalized question is O(1)-Lipschitz on a domain of O(1) radius with fixed accuracy. Source does not prove a joint poly(d,1/epsilon) upper bound for all radial functions, and the row informal baseline incorrectly suggests it does.
audit.replace_with: Require O(1) Lipschitz constant, O(1) domain radius and constant L2 accuracy, with an explicit natural probability law; ask a nonradial depth2-versus3 separation beyond the radial upper bound, or sharpen the radial epsilon dependence.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: verify normalization under scaling/dilation and optimize one quantitative approximation exponent; the normalized nonradial separation is a programme absent a concrete candidate.
audit.locator: 1904.06984 Introduction exact posed question PDF p3,Theorem1 p5/Assumption1 p4;1512.03965 Theorem1 main separation. The locator is introduction, not an unverified conclusion.

title: Zero-one laws for graph neural networks on random graphs
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Adam-Day, Iliant and Ceylan prove that for Erdős–Rényi graphs G(n, p) with fixed p, every graph neural network binary classifier from a broad class (mean-aggregation or graph convolutional networks with Lipschitz activations and random node features) outputs the same value with probability tending to 0 or 1 as n → ∞. Extend the zero-one law to sparse random graphs (p = c/n), where local structure does not concentrate, or to other aggregation schemes (max, attention), or exhibit a GNN classifier whose output probability converges to a value strictly between 0 and 1 on G(n, c/n).
statement_caveat: The dense case is proved; sparse graphs are posed as the natural open extension (to verify their conclusion).
source: S. Adam-Day, T. M. Iliant and İ. İ. Ceylan, Zero-One Laws of Graph Neural Networks, arXiv:2301.13060 (2023); N. Keriven, A. Bietti and S. Vaiter, Convergence and Stability of Graph Convolutional Networks on Large Random Graphs, arXiv:2006.01868 (2020)
locator: to verify: Adam-Day et al., Section 6 (limitations and open questions).
why_important: It is the GNN analogue of the zero-one laws for first-order logic on random graphs (Glebskii et al.; Fagin), and bounds what GNNs can distinguish on random inputs.
where_it_stands: Open for sparse graphs as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2023.

title: Graph neural networks on sparse random graphs: limits and transferability
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Keriven, Bietti and Vaiter (arXiv:2006.01868) prove that graph convolutional networks on latent-position random graphs with edge density alpha_n >= C log(n)/n converge to a continuous limit network, with error O(1/sqrt n + 1/sqrt(n alpha_n)). At constant average degree (G(n, c/n), or a finite-type stochastic block model with bounded node features and a stated convention for isolated vertices) node outputs keep local randomness, and the limit object is the network run on the local weak limit, a marked Galton-Watson tree. For a message-passing network of depth L with bounded Lipschitz updates, bound the distance (bounded-Lipschitz or Wasserstein) between the law of the output at a uniform root and the tree output, and between the empirical output measure (or a pooled average) and its limit, with explicit dependence on n, c and L, including L growing with n.
statement_caveat: For sparse graphs the graphon limit degenerates; local-limit approaches exist for message passing but quantitative GNN results are limited (to verify).
source: N. Keriven, A. Bietti and S. Vaiter, Convergence and Stability of Graph Convolutional Networks on Large Random Graphs, arXiv:2006.01868 (2020)
locator: to verify: Keriven et al., conclusion (sparse regime).
why_important: Real graphs are sparse; without a sparse limit theory GNN transfer between graph sizes has no guarantee.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2020.

audit.status_ref: Keriven-Bietti-Vaiter2006.01868 Theorem1 PDF p5, fully opened with model/assumptions p4, already handles alpha_n>=C*log(n)/n and error C1/sqrt(n)+C2/sqrt(n*alpha_n), plus pooling concentration. Thus logarithmic average-degree convergence is in the source. Constant expected-degree local-weak limits are a different target and their current quantitative GNN status remains uncleared.
audit.statement_ok: NO: dense-only baseline is false; the cited theorem explicitly treats relatively sparse logarithmic-degree latent graphs. For constant-degree graphs node outputs retain local randomness, so specify convergence in law of rooted outputs, empirical output measures or pooled averages, rather than the same deterministic nodewise continuous limit.
audit.replace_with: Fix a bounded-depth message-passing architecture on G(n,c/n) or a finite-type SBM with bounded features and a rule for isolated nodes. Bound a metric between rooted-output laws or empirical output measures and a marked Galton-Watson-tree output; track depth growth and pooling separately.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: couple radius-L neighborhoods in G(n,c/n) to a Poisson Galton-Watson tree for fixed c,L and bounded local observables. Track collision/truncation errors, then translate to the specified GNN output. Do not offer the already-proved log-degree theorem as new.
audit.locator: 2006.01868 Introduction PDF p2 relatively sparse regime; model5/assumptions6 PDF p4;Theorem1 PDF p5. Exact unproved constant-degree author-posed GNN theorem was not located.

title: The scaling limit of trained deep residual networks
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Consider ResNets h_{k+1} = h_k + L^{−beta} sigma(A_k h_k) of depth L. Cohen, Cont, Rossier and Xu find empirically that trained weights A_k, viewed as functions of k/L, scale either like a smooth function (giving a neural ODE limit) or like a rough process (giving an SDE-type limit), depending on initialization and beta. Prove, for gradient descent training of a deep ResNet with a natural initialization, which limit the trained network converges to as L → ∞, and prove convergence of the training dynamics to the corresponding limiting (ODE or SDE) training dynamics.
statement_caveat: Results exist for linear ResNets and for the infinite-depth limit at initialization (to verify Marion et al. on implicit regularization of deep residual networks).
source: A.-S. Cohen, R. Cont, A. Rossier and R. Xu, Scaling Properties of Deep Residual Networks, arXiv:2105.12245 (2021)
locator: to verify: Cohen et al., conclusion.
why_important: It decides whether the neural-ODE picture of deep ResNets is accurate for trained networks, connecting deep learning with rough paths and stochastic analysis.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICML 2021.

title: Which high-dimensional function classes do deep networks learn without the curse of dimensionality?
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Poggio et al. argue that deep networks avoid the curse of dimensionality for compositional functions f = f_1 ∘ ... with each constituent depending on few variables (hierarchically local), while shallow networks need width exponential in d. Prove a statistical (not only approximation) separation: a natural compositional function class in which a deep network trained by gradient descent (or ERM over a size-restricted class) attains error n^{−r} with r independent of d, while every kernel method or shallow network needs n exponential in d for constant error.
statement_caveat: Approximation-theoretic versions are proved; sample-complexity separations exist for specific constructions (e.g. T294's hierarchical models, T231 leap functions) but not for the general compositional class.
source: T. Poggio, H. Mhaskar, L. Rosasco, B. Miranda and Q. Liao, Why and When Can Deep -- but Not Shallow -- Networks Avoid the Curse of Dimensionality: a Review, arXiv:1611.00740 (2016)
locator: to verify: the review's open questions section.
why_important: It is the most common explanation of why deep learning works in high dimension; it has no proof for trained networks.
where_it_stands: Open (statistical, trained-network version).
note: Fame: the Poggio et al. review is very widely cited.

title: The curse of parametric complexity in operator learning
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Lanthaler and Stuart prove that for general classes of Lipschitz (or C^k) operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces, any operator-learning architecture defined by a fixed number of parameters needs a number of parameters exponential in 1/epsilon to reach accuracy epsilon. Identify natural operator classes (e.g. solution operators of elliptic or parabolic PDEs with random coefficients, or Hamilton–Jacobi equations) for which neural operators or DeepONets achieve polynomial complexity in 1/epsilon, and prove matching sample-complexity bounds for learning them from random input functions.
statement_caveat: Positive results exist for specific PDE operators with structure; a general characterization is open.
source: S. Lanthaler and A. M. Stuart, The Parametric Complexity of Operator Learning, arXiv:2306.15924 (2023); S. Lanthaler, S. Mishra and G. E. Karniadakis, Error estimates for DeepOnets: A deep learning framework in infinite dimensions, arXiv:2102.09618 (2021); N. Kovachki et al., Neural Operator: Learning Maps Between Function Spaces, arXiv:2108.08481 (2021)
locator: to verify: Lanthaler–Stuart, the discussion of beating the curse.
why_important: Operator learning is the main use of networks in scientific computing (weather, PDE surrogates) and inputs are random fields, so its sample complexity is a question in infinite-dimensional probability.
where_it_stands: Open (general characterization).
note: Fame: Neural Operator (JMLR 2023) and DeepONet are standard.

title: Transformers as amortized Bayesian inference: approximation and generalization
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Müller et al. train transformers on datasets sampled from a prior over data-generating processes so that the network outputs the posterior predictive distribution (prior-data fitted networks). Give quantitative guarantees: for a given prior (e.g. a Gaussian process prior), bound the size of transformer needed to approximate the posterior predictive within epsilon in KL uniformly over datasets of size N, and the number of pretraining datasets needed, and show that the pretrained network's predictions converge to the Bayes predictor as both grow.
statement_caveat: Empirical results are strong (e.g. TabPFN); theory is limited to consistency-type arguments (to verify).
source: S. Müller, N. Hollmann, S. Pineda Arango, J. Grabocka and F. Hutter, Transformers Can Do Bayesian Inference, arXiv:2112.10510 (2021)
locator: to verify: Müller et al., discussion of theory.
why_important: Amortized inference by sequence models is how in-context learning is used in practice; its guarantees are a question about approximating posterior maps.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICLR 2022; TabPFN (Nature 2025, to verify) made the approach widely used.

title: Sample complexity of attention for sparse token retrieval
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: In single-location regression, a sequence of L tokens x_1..x_L ∈ R^d is observed, one unknown position J carries the signal y = <v*, x_J> (with J identified by a latent direction k*), and the rest are noise. Marion et al. show a simplified attention layer trained by projected gradient descent attains the Bayes-optimal rate, while linear models fail. Determine the optimal sample complexity in d and L and prove that standard softmax attention trained by gradient descent from a random initialization achieves it, and extend to k-sparse retrieval and token-selection tasks of Sanford, Hsu and Telgarsky.
statement_caveat: Sanford, Hsu and Telgarsky prove representational separations (attention needs width log L for sparse averaging, recurrent and feed-forward models need more); trainability and sample complexity are the open part.
source: P. Marion, R. Berthier, G. Biau and C. Boyer, Attention layers provably solve single-location regression, arXiv:2410.01537 (2024); C. Sanford, D. Hsu and M. Telgarsky, Representational Strengths and Limitations of Transformers, arXiv:2306.02896 (2023)
locator: to verify: Marion et al., conclusion.
why_important: Sparse retrieval from long contexts is what attention is for; this is its statistical theory.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: Sanford–Hsu–Telgarsky (NeurIPS 2023) is a reference for transformer expressivity.

title: Transformers learning nonlinear features in context
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Pretrain a transformer on prompts where y_i = f_w(x_i) for a low-dimensional (single- or multi-index) nonlinear target whose index directions vary across prompts. Oko et al. and Kim and Suzuki prove that, after pretraining (by a staged or mean-field analysis), the transformer learns in context with a sample complexity depending on the intrinsic dimension rather than the ambient one. Prove the same for joint end-to-end gradient training of a standard architecture (softmax attention plus MLP) and determine the optimal in-context sample complexity as a function of the information exponent of the link.
statement_caveat: Existing results use layerwise training, mean-field limits, or simplified attention.
source: K. Oko, Y. Song, T. Suzuki and D. Wu, Pretrained transformer efficiently learns low-dimensional target functions in-context, arXiv:2411.02544 (2024); J. Kim and T. Suzuki, Transformers Learn Nonlinear Features In Context: Nonconvex Mean-field Dynamics on the Attention Landscape, arXiv:2402.01258 (2024)
locator: to verify: Oko et al., open directions.
why_important: It joins the single-index theory of feature learning (T230, T231) with in-context learning (T325).
where_it_stands: Open for end-to-end training of standard architectures.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2024 / ICML 2024 results of the Suzuki and Wu groups.

title: Approximation rates of distributions by deep generative networks
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Every distribution on R^d with finite moments is the push-forward of a one-dimensional uniform (or a Gaussian) by a ReLU network of sufficient size (Lu and Lu; Yang, Li and Wang). Determine the optimal Wasserstein approximation rate W_1(G_#mu, nu) as a function of the number of network parameters, for target distributions nu supported on (or concentrated near) a k-dimensional set, and show that it depends on the intrinsic dimension k and not on d; give matching lower bounds.
statement_caveat: Yang, Li and Wang show that low-dimensional latent noise suffices for W_1 approximation with rates; optimality and the dependence on target regularity are open (to verify).
source: Y. Lu and J. Lu, A Universal Approximation Theorem of Deep Neural Networks for Expressing Probability Distributions, arXiv:2004.08867 (2020); Y. Yang, Z. Li and Y. Wang, On the capacity of deep generative networks for approximating distributions, arXiv:2101.12353 (2021)
locator: to verify: Yang–Li–Wang, conclusion.
why_important: It is the approximation theory behind every push-forward generative model (GANs, flows, consistency models).
where_it_stands: Open (sharp rates).
note: Fame: moderate; standard references in the approximation theory of generative models.

title: Batch normalization orthogonalizes representations: depth rate and training
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Daneshmand et al. prove that in deep random linear networks with batch normalization, the Gram matrix of a batch of n representations converges to (a multiple of) the identity as depth L grows, with a rate depending on width. Prove the orthogonalization for nonlinear (e.g. ReLU or tanh) networks with batch normalization at initialization, with an explicit rate in L and width, and show it persists along gradient training; contrast with Yang et al.'s result that batch normalization causes gradient explosion with depth.
statement_caveat: Linear-activation results and mean-field computations exist; nonlinear rigorous results are limited (to verify).
source: H. Daneshmand, A. Joudaki and F. Bach, Batch Normalization Orthogonalizes Representations in Deep Random Networks, arXiv:2106.03970 (2021); G. Yang, J. Pennington, V. Rao, J. Sohl-Dickstein and S. S. Schoenholz, A Mean Field Theory of Batch Normalization, arXiv:1902.08129 (2019)
locator: to verify: Daneshmand et al., the nonlinear case in the conclusion.
why_important: Normalization layers are in every modern network; this is the random-matrix account of why they prevent rank collapse (compare T254).
where_it_stands: Open for nonlinear networks as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2021 spotlight (to verify).

title: Global convergence of training large transformers
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Gao et al. study gradient flow for transformers in a joint large-width and large-depth (mean-field, residual-ODE) limit and prove that, under assumptions on the limit dynamics, training converges to a global minimizer of the regularized loss. Remove the structural assumptions: prove global convergence of gradient training for a deep transformer with softmax attention and MLP blocks in a standard scaling limit, from a generic initialization, for a natural class of data distributions.
statement_caveat: The result is a mean-field PDE argument in the spirit of T223, with assumptions that are not verified for natural data (to verify their list).
source: C. Gao, Y. Cao, Z. Li, Y. He, M. Wang, H. Liu, J. M. Klusowski and J. Fan, Global Convergence in Training Large-Scale Transformers, arXiv:2410.23610 (2024)
locator: to verify: Gao et al., the assumptions of the main theorem.
why_important: It is the transformer version of the mean-field global convergence problem (T223), for the architecture that matters most now.
where_it_stands: Open without the assumptions.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2024.

title: Random features versus neural networks for learning a single neuron
domain_name: Deep learning: approximation, expressivity, attention and architectures
statement: Yehudai and Shamir prove that random-features models (and hence the NTK regime) need width or weight norm exponential in d to approximate a single ReLU neuron x ↦ ReLU(<w*, x>) under the standard Gaussian, while a neural network learns it with poly(d) samples by gradient descent. Determine the exact trade-off between number of random features N, sample size n and accuracy for single-neuron and single-index targets (lower bounds polynomial in d of the correct degree, matching upper bounds), and the threshold in N/d at which random features begin to fit a neuron of degree-k Hermite content.
statement_caveat: Polynomial-scaling results (Mei, Misiakiewicz and Montanari for random features; T261) answer this for polynomial targets in some regimes; the single-ReLU case at the exact degree threshold is to be checked.
source: G. Yehudai and O. Shamir, On the Power and Limitations of Random Features for Understanding Neural Networks, arXiv:1904.00687 (2019)
locator: to verify: Yehudai–Shamir, discussion of tightness.
why_important: It is the quantitative form of 'feature learning beats kernels', the separation behind T238 and T230.
where_it_stands: Partly settled; exact trade-offs open as far as the writer knows (to verify).
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2019.

title: The law of robustness for two-layer networks: achievability and gradient descent
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Bubeck and Sellke prove that any function class smoothly parametrized by p parameters with polynomially bounded weights that interpolates n noisy labels of data in R^d satisfying isoperimetry must contain only interpolators of Lipschitz constant at least of order sqrt(n·d/p). Bubeck, Li and Nagaraj conjecture that this is achieved by two-layer networks: for every k between n/d and n, generic data can be interpolated by a two-layer ReLU network with k neurons and Lipschitz constant O(sqrt(n/k)). Prove the conjecture in the full range of k, and decide whether gradient descent from a standard initialization finds such a smooth interpolator.
statement_caveat: The lower bound is proved in general; Bubeck, Li and Nagaraj prove the upper bound in part of the range (to verify later work on the remaining range).
source: S. Bubeck and M. Sellke, A Universal Law of Robustness via Isoperimetry, arXiv:2105.12806 (2021); S. Bubeck, Y. Li and D. Nagaraj, A law of robustness for two-layers neural networks, arXiv:2009.14444 (2020)
locator: to verify: Bubeck–Li–Nagaraj, the conjecture as stated in the introduction.
why_important: It explains, through isoperimetry, why robust interpolation needs far more parameters than plain interpolation, and so why large models are more robust.
where_it_stands: Lower bound proved; achievability by networks and by gradient descent open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: Bubeck–Sellke won the NeurIPS 2021 outstanding paper award.

title: Adversarial examples in random networks of every width profile
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: For a random ReLU network f: R^d → R with iid Gaussian weights and an input x on the sphere of radius sqrt(d), Daniely and Schacham show that with high probability there is an adversarial perturbation of norm O(||x||/sqrt(d)) changing the sign of f(x) when widths decrease; Bartlett, Bubeck and Cherapanamjeri and Montanari and Wu extend this, showing a single gradient step suffices for wide networks with general activations. Not every depth and width profile works: for depth at least d^3 with equal large widths the network has the same sign on the whole sphere with probability at least 0.9 (Bartlett, Bubeck and Cherapanamjeri, arXiv:2106.12611, Theorem 3.1), and a width-one bottleneck gives zero gradient with probability 1/2; two-layer networks with arbitrary diverging widths are covered by Montanari and Wu (arXiv:2203.17209, Theorem 2.1). Prove that for every depth up to a power d^c below that threshold and every width profile whose widths all diverge (including bottlenecks much narrower than d and later layers much wider than d) the perturbation of order ||x||/sqrt(d) exists and is found by one gradient step, or find the depth at which it stops existing.
statement_caveat: Each paper covers a range of width profiles; a statement for all profiles is the open part (to verify).
source: A. Daniely and H. Schacham, Most ReLU Networks Suffer from l2 Adversarial Perturbations, arXiv:2010.14927 (2020); P. L. Bartlett, S. Bubeck and Y. Cherapanamjeri, Adversarial Examples in Multi-Layer Random ReLU Networks, arXiv:2106.12611 (2021); A. Montanari and Y. Wu, Adversarial Examples in Random Neural Networks with General Activations, arXiv:2203.17209 (2022)
locator: to verify: Montanari–Wu, introduction (which width regimes remain).
why_important: It shows adversarial examples are a generic geometric property of random networks, not an artefact of training.
where_it_stands: Partly solved (many regimes proved).
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2020/2021; the result 'one gradient step finds adversarial examples' is widely quoted.

audit.status_ref: Bartlett-Bubeck-Cherapanamjeri2106.12611 Theorem1.1 PDF p2, opened in full, proves a single-gradient-step adversarial example for fixed depth with lower bounds on minimum widths relative to log(max width). Montanari-Wu2203.17209 Theorem2.1 PDF p4, opened in full, removes upper bounds on two-layer width growth for any diverging m,d under the stated nonconstant regular activation assumptions; probability tends to one and relative perturbation tends to zero. It does not give a universal dimension-free O(1)-norm bound at probability tending to one. Moreover2106.12611 Theorem3.1 PDF p10, now opened in full, gives depth ell>=d^3 and equal widths (ell*d)^20<=k<=exp(sqrt(ell)); with probability>=0.9 all unit-sphere outputs differ relatively by at most C*sqrt(log(d)/d). For sufficiently large d they all have the same sign, so arbitrary growing depth is already refuted in the cited source.
audit.statement_ok: NO: every depth and every width includes bounded bottlenecks, for which a width-one ReLU has zero gradient with probability1/2. The claimed O(||x||/sqrt(d)) high-probability bound also hides probability-dependent/growing constants: Montanari-Wu Theorem2.1 uses a slowly diverging step sequence and o(||x||). Arbitrarily large diverging widths are already covered by its source, so this is not an untouched width regime.
audit.replace_with: Specify fixed or growing depth, minimum-width divergence, Gaussian weight scaling and a success probability delta. Ask for a quantitative norm/success-probability tradeoff in a stated growing-depth or narrow-but-diverging bottleneck regime outside the opened theorems.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: width-one zero-gradient obstruction completed in T344_bottleneck.md. A quantitative bottleneck-width failure bound is a concrete corrected target; arbitrary depth requires a separate programme.
audit.locator: 2010.14927 Theorem3.1 (shrinking widths; gradient flow and polylog factors);2106.12611 Theorem1.1 PDF p2;2203.17209 Introduction PDF p2 Arbitrary width, Theorem2.1 PDF p4 and Remark2.1. 2106.12611 Section3 The Impact of Depth, Theorem3.1 PDF p10.

title: Are adversarial examples a consequence of computational limits?
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Bubeck, Price and Razenshteyn propose that robust classifiers may exist and be statistically learnable but not efficiently learnable, and Bubeck, Lee, Price and Razenshteyn build such tasks from cryptographic pseudorandom generators. Find a natural data distribution (e.g. a mixture of two Gaussians in R^d or a planted sparse model) for which robust classification within ℓ2 or ℓ∞ radius epsilon is information-theoretically possible with poly(d) samples but computationally hard under a standard average-case assumption (planted clique, low-degree, SQ), or prove that for Gaussian mixtures robust learning is as easy computationally as it is statistically.
statement_caveat: The known separations use cryptographic constructions rather than natural distributions.
source: S. Bubeck, E. Price and I. Razenshteyn, Adversarial examples from computational constraints, arXiv:1805.10204 (2018); S. Bubeck, Y. T. Lee, E. Price and I. Razenshteyn, Adversarial Examples from Cryptographic Pseudo-Random Generators, arXiv:1811.06418 (2018)
locator: to verify: Bubeck–Price–Razenshteyn, open questions.
why_important: It asks whether adversarial vulnerability is about statistics, geometry, or computation.
where_it_stands: Open for natural distributions as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICML 2019.

title: The limits of randomized smoothing for certified robustness in high dimension
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Randomized smoothing certifies an ℓ2 robustness radius proportional to sigma·Φ^{-1}(p) for the Gaussian-smoothed classifier (Cohen, Rosenfeld and Kolter). For ℓ_p with p > 2, Blum et al. and others show any smoothing distribution certifies only radius of order d^{1/p − 1/2} relative to the ℓ2 radius. Determine the optimal certified ℓ_p radius (p > 2, including ℓ∞) achievable by any randomized smoothing scheme as a function of d at fixed clean accuracy, with matching upper and lower bounds, and identify the optimal smoothing distribution.
statement_caveat: Barrier theorems for broad classes of distributions exist; whether non-product or input-dependent smoothing escapes them is open (to verify).
source: J. M. Cohen, E. Rosenfeld and J. Z. Kolter, Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized Smoothing, arXiv:1902.02918 (2019); A. Blum, T. Dick, N. Manoj and H. Zhang, Random Smoothing Might be Unable to Certify l∞ Robustness for High-Dimensional Images, arXiv:2002.03517 (2020)
locator: to verify: Blum et al., main theorem and the classes it covers.
why_important: Randomized smoothing is the only certification method that scales to large networks; its limits are a Gaussian isoperimetry question.
where_it_stands: Partly settled (barriers for classes of distributions).
note: Fame: Cohen et al. (ICML 2019) is the standard certification method.

title: The Amit–Gutfreund–Sompolinsky capacity of the Hopfield model
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: In the Hopfield model with N neurons and M = alpha·N iid uniform ±1 patterns xi^mu, with energy H(sigma) = −(1/(2N)) Σ_mu (Σ_i xi_i^mu sigma_i)², prove that at zero temperature there are, with high probability, local minima of H (fixed points of the zero-temperature dynamics) with overlap close to 1 with each pattern if and only if alpha < alpha_c, where alpha_c ≈ 0.138 is the replica-symmetric value of Amit, Gutfreund and Sompolinsky; and prove the replica-symmetric free energy in the retrieval phase.
statement_caveat: Retrieval states are proved to exist for small alpha (Newman: alpha < 0.056; Loukianova: alpha < 0.071; to verify Talagrand's bounds); the replica-symmetric formula is proved at high temperature or small alpha (Talagrand; Bovier and Gayrard). The threshold 0.138 is not proved.
source: D. J. Amit, H. Gutfreund and H. Sompolinsky, Storing infinite numbers of patterns in a spin-glass model of neural networks, Phys. Rev. Lett. 55 (1985) 1530; M. Talagrand, Rigorous results for the Hopfield model with many patterns, Probab. Theory Related Fields 110 (1998) 177-276
locator: to verify: Talagrand 1998 and Talagrand's 'Mean Field Models for Spin Glasses', vol. 1, chapter on the Hopfield model (open problems listed there).
why_important: The Hopfield model is the founding model of neural associative memory (2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for Hopfield) and the ancestor of modern attention (T348).
where_it_stands: Open (the 0.138 threshold).
note: Fame: one of the best-known predictions of the statistical physics of neural networks; listed by Talagrand among open problems.

title: The exact capacity of dense associative memories
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: For the continuous dense associative memory with log-sum-exp energy (Ramsauer et al.; one step is softmax attention) at fixed inverse temperature beta, with M = e^(alpha N) patterns iid uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt N, Lucibello and Mezard (arXiv:2304.14964) compute a threshold alpha_1 below which a typical pattern is retrieved (Section II, Eq. 7) and a union-bound lower bound alpha_lower on the capacity for all patterns at once (Section III, Eq. 10). Prove that a typical pattern is a fixed point with a basin of stated radius exactly when alpha < alpha_1, and determine the all-pattern capacity alpha_c, closing alpha_lower <= alpha_c <= alpha_1. The discrete models with energies F(x) = x^n or exp(x) on binary patterns, where Demircigil et al. (arXiv:1702.01929) prove exponential storage with error correction for alpha < I(1 - 2 rho)/2, are a separate question: the sharp constant there.
statement_caveat: Order-of-magnitude capacities are proved; sharp constants are open (to verify).
source: D. Krotov and J. J. Hopfield, Dense Associative Memory for Pattern Recognition, arXiv:1606.01164 (2016); M. Demircigil, J. Heusel, M. Löwe, S. Upgang and F. Vermet, On a model of associative memory with huge storage capacity, arXiv:1702.01929 (2017); C. Lucibello and M. Mézard, The Exponential Capacity of Dense Associative Memories, arXiv:2304.14964 (2023); H. Ramsauer et al., Hopfield Networks is All You Need, arXiv:2008.02217 (2020)
locator: to verify: Lucibello–Mézard, the capacity formula and its non-rigorous status.
why_important: It is the memory capacity of softmax attention viewed as an associative memory.
where_it_stands: Open (sharp constants).
note: Fame: Krotov–Hopfield and Ramsauer et al. are widely cited; PRL 2024 for Lucibello–Mézard (to verify).

audit.status_ref: Demircigil-et-al1702.01929 Theorem1.3/Remark1.4 PDF p4, fully opened, proves exponential storage and random-Hamming-error correction for binary patterns in its discrete exponential-interaction dynamics, alpha<I(1-2rho)/2. Lucibello-Mezard2304.14964 SectionII Eq7 PDF p2 gives a typical-pattern threshold, while SectionIII Eq10 p3 is a union-bound lower bound on all-pattern capacity, with equality only in special ensembles. The latter is not generally an exact all-pattern formula theorem.
audit.statement_ok: NO: the row mixes discrete polynomial/exponential update energies with the continuous log-sum-exp-plus-quadratic attention model, and confuses a typical-pattern threshold with all-pattern capacity. Fix pattern ensemble, temperature/scaling, discrete versus continuous states, asymptotic error criterion and random versus adversarial basin initialization.
audit.replace_with: Select the continuous Gaussian-pattern model with fixed temperature and ask a rigorous all-pattern threshold closing alpha_c_lower<=alpha_c<=alpha1, or prove the typical-pattern/basin statement under exact uniformity assumptions. Keep discrete polynomial memories as a separate question.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: verify a fixed-state large-deviation calculation or finite union-bound capacity lower bound, then identify the missing uniform-in-neighborhood step. Full sharp all-pattern capacity across ensembles is a programme.
audit.locator: 2304.14964 Eq1-2 PDF p1 (continuous energy/update),SectionII Eq7 p2 (alpha1),SectionIII Eqs8-10 p3 (all-pattern lower bound),SectionIV p3 (basin restriction);1702.01929 Theorem1.3 p4. Main source abstract expressly says exact typical thresholds and lower bounds for all patterns.

title: The storage capacity of committee machines with many hidden units
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Tree committee machine: N weights split into K disjoint groups of N/K inputs, hidden units sign(w_k . x_k), or ReLU with half the output weights +1 and half -1, output the sign of the sum of the hidden outputs; spherical weights; P = alpha N patterns with iid standard Gaussian inputs and iid uniform labels; N tends to infinity first, then K. The capacity alpha_c(K) is the threshold above which, with high probability, no weights store all the patterns. Replica calculations with replica-symmetry breaking predict growth like sqrt(log K) for sign units (Monasson and Zecchina) and a finite limit for ReLU units (Baldassi, Malatesta and Zecchina, arXiv:1907.07578, one-step RSB estimate about 2.66 in its 2024 version); Mitchison and Durbin bound the capacity per weight above by order log K. Prove that alpha_c(K) is a sharp threshold and find its large-K asymptotics for sign and for ReLU units.
statement_caveat: Rigorous results exist for K = 1 (the perceptron); for K ≥ 2 only bounds are known (to verify).
source: C. Baldassi, E. M. Malatesta and R. Zecchina, Properties of the geometry of solutions and capacity of multi-layer neural networks with Rectified Linear Units activations, arXiv:1907.07578 (2019); R. Monasson and R. Zecchina, Weight space structure and internal representations: a direct approach to learning and generalization in multilayer neural networks, Phys. Rev. Lett. 75 (1995) 2432
locator: to verify: Baldassi–Malatesta–Zecchina, introduction (the sign and ReLU predictions and the Mitchison–Durbin bound).
why_important: It is the memorization capacity of the simplest two-layer network, the counting question behind overparameterization.
where_it_stands: Open (predictions non-rigorous).
note: Fame: classical problem of the statistical physics of learning (Gardner programme).

audit.status_ref: Baldassi-Malatesta-Zecchina1907.07578 PDF pp1-3, fully opened, gives replica-symmetric and1RSB predictions for a tree committee; no rigorous deciding theorem for the corrected large-K capacity was opened. v6May2024 corrects the1RSB ReLU estimate to approximately2.6643, explicitly noting a prior numerical saddle error. These predictions are not rigorous capacity theorems.
audit.statement_ok: NO: row states N inputs,K fully connected hidden units and load P/(NK), while cited source has K disjoint input groups,N total first-layer weights and load P/N. For ReLU the source fixes half output weights+1 and half-1; all-positive ReLU votes at zero threshold cannot provide negative margins. Specify spherical/binary weights, input and label law, margin, architecture and order of N,K limits.
audit.replace_with: Use the tree-committee model with N total weights and balanced fixed ReLU output signs, or explicitly ask a different fully connected model with NK weights. Fix weight constraint and N-then-K limit before asking a rigorous upper/lower capacity theorem.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: model mismatch and positive-ReLU-vote obstruction completed in T349_positive_ReLU_votes.md; a finite-K first-moment feasibility bound is a concrete narrowed route. Sharp large-K replica prediction is a programme.
audit.locator: 1907.07578 The model Eq1 PDF pp1-2;balanced ReLU output signs and load p=alphaN pp1-2;Critical Capacity Eqs3-6 p2;1RSB estimate and correction footnote p3. No numbered open-problem locator was found.

title: Neural scaling laws for nonlinear trained networks
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Test loss of large models decreases as a power law in parameters, data and compute (Kaplan et al.; Hoffmann et al.). Solvable linear models (random-feature regression trained by SGD with power-law data spectra) reproduce these laws and their compute-optimal exponents rigorously (Paquette et al.; Lin et al.). Prove power-law scaling of the test loss in width, sample size and training time, with explicit exponents, for a nonlinear model trained by SGD in the feature-learning regime, e.g. a two-layer network learning a power-law sum of single-index (or multi-index) components, and derive its compute-optimal allocation.
statement_caveat: Heuristic and dynamical-mean-field models (Bordelon, Atanasov and Pehlevan) and data-manifold arguments (Bahri et al.; Maloney et al.) exist; a rigorous nonlinear result with feature learning is open.
source: J. Kaplan et al., Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models, arXiv:2001.08361 (2020); J. Hoffmann et al., Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models, arXiv:2203.15556 (2022); E. Paquette, C. Paquette, L. Xiao and J. Pennington, 4+3 Phases of Compute-Optimal Neural Scaling Laws, arXiv:2405.15074 (2024); L. Lin, J. Wu, S. M. Kakade, P. L. Bartlett and J. D. Lee, Scaling Laws in Linear Regression: Compute, Parameters, and Data, arXiv:2406.08466 (2024); B. Bordelon, A. Atanasov and C. Pehlevan, A Dynamical Model of Neural Scaling Laws, arXiv:2402.01092 (2024); Y. Bahri, E. Dyer, J. Kaplan, J. Lee and U. Sharma, Explaining Neural Scaling Laws, arXiv:2102.06701 (2021); A. Maloney, D. A. Roberts and J. Sully, A Solvable Model of Neural Scaling Laws, arXiv:2210.16859 (2022)
locator: to verify: Paquette et al., discussion of nonlinear extensions.
why_important: Scaling laws decide how compute is spent on frontier models; their mathematical basis beyond linear models is unknown.
where_it_stands: Open for nonlinear feature-learning models as far as the writer knows (2025-26 progress to verify).
note: Fame: Kaplan et al. and Chinchilla (Hoffmann et al.) are among the most influential empirical results in deep learning.

title: Beating power-law scaling by data pruning
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Sorscher et al. compute, with the replica method for a teacher-student perceptron, that keeping only the hardest (or a well-chosen fraction of) training examples according to a pruning metric changes the test-error decay from a power law in the dataset size to an exponential one, given a good enough metric. Prove this rigorously for the perceptron model (or for ridge or logistic regression in the proportional regime): the test error of the estimator trained on the pruned set as a function of the data size, pruning fraction and metric quality.
statement_caveat: Rigorous asymptotics for data selection in proportional regressions exist in some settings (to verify Kolossov et al. 2023 and related); the exponential-scaling claim is the open part.
source: B. Sorscher, R. Geirhos, S. Shekhar, S. Ganguli and A. S. Morcos, Beyond neural scaling laws: beating power law scaling via data pruning, arXiv:2206.14486 (2022)
locator: to verify: Sorscher et al., the perceptron theory section.
why_important: Whether data quality can replace data quantity is a central practical question, and the perceptron gives it an exact form.
where_it_stands: Open (rigorous version) as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2022 outstanding paper award (to verify).

title: Privacy of hidden-state noisy SGD for nonconvex losses
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Projected noisy SGD on a compact convex domain of diameter D, with per-example losses that are L-Lipschitz and M-smooth but not convex, fixed step eta and Gaussian noise of variance sigma^2 per step, releasing only the last iterate. For convex losses Altschuler and Talwar (arXiv:2205.13710, Theorem 1.3) show that the Renyi privacy loss of order alpha plateaus at order alpha L^2/(n^2 sigma^2) times min(T, D n/(L eta)) as the number of steps T grows; without convexity, a time-uniform bound that does not decrease with n follows from the last noisy step alone. Find geometric conditions on the nonconvex losses (for example a one-point dissipativity condition, or a bound on the negative curvature relative to eta and sigma) under which the time-uniform Renyi bound decreases with n at the convex rate, and construct a smooth nonconvex loss on a compact domain for which the plateau is of order alpha L^2/sigma^2 times a constant independent of n.
statement_caveat: For general (non-smooth or adversarial) updates, hidden-state privacy can fail to improve on composition; the natural smooth nonconvex case is open (to verify recent results).
source: J. M. Altschuler and K. Talwar, Privacy of Noisy Stochastic Gradient Descent: More Iterations without More Privacy Loss, arXiv:2205.13710 (2022)
locator: to verify: Altschuler–Talwar, conclusion (nonconvex losses as open).
why_important: Training large networks with differential privacy uses the composition bound over all iterates; a hidden-state bound would allow far more training at the same privacy.
where_it_stands: Open for nonconvex losses as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2022.

audit.status_ref: Altschuler-Talwar2205.13710 informal Theorem1.3 PDF p5: RDP scales alpha*L^2/(n^2*sigma^2)*min(T,D*n/(L*eta)) in a specified large parameter regime; theorem opened in full. Section1.2 p6 raises relaxing convexity. Own elementary bounded-mean Gaussian-mixture proposition in T352_compact_Gaussian_bound.md proves a crude time-uniform alpha*(D+2eta G)^2/(2v^2) bound without convexity for fixed final noise v>0 and uniformly bounded gradients.
audit.statement_ok: NO: asks merely for any finite time-uniform bound, while meaningful source comparison is sample-dependent sharp amplification. With fixed positive Gaussian noise, compact projected states and uniform bounded gradients, a crude bound already follows from the final step alone. Conversely smoothness without a uniform gradient/data bound and an unspecified decaying-noise schedule does not give a well-posed universal claim.
audit.replace_with: For projected noisy SGD on a compact domain with uniformly L-Lipschitz M-smooth nonconvex per-example losses and fixed step/noise, identify geometric assumptions yielding a useful n-dependent time-uniform RDP plateau, specifying alpha, noise convention and its dependence on geometry; compare subsequent nonconvex privacy literature before calling this open.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: bounded-last-step-mean Renyi proof completed as a statement diagnostic; does not supply the useful n-dependent rate or novelty clearance.
audit.locator: 2205.13710 Theorem1.3 PDF p5, discussion of convexity and non-uniform stepsizes PDF p6; Section2.1 p10 Lipschitz/smooth assumptions; Definition2.13 p13 projected noisy iteration.

title: Exact privacy of DP-SGD with shuffled batches
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Privacy accounting for DP-SGD assumes Poisson subsampling of each batch, while implementations shuffle the data and take fixed-size batches. Chua et al. show the privacy guarantee of shuffling can be substantially worse than the Poisson accounting. Determine the exact (or asymptotically tight) Rényi or (epsilon, delta) privacy of the Gaussian mechanism over one or several epochs with shuffled fixed-size batches, as a function of noise level, batch size and number of epochs, and compare it with Poisson subsampling.
statement_caveat: Lower bounds (auditing-style) and upper bounds for shuffling exist and do not meet (to verify).
source: L. Chua et al., How Private are DP-SGD Implementations?, arXiv:2403.17673 (2024); M. Nasr, S. Song, A. Thakurta, N. Papernot and N. Carlini, Adversary Instantiation: Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Machine Learning, arXiv:2101.04535 (2021)
locator: to verify: Chua et al., the comparison and open questions.
why_important: Every deployed DP training run states a privacy level; this question is whether those levels are true.
where_it_stands: Open (tight accounting) as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICML 2024.

title: Convergence of Adam with the hyperparameters used in practice
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Reddi, Kale and Kumar construct convex problems where Adam with fixed beta_1, beta_2 diverges. Zhang et al. show Adam converges to a neighbourhood of stationary points for smooth nonconvex objectives when beta_2 is chosen large depending on the problem (after beta_1, n are fixed). Prove (or disprove) that Adam with beta_1 < sqrt(beta_2), beta_2 close to 1 independent of the problem, and a decaying or small constant step size, converges to stationary points on smooth nonconvex finite-sum objectives under standard noise assumptions, and explain the empirical advantage of Adam over SGD on transformer losses in a provable model.
statement_caveat: Many partial results (problem-dependent hyperparameters, bounded gradients, affine noise) exist.
source: S. J. Reddi, S. Kale and S. Kumar, On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond, arXiv:1904.09237 (2019); Y. Zhang, C. Chen, N. Shi, R. Sun and Z.-Q. Luo, Adam Can Converge Without Any Modification On Update Rules, arXiv:2208.09632 (2022)
locator: to verify: Zhang et al., the discussion of problem-dependent beta_2.
why_important: Adam trains nearly every large model; its convergence in the regime used is still not established.
where_it_stands: Partly solved.
note: Fame: Reddi et al. was an ICLR 2018 best paper.

title: Long-time validity of the SDE approximation of SGD
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: SGD with step eta and gradient-noise covariance Sigma is approximated in the weak sense by the stochastic modified equation over ordinary time t = k eta of order 1 with error O(eta) (Li, Tai and E). Li, Wang and Arora (arXiv:2110.06914, Theorem 4.6) prove a weak limit over k = floor(T/eta^2) steps near a manifold of minimizers, for smooth losses whose Hessian has constant rank on the manifold, started in an attracting neighbourhood the iterates do not leave; the slow drift reduces the trace of the Hessian when Sigma is proportional to the Hessian. For a stated class (smooth loss, a minimizer manifold with constant-rank Hessian or a stated stratified singular set, a noise class with moment bounds and a non-explosion condition), prove sup over k <= T/eta^2 of |E f(theta_k) - E f(X_(k eta^2))| <= C(T) eta^a with explicit a > 0 and C(T), for f in a stated test-function norm. The comparison of the invariant laws of SGD and of the limiting process, over all times, is a separate question.
statement_caveat: Validity conditions for the SDE model are studied empirically (Li, Malladi and Arora) and for adaptive methods (Malladi et al.).
source: Q. Li, C. Tai and W. E, Stochastic modified equations and adaptive stochastic gradient algorithms, arXiv:1511.06251 (2015); Z. Li, S. Malladi and S. Arora, On the Validity of Modeling SGD with Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs), arXiv:2102.12470 (2021); Z. Li, T. Wang and S. Arora, What Happens after SGD Reaches Zero Loss? --A Mathematical Framework, arXiv:2110.06914 (2021); S. Malladi, K. Lyu, A. Panigrahi and S. Arora, On the SDEs and Scaling Rules for Adaptive Gradient Algorithms, arXiv:2205.10287 (2022)
locator: to verify: Li–Wang–Arora, assumptions of the main theorem.
why_important: The SDE picture underlies most explanations of SGD's implicit regularization and of learning-rate scaling rules.
where_it_stands: Open in the stated generality.
note: Fame: the stochastic modified equations paper (ICML 2017) is standard.

audit.status_ref: Li-Wang-Arora2110.06914 Theorem4.6 PDF p7, opened in full with Assumptions3.1-3.2 p5 and Remark4.7 p8, proves a weak manifold limit on k=floor(T/eta^2) steps under smoothness, Hessian-rank and local-basin/nonexit assumptions. Corollary5.1 PDF p8 gives isotropic-noise log-pseudodeterminant drift; Corollary5.2 p9 gives Hessian-trace drift specifically when Sigma=c Hessian(L). None is an explicit generic long-time error bound without replacement stability hypotheses.
audit.statement_ok: NO: specify ordinary time t=k*eta versus slow time s=k*eta^2. Source eta^-2 is an iteration count, not ordinary SDE time. Trace-Hessian regularization is noise-model-specific, and the source needs attraction in a neighborhood U, not global attraction from all parameter space. Removing all such assumptions without replacement does not define a uniform approximation class.
audit.replace_with: Choose a loss/noise class allowing a specified stratified or singular minimizer geometry, state moment/nonexplosion/basin conditions and a test-function norm, and ask an explicit error uniform for k<=T/eta^2. Keep all-time invariant-law comparison as a distinct limit problem.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: two-clock and exact quadratic stationary-variance checks completed in T355_two_clocks.md. A controlled singular quadratic or piecewise-smooth two-basin example could isolate a corrected failure/success condition; generic neural theorem remains a programme.
audit.locator: 2110.06914 Assumptions3.1-3.2 p5,Lemma4.2 p6,Theorem4.6 p7,Remark4.7/Corollary5.1 p8,Corollary5.2 p9.1511.06251 Theorem1 finite-horizon weak SME;2205.10287 Theorems4.2/4.5 are adaptive-algorithm scaling, not unrestricted SGD.

title: Model collapse under recursive training on generated data
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Fit a model to data, sample a new dataset from the fitted model, refit, and repeat. Shumailov et al. show that for Gaussians fitted by maximum likelihood the fitted variance collapses to 0 and tails disappear; Dohmatob et al. describe collapse as a change of scaling laws; Gerstgrasser et al. show that if data accumulate (real plus all synthetic generations), the test error stays bounded in linear regression. For nonparametric density estimators (kernel density estimation, or a score-based diffusion model in a solvable regime), determine the conditions on the fraction of real data retained at each generation under which the generation-t model stays within bounded distance of the true distribution for all t, and the rate of tail loss otherwise.
statement_caveat: Results are for Gaussian, linear and simple discrete models.
source: I. Shumailov et al., The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget, arXiv:2305.17493 (2023); E. Dohmatob, Y. Feng, P. Yang, F. Charton and J. Kempe, A Tale of Tails: Model Collapse as a Change of Scaling Laws, arXiv:2402.07043 (2024); M. Gerstgrasser et al., Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data, arXiv:2404.01413 (2024)
locator: to verify: Gerstgrasser et al., discussion of nonlinear models.
why_important: Future models will be trained on data produced by earlier models; whether that degrades them is a question about iterated estimation as a Markov chain on distributions.
where_it_stands: Open beyond simple models.
note: Fame: Shumailov et al. (Nature 2024) was widely covered.

title: Overconfidence of overparameterized classifiers
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Bai, Mei, Wang and Xiong prove that logistic regression fitted by maximum likelihood in the proportional regime (n, d → ∞, n/d fixed) is overconfident: its predicted probabilities exceed the true conditional probabilities, even without overparameterization. Prove a comparable theorem for a two-layer network trained by gradient descent on cross-entropy in a solvable regime (random features, or mean-field with a single-index teacher): characterize the calibration error as a function of n/d, width and training time, and show whether early stopping yields calibration.
statement_caveat: Empirical overconfidence of modern networks is well documented (Guo et al. 2017); theory is limited to linear and random-features models (to verify).
source: Y. Bai, S. Mei, H. Wang and C. Xiong, Don't Just Blame Over-parametrization for Over-confidence: Theoretical Analysis of Calibration in Binary Classification, arXiv:2102.07856 (2021)
locator: to verify: Bai et al., conclusion (networks as open).
why_important: Calibrated probabilities are what make a classifier's confidence usable; it is a question about the limiting law of a trained predictor's outputs.
where_it_stands: Open for networks as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICML 2021.

title: Intrinsic robustness of natural data distributions
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: By concentration of measure, every classifier for a distribution with good isoperimetry (e.g. the push-forward of a Gaussian by an L-Lipschitz generator) has adversarial examples at distance O(L/sqrt(d))·(constant) from most inputs (Fawzi, Fawzi and Fawzi; Shafahi et al.; Mahloujifar et al.). Determine the intrinsic robustness, the best robust accuracy at radius epsilon achievable by any classifier, for such generative-model distributions with well-separated classes, and close the gap between the concentration upper bound and robust accuracy achievable by explicit (or efficiently computable) classifiers.
statement_caveat: The concentration bounds are often far from what classifiers achieve on real data; whether the bound or the classifiers are loose is open.
source: A. Fawzi, H. Fawzi and O. Fawzi, Adversarial vulnerability for any classifier, arXiv:1802.08686 (2018); A. Shafahi, W. R. Huang, C. Studer, S. Feizi and T. Goldstein, Are adversarial examples inevitable?, arXiv:1809.02104 (2018); S. Mahloujifar, D. I. Diochnos and M. Mahmoody, The Curse of Concentration in Robust Learning: Evasion and Poisoning Attacks from Concentration of Measure, arXiv:1809.03063 (2018)
locator: to verify: Fawzi et al., discussion of tightness.
why_important: It decides whether robustness is limited by the data's geometry or by our classifiers; compare D. Tsipras et al., Robustness May Be at Odds with Accuracy, arXiv:1805.12152 (2018).
where_it_stands: Open (tight characterization).
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2018 / ICLR 2019; the concentration explanation of adversarial examples is well known.

title: Optimal scaling laws for associative memories
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Store N input-output token pairs (x, y) with inputs drawn from a Zipf law with exponent alpha in a d×d matrix W, using random embeddings in R^d, and predict y by argmax over outputs of <u_y, W e_x>. Cabannes, Dohmatob and Bietti derive the scaling of the error in N and d for outer-product memories and for some optimizer-trained memories. Determine the optimal error achievable by any d×d matrix (an information-theoretic scaling law in d and N for given alpha), and whether gradient descent on the cross-entropy loss attains it.
statement_caveat: Upper bounds for specific storage rules are proved; optimality over all matrices is the open part (to verify).
source: V. Cabannes, E. Dohmatob and A. Bietti, Scaling Laws for Associative Memories, arXiv:2310.02984 (2023)
locator: to verify: Cabannes et al., conclusion.
why_important: Factual recall in transformers is stored in such matrices; this is the solvable model of how much a layer can remember.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICLR 2024.

title: Convergence and generalization of adversarial training
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Adversarial training minimizes the robust loss min_theta E max_{||delta|| ≤ epsilon} ℓ(f_theta(x + delta), y) by alternating gradient ascent on delta and descent on theta. Gao et al. prove that for sufficiently overparameterized two-layer networks (in an NTK-type regime) adversarial training reaches small robust training loss, with width requirements that grow quickly. Prove convergence with width polynomial in n and d in a feature-learning regime, and prove a theorem explaining robust overfitting (robust test error rising with training while robust training error falls) in a solvable model.
statement_caveat: Robust overfitting is documented empirically (Rice, Wong and Kolter 2020); its theory is in early stages (to verify).
source: R. Gao, T. Cai, H. Li, L. Wang, C.-J. Hsieh and J. D. Lee, Convergence of Adversarial Training in Overparametrized Neural Networks, arXiv:1906.07916 (2019)
locator: to verify: Gao et al., width requirement and open questions.
why_important: Adversarial training is the main practical defence; whether and why it works is open.
where_it_stands: Open (polynomial-width convergence and robust overfitting).
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2019.

title: Emergence of skills from random skill graphs
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Arora and Goyal model language-model competence by a random bipartite graph between skills and text pieces and show that, as the model's loss decreases along a scaling law, competence on combinations of k skills emerges sharply, with thresholds derived from random-graph concentration. Michaud et al. propose a 'quanta' model in which scaling laws arise from learning discrete units in order of a Zipf-distributed frequency. Prove that, for a trained network in a solvable model (e.g. multitask sparse parity or a sum of single-index tasks with Zipfian frequencies), the loss follows a power law while individual task accuracies jump sharply, and identify the exponents from the frequency law.
statement_caveat: Both theories are statistical models of the outcome, not theorems about trained networks.
source: S. Arora and A. Goyal, A Theory for Emergence of Complex Skills in Language Models, arXiv:2307.15936 (2023); E. J. Michaud, Z. Liu, U. Girit and M. Tegmark, The Quantization Model of Neural Scaling, arXiv:2303.13506 (2023)
locator: to verify: Michaud et al., the multitask sparse parity experiments.
why_important: Emergent abilities are the most debated phenomenon of scaling; a trained-network theorem would decide whether they are real or an artefact of metrics.
where_it_stands: Open.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2023; the emergence debate is widely followed.

title: Optimal convergence rates of SGD with random reshuffling
domain_name: Deep learning: robustness, privacy, memory and scaling
statement: Random reshuffling: each epoch takes a fresh uniform permutation of the n components; K epochs; constant step chosen knowing n and K; the output is the last iterate. For sums of L-smooth components whose average is mu-strongly convex, with gradient variance sigma_*^2 at the optimum, Safran and Shamir (arXiv:1908.00045) prove lower bounds already for quadratics, and Mishchenko, Khaled and Richtarik (arXiv:2006.05988) prove upper bounds for strongly convex sums and for nonconvex stationarity. Determine the optimal last-iterate rate in this oracle class, with matching upper and lower bounds in n, K and kappa = L/mu in both regimes K < kappa and K >= kappa, and the optimal rate to an epsilon-stationary point (min over iterates of the gradient norm) for L-smooth nonconvex sums with bounded variance. Single shuffling and with-replacement sampling are separate classes.
statement_caveat: Upper and lower bounds for general strongly convex functions differ by condition-number factors; nonconvex lower bounds are incomplete (to verify).
source: I. Safran and O. Shamir, How Good is SGD with Random Shuffling?, arXiv:1908.00045 (2019); K. Mishchenko, A. Khaled and P. Richtárik, Random Reshuffling: Simple Analysis with Vast Improvements, arXiv:2006.05988 (2020)
locator: to verify: Safran–Shamir, the open questions in the conclusion.
why_important: Every network is trained with reshuffled epochs; the theory still mostly analyses sampling with replacement.
where_it_stands: Partly solved.
note: Fame: COLT 2020; reshuffling is a recognized open problem (to verify the COLT open-problem note by Bottou 2009 on random reshuffling).

audit.status_ref: Safran-Shamir1908.00045 Theorem1 PDF p5, opened in full, lower-bounds fresh reshuffling by c*min(lambda,(G^2/lambda)*[(nK)^-2+(nK^3)^-1]) for its constant-step final-iterate class. Theorem2 p7 gives the distinct single-shuffle Omega(1/(nK^2)) lower bound. Mishchenko-Khaled-Richtarik2006.05988 Theorem2 PDF p7 and Theorem4 p8, opened in full with variance Assumption2, give strongly convex-sum and nonconvex-stationarity upper bounds; they are not current minimax matching results.
audit.statement_ok: NO: row baseline mixes single shuffling with fresh-per-epoch reshuffling and suppresses K/n regimes. Specify stepsize policy, output iterate/averaging, individual versus sum convexity, gradient-variance constants, initial gap/radius and stationarity norm. A universal optimal dependence on n,K,condition number is not defined without this oracle class.
audit.replace_with: Fix fresh reshuffling, a particular component-variance class, constant or scheduled steps, last iterate versus best/random iterate and exact regime K/n. Ask a specific missing condition-number factor or nonconvex oracle lower bound after surveying later refinements.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: derive exact one-dimensional quadratic epoch recursions and separate K<<n from K>>n using the opened bounds. A matching minimax nonconvex theorem is a programme, and existing quadratic rates are not new.
audit.locator: 1908.00045 Remark4 and Theorem1 p5,Theorem2 and explicit remaining single-shuffle questions p7;2006.05988 Theorem2 p7 and Theorem4/Assumption2 p8, with an exact optimal-all-accuracies question after Theorem2 p7.

title: Does gradient descent on two-layer ReLU networks reach the global max-margin solution?
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: For homogeneous networks trained by gradient flow on the logistic or exponential loss of separable data, Lyu and Li and Ji and Telgarsky prove that the parameters converge in direction to a KKT point of the margin-maximization problem min ||theta||² subject to y_i f_theta(x_i) ≥ 1. Decide whether, for two-layer ReLU networks and natural data (e.g. Gaussian inputs with labels from a teacher network, or orthogonal-ish inputs), the limit direction is a global maximizer of the normalized margin with high probability over the initialization, or exhibit natural cases where gradient flow converges to a strictly suboptimal KKT point.
statement_caveat: Known: KKT points need not be local maxima in general (Vardi, Shamir and Srebro); global optimality is known for special data (e.g. linearly separable with specific structure, or nearly orthogonal inputs).
source: K. Lyu and J. Li, Gradient Descent Maximizes the Margin of Homogeneous Neural Networks, arXiv:1906.05890 (2019); Z. Ji and M. Telgarsky, Directional convergence and alignment in deep learning, arXiv:2006.06657 (2020)
locator: to verify: Lyu–Li, conclusion (global optimality of the KKT direction as open).
why_important: Max-margin implicit bias is the main explanation of why gradient-trained classifiers generalize; whether it is the global margin decides what bound applies.
where_it_stands: Open for general data as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICLR 2020 / NeurIPS 2020; the implicit-bias programme following Soudry et al. 2018.

title: The optimization landscape of overcomplete random tensor decomposition
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Given T = Σ_{i=1}^n a_i^{⊗4} with a_i iid uniform on the unit sphere of R^d and n = d^{1+δ}, consider maximizing f(x) = <T, x^{⊗4}> over the unit sphere. Ge and Ma prove that for n up to d^{2−ε}... (to verify the exact range) all local maxima with objective above a threshold are close to some ±a_i. Prove that for every n ≤ c·d², with high probability, every local maximum of f (or of a natural regularized objective) is close to a component, so that gradient ascent from a random start recovers components, or exhibit spurious local maxima in part of this range.
statement_caveat: Sum-of-squares algorithms decompose random overcomplete tensors up to n ~ d^{1.5} and beyond (to verify); the landscape result for simple local search covers only part of the range with superlevel-set conditions.
source: R. Ge and T. Ma, On the Optimization Landscape of Tensor Decompositions, arXiv:1706.05598 (2017)
locator: to verify: Ge–Ma, main theorem (range of n and the superlevel condition) and open questions.
why_important: Tensor decomposition is the model nonconvex problem behind learning latent-variable models and two-layer networks (whose population loss under Gaussian inputs is a sum of tensor decompositions).
where_it_stands: Open in the full range as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: NeurIPS 2017 best paper (to verify).

title: End-to-end gradient training learns deep hierarchical functions
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Allen-Zhu and Li show that a deep network (a residual architecture with quadratic activations) trained by SGD learns a class of hierarchical functions (compositions of low-degree polynomials over L levels) with polynomial samples and time, while shallow and kernel methods cannot, using 'backward feature correction' between layers. Prove such a result for a standard architecture (ReLU or other common activations, standard initialization and parameterization), with all layers trained simultaneously, for a natural hierarchical target class of depth L ≥ 3, with sample complexity polynomial in d and exponential improvement over any kernel method.
statement_caveat: Most positive results train layers sequentially or use special architectures; three-layer results exist for restricted targets (to verify Nichani, Damian and Lee 2023).
source: Z. Allen-Zhu and Y. Li, Backward Feature Correction: How Deep Learning Performs Deep (Hierarchical) Learning, arXiv:2001.04413 (2020)
locator: to verify: the paper's discussion of its architectural assumptions.
why_important: It is the training-dynamics form of 'why deep beats shallow' (compare T294, T334).
where_it_stands: Open for standard architectures.
note: Fame: COLT 2023 (to verify); well-cited.

title: Catastrophic forgetting under random task orderings
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: In continual linear regression, a model is fit (by gradient descent to convergence, i.e. projection) on a sequence of T tasks, each a consistent linear system in R^d, cycling or sampling tasks from a fixed collection. Evron et al. bound the forgetting (loss on earlier tasks after k steps) and show it can be arbitrarily bad for adversarial orderings but decays for cyclic and random orderings. Determine the optimal worst-case rate of forgetting after k iterations under uniformly random task ordering, as a function of k (independent of d and of the task similarity), with matching lower bounds.
statement_caveat: Evron et al. give a rate for random orderings with dimension dependence; dimension-free rates were later obtained in part (to verify 2024-25 work, e.g. on the connection with Kaczmarz methods and random products of projections).
source: I. Evron, E. Moroshko, R. Ward, N. Srebro and D. Soudry, How catastrophic can catastrophic forgetting be in linear regression?, arXiv:2205.09588 (2022)
locator: to verify: Evron et al., open questions on random orderings.
why_important: It is the solvable model of continual learning, and reduces to products of random projections (random Kaczmarz) — a probability problem.
where_it_stands: Possibly partly solved since; to verify.
note: Fame: COLT 2022.

title: Global convergence of mean-field training for networks with three or more layers
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: For two-layer networks the mean-field limit of gradient descent is a Wasserstein gradient flow whose stationary points (under conditions) are global minimizers (T223). For networks with L ≥ 3 layers, Nguyen and Pham construct a rigorous mean-field limit (neuronal embeddings) and prove global convergence under strong assumptions (e.g. full support of the weight distributions that is preserved by the dynamics). Prove global convergence of the mean-field limit of gradient descent for a three-layer network with standard (e.g. iid Gaussian) initialization without assumptions that are not known to hold.
statement_caveat: Other works (Sirignano–Spiliopoulos, Araújo–Oliveira–Yukimura, Fang et al.) give limits with degenerate behaviour or under modified scalings.
source: P.-M. Nguyen and H. T. Pham, A Rigorous Framework for the Mean Field Limit of Multilayer Neural Networks, arXiv:2001.11443 (2020)
locator: to verify: Nguyen–Pham, the global convergence theorem's assumptions.
why_important: The mean-field theory explains feature learning for two layers; without a deep version it does not describe deep networks.
where_it_stands: Open without strong assumptions as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: Math. Stat. and Learning (to verify); key reference for deep mean-field limits.

title: Large step sizes for logistic regression and networks: non-monotone acceleration
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Wu, Bartlett, Telgarsky and Yu prove that gradient descent on the logistic loss of linearly separable data with an arbitrarily large constant step size eta converges, with an initial non-monotone phase, and reaches loss O(1/(eta·t)) after a burn-in, so larger steps optimize faster. Prove the analogous statement for two-layer networks (or deep homogeneous networks) on separable data: gradient descent with a large constant step size converges, and its speed after the non-monotone phase improves with the step size, explaining the edge-of-stability phenomenon for classification.
statement_caveat: Extensions to some nonlinear predictors in the near-linear regime exist (to verify).
source: J. Wu, P. L. Bartlett, M. Telgarsky and B. Yu, Large Stepsize Gradient Descent for Logistic Loss: Non-Monotonicity of the Loss Improves Optimization Efficiency, arXiv:2402.15926 (2024)
locator: to verify: Wu et al., conclusion (networks as open).
why_important: Practice uses step sizes far above the classical 2/L stability limit; this asks for a theory of why that works (compare T226, T227).
where_it_stands: Open for networks as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: COLT 2024.

title: Convergence of temporal-difference learning with neural networks beyond the lazy regime
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Temporal-difference learning with a value function parameterized by a neural network is not a gradient method and can diverge.
