Prove error bounds for one-step and few-step generation with consistency models trained by consistency distillation or consistency training, in Wasserstein or total-variation distance, in terms of the training loss, with explicit dependence on dimension and the number of steps, and identify when multi-step sampling improves on one step.
statement_caveat: Some bounds exist under strong Lipschitz assumptions (to verify 2023-25 work); sharp guarantees are open.
source: Y. Song, P. Dhariwal, M. Chen and I. Sutskever, Consistency Models, arXiv:2303.01469 (2023)
locator: to verify: Song et al., discussion.
why_important: One-step generation is how diffusion models are deployed fast; its accuracy is not understood.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICML 2023.

title: The tighter-bound paradox of importance-weighted autoencoders
domain_name: Deep learning: sampling, diffusion and generative models
statement: The importance-weighted bound with K samples tightens the evidence lower bound as K grows, but Rainforth et al. show that the signal-to-noise ratio of the gradient estimator for the inference network decays like K^{−1/2}, so tighter bounds can hurt learning of the encoder. Determine the optimal K (as a function of the training budget and model) for joint learning of generative and inference networks, and prove convergence rates for the doubly reparameterized or other estimators that fix the SNR decay.
statement_caveat: SNR asymptotics are proved; optimization-level guarantees are open (to verify).
source: T. Rainforth, A. R. Kosiorek, T. A. Le, C. J. Maddison, M. Igl, F. Wood and Y. W. Teh, Tighter Variational Bounds are Not Necessarily Better, arXiv:1802.04537 (2018)
locator: to verify: Rainforth et al., conclusion.
why_important: It is the clearest example of a Monte Carlo variance trade-off governing deep generative training.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICML 2018.

title: Scaling laws for reward-model overoptimization
domain_name: Deep learning: generalization, implicit bias and overparametrization
statement: Gao, Schulman and Hilton find that optimizing a policy against a learned proxy reward first increases and then decreases the true ('gold') reward, with the gold reward following simple functional forms in sqrt(KL) between policy and initial policy (e.g. d·(α − β·d) for best-of-n and d·(α − β·log d) for RL, d = sqrt(KL)). Derive these forms in a probabilistic model of the proxy-gold relationship (e.g. proxy = gold + heavy- or light-tailed noise, best-of-n selection), and determine how the turning point scales with the size of the reward model's training data.
statement_caveat: Best-of-n under Gaussian errors is partly analyzed; the RL form and the data scaling are empirical (to verify).
source: L. Gao, J. Schulman and J. Hilton, Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization, arXiv:2210.10760 (2022)
locator: to verify: Gao et al., Section on theory.
why_important: Goodhart's law in RLHF is a statement about extreme-value statistics of proxy errors.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: ICML 2023.

title: Offline reinforcement learning with function approximation: what coverage is needed?
domain_name: Deep learning: high-dimensional learning, statistical physics and computational limits
statement: Foster, Krishnamurthy, Simchi-Levi and Xu prove that offline RL with realizable value functions and an all-policy concentrable data distribution still requires sample size exponential in some parameter without further conditions (e.g. Bellman completeness). Characterize the weakest structural condition on the function class and the data distribution under which offline policy evaluation and optimization with general function approximation are possible with polynomially many samples.
statement_caveat: Bellman completeness or single-policy concentrability with pessimism suffices; lower bounds rule out realizability alone; the exact boundary is open (to verify).
source: D. J. Foster, A. Krishnamurthy, D. Simchi-Levi and Y. Xu, Offline Reinforcement Learning: Fundamental Barriers for Value Function Approximation, arXiv:2111.10919 (2021)
locator: to verify: Foster et al., open questions.
why_important: Learning from logged data is how RL is applied when exploration is unsafe; the boundary sets what is learnable.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: COLT 2022.

title: Does momentum accelerate stochastic gradient descent?
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Realizable streaming least squares: y = (w*, x) with x of covariance H, a fourth-moment bound E[|x|^2 x x^T] <= R^2 H, one fresh sample per step. Compare the heavy-ball recursion w_(t+1) = w_t - eta g_t + beta (w_t - w_(t-1)) with plain SGD, each at its optimal tuning: for a stated family of distributions (for example Gaussian x whose covariance has a power-law spectrum), compute the mean-square convergence rate of heavy ball at optimal (eta, beta) and decide for which members it beats SGD, separating the bias and variance terms and the effect of the mini-batch size. Kidambi, Netrapalli, Jain and Kakade show heavy ball gives no improvement in general; the accelerated stochastic method of Jain et al. and Nesterov momentum are different recursions and are kept apart.
statement_caveat: For least squares the picture is mostly settled; for nonconvex networks it is open (to verify).
source: R. Kidambi, P. Netrapalli, P. Jain and S. M. Kakade, On the insufficiency of existing momentum schemes for Stochastic Optimization, arXiv:1803.05591 (2018); P. Jain, S. M. Kakade, R. Kidambi, P. Netrapalli and A. Sidford, Accelerating Stochastic Gradient Descent For Least Squares Regression, arXiv:1704.08227 (2017)
locator: to verify: Kidambi et al., conclusion.
why_important: Momentum is in every deep-learning optimizer; whether its benefit is acceleration or something else is not settled.
where_it_stands: Open for networks.
note: Fame: ICLR 2018 oral (to verify).

audit.status_ref: Kidambi-Netrapalli-Jain-Kakade1803.05591 Proposition3 PDF p4, fully read with the two-coordinate realizable distribution pp3-4, proves asymptotic HB lower rate exp(-500t/kappa), any fixed step and momentum in[0,1]. NAG lower bound remains a conjecture explicitly p5. Jain-Kakade-Kidambi-Netrapalli-Sidford1704.08227 Theorem1/Corollary2 PDF p9, fully read with A1/A2 and definitions pp7-8, proves tail-averaged special ASGD bias exp(-n/(20 sqrt(kappa*kappa_tilde))) plus11*sigma^2*d/n after burn-in. This algorithm is not ordinary HB or the NAG recursion of the first paper.
audit.statement_ok: NO: repaired HB-versus-NAG distinction is correct. Define the exact momentum recursion, oracle, batch, sample/iteration budget, last versus averaged iterate, noise and bias/variance accuracy regime. Optimal rates depend on fourth moments/statistical condition number, not covariance alone. General network gains is a programme rather than one quantified claim.
audit.replace_with: Fix realizable fresh-sample least squares and one HB recursion, then classify its mean-square spectral radius for a specified distribution family versus optimally tuned SGD; separate mini-batch acceleration and additive-noise floors. Keep ordinary NAG and special ASGD distinct.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: exact heavy-ball covariance operator derived in T417_moment_operator.md; a low-dimensional finite-support family admits an explicit spectral/stability calculation. A full network classification is a PROGRAMME.
audit.locator: 1803.05591 Proposition3 PDF p4;NAG conjecture p5;experimental questions p6.1704.08227 A1/A2 p7,Algorithm1 and condition numbers p8,Theorem1/Corollary2/Sec2.3 open problems p9.

title: Optimal regret for Gaussian-process bandits
domain_name: Deep learning: high-dimensional learning, statistical physics and computational limits
statement: Srinivas, Krause, Kakade and Seeger prove that GP-UCB has regret Õ(sqrt(T·γ_T)·β_T), where γ_T is the maximal information gain of the kernel; Scarlett, Bogunovic and Cevher prove lower bounds for the squared-exponential and Matérn kernels. For the Matérn kernel with smoothness ν in dimension d, upper bounds for GP-UCB do not match the lower bound T^{(ν+d)/(2ν+d)}. Determine whether GP-UCB (or Thompson sampling) attains the lower bound, as asked by Vakili et al. (COLT 2021 open problem).
statement_caveat: Elimination-type algorithms attain the optimal rate (Salgia et al.; Li and Scarlett, to verify); for GP-UCB itself the question was posed as a COLT open problem.
source: N. Srinivas, A. Krause, S. M. Kakade and M. Seeger, Gaussian Process Optimization in the Bandit Setting: No Regret and Experimental Design, arXiv:0912.3995 (2009); J. Scarlett, I. Bogunovic and V. Cevher, Lower Bounds on Regret for Noisy Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization, arXiv:1706.00090 (2017)
locator: to verify: S. Vakili, J. Scarlett and T. Javidi, Open Problem: Tight Online Confidence Intervals for RKHS Elements, COLT 2021.
why_important: Bayesian optimization with GPs is how hyperparameters of networks are tuned; whether its standard algorithm is optimal is open.
where_it_stands: Open (GP-UCB optimality) as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: Srinivas et al. ICML 2010 test-of-time award; COLT 2021 open problem.

title: Why does low-rank adaptation (LoRA) work?
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Isotropic linear regression with a pretrained matrix W0 in R^(d_out x d_in), target W0 + Delta with Delta of rank r (or approximately rank r with stated singular values), n samples x ~ N(0, I) and Gaussian label noise. LoRA trains W0 + B A, B in R^(d_out x r), A in R^(r x d_in), from B = 0 and A random at a stated scale, by gradient descent on the square loss. Prove convergence to excess risk within a constant factor of full fine-tuning on the same data, with sample complexity of order r (d_in + d_out) times a condition-number factor and an iteration count depending on the conditioning of Delta, or exhibit a Delta for which it fails. Zeng and Lee characterize the expressive power of low-rank adaptation; the training guarantee is the question.
statement_caveat: Expressivity is known; training guarantees exist in linear or NTK regimes (to verify 2024-25 work).
source: Y. Zeng and K. Lee, The Expressive Power of Low-Rank Adaptation, arXiv:2310.17513 (2023)
locator: to verify: Zeng–Lee, conclusion.
why_important: LoRA is the standard way to adapt large models; it is a nonconvex low-rank matrix problem with random initialization.
where_it_stands: Open beyond linear or lazy regimes.
note: Fame: ICLR 2024.

audit.status_ref: Zeng-Lee2310.17513 Theorem3 PDF p6, fully read with Assumption1 and problem setting pp4-5, proves existential exact representation on bounded input support under rank/non-singularity conditions and allows updating all biases. Theorem5 p6 gives approximation bounds involving discarded singular values and network norms. These are not GD convergence or sample-complexity guarantees from standard B=0,A-random initialization.
audit.statement_ok: NO: define data law, network, loss, low-rank notion, trainable biases, comparator and convergence precision. Rank closeness does not supply a favorable GD basin. Sample dependence must retain ambient dimensions, typically r*(d_in+d_out-r), or specify additional structure; scalar-output rank-one linear updates already have p free coordinates.
audit.replace_with: Choose isotropic linear regression or a specified active-ReLU basin, compare LoRA GD with full fine-tuning under the same data, and target rates in r*(d_in+d_out) with conditioning and initialization dependence. Check later exact linear/NTK guarantees before claiming a new result.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: rank-one ambient-sample lower bound and dead-ReLU initialization diagnostic completed in T419_rank_diagnostics.md. These delimit assumptions and do not solve beyond-lazy LoRA training.
audit.locator: 2310.17513 problem setting/bias footnote PDF p4;Lemma2 p5;Assumption1,Theorems3/5,Corollary4 p6;empirical optimization discrepancy and limitations p9.

title: Is deep learning a renormalization group flow?
domain_name: Deep learning: random networks and infinite-width or infinite-depth limits
statement: Mehta and Schwab construct an exact mapping between the variational renormalization group and deep restricted Boltzmann machines, and Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick argue that deep networks are efficient because physical data are generated hierarchically, as in coarse-graining. Make one such claim a theorem: e.g. prove that for data from a critical (or near-critical) Ising model on a lattice, a deep network trained by maximum likelihood (an RBM stack or a deep generative model) learns layers that implement a coarse-graining whose fixed point is the RG fixed point, or prove that depth reduces the size needed to represent the critical distribution to a given accuracy.
statement_caveat: The mapping is exact only in a specific construction; the 'learned layers implement RG' claim is empirical and disputed.
source: P. Mehta and D. J. Schwab, An exact mapping between the Variational Renormalization Group and Deep Learning, arXiv:1410.3831 (2014); H. W. Lin, M. Tegmark and D. Rolnick, Why does deep and cheap learning work so well?, arXiv:1608.08225 (2016)
locator: to verify: Lin–Tegmark–Rolnick, discussion of hierarchical generative processes.
why_important: It would connect the success of depth to the mathematics of critical phenomena.
where_it_stands: Open (rigorous form).
note: Fame: Mehta–Schwab widely cited in physics; Lin–Tegmark–Rolnick in J. Stat. Phys. 2017.

title: Adaptive edge of stability: the preconditioned sharpness
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: Cohen et al. observe that full-batch adaptive methods run at an adaptive edge of stability: the top eigenvalue of the preconditioned Hessian P^(-1) H settles near the threshold 38/eta for Adam with beta1 = 0.9, while the raw sharpness keeps growing. With a fixed epsilon the preconditioned sharpness is at most |H|/epsilon, so epsilon must shrink with eta. For a randomly initialized rank-one or diagonal quadratic or deep linear model, full-batch Adam (or RMSProp) with stated betas, bias correction and epsilon = epsilon(eta) tending to 0 at a stated rate, prove that after a burn-in the preconditioned sharpness, or the curvature along the active direction, rises to and stays within o(1/eta) of the threshold while the loss decreases non-monotonically; characterize when the active-direction curvature rather than the top sharpness tracks the threshold.
statement_caveat: Gradient-descent EoS has partial proofs (self-stabilization, compare T226); the adaptive version is open (to verify).
source: J. M. Cohen, B. Ghorbani, S. Krishnan, N. Agarwal, S. Medapati, M. Badura, D. Suo, D. Cardoze, Z. Nado, G. E. Dahl and J. Gilmer, Adaptive Gradient Methods at the Edge of Stability, arXiv:2207.14484 (2022)
locator: to verify: Cohen et al., conclusion.
why_important: Adam trains essentially all large models; its stability regime decides what learning rates work.
where_it_stands: Open as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: widely cited follow-up to the EoS paper (ICLR 2021).

audit.status_ref: Cohen et al.2207.14484 AppendixA.1 Lemma2 PDF p14, fully read with recurrence, gives the frozen EMA-heavy-ball quadratic threshold 2*(1+beta1)/(eta*(1-beta1)),38/eta at beta1=.9; the adaptive-Adam claim is empirical. Fong-Yang2608.20638 Proposition3.1 and Theorems3.2/3.3 PDF pp5-6, fully opened, prove an exact rank-one 2-cycle and finite regime-exit/crossing statements under w_max>2 and, with momentum,beta2>beta1^2. These are partial rigorous adaptive EoS results, not eventual top-eigenvalue O(eta^c) attraction for general networks. Additional2608.20638 Theorems3.4/3.5 PDF p7 fully opened: diagonal-quadratic Adam active-curvature alternatives and general C2 bounded-Hessian gradient-coercive nondegenerate-stationary RMSProp active-curvature crossings around2 up to C_f epsilon/eta, with never-finitely-stationary assumption. These do not give the row uniform eventual eta^c band for Adam; raw inactive-direction sharpness has a source counterexample.
audit.statement_ok: NO: quantify the data/model, initialization, beta parameters, bias correction, epsilon relative to eta, probability and time interval. Fixed epsilon and bounded Hessian preclude attraction to a threshold diverging as1/eta for all small eta. Distinguish frozen stability from adaptive dynamics and maximum sharpness from active directional curvature.
audit.replace_with: Choose random-initialized rank-one or diagonal quadratic/deep-linear model and specify epsilon/eta scaling, burn-in and observable. Improve a particular theorem from the2026 rank-one analysis or characterize when active curvature, rather than top sharpness, tracks the threshold.
audit.solver_shape: DAYS: frozen-threshold and epsilon-regime diagnostic completed in T421_threshold_diagnostic.md. Generic top-sharpness attraction for nonlinear networks is a PROGRAMME.
audit.locator: 2207.14484 empirical statement PDF p1;fixed/adaptive preconditioning p3;AppendixA.1 Lemma2 p14.2608.20638 definitions/rank-one reduction and Proposition3.1/Theorem3.2 p5,Theorem3.3 p6;sharpness-directional distinction pp6-7.

title: The critical batch size and the gradient noise scale
domain_name: Deep learning: training dynamics and optimization
statement: McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei et al. predict that the critical batch size is about the gradient noise scale B_noise = tr(Sigma)/|G|^2 and that steps and examples trade off as (S/S_min - 1)(E/E_min - 1) = 1. For online SGD on high-dimensional linear regression with Gaussian inputs, a power-law covariance spectrum and a power-law target (stated exponents), and a step size tuned optimally (constant or a stated schedule) for each batch size B, compute the number of steps S(B) and examples E(B) needed to reach excess risk epsilon, prove two-sided bounds with explicit constants on the trade-off curve, and express the critical batch size through the exponents and epsilon, comparing it with B_noise and B_simple along training.
statement_caveat: Results for linear regression with power-law spectra exist (to verify 2024-25 work on critical batch size scaling); the network case is open.
source: S. McCandlish, J. Kaplan, D. Amodei and the OpenAI Dota Team, An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training, arXiv:1812.06162 (2018)
locator: to verify: McCandlish et al., Section 2 (the model's derivation from a quadratic approximation).
why_important: The critical batch size decides how far data-parallel training of large models can be scaled.
where_it_stands: Open for networks as far as the writer knows.
note: Fame: the gradient noise scale is used to plan large training runs.

State a two-sided approximate frontier with constants rather than universal exact equality; extend to feature learning only after that baseline.
